This study investigated the longitudinal trends of Salmonella serovars and the molecular epidemiology of colistin resistance in 4,198 isolates from cattle, pigs, chickens, and ducks in South Korea (2019–2024). Among the 93 serovars identified, S. Infantis (40.

title: Hederagenin Promotes Sorafenib Sensitivity in Hepatocellular Carcinoma Through Suppressing SLC7A11 Expression and Inducing Ferroptosis
creator: Hai‐mei Jiang, Yu‐wan Zhou, Jian‐yu Zhang, Fu‐zhen Pan, Jin‐Fang Zhang, Ya‐ge Zhang
description: Sorafenib (SOR) significantly improves the survival rate for patients with advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Nevertheless, the clinical efficacy is restricted by the development of acquired resistance. Therefore, enhancing susceptibility of HCC cells to SOR is of critical importance for patients with advanced disease. Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) possesses considerable potential to overcome SOR resistance.

title: Updates in the pathophysiology of COVID-19 infection in male reproductive and sexual health: a literature review
creator: Meshari A. Alzahrani, Khalid O. Alkhani, Abdullah M. Alassaf, Jehad I. Alorainy, Saleh Binsaleh, Raed Almannie
description: This extensive comprehensive review explores the impact of the Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic on men’s sexual and reproductive health. We conducted a literature review focusing on the possible pathophysiology by which severe acute respiratory syndrome corona virus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) affects men’s sexual and reproductive systems.

title: Profiling Hydrolysis Rates of αS1‐Casein to αS1‐I‐Casein During Cheese Ripening by Intact‐Protein Liquid Chromatography–High Resolution Mass Spectrometry
creator: Sebastiaan Dolman, Marjolein van der Eijk, Loes Bevers, Kees Muijlwijk, Mee Loke Lim, Margriet Hendriks, Nicolas Abello, Rob van der Hoeven
description: RationaleThe proteolytic behavior of chymosins during cheese ripening impacts cheese texture, flavor, and quality. Especially, the specific hydrolysis of αS1‐casein to αS1‐I‐casein is relevant for early cheese texture development, and this activity varies between chymosin variants. Accurate profiling of αS1‐casein and αS1‐I‐casein during cheese ripening is crucial for understanding these differences between chymosins and the impact on cheese quality.

title: Correction: Diagnostic accuracy of deep learning vs. human raters for detecting osteoporotic vertebral compression fractures in routine CT scans
creator: Evamaria O. Riedel, David Schinz, Matthias Keicher, Sebastian Rühling, Malek El Husseini, Chantal Pellegrini, Thomas Baum, Michael Dieckmeyer, Luca Malagutti, Isabel Seeger, Anna S. Walburga, Benedikt Wiestler, Nico Sollmann, Maximilian T. Löffler, Arthur Wagner, Jan S. Kirschke
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). g/10.1007/s00330-026-12393-y, published online 24 February 2026 The authors regret to inform that an error occurred in the statistical analysis presented in Tables 1–4 of the original article. Due to a default setting in the statistical software (R), the negative class (no fracture) was incorrectly assigned as the ‘positive class’ for the calculation of sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), and negative predictive value (NPV).

title: Biopterin metabolism and nitric oxide recoupling in cancer
creator: Gene Chatman Clark, Alan Lai, Aashri Agarwal, Zheng Liu, Xiang-Yang Wang
description: Tetrahydrobiopterin is a cofactor necessary for the activity of several enzymes, the most studied of which is nitric oxide synthase. The role of this cofactor-enzyme relationship in vascular biology is well established. Recently, tetrahydrobiopterin metabolism has received increasing attention in the field of cancer immunology and immunotherapy due to its involvement in the cytotoxic T cell response.

title: CT-guided spinal nerve root adhesiolysis for refractory atypical symptoms in cervical disc herniation: a retrospective cohort study
creator: Qiong Xian, Yang Mao-jiang, Yang Hong-ying, Yang Han-feng, Xu Xiao-xue, Du Yong
description: ObjectiveTo evaluate the clinical efficacy and safety of CT-guided spinal nerve root adhesiolysis in treating refractory atypical symptoms—specifically dizziness and tinnitus—in patients with cervical disc herniation (CDH).MethodsThis retrospective cohort study included 256 patients with CDH presenting with persistent atypical symptoms who had failed conservative therapy for at least 3 months.

title: Parents’ and Children’s Perceptions and Attitudes Towards Traditional and Novel Plant-Based Meat Alternatives: A Scoping Review
creator: Ai Ting Goh, Yunfan Mo, Jessica C McCormack, Indrawati Oey, Joanne Hort, Mei Peng
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The growing popularity of plant-based meat alternatives (PBMAs) as a sustainable dietary option highlights the need to understand family perceptions to support their integration into daily diets. Early-life food preferences often stem from parents or caregivers. This scoping review synthesized existing findings on parents’ and children’s perceptions of traditional and novel PBMAs and identified motivators and barriers to adopting them in family meals.

title: Case report: ZFYVE19 gene mutation is associated with familial cholestasis
creator: Mei-Yan Xue, Ling-Ling Huang, Yue-Yong Zhu, Qi Zheng
description: The etiology of cholestatic liver disease is complex, with clinical manifestations being nonspecific, and biochemical abnormalities mainly characterized by elevated alkaline phosphatase (ALP) and glutamyl transpeptidase (GGT). Due to the lack of specific symptoms and diverse causes, the diagnosis poses certain challenges. Here, we present a case of liver cirrhosis with predominant cholestatic features of unknown etiology.

title: RESULT-Hip. The impact of restrictive compared with liberal transfusion strategy on cardiac injury and death in patients undergoing surgery for hip fracture
creator: The RESULT Hip Study Group
description: AimsHip fracture is a global health issue. Complications are common, leading to reduced quality of life or death. These occur more frequently if anaemia is present. We hypothesize that correcting anaemia in the perioperative period may decrease major adverse cardiac events (MACE) and death after hip fracture.

title: Spatiotemporal Computational Meta‐Imager for Broadband Dual‐Layer Optical Convolution
creator: Mengguang Wang, Chenglong Zheng, Huaping Zang, Changwei Zhang, Huai Xia, Chang Wang, Zhenrong Zheng
description: Optical neural networks face a tradeoff between device footprint and computational expressivity: deep systems are bulky, whereas single‐layer hardware lacks intrinsic depth and native negative‐weight support. We experimentally demonstrate a single‐layer metalens imager with “spatiotemporal intrinsic depth” for equivalent broadband dual‐layer convolution.

title: Single-cell landscape of immune remodeling in alopecia areata suggests MIF + fibroblasts and their potential ligand-receptor crosstalk with dendritic cells
creator: Xuemei Lan, Haiyan Li, Yunting Xiao
description: BackgroundAlopecia areata (AA) is an autoimmune hair loss disorder. Although autoreactive CD8+ T cells are central effectors, the roles of stromal and epithelial compartments in sustaining inflammation remain unclear.MethodsThis study analyzed publicly available scRNA-seq data from the GEO database (GSE212450, GSE233906), comprising 15 scalp samples from normal skin (NS), non-lesional (NL), and AA conditions.

title: Archetypal analysis of pain measures in a diverse population-based cohort: Exploring cross-sectional relationships with outcomes
creator: Parsa Pazooki, Liubov Arbeeva, Simoni Tomar, Carolina Alvarez, Tessa Walker, Yvonne M Golightly, B Duncan X Lascelles, Amanda E Nelson
description: ObjectivePain experiences are complex, multifactorial, and subjective. Pain phenotyping can provide a holistic view of pain experiences by identifying distinct pain profiles. This study aimed to characterize chronic pain phenotypes using multiple validated osteoarthritis (OA) pain measures and assess their associations with functional and psychological outcomes.

title: Survival and morbidity in very preterm infants in Shenzhen: a multi-center study
creator: Tingting Li, Guofei Zhang, Rui Li, Shengnan He, Fangshi Zhang, Xudong Yan, Zhangbin Yu, Yingmei Xie, Guichao Zhong
description: ObjectiveTo analyze survival and morbidity among very preterm infants (VPIs) in Shenzhen and explore factors associated with survival without major morbidity.MethodsBetween January 2022 and December 2022, 797 infants were admitted to 25 neonatal intensive care units in Shenzhen with gestational age (GA) < 32 weeks, excluded discharged against medical advice, insufficient information, and congenital malformation, 742 VPIs were included.

title: Lewis Acid‐Catalyzed Strain‐Enabled (3+3) Annulation of Bicyclo[1.1.0]Butanes With Indolylalcohols: Synthesis of Indole‐Fused Aza‐Bicyclo[3.1.1]Heptanes
creator: Mainak Dey, Tuhin Subhra Das Mahapatra, Pragya Sharma, Manoj V Mane, Chinmoy Kumar Hazra
description: Strain release has long inspired the discovery of unique reactivity, enabling diverse synthetically valuable transformations. Bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs), due to their high ring strain, have emerged as versatile building blocks for constructing complex bicyclic architectures. Herein, we report a Lewis acid‐catalyzed formal (3 + 3) annulation of BCBs with indolyl alcohols, providing rapid access to indole‐fused aza‐bicyclo[3.1.1]heptanes.

title: Overcoming barriers and enhancing strategies in organ transplantation systems: a systematic review
creator: Priya Sharma, Nipin Kalal, Nimarta Rana
description: BackgroundOrgan transplantation is one of the major achievements of modern medicine, yet the global shortage of organs remains a serious challenge. This shortage increases mortality among patients on waiting lists. Although up to 80% of people support organ donation, far fewer register as donors, creating a clear “knowledge–action gap.

title: Using Normalisation Process Theory to Develop a Complex Intervention: A Qualitative Case Study of Screening for Homelessness in Healthcare Settings
creator: Nilakshi Gunatillaka, Tze Lin Chai, Suzanne Nielsen, Belinda Hammond, Kimberley Norman, Helen Skouteris, Elizabeth Sturgiss
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background and AimsNormalisation Process Theory (NPT) seeks to describe and explain how a complex intervention can be embedded into an existing health and social care system. NPT is frequently used to evaluate interventions, and less frequently to design them.We demonstrate how NPT can be applied to exploratory qualitative data to understand the potential barriers and facilitators to the implementation of a new intervention in a health setting using the NPT framework.

title: Mechanistic study on the reduction of TNF-α and β-CTX levels in RA patients by moxibustion combined with western medication through regulation of the Wnt/β-catenin pathway
creator: Hui Wang, Heshan Chen, Yuan Li, Yi Yang, Xiaojuan Hong, Ping Wu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background and aimsThe pathological core of rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is progressive bone destruction driven by chronic inflammation. The Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway plays a key regulatory role in bone metabolism, but it is disrupted by the inflammatory environment in RA. This study investigates the mechanism by which moxibustion combined with conventional Western medicine modulates the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway to coordinate inflammation and bone metabolism in rheumatoid arthritis (RA).MethodsThis study randomly assigned 70 patients to a moxibustion group (n=35) and a control group (n=35).

title: Proteome analysis of the prefrontal cortex and the application of machine learning models for the identification of potential biomarkers related to suicide
creator: Manuel Alejandro Rojo-Romero, Nora Andrea Gutiérrez-Nájera, Carlos Sabás Cruz-Fuentes, Ana Luisa Romero-Pimentel, Roberto Mendoza-Morales, Fernando García-Dolores, Mirna Edith Morales-Marín, Xóchitl Castro-Martínez, Elier González-Sáenz, Jonatan Torres-Campuzano, Tania Medina-Sánchez, Karla Hernánde
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). IntroductionSuicide is a significant public health problem, with increased rates in low- and middle-income countries such as Mexico; therefore, suicide prevention is important. Suicide is a complex and multifactorial phenomenon in which biological and social factors are involved. Several studies on the biological mechanisms of suicide have analyzed the proteome of the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) in people who have died by suicide.

title: Single-cell extracellular vesicle-program scoring maps immunometabolic rewiring and immune crosstalk of mesenchymal stromal cells in intervertebral disc degeneration, prioritizing AP2S1 and CSTB
creator: Fengyu Ma, Kelv Shen, Ziqiang Wu, Hanshi Yang, Mingzhe Yu, Zhendong Huang, Fengxuan Han, Zhengfeng Lu
description: BackgroundIntervertebral disc degeneration (IDD) is increasingly viewed as an immune-perturbed and metabolically stressed niche rather than a purely mechanical or aging-related disorder. Mesenchymal stromal cells (MSCs) and their extracellular vesicles (EVs) may shape local immune signaling, yet MSC EV–associated transcriptional programs and their immune-network context remain poorly defined at single-cell resolution.

title: Economic autonomy as a determinant of physical activity behavior in Chinese older adults
creator: Yuanheng Liu, Xianglin Luo, Hao Xu
description: BackgroundThe physical activity of the old people is affected by many factors, and the economic situation is an important factor affecting the physical activity. However, the relationship between economic autonomy and physical activity patterns among older adult Chinese has not been fully studied.

title: Interferon receptor gene dosage differentially regulates hypoxia-induced platelet activation and pulmonary hypertension in down syndrome
creator: Janelle N. Posey, Mariah Jordan, Amanda Olsen-Dufour, Thi-Tina N. Nguyen, Christine Farrell, Caitlin V. Lewis, Jamie L. Archambault, Christina Sul, Daniel Colon-Hidalgo, Eva S. Nozik, Joaquin M. Espinosa, Kelly D. Sullivan, Cassidy Delaney
description: Trisomy 21 (T21) results in Down syndrome (DS), a condition associated with a high prevalence of pulmonary complications. Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is a significant comorbidity in individuals with T21. Inflammation is a well-established driver of PH, and growing evidence implicates platelets as active contributors to inflammatory-mediated pulmonary vascular disease and PH.

title: Data sources and applied methods for paclitaxel safety signal discernment
creator: Laura Elisabeth Gressler, Erika Avila-Tang, Jialin Mao, Alejandra Avalos-Pacheco, Fadia T. Shaya, Yelizaveta Torosyan, Alexander Liebeskind, Madris Kinard, Christina D. Mack, Sharon-Lise Normand, Mary E. Ritchey, Danica Marinac-Dabic
description: BackgroundFollowing the identification of a late mortality signal, the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) convened an advisory panel that concluded that additional clinical study data are needed to comprehensively evaluate the late mortality signal observed with the use of drug-coated balloons (DCB) and drug-eluting stent (DES).

title: Healthcare exceptionalism in patient perspectives on AI: implications for policy and practice
creator: Paige Nong, Molin Ji, Jodyn Platt
description: IntroductionEvolving healthcare policy and debates about patient protections require empirical evidence on public perspectives to promote trust and sustainability. If the public does not see AI in healthcare as fundamentally distinct from AI in other domains, major policy intervention or fundamental changes to AI governance may not be necessary.

title: Social support, educational, and behavioral modification interventions for improving household disaster preparedness in the general community-dwelling population: a systematic review and meta-analysis
creator: Taryn Amberson, Tara Heagele, Tamar Wyte-Lake, Mary Pat Couig, Sue Anne Bell, Manoj J Mammen, Valerie Wells, Jessica Castner
description: BackgroundThe efficacy of household emergency preparedness interventions for community-dwelling, non-institutionalized people is largely unknown.ObjectiveTo ascertain the state of the science on social support, educational, and behavioral modification interventions to improve all-hazard household disaster preparedness.DesignSystematic review and meta-analysis.MethodsDatabases, trial registers, reports, and websites were searched, and citation trails followed utilizing replicable methods.

title: Therapeutic Peptide‐Programmed Liquid‐Crystalline Topology Switching for pH‐Gated Postoperative Cancer Immunotherapy
creator: Yan Yan, Bin Chen, Yanqing Wang, Yuxi Hou, Zhenlin Ma, Zini Yang, Xia Yin, Yiling Chen, Litao Huang, Menghan Cai, Xinlin Liu, Yi Zhun Zhu, Li Ye
description: Stimuli‐responsive depots for postoperative cancer therapy often treat therapeutic payloads as passive cargo, resulting in premature leakage and limited on‐demand activation. Herein, we report a therapeutic peptide‐programmed liquid‐crystalline depot in which the Vpr‐derived antitumor peptide (VDAP) functions simultaneously as an immunotherapeutic effector and a supramolecular topology regulator.

title: Power and vulnerability: managing sensitive language in organizational communication
creator: Patrick G. T. Healey, Prashant Khare, Ignacio Castro, Gareth Tyson, Mladen Karan, Ravi Shekhar, Stephen McQuistin, Colin Perkins, Matthew Purver
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Organizational responsibilities can give people power but also expose them to scrutiny. This tension leads to divergent predictions about the use of potentially sensitive language: power might license it, while exposure might inhibit it. Analysis of peoples' language use in a large corpus of organizational emails using standardized Linguistic Inquiry and Word Count (LIWC) measures shows a systematic difference in the use of words with potentially sensitive (ethnic, religious, or political) connotations.

title: Persistent Photoluminescence Superlinearity Beyond Static Recombination Physics in Metal Halide Perovskites
creator: Mehri Ghasemi, Qi Li, Baohua Jia, Xiaoming Wen
description: Persistent intermediate power‐law exponent (β) values in metal halide perovskites commonly occur across excitation regimes in which assignment to a single carrier‐population recombination limit becomes ambiguous. Their strong dependence on excitation conditions further indicates that excitation‐dependent photoluminescence cannot always be interpreted uniquely through a static Shockley‐Read‐Hall (SRH)‐bimolecular‐Auger recombination picture.

title: Surviving ChatGPT in healthcare
creator: Zhengliang Liu, Lu Zhang, Zihao Wu, Xiaowei Yu, Chao Cao, Haixing Dai, Ninghao Liu, Jun Liu, Wei Liu, Quanzheng Li, Dinggang Shen, Xiang Li, Dajiang Zhu, Tianming Liu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). At the dawn of of Artificial General Intelligence (AGI), the emergence of large language models such as ChatGPT show promise in revolutionizing healthcare by improving patient care, expanding medical access, and optimizing clinical processes. However, their integration into healthcare systems requires careful consideration of potential risks, such as inaccurate medical advice, patient privacy violations, the creation of falsified documents or images, overreliance on AGI in medical education, and the perpetuation of biases.

title: Pro-environmental behavioral intention in university energy-saving contexts: extending the Value–Belief–Norm framework with institutional support
creator: Xiaolin Zhang, Songyu Jiang, Jirawan Deeprasert
description: ObjectiveWith increasing energy demands across the globe and increased focus in sustainable development agenda, higher education institutions (HEIs) are relevant in developing energy-saving cognitions and attitudes of students.PurposeThis paper will examine how university leadership, sustainability-oriented education, environmental values, environmental beliefs, and personal norms influence and affect the pro-environmental behavioral intention (PEBI) of HEIs students.

title: Magnetoelectric Multiferroics for the Next‐Generation Ultralow‐Power Electronics
creator: Yang Liu, Yunlong Sun, Hao Luo, Duoduo Zhao, Yuhan Zeng, Xuzihan Zhang, Zhewei Liu, Hao Peng, Zhijing Zhang, Jack Yang, Ji Zhang, Danyang Wang, Junjie Shi, Sean Li
description: Magnetoelectric multiferroics enable voltage control of magnetic states for low‐energy, non‐volatile memory and logic. Their practical value, however, depends on the complete device pathway, not coupling strength alone. This Review evaluates materials, switching mechanisms, and devices against these requirements, distinguishing measured performance from projected targets.

title: Data‐Driven and Physics‐Informed Modeling Perspectives for Soft Manipulators: From SINDy to Hybrid Intelligence
creator: Wenbo Hui, Yunyi Wang, Teng Zhang, Yang Chen, Min Pan
description: Soft manipulators offer a route to safer, more adaptive and physically intelligent robots, but their compliant bodies remain difficult to model, predict and control. Large deformation, distributed actuation, hysteresis, material variability and contact‐rich interaction challenge both classical mechanics‐based models and purely data‐driven approaches.

title: Molecular phylogenetic analyses reveal multiple long-distance dispersal events and extensive cryptic speciation in Nervilia (Orchidaceae), an isolated basal Epidendroid genus
creator: Stephan W. Gale, Jihong Li, Somran Suddee, Paweena Traiperm, Craig I. Peter, Tomas Buruwate, Benjamin J. Crain, Melissa K. McCormick, Dennis F. Whigham, Arni Musthofa, Khyanjeet Gogoi, Katsura Ito, Yukio Minamiya, Tatsuya Fukuda, Sven Landrein, Tomohisa Yukawa
description: IntroductionThe terrestrial orchid genus Nervilia is diagnosed by its hysteranthous pattern of emergence but is nested among leafless myco-heterotrophic lineages in the lower Epidendroideae. Comprising ca. 80 species distributed across Africa, Asia and Oceania, the genus remains poorly known and plagued by vague and overlapping species circumscriptions, especially within each of a series of taxonomically intractable species complexes.

title: Thioredoxin‐2 Alleviates Osteoporosis by Restraining FOXO3a Nuclear Translocation
creator: Chi Zhan, Zhaocai Zhou, Yue Ding, Rong Lian, Xinyu Li, Xintong Zhang, Jie Cao, Zhonghui Tang, Zhengmei Lin, Zhi Song, Feng He
description: Osteoporosis is a prevalent age‐ and disease‐associated skeletal disorder characterized by bone loss, remodeling imbalance, and vascular niche deterioration, yet how endothelial redox dysfunction drives this process remains unclear. Here, we identify mitochondrial thioredoxin‐2 (TRX2) as an endothelial safeguard against osteoporotic bone loss.

title: Association of work ability with job burnout and sleep quality among biosafety laboratory personnel in Xinjiang, China: a cross-sectional study
creator: Keke Ju, Ruikai Wu, Jing Yu, Lei Ding, Mengjie Xia, Jiwen Liu, Yaoqin Lu
description: BackgroundIn recent years, the importance of biosafety research has garnered significant attention due to its critical implications for public health and safety. Biosafety Laboratory (BSL) personnel face numerous challenges as they work with high-risk pathogens, including high-pressure environments, stringent safety protocols, and the risk of infection.

title: Foundation Model‐Enabled Pathology‐Informed MRI Model for Preoperative Prediction of Vessels Encapsulating Tumor Clusters in Resectable Hepatocellular Carcinoma: A Multicenter Retrospective Study
creator: Zhehan Shen, Wanmin Liu, Xiaoming Li, Wenjie Zou, Yiman Li, Jie Yuan, Yasen Yimit, Shihang Wang, Linhao Qu, Hui Dong, Wei Chen, Ningyang Jia, Peijun Wang
description: Vessels encapsulating tumor clusters (VETC) are an aggressive vascular phenotype of hepatocellular carcinoma that is usually determined after surgery. A foundation model‐enabled framework for pathology‐informed VETC prediction on pretreatment magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), termed PIVOT, uses paired preoperative multiparametric MRI, postoperative hematoxylin and eosin whole‐slide images, and CD34 immunohistochemistry during model development, while inference requires only preoperative MRI.

title: Psychological contract, psychological capital, career plateau, and job embeddedness among early-career nurses: a serial mediation model
creator: Ximei Wang, Yujuan Qin, Qin Mao, Jianying Wang
description: BackgroundEarly-career nurses are critical for sustaining the nursing workforce, yet they are particularly vulnerable to stress, role transition difficulties, and turnover. Job embeddedness offers an important lens for understanding why nurses stay, but the psychological mechanisms linking organizational perceptions to embeddedness remain insufficiently understood in this population.

title: Arthroscopic Saucerization and Anatomic Repair of a Wrisberg Variant Discoid Lateral Meniscus: A Physeal‐Sparing Knotless Anchor Technique
creator: Stephen Rossettie, Ann Hu, Dan Griffin, Greg Perraut, Ryan Murray
description: Discoid lateral meniscus (DLM) is a congenital variant of the knee characterized by an abnormally shaped meniscus prone to tearing and instability. When symptomatic, the treatment plan is based on the location and pattern of the tear, as well as the presence of instability. In most cases, posterior horn instability is present, but some meniscotibial or root attachments remain.

title: Breast milk preservation: thermal and non-thermal processes and their effect on microorganism inactivation and the content of bioactive and nutritional compounds
creator: Alejandro Núñez-Delgado, Victoria Margarita Mizrachi-Chávez, Jorge Welti-Chanes, Samantha Thania Macher-Quintana, Cristina Chuck-Hernández
description: Human Breast Milk (HBM) is widely acknowledged as the best nutritional source for neonates. Data indicates that, in 2019, 83.2% of infants in the United States received breast milk at birth, slightly reducing to 78.6% at 1 month. Despite these encouraging early figures, exclusive breastfeeding rates sharply declined, dropping to 24.9% by 6 months.

title: Breast acinic cell carcinoma with weak progesterone receptor expression: a case report and literature review
creator: Caiyun Bai, Xiaodong Xin, Yisen Yang, Fengjiang Qu, Zhimin Fan
description: RationaleAcinic cell carcinoma (AcCC) of the breast is an extremely rare malignant epithelial tumor characterized by acini cell differentiation, clinical low-grade malignancy, and a molecular triple-negative subtype.Patient concernA 47-year-old female presented with a 1-month history of a painless mass in her right breast.DiagnosisUltrasound imaging, mammography and magnetic resonance imaging revealed a lesion, approximately 3.0cm×1.

title: Bring the pain: wounding reveals a transition from cortical excitability to epithelial excitability in Xenopus embryos
creator: Leslie A. Sepaniac, Nicholas R. Davenport, William M. Bement
description: The cell cortex plays many critical roles, including interpreting and responding to internal and external signals. One behavior which supports a cell’s ability to respond to both internal and externally-derived signaling is cortical excitability, wherein coupled positive and negative feedback loops generate waves of actin polymerization and depolymerization at the cortex.

title: Arthroscopic Circumferential Labral Repair and Biceps Tenodesis in Elite Throwing Athletes: Technical Considerations
creator: Michael Nocek, Brendon C Mitchell, Lorenz Fritsch, Alan D Villegas Meza, Caroline B Herrmann, Peter J Millett
description: SLAP lesions are a common cause of shoulder pain in overhead athletes and are often seen together with circumferential labral tearing, partial‐thickness rotator cuff tearing, and biceps pathology. Isolated repair of the superior labrum has produced inconsistent outcomes, with low return‐to‐play rates in professional throwers.

title: Green toxicology only becomes beautiful through AI
creator: Alexandra Maertens, Thomas Hartung
description: Green Toxicology extends the principles of Green Chemistry by embedding toxicological foresight into chemical design, with the aim of preventing hazards before substances reach markets or the environment. Its conceptual pillars—prevention, precaution, life-cycle thinking, and avoidance of regrettable substitutions—align closely with sustainability agendas such as the European Green Deal and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals.

title: Tubocapsenolide A Overcomes Oxaliplatin Resistance in Colorectal Cancer by Targeting PLK1 to Impair CEP55–ESCRT‐Associated Vesicular Damage Clearance
creator: Yueying Yang, Jing Liang, Lu Wang, Hongyan Zhang, Zhiruo Zhang, Yang Liu, Rui Zhu, Wen Xu, Shaohua Xu, Dejuan Sun, Ke Xiang, Yali Wang, Zhimin Fan, Zheng Wang, Hua Li, Lixia Chen
description: Oxaliplatin (L‐OHP) is a first‐line chemotherapeutic agent for advanced colorectal cancer (CRC) and postoperative adjuvant therapy. However, acquired L‐OHP resistance remains a clinical obstacle. Here, we identify Tubocapsenolide A (TA), a natural withanolide isolated from Tubocapsicum anomalum, as a promising antitumor agent that suppresses CRC growth and sensitizes L‐OHP‐resistant CRC to L‐OHP.

title: How does climate change impact health in the African primary care context?
creator: Christian Lueme Lokotola
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Primary health care in the African setting is the foundational level for accessing health services; but the quality of services is often challenged by different systemic vulnerabilities. Climate change occurs as a threat multiplier that amplifies these vulnerabilities. This continuing professional development article aims to update the knowledge of primary care providers with evidence-based information on the impact of climate change on health, healthcare services and facilities.

title: Pyrolyzed Photoresist as a Continuous‐Tone Mask for Grayscale Lithography
creator: Tielyr D Creason, Gavin C Gee, Zachary T Piontkowski, Toai Ton‐That, Robert Reyna, Edward R Arata, Mason Risley, Jacob D Boissiere, Bryan Kaehr, D Bruce Burckel
description: Grayscale lithography enables single‐step fabrication of continuous 3D surface relief for complex optics, MEMS, and scalable replication templates. However, its broad adoption is hindered by the cost, complexity, and resolution constraints associated with fabricating high‐quality grayscale masks. Here, we address this challenge by developing a method to produce continuous‐tone photolithography masks/reticles through the pyrolysis of 2.

title: Posterior inference of Hi-C contact frequency through sampling
creator: Yanlin Zhang, Christopher J. F. Cameron, Mathieu Blanchette
description: Hi-C is one of the most widely used approaches to study three-dimensional genome conformations. Contacts captured by a Hi-C experiment are represented in a contact frequency matrix. Due to the limited sequencing depth and other factors, Hi-C contact frequency matrices are only approximations of the true interaction frequencies and are further reported without any quantification of uncertainty.

title: Poloxamer‐Enabled Thermoresponsive Biobased Controlled‐Release Fertilizer for On‐Demand Nutrient Delivery
creator: Jiahui Liu, Junyin Li, Ziyao Li, Xiangjie Zhao, Fengyan Fang, Yan Liu, Songyuan Wang, Boning Su, Yuanyuan Yao, Bin Gao, Shugang Zhang, Yuechao Yang
description: Synchronizing nutrient release of fertilizers with crop uptake remains a central challenge in precision agriculture. Here, we present a novel temperature‐responsive biobased controlled‐release fertilizer (TRBFs) incorporating Poloxamer 407 (F127) as a thermal switch within a castor oil‐derived polyurethane coating. The optimized TRBF10 (3 wt.% coating rate, 10 wt.

title: PBRM1 Deficiency in Microglia Leads to Excessive Neurogenesis and Autism‐Like Behaviors via the CCL5‐CCR1/5‐β‐catenin Signaling Axis
creator: Yang‐Yang Duan, Lin‐Fei Jiao, Pei‐Pei Liu, Chun‐Hui Duan, Xiao Li, Zi‐Han Zhang, Yue‐Qi Zhang, Xin‐Li Ouyang, Hong‐Zhen Du, Sha Liu, Yi Tang, Zhao‐Qian Teng, Chang‐Mei Liu
description: The prevalence of autism spectrum disorder (ASD), a heterogeneous neurodevelopmental disorder with limited effective therapeutic drugs, has been rising worldwide. Missense mutations in Polybromo 1 (Pbrm1), a core component of the SWI/SNF (switch/sucrose non‐fermentable) chromatin remodeling complex, have been identified as a risk factor for ASD; however, whether PBRM1 loss of function contributes to the pathogenesis remains elusive.

title: Atorvastatin improves hyperlipidemia-induced erectile dysfunction via PKA-associated eNOS phosphorylation at the Ser633 site
creator: Xinghao Zhang, Xu Wang, Ziheng Zhang, Ziyang Han, Yang Sun, Xue Yang, Yun Chen
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionHyperlipidemia contributes to vasculogenic erectile dysfunction (ED) by reducing endothelial nitric oxide bioavailability. Although atorvastatin has been reported to improve ED, the upstream mechanism by which it restores endothelial nitric oxide synthase (eNOS) activity remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the therapeutic effect of atorvastatin in hyperlipidemia-induced erectile dysfunction (HLED) and to determine whether protein kinase A (PKA)-associated phosphorylation of eNOS at Ser633 contributes to this effect.MethodsHyperlipidemia-induced erectile dysfunction was induced in rats by a high-fat diet.

title: Gut microbiota mediates the pro-pyroptosis effect of xierezhuyubuxu decoction in hepatocellular carcinoma
creator: Zhili Zeng, Mingxuan Feng, Fan He, Enxin Zhang, Xiushen Li, Zebiao Cao
description: IntroductionXierezhuyubuxu decoction (XRZYBXD) is prepared by adding and reducing the Dahuang Zhechong Pill, which is a traditional Chinese medicinal formula in “The Synopsis of Prescriptions of the Golden Chamber”. XRZYBXD has previously been reported to have good efficacy in treating Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) in clinical and basic research. However, its underlying mechanism in treating HCC has not been fully elucidated.

title: Symptom‐Driven Prediction of Chronic Multimorbidity with a Macro–Micro Heterogeneous Graph Neural Network
creator: Yiheng Ye, Miaoru Han, Siqiao Tang, Zongxiang Zhang, Haichen Shen, Bingzhen Sun, Yan Zhang, Xiaodong Chu, Lijuan Deng, Chaoyang Zheng, Qingchun Huang, Kun Bao, Ronghua Zhang, Yong Wang, Fengwei Zhang, Xiaoli Chu
description: The growing prevalence and complexity of multimorbidity pose significant challenges to healthcare systems worldwide. Here, we developed a heterogeneous graph neural network framework for multilabel multimorbidity prediction. The framework jointly encodes symptom and diagnostic information within a heterogeneous graph and incorporates biomedical knowledge subgraphs on both the disease and symptom sides.

title: Male mouse skeletal muscle lacking HuR shows enhanced glucose disposal at a young age
creator: Robert C. Noland, Sujoy Ghosh, Carlos J. Crisanto, Antonio Aleman, McKenna K. Chaney, Maitri K. Chauhan, Layla G. Loftis, Ally C. Goad, Christin F. Rickman, Samuel E. Velasquez, Jaycob D. Warfel
description: IntroductionMetabolic flexibility is the ability of a system to switch between metabolic substrates. Human and murine skeletal muscle tissues and cells with decreased activity of the regulatory RNA-binding protein, human antigen R (HuR), have decreased capacity for fat oxidation, and thus decreased metabolic flexibility.

title: Lactiplantibacillusplantarum APsulloc331261 (GTB1™) promotes butyrate production to suppress mucin hypersecretion in a murine allergic airway inflammation model
creator: Hye-Shin Kim, Bobae Kim, Wilhelm H. Holzapfel, Hyeji Kang
description: IntroductionAllergic airway diseases are one of the serious health problems in worldwide and allergic airway inflammation is a prerequisite led to the exacerbated situation such as mucus hypersecretion, epithelial barrier damage and microbiota dysbiosis. Because of side effects and low efficiencies of current therapeutics, the need for novel alternatives has been urged.

title: Extensive necrotizing fasciitis of the thoracic wall and retroperitoneum following penetrating trauma: A case report of severe septic shock and multistage surgical management
creator: Parham Khoshdani Farahani
description: IntroductionNecrotizing fasciitis (NF) of the thoracic wall with retroperitoneal extension is an exceptionally rare and life-threatening condition. It is associated with high morbidity and mortality due to its rapid progression, diagnostic difficulty, and complex surgical requirements.Case presentationA previously healthy male developed fulminant NF following minor penetrating thoracic trauma. He presented with septic shock, leukocytosis (WBC 54,000/μL), and lactic acidosis.

title: Hepatocyte CBX2 Safeguards Hepatic Lipid Homeostasis by Elevating Ca2+‐CaMKK2‐AMPK Signaling to Counter MASLD
creator: Xiang Wei, Li Lin, Xiuyun Wang, Hui Du, Menglong Zhang, Kechao Tang, Han Gao, Xinrui Xie, Jingya Gao, Xu Wang, Zhenglin Wang, Siwei Huang, Lei Zhang, Fang Gu, Gong‐Hong Wei, Yinliang Qi, Wei Chen, Yongsheng Chang, Huabing Zhang
description: Metabolic dysfunction‐associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) affects approximately one‐third of adults and lacks effective pharmacological therapies. Here, we identify Chromobox 2 (CBX2), a Polycomb‐associated chromatin regulator, as a previously unrecognized regulator of hepatic lipid homeostasis. CBX2 expression is markedly reduced in hepatocytes from patients with MASLD, multiple mouse models (db/db, ob/ob, HFD, and HFHC), and steatotic hepatocytes in vitro.

title: Comparing feature selection and machine learning approaches for predicting CYP2D6 methylation from genetic variation
creator: Wei Jing Fong, Hong Ming Tan, Rishabh Garg, Ai Ling Teh, Hong Pan, Varsha Gupta, Bernadus Krishna, Zou Hui Chen, Natania Yovela Purwanto, Fabian Yap, Kok Hian Tan, Kok Yen Jerry Chan, Shiao-Yng Chan, Nicole Goh, Nikita Rane, Ethel Siew Ee Tan, Yuheng Jiang, Mei Han, Michael Meaney, Dennis Wang, Juss
description: IntroductionPharmacogenetics currently supports clinical decision-making on the basis of a limited number of variants in a few genes and may benefit paediatric prescribing where there is a need for more precise dosing. Integrating genomic information such as methylation into pharmacogenetic models holds the potential to improve their accuracy and consequently prescribing decisions.

title: Clinical Outcomes and Use of Implantable Cardioverter-Defibrillator in Ischemic Heart Failure Patients with Reduced Ejection Fraction: A Retrospective Observational Study
creator: Kyung Hoon Cho, Ki Hong Lee, Yong-Kyu Lee, Seok Oh, Yongwhan Lim, Joon Ho Ahn, Seung Hun Lee, Dae Young Hyun, Min Chul Kim, Doo Sun Sim, Young Joon Hong, Ju Han Kim, Youngkeun Ahn, Jang Hoon Lee, Joo-Yong Hahn, Yu-Ri Kim, Nam Sik Yoon, Hyung Wook Park, Weon Kim, Myung Ho Jeong, on behalf of the Kore
description: Limited data exist regarding the real-world practices and clinical outcomes in patients with ischemic heart failure with reduced left ventricular ejection fractions (LVEFs). Using nationwide registry data from South Korea, we aimed to investigate long-term outcomes and clinical practices, especially implantable cardioverter defibrillators (ICDs) implantation, in patients with reduced LVEFs at least 40 days after acute myocardial infarction (AMI).

title: Multiscale Regulation of Ru‐Based Catalysts for Upgrading Biomass‐Derived Levulinic Acid and Levulinates to γ‐Valerolactone: Mechanisms, Advances, and Challenges
creator: Xin Ni, Cailu Xiao, Gongbing Zhou, Jingzi Zhang
description: γ‐Valerolactone (GVL) serves as a bridge connecting biomass‐derived levulinic acid (LA) and its esters to value‐added chemicals. Ru‐based catalysts exhibit high efficiency for LA/levulinates‐to‐GVL conversion, owing to their strong C═O activation ability, excellent GVL selectivity, and compatibility to diverse hydrogen sources such as H2, formic acid (FA), and alcohols.

title: Training for complexity: Fostering interdisciplinary thinking in One Health graduate education
creator: Kristen Sullivan, Meredith R Spence Beaulieu, Jade Lyons, Emily Floess, Alexandria P Nelson, Caitlin G Niven, Savanna K Smith, Chenxing Xie, Michael Reiskind
description: Graduate training in One Health must equip students to think across disciplines and address complex health challenges through integrative approaches. While case-based and project-based learning are increasingly used to support these goals, there is limited research on how graduate students engage in interdisciplinary exchange, particularly through peer feedback.

title: A pH-responsive composite hydrogel based on konjac glucomannan and its oxidized derivatives: synthesis, characterization and swelling behavior
creator: Chongyang Zhu, Cunhuan Xu, Xueqing Zhu, Xiang Ma, Hongmin Geng, Cong Sun
description: A novel pH-responsive hydrogel composed of oxidized konjac glucomannan (OKGM) and konjac glucomannan (KGM) was fabricated using sodium trimetaphosphate as a crosslinker for intestinal-targeted delivery applications. A series of OKGM samples with carboxyl contents ranging from 1.35% to 5.59% and degree of oxidation (DO) values from 0.49 to 2.01 was successfully prepared.

title: Left Ventricular Hypertrabeculation: Historical Evolution, Diagnostic Pitfalls, and a Pragmatic Clinical Approach
creator: Alessandro Parodi, Marika Martini, Annagrazia Cecere, Lorena Iezzi, Ilaria Rigato, Barbara Bauce
description: Left ventricular hypertrabeculation (LVHT), previously referred to as left ventricular non-compaction (LVNC), has experienced fluctuating recognition in cardiology. Once defined as a primary genetic cardiomyopathy, this intriguing myocardial feature is now considered a “trait” in the most recent guidelines. However, the understanding of this phenomenon remains incomplete.

title: Lung cancer, comorbidities, and medication: the infernal trio
creator: Hélène Pluchart, Sébastien Chanoine, Denis Moro-Sibilot, Christos Chouaid, Gil Frey, Julie Villa, Bruno Degano, Matteo Giaj Levra, Pierrick Bedouch, Anne-Claire Toffart
description: Most patients with lung cancer are smokers and are of advanced age. They are therefore at high risk of having age- and lifestyle-related comorbidities. These comorbidities are subject to treatment or even polypharmacy. There is growing evidence of a link between lung cancer, comorbidities and medications. The relationships between these entities are complex.

title: Zerovalent transition-metal inverse-sandwich complexes of a diborataanthracene dianion
creator: Alexander Gerstner, Merle Arrowsmith, Maximilian Dietz, Cornelius Mihm, Holger Braunschweig
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The 9,10-dihydro-9,10-diboraanthracene (9,10-DHDBA) 2,3,6,7,9,10-Me6-9,10-DHDBA (2) reacted with 1 equiv. [(MeCN)3Cr(CO)3] to yield the unsymmetrical half-sandwich complex [(η6-2)Cr(CO)3] (2-Cr), in which the Cr(CO)3 unit binds exclusively to one DHDBA benzo ring. Reactions of 2 with 2 equiv. [(MeCN)3M(CO)3] (M = Cr, Mo, W) yielded the centrosymmetric slipped inverse-sandwich complexes [{µ-(η6,η′6-2)}{M(CO)3}2] (2-M2), in which each M(CO)3 unit binds to one of the DHDBA benzo rings, one above and one below the DHDBA plane.

title: Acinar‐Derived Organoids Reveal Stage‐Specific Control of Acinar Plasticity
creator: Yongfei Hou, Siyu Li, Chunying Li, Zhifan Lin, Dan He, Li Yang, Liping Fu, Qianyue Zhang, Tianping Zhou, Yao Yao, Xiaolei Yin
description: Adult pancreatic acinar cells undergo ordered metaplastic conversion during injury and tumor initiation. Whether individual cells retain redifferentiation capacity after metaplastic expansion, and what signals each transition requires, remains unknown. Here, using organoids derived from single acinar cells, we show that expanded acinar‐lineage organoids can reacquire acinar features under stage‐specific culture conditions.

title: Deciphering Electrochemical Generation, Transport, and Reactivity of Hydrogen Species in the Electrochemical Palladium Membrane Reactor
creator: Samuel J. Shin, Su Bin Roh, Hyun‐Tak Kim, Kwan‐Young Lee, Soo Min Kim, Ji Hoon Park, Minju Park
description: Electrochemical palladium membrane reactor (ePMR) enables hydrogenation chemistry by mechanically separating, but (electro)chemically coupling reduction and chemical hydrogenation by transporting hydrogen species through a dense Pd membrane, yet the identity and transport mechanism of the reactive hydrogen species remain underdefined.

title: The bacterial and archaeal communities of flies, manure, lagoons, and troughs at a working dairy
creator: Tawni L. Crippen, Dongmin Kim, Toni L. Poole, Sonja L. Swiger, Robin C. Anderson
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundFundamental investigations into the location, load, and persistence of microbes, whether beneficial or detrimental, are scarce. Many questions about the retention and survival of microbes on various surfaces, as well as the load necessary for spread, exist. To answer these questions, we must know more about where to find various microbes and in what concentrations, the composition of the microbial communities, and the extent of dissemination between various elements.

title: HECTD1 Directs HIF‐1α to Facilitate Intestinal Inflammation and Carcinogenesis via Promoting Th17 Differentiation and Glycolysis
creator: Shuiyu Xu, Qiaoqiao Han, Feixiang Wang, Yuerong Zhang, Haoran Feng, Kun Liu, Fang Xiu Luo, Fei Yuan, Xuesong Zhao, Xiaoyan Yu, Haiyan Huang, Qiang Zou, Ren Zhao
description: Targeting glucose metabolism in Th17 cells may be beneficial for treating inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and colitis‐associated cancer (CAC), however, the molecular mechanisms orchestrating Th17 cell metabolism remain unclear. Here, we revealed that HECTD1 regulates IGF2BP3‐dependent HIF‐1α translation to promote Th17 cell glycolysis and differentiation and that HECTD1 expression correlates with IBD and CAC pathogenesis.

title: Late finding of a dermoid cyst in a posterior fossa intra-axial lesion: A rare case report
creator: Rohadi Rohadi, Kadek Dede Frisky Wiyanjana, Agung Bagus Sista Satyarsa, Dewa Putu Wisnu Wardhana, Nyoman Golden, Januarman
description: Background: Intracranial dermoid cysts are rare congenital inclusion cysts derived from ectodermal elements and account for a very small proportion of intracranial lesions. Although they are usually slow-growing and may remain clinically silent for years, they can become symptomatic once they exert mass effect or obstruct cerebrospinal fluid pathways.

title: CeO2‐Based Electrocatalysts for the Oxygen Evolution Reaction: Design, Dynamic Mechanisms, and Electrolyte Adaptability
creator: Zhen Cui, Ailing Song, Zirui Cui, Manman Duanmu, Zhipeng Ma, Hao Liu, Guangjie Shao, Xinyi Tan, Guoxiu Wang, Hao Tian
description: CeO2‐based electrocatalysts are promising for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) owing to their distinctive Ce3+/Ce4+ redox flexibility, large oxygen‐storage capacity, and lattice adaptability. More importantly, CeO2 can dynamically regulate catalyst surface reconstruction and electronic structure while significantly enhancing catalytic activity and long‐term stability.

title: Characteristics of bacterial communities in rhizosphere and bulk soil in Fe-deficient citrus growing in coastal saline-alkali land
creator: Tianchi Jiang, Jiuzhou Chen, Yu Huang, Xiaoyan Chang, Yuping Wu, Gaoping Liu, Runze Wang, Kuan Xu, Lingli Lu, Haizhong Lin, Shengke Tian
description: AimsCitruses often occur with imbalance in iron nutrition in coastal saline-alkali lands, which severely limits the yield and quality of the fruit. In the rhizosphere, the salt content plays a crucial role in reducing uptake of iron, as well as the activity and abundance of bacteria.

title: Self-perception evolution among university student TikTok users: evidence from China
creator: Jinsheng (Jason) Zhu, Yan Ma, Guoen Xia, Sabariah Mohamed Salle, Hongye Huang, Shahrul Nazmi Sannusi
description: The effects of short movies on social media platforms are gaining worldwide popularity and are now attracting global academic attention. Employing self-perception theory and qualitative research methodology, the study examines the influence of short video applications (TikTok) on app-user engagement and evaluates the self-perceived cognitive psychological understanding of Chinese university students.

title: High-throughput sequencing explores the genetic variability of endophytic bacteria in three Sichuan bamboo species (Phyllostachys edulis, Bambusa rigida, and Pleioblastus amarus)
creator: Kuan Yan, Xinyi Li, Yu Cai, Lina Meng, Qin Wei, Xianming Zhao, Rania M. Y. Heakel, Amr M. Atif, Mohamed A. Abd Elhamid, Salma A. Soaud, Ahmed H. El-Sappah
description: IntroductionBamboo is a sustainable and degradable resource for sustenance, high-strength cellulose microfibers, and synthetic fiber in China. Endophytic bacteria enhance root development and ethylene levels, benefiting the host plants’ physiology.MethodsWe investigated the population, diversity, and abundance of endophytic bacteria in the leaves of three bamboo species—Phyllostachys edulis, Bambusa rigida, and Pleioblastus amarus—using high-throughput 16S rDNA sequencing.

title: A rare combination of a meningioma and an ethmoidal meningoencephalocele with osteo-dural defect: Diagnostic and therapeutic challenges
creator: Dzeutouo Fobasso Ornella, Ababacar Sall Basse, Thierno Boubacar Diallo, Souleymane Diallo, Sagar Diop, Ibrahima Tine, Abdou Azize Diop
description: Background: Meningiomas are common, benign intracranial tumors, while meningoencephaloceles are rare congenital or acquired anomalies commonly associated with a dural defect. Their association is exceptional and poses a diagnostic and therapeutic challenge.Case Description: We present a case of a 35-year-old female patient who presented with chronic headaches, blindness, and decreased hearing for 2 years.

title: Preliminary study on the participation of TLR9 on erythrocyte surface combined with mtDNA in the monitoring of infectious diseases
creator: Ling Xiao, Haixia Xu, Siwei Liu, Zhanrui Cheng, Yujie Kong, Li Tian
description: BackgroundTLR9 is typically found within cells and plays a crucial role in identifying pathogenic and self-DNA in chronic inflammation and immune complexes. Recent discoveries indicate its presence on the surface of human red blood cells, where it engages in immune regulation by binding to free mtDNA.

title: Molecular Signatures of HIV‐Induced Neuroinflammation and Neurodegeneration in Human Cerebral Organoids: Identification of Therapeutic Targets for NeuroHIV
creator: Karthick Chennakesavan, Malaroviyam Samikkannu, Shreyan Gupta, Olasunkanmi Israel Tayo, Arpan Acharya, James J. Cai, Siddappa N. Byrareddy, Thangavel Samikkannu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). HIV‐associated neurological complications remain a major concern in people living with HIV (PWH), even under effective viral suppression with combination antiretroviral therapy (cART), underscoring unresolved mechanisms driving HIV‐related neurodegeneration. To address this gap, we used HIV‐1‐infected human cerebral organoids (hCOs) containing microglia as a physiologically relevant three‐dimensional model of the central nervous system (CNS) and validated key findings in the brain region of simian immunodeficiency virus (SIV)‐infected, cART‐treated rhesus macaque model.

title: Analyzing and computing humans by means of the brain using Brain-Computer Interfaces - understanding the user – previous evidence, self-relevance and the user’s self-concept as potential superordinate human factors of relevance
creator: Cornelia Herbert
description: Brain–computer interfaces (BCIs) are well-known instances of how technology can convert a user’s brain activity taken from non-invasive electroencephalography (EEG) into computer commands for the purpose of computer-assisted communication and interaction. However, not all users are attaining the accuracy required to use a BCI consistently, despite advancements in technology.

title: Unraveling the complexity of Disorders of the Gut-Brain Interaction: the gut microbiota connection in children
creator: Dimas Rosa, Roberto Arturo Zablah, Rodrigo Vazquez-Frias
description: “Disorders of Gut-Brain Interaction (DGBIs),” formerly referred to as “Functional Gastrointestinal Disorders (FGIDs),” encompass a prevalent array of chronic or recurring gastrointestinal symptoms that notably impact the quality of life for affected children and their families. Recent studies have elucidated the intricate pathophysiology of DGBIs, underscoring their correlation with gut microbiota.

title: Exploring public attitudes of continuing care retirement communities in China: a sentiment analysis of China’s social media Weibo
creator: Xuechun Wang, Bo Xia, Qing Chen, Martin Skitmore, Huiming Liu
description: IntroductionThe traditional family responsibility system faces challenges as China undergoes rapid demographic shifts with an increasingly older population. Recognizing the potential of market-driven senior care, Continuing Care Retirement Communities (CCRCs) have emerged as a significant alternative. However, cultural stigmas and concerns about the quality, services, and health of older adults in these facilities raise questions over their broad acceptance.

title: Habitat‐Specific Design Strategies for Untethered Soft Robots
creator: Siyang Li, Zhikun Miao, Tuck‐Whye Wong, Tiefeng Li
description: Untethered soft robots are governed by habitat‐specific constraints because operation without physical tethers requires their compliant structures, actuation mechanisms, and energy‐delivery pathways to remain compatible with the environment. Adopting a habitat‐centric framework, this review compares untethered soft robots across terrestrial, aquatic, aerial, and in vivo environments.

title: Reconstruction of the human nipple–areolar complex: a tissue engineering approach
creator: Louis Maistriaux, Vincent Foulon, Lies Fievé, Daela Xhema, Robin Evrard, Julie Manon, Maude Coyette, Caroline Bouzin, Yves Poumay, Pierre Gianello, Catherine Behets, Benoît Lengelé
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Introduction: Nipple–areolar complex (NAC) reconstruction after breast cancer surgery is challenging and does not always provide optimal long-term esthetic results. Therefore, generating a NAC using tissue engineering techniques, such as a decellularization–recellularization process, is an alternative option to recreate a specific 3D NAC morphological unit, which is then covered with an in vitro regenerated epidermis and, thereafter, skin-grafted on the reconstructed breast. Materials and methods: Human NACs were harvested from cadaveric donors and decellularized using sequential detergent baths.

title: Four novel mutations identification in 17 beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase-3 deficiency and our clinical experience: possible benefits of early treatment
creator: Yunpeng Wang, Yu Xu, Huijiao Zhang, Danyang Yin, Yiming Pan, Xiwen He, Shuaiting Li, Zhi Cheng, Gaohui Zhu, Ting Zhao, Huizhe Huang, Min Zhu
description: IntroductionIndividuals with 17-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 3 (17β-HSD3) deficiency face a multitude of challenges, primarily concerning genital appearance, potential malignancy risks, and fertility issues. This study reports our findings from an investigation involving five individuals affected by 17β-HSD3 deficiency, ranging in age from pre-adolescence to adolescence. Notably, we identified four previously unreported mutations in these subjects.

title: Physics‐Guided Multi‐Channel Restoration for Efficient and Accurate Atomic Force Microscopy Imaging
creator: Jaeuk Sung, Hongseok Kim, Seungjae Heo, Jin Tae Moon, Jangwoo Ko, Panithan Sriboriboon, Dong‐Gyu Lee, Sanghyun Jo, Hee Han, Jungho Ryu, Woo Lee, Jinseong Heo, Hyun‐Cheol Song, Yunseok Kim
description: Scientific imaging instruments often acquire multiple physically complementary signals within a single measurement. In atomic force microscopy (AFM), high‐throughput imaging requires higher scan speeds, however, image quality is fundamentally limited by multiple distortions. These artifacts are further amplified for sharp nano/microstructures, making accurate image restoration inherently challenging.

title: Reply to Dr. Vadhithala’s Letter to the Editor re: Marc A. Furrer, Benjamin Lyttwin, Michael S. Pärli, et al. Incidental Prostate Cancer Is an Uncommon but Clinically Non-negligible Cause of Death in Selected Long-term Survivors of Urothelial Carcinoma—Oncological Outcomes and a Proposed Follow-up S
creator: Marc A Furrer, Patrick Y Wuethrich, Niall M Corcoran
description: for their thoughtful and well-structured reflections addressing our recently published study [1] and for providing the opportunity to further clarify the issues raised in their comment. Their appraisal is balanced and constructive, and it highlights several methodological and interpretative aspects that are important for the broader understanding of incidental prostate cancer in the setting of radical cystoprostatectomy.

title: A Chiral Virus‐Like Nanoplatform That Broadly Mediates Antibiotic Delivery to the Brain for Bacterial Meningitis Therapy
creator: Qianqian Xu, Xuting Zheng, Huinan Tong, Ying Liu, Xiaoxi Fan, Miao Xu, Ziyan Zhang, Li Zhang, Mingyan Liu, Ting Du, Heran Li, Guojun Liu
description: Blood‐brain barrier (BBB) preserves brain homeostasis yet restricts therapeutics; in bacterial meningitis, antibiotics’ limited penetration impairs delivery to the parenchyma and cerebrospinal fluid, constraining efficacy and motivating strategies to overcome the barrier. To address this, we developed a chiral virus‐mimicking mesoporous silica nanostructure (CVSN) functionalized with L‐alanine for antibiotic delivery.

title: Hint2 deficiency aggravates mitochondria-associated ferroptosis in lung ischemia-reperfusion injury
creator: Yan Liu, Zhenghaolan Zou, Ke Yi, Xiangchao Ding, Wenyang Jiang, Jianjian Yang, Tianrui Chen, Ning Li, Huiqing Lin
description: SummaryMitochondria-associated ferroptosis is critical in lung ischemia-reperfusion (LI/R) injury. This study examined the role of mitochondrial protein Hint2 in LI/R using mouse models and alveolar epithelial cells. We found that LI/R and hypoxia/reoxygenation (H/R) reduced Hint2 expression. AT2-specific Hint2 knockout exacerbated lung injury, inflammation, and ferroptosis, while promoting mitochondrial fission.

title: Intelligent Field‐Adaptive Electrohydrodynamic Printing for Curved Conformal Electronics
creator: Chang Liu, Yiwen Feng, Xu Chen, Kaiwen Chen, Ran Zhang, Xiaopeng Zhang, Liujia Suo, Xiangji Chen, Zefei Li, Fengshu Wang, Ruixuan Xu, Shuaiwu Liu, Shiwen Liang, Lingjie Kong, Dazhi Wang
description: Curved conformal electronics are increasingly important for wearable devices, biosensing, and advanced communication systems, requiring high‐resolution and high‐precision manufacturing on complex surfaces. Electrohydrodynamic printing is a promising method for fabricating conformal electronics, but its application on curved insulating substrates is hindered by local electric‐field disturbances arising from residual charge accumulation and spatial variations, leading to poor dimensional control.

title: To Be or Not to Be Eutectic: Anomalous Glass Forming Ability Governed by Melt Structural Complexity
creator: Wei Chen, Xuerui Wei, Chengzhe Wang, Zhichao Lu, Fan Zhang, Yan Huang, Yibo Zhang, Liang Wang, Saichao Cao, Chunyin Zhou, Ke Yang, Zhendong Fu, Jinkui Zhao, Dongbai Sun, Fanqiang Meng, Zhou Zhou, Xun‐li Wang, Weihua Wang, Dong Ma
description: For decades, the search for metallic glass formers has followed a simple rule: go for the eutectics. However, this conventional wisdom has been challenged by a lingering mystery—certain congruent melting alloys exhibit higher glass‐forming ability (GFA) than their eutectic neighbors. Here, we unravel this anomaly by probing the structure of high‐temperature melt—the direct precursor to a glass.

title: The consciousness of virtue: uncovering the gaps between educational specialists and the general public in their understanding of virtue in Japan
creator: Koji Tachibana, Eisuke Nakazawa
description: Virtue is a normative concept that constitutes social and moral codes. The notion of virtue can be identified in both the West and the East. Since this concept was revived in academia in the 20th century after a long sinking into oblivion, contemporary professional researchers, but not the general public, may be familiar with this notion.

title: Extracellular vesicles in the treatment of oxidative stress injury: global research status and trends
creator: Wenwen Zhang, Bin Gan, Tingyu Wang, Xiangjie Yang, Yuanye Xue, Yuanqing Zhong, Xintong He, Xinsheng Peng, Yanfang Zhou, Xiaoyan Cheng
description: Objective: The aim of this study was to conduct a bibliometric analysis of the literature on “Extracellular Vesicles in the Treatment of Oxidative Stress Injury” and to reveal its current status, hot spots and trends. Methods: The relevant literature was obtained from the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC) on 29 April 2023.

title: AKAP1 Protects Retinal Ganglion Cells and Preserves Vision by Improving Mitochondrial and Synaptic Health in Glaucomatous Neurodegeneration
creator: Tonking Bastola, Keun‐Young Kim, Ziyao Shen, Guy A. Perkins, Muna Poudel, Yoonjin Lim, Hyejeong Choi, Soo‐Ho Choi, Mark H. Ellisman, Robert N. Weinreb, Won‐Kyu Ju
description: Glaucoma, a leading cause of irreversible blindness, is characterized by progressive loss of retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) and lacks effective neuroprotective therapies. Despite evidence implicating mitochondrial dysfunction in glaucoma, the mechanisms linking elevated intraocular pressure, synaptic dysfunction, mitochondrial failure, and RGC death remain incompletely understood.

title: Astrocyte‐Associated ABCA1/APOE Responses Accompany Hippocampal Lipid Remodeling and Ectopic Neuronal Accumulation During Epileptogenesis
creator: Lu Chen, Xiao‐Rui Shi, Jia‐Yi Chen, Ying‐Ting Wang, Le Du, Yang Ni, Jun‐Min Chen, An‐Chen Guo, Qian Wu, Jian‐Ping Wu, Qun Wang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Temporal lobe epilepsy (TLE) is characterized by progressive hippocampal remodeling, including reactive astrogliosis and aberrant neuronal positioning. Although lipid disturbances are implicated in epileptogenesis, how astrocyte‐associated lipid responses relate to hippocampal remodeling remains poorly understood. Here, human TLE and kainic acid (KA)‐treated mouse transcriptomic datasets identified ATP‐binding cassette transporter A1 (ABCA1)/Abca1 as a nominal astrocyte‐associated candidate, while KA‐ and pilocarpine‐induced status epilepticus (SE) elicited astrocyte‐associated ABCA1/apolipoprotein E (APOE) responses.

title: qcGEM: A Graph‐Based Molecular Representation With Quantum Chemistry Awareness
creator: Haoyu Wang, Ziyan Zhang, Swee Hong Ng, Haipeng Gong
description: The advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) has reshaped drug discovery. AI‐based models typically rely on molecular representations for prediction. However, the absence of physically grounded information in mainstream molecular representations not only limits the model performance in practical applications but also hinders mechanistic understanding and exploitation by humans.

title: The dual interpretation of edge time series: Time-varying connectivity versus statistical interaction
creator: Haily Merritt, Amanda Mejia, Richard Betzel
description: SummaryBrain activity and connectivity have been linked to ongoing behavior and mentation but usually in isolation and almost never in the same model. Here, we show that “edge time series”—a recently proposed method for tracking moment-to-moment connectivity changes—are equivalent to an interaction term in a linear model.

title: Single-cell transcriptomic comparison of tubular segment maturation in advanced human in vitro kidney models
creator: Carla Pou Casellas, Fjodor A Yousef Yengej, Carola ME Ammerlaan, Gisela G Slaats, Maarten B Rookmaaker, Marianne C Verhaar, Hans Clevers
description: SummaryIn vitro kidney models play a crucial role in the study of renal development, (patho)physiology, drug development, and potential applications in bioartificial kidneys. Human in vitro kidney models have recently advanced significantly with the development of (induced) pluripotent stem cell ((i)PSC)-derived organoids, tissue/urine-derived tubuloids, and iPSC organoid-derived tubuloids (iPSCod tubuloids).

title: Epigenomic regulation of neural crest differentiation in human-induced pluripotent stem cells
creator: Kyosuke Mukae, Maya Shindo, Tianyuan Shi, Ritsuko Onuki, Satoshi Yamashita, Naoko Hattori, Toshikazu Ushijima, Miki Ohira, Takehiko Kamijo
description: SummaryNeural crest cells (NCCs) drive vertebrate development through lineage specific differentiation into diverse tissues. Cranial (cNCCs) and trunk NCCs (tNCCs) exhibit distinct developmental trajectories that require coordinated epigenomic regulation. Aberrant NCC differentiation is associated with diseases including tumors. Epigenetic mechanisms such as histone modifications and DNA methylation are crucial for regulating NCC differentiation.

title: Premature Infant Gut Microbiome relationships with childhood behavioral scales: preliminary insights
creator: Samia Valeria Ozorio Dutra, Anujit Sarkar, Ji Youn Yoo, Emily Shaffer-Hudkins, Maureen Groer
description: IntroductionVery Low Birth Weight (VLBW) infants, born weighing less than 1,500 grams, are at risk for both gut dysbiosis and later neuropsychological developmental deficits. Behavioral effects, while related to neurodevelopment, are often more subtle and difficult to measure. The extent of later neurobehavioral consequences associated with such microbial dysbiosis has yet to be determined.

title: Applications of human-machine collaborative decision-making: A review of research with recent developments
creator: Yun Luo, Yanpuze Hao, Haochen Gong, Bo Li
description: SummaryThis study comprehensively reviews human-machine collaborative decision-making (HMCD) methods and applications across management science, the military, healthcare, and manufacturing. We propose a dual-layer analytical framework. The first layer decomposes HMCD into four sequential stages, namely attribute determination, weight assignment, information aggregation, and decision-making.

title: Selective Prescribing of First‐Line SGLT2 Inhibitor and GLP‐1 RA in Adults With Severe Mental Illness and Type 2 Diabetes
creator: Yueh‐Yi Chiang, Chixiang Chen, Xiaojuan Li, Charmaine D. Rochester‐Eyeguokan, Wendy Camelo Castillo, Susan dosReis
description: PurposeSGLT2 inhibitors (SGLT2i) and GLP‐1 receptor agonists (GLP‐1 RA) provide cardiovascular (CV) benefits, but their first‐line use among adults with severe mental illness (SMI) is not well characterized. We evaluated selective prescribing of SGLT2i, GLP‐1 RA, and metformin among adults with SMI and type 2 diabetes (T2D).

title: Development, validation, and implementation of the antibody-secreting cell maturity index: Universal prediction of human plasma cell maturity
creator: Tobit D Steinmetz, Guiyou Yang, Tessa de Nooijer, Nisha van der Meer, Naomi Karmi, Rick Wilbrink, Hendrika Bootsma, Gwenny M Verstappen, Frans GM Kroese
description: SummaryDefining the maturity of long-lived antibody-secreting cells (ASCs) is important for vaccine optimization and research into autoimmune diseases, but current assessment of plasma cell maturity is limited. We developed a universal, robust method to define plasma cell maturity using a meta-analysis of public, human cytometry data, with harmonized expression of ASC maturity markers across samples.

title: Outcomes of critically ill patients with newly diagnosed Burkitt’s lymphoma: a monocentric retrospective study
creator: Fabiola Cammarota, Charlotte Degoutte, Laure Calvet, Dara Chean, Claire Fieschi, Catherine Thieblemont, Gennaro De Pascale, Michael Darmon, Lara Zafrani, Massimo Antonelli, Elie Azoulay, Thibault Dupont
description: BackgroundBurkitt’s lymphoma (BL) can lead to intensive care unit (ICU) admission at diagnosis and treatment initiation for management of disease-related complications such as tumor lysis syndrome (TLS) and acute kidney injury (AKI). Data on the outcomes and prognostic factors in this population of critically ill patients remain limited.

title: Successful application of dietary ketogenic metabolic therapy in patients with glioblastoma: a clinical study
creator: Andreas Kiryttopoulos, Athanasios E. Evangeliou, Irene Katsanika, Ioannis Boukovinas, Nikolaos Foroglou, Basilios Zountsas, Angeliki Cheva, Vaios Nikolopoulos, Thomas Zaramboukas, Tomas Duraj, Thomas N. Seyfried, Martha Spilioti
description: IntroductionGlioblastoma multiforme (GBM) ranks as one of the most aggressive primary malignant tumor affecting the brain. The persistent challenge of treatment failure and high relapse rates in GBM highlights the need for new treatment approaches. Recent research has pivoted toward exploring alternative therapeutic methods, such as the ketogenic diet, for GBM.

title: Viral pancreatitis: research advances and mechanisms
creator: Xianqiang Yu, Minchao Wang, Qingming Kong
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Acute pancreatitis is caused by trypsinogen activation in acinar cells caused by various injury forms (gallstone, high triglycerides, alcohol, etc.). Viral pancreatitis is a clinically rare disease type, which is easily neglected by clinicians and causes serious adverse consequences. Viral pancreatitis involves the entry of viruses into pancreatic cells, triggering inflammation, immune response activation, and enzymatic autodigestion, leading to tissue damage and potential complications. At present, there are few available reports on viral pancreatitis, most of which are case reports.

title: Strengthening primary health care in low- and middle-income countries: furthering structural changes in the post-pandemic era
creator: J. C. Alegre, Suneeta Sharma, Farley Cleghorn, Carlos Avila
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Strengthening primary health care (PHC) is the most cost-effective approach in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs) to achieve sustainable universal health coverage (UHC), protect against health shocks, and promote health and wellbeing for all people. It has been 45 years since PHC was put on the global agenda followed by multiple efforts to advocate for more funding and improved performance of PHC.

title: Arthroscopic Bursal Acromial Reconstruction With a Porcine Extracellular Matrix Graft
creator: Anton Ulstrup, Charlotte Stenqvist
description: Reinsertion of superior or posterosuperior rotator cuff ruptures in the elderly is often not possible. Patients can be left with symptoms of pain, loss of strength, and active range of motion. Bursal acromial reconstruction is an anchorless operative treatment method for painful, irreparable superior or posterosuperior rotator cuff ruptures in the elderly with a functional range of motion.

title: Connection between nutrition and oncology in dogs and cats: perspectives, evidence, and implications—a comprehensive review
creator: Andressa R. Amaral, Gabriela L. F. Finardi, Pedro H. Marchi, Natália M. C. de Oliveira, Leonardo A. Príncipe, Natacha Teixeira, Maria C. F. Pappalardo, Laís O. C. Lima, Juliana V. Cirillo, Júlio Cesar de C. Balieiro, Thiago H. A. Vendramini
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Oncology has become one of the most influential and studied areas in both human and companion animal health. In veterinary practice, cancer represents a significant challenge, especially concerning cats and dogs. Nutrition plays a crucial role in the management of oncology patients in veterinary medicine; however, is often nonspecific and reliant on data from other species and diseases, highlighting the need for a comprehensive review of the latest developments in this field.

title: Harnessing Methylselenol (CH3SeH): A Highly Effective Platform for Stimuli‐Responsive Delivery With Therapeutic Potential
creator: Wenfang Liang, Liyue Wang, Xuan Wang, Xinran Li, Hao Xing, Lu Sun, Zhen Xi, Long Yi
description: Methylselenol (CH3SeH) is not only a key selenium (Se) metabolite but also a potent therapeutic molecule. Chemical tools for stimulus‐responsive delivery of CH3SeH should be crucial for exploring Se‐related biomedicine. Nevertheless, the classical 1,6‐self‐immolation is inefficient in releasing the poorly leaving selenol, and donation platforms for triggerable release of the CH3SeH remain lacking.

title: H‐Bonding‐Induced Repulsion Between Small Groups Toward a Highly Puckered Benzene
creator: Chaofeng Zhao, Qi Sun, Ning Ding, Xiaoting Ren, Jinxuan He, Shenghua Li, Siping Pang
description: Benzene ring puckering generally arises from the strong repulsion between bulky substituents, while in this study, we present that benzene ring puckering can be achieved by repulsion between small substituents (nitro and methyl groups) facilitated by hydrogen‐bonding attraction, as exemplified in 1,3,5‐trinitro‐2,4,6‐trimethylaminobenzene.

title: Community-engaged curriculum development using racial justice and biomedical lenses to address COVID-19 vaccine hesitancy in black individuals with rheumatologic conditions
creator: Eseosa Olive Osaghae, Greta Sirek, Tonya Roberson, Mia Chandler, Ariel Childs, Monica Crespo-Bosque, Gina Curry, Amar Dhand, Mary Dollear, Alice Eggleston, Nnenna Ezeh, Dieufort Fleurissaint, Denice Garrett, Gail Granville, Muriel Jean-Jacques, Elena Losina, Holly Milaeger, Lutfiyya Muhammad, Mary A
description: Despite the efficacy of the COVID-19 vaccine in reducing mortality and illness severity, racial inequities in vaccination uptake persist. Among individuals with rheumatologic conditions who are often immunocompromised, the impact of disparities in preventive care threatens to widen existing inequities in adverse outcomes related to COVID-19 infection.

title: Hyperbaric Oxygen Treatment as a Novel Add-on in Selected Patients with Infective Endocarditis – A Safety and Feasibility Trial
creator: Mia Marie Pries-Heje, Christian Johann Lerche, Emil Fosbøl, Martin Forchhammer, Rasmus Bo Hasselbalch, Franziska Schwartz, Anne Sofie L Siebert, Peter Østrup Jensen, Henrik Rottensten, Kasper Iversen, Henning Bundgaard, Ole Hyldegaard, Claus Moser
description: BackgroundInfective endocarditis (IE) is associated with a high morbidity and mortality. Adjunctive hyperbaric oxygen (HBO2) treatment may enhance bactericidal effects of antibiotics and improve outcomes in patients with IE We conducted an open label, feasibility, and safety trial, including exploratory biomarker analyses, to evaluate HBO2-therapy in patients with IE.

title: NOD1, NOD2, PYDC1, and PYDC2 gene polymorphisms in ovarian endometriosis
creator: Hakan Kula, Beste Balbal, Tunc Timur, Pelin Yalcın, Onur Yavuz, Sefa Kızıldag, Emine Cagnur Ulukus, Cemal Posaci
description: BackgroundEndometriosis, a prevalent chronic gynecologic disorder, significantly impacts women’s health, with both genetic and environmental factors contributing to its heritability. Within the adaptive immune system, the NOD-like receptors (NLR) pathway plays pivotal roles in various autoinflammatory diseases, regulating interleukins, proinflammatory cytokines, and NF-κB activity.

title: Effect of Pulsed Radiofrequency with Various Time-Course on Rheumatoid Arthritis Joint Pain in Rats
creator: Xin Li, Meng Wang, YingDi Wang, Gang Zhao, Ju Gao, Cunjin Wang
description: ObjectiveThis study aimed to evaluate the effect of pulsed radiofrequency (PRF) treatment with various time courses on rheumatoid arthritis (RA)-caused joint pain and pathological damage in rats.MethodsSD rats were randomly assigned to five groups: a sham group, an RA group, a PRF/1min group, a PRF/2min group, and a PRF/3min group.

title: The Value of NLR, PLR, MLR, and SII Combined with Lower Respiratory Tract Symptoms in Predicting Pulmonary Complications in Non-Risk-Factor Influenza A Patients
creator: Shanmu Ai, Haojie Wu, Rui Gu, Sen Zhang, Jie Luo, Fang Xu
description: ObjectiveTo analyze the predictive value of blood cell count results, derived indicators, and patient symptoms for pulmonary complications in non-risk-factor influenza A patients.MethodsA retrospective cohort study analyzed 54 non-risk-factor influenza A patients. Those with pulmonary complications were assigned to the PC group, while the others were placed in the NPC group.

title: Applications of synchrotron light in seed research: an array of x-ray and infrared imaging methodologies
creator: Paula Ashe, Kaiyang Tu, Jarvis A. Stobbs, James J. Dynes, Miranda Vu, Hamid Shaterian, Sateesh Kagale, Karen K. Tanino, Janitha P. D. Wanasundara, Sally Vail, Chithra Karunakaran, Teagen D. Quilichini
description: Synchrotron radiation (SR) provides a wide spectrum of bright light that can be tailored to test myriad research questions. SR provides avenues to illuminate structure and composition across scales, making it ideally suited to the study of plants and seeds. Here, we present an array of methodologies and the data outputs available at a light source facility.

title: Ehf and Fezf2 regulate late medullary thymic epithelial cell and thymic tuft cell development
creator: Sören Lammers, Victor Barrera, Philip Brennecke, Corey Miller, Joon Yoon, Jared Balolong, Mark S. Anderson, Shannan Ho Sui, Lars M. Steinmetz, Ulrich H. von Andrian, Kristin Rattay
description: Thymic epithelial cells are indispensable for T cell maturation and selection and the induction of central immune tolerance. The self-peptide repertoire expressed by medullary thymic epithelial cells is in part regulated by the transcriptional regulator Aire (Autoimmune regulator) and the transcription factor Fezf2. Due to the high complexity of mTEC maturation stages (i.e.

title: Clinical significance and functional characterization of RRN3 in gastric cancer: insights from pan-cancer analysis and experimental validation
creator: Ruofan He, Qingqing Xing, Songyi Liu, Shiwei Lin, Xiang Lin, Jianxin Ye
description: IntroductionRRN3 is a nucleolar protein required for ribosome biogenesis, but its role in cancer remains insufficiently defined. This study aimed to systematically evaluate the clinical relevance, molecular characteristics, immune-related features, and biological function of RRN3 across cancers, with a particular focus on gastric cancer (GC).

title: Examining the impact of chronic diseases on activities of daily living of middle-aged and older adults aged 45 years and above in China: a nationally representative cohort study
creator: Zhonghua Ai, Churou Tang, Xuan Wen, Karthikesu Kartheepan, Songyuan Tang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundChina has by far one of the fastest-aging populations in the world.
