Increasing age is often accompanied by an increasing prevalence of chronic diseases and impaired Activities of Daily Living (ADL). The aim of this study was to analyze the effects of chronic diseases on ADL in Chinese middle-aged and older adults and to provide a scientific basis for delaying the impairment of ADL and prolonging the self-care life expectancy of middle-aged and older adults.MethodsThis investigation utilized the survey information of 10,096

title: A Nova Fronteira do Ultrassom de Point-of-Care: Ultrassom de Pulmão na Cardiopatia Congênita
creator: Maria Estefânia Bosco Otto, Maria Estefânia Bosco Otto
description: terapêuticas. O artigo de Donmez et al.1 discute de forma direta o papel do USP na avaliação de edema pulmonar em crianças com cardiopatia congênita (CC). Em uma coorte retrospectiva de 62 crianças, o estudo observou edema pulmonar em 53% pela USP e em 58% pela radiografia.

title: Alteration of the gut microbiota profile in children with autism spectrum disorder in China
creator: Hui Li, Wei Guo, Sijie Li, Bishao Sun, Ningshan Li, Dongjing Xie, Zongming Dong, Dan Luo, Wei Chen, Weihua Fu, Ji Zheng, Jingzhen Zhu
description: BackgroundAutism spectrum disorder (ASD) is associated with alterations in the gut microbiome. However, there are few studies on gut microbiota of children with ASD in China, and there is a lack of consensus on the changes of bacterial species.PurposeAutism spectrum disorder (ASD) is associated with alterations in the gut microbiome.

title: Contribution and expression of renal drug transporters in renal cell carcinoma
creator: Yawen Zuo, Tong Li, Shilei Yang, Xuyang Chen, Xufeng Tao, Deshi Dong, Fang Liu, Yanna Zhu
description: Renal cell carcinoma (RCC) is a common substantive tumor. According to incomplete statistics, RCC incidence accounts for approximately 90% of renal malignant tumors, and is the second most prevalent major malignant tumor in the genitourinary system, following bladder cancer. Only 10%–15% of chemotherapy regimens for metastatic renal cell carcinoma (mRCC) are effective, and mRCC has a high mortality.

title: Systemic toxicity assessment of tissue conditioners modified with nystatin and chlorhexidine in a rat model of denture stomatitis
creator: Gustavo Simão Moraes, Thaís Albach, Carolina Yoshi Campos Sugio, Victoria Schlumberger Cachoeira, Falyne Kiratcz, Eduardo Bauml Campagnoli, Fabio André Dos Santos, Karin Hermana Neppelenbroek, Vanessa Migliorini Urban
description: Denture stomatitis is a condition that commonly affects the palatal mucosa of denture wearers. Recently, several treatments have shown promising results, including the addition of antimicrobial drugs to tissue conditioners. However, before initiating clinical trials, the safety profile of this modified material must be assessed.

title: AI‐EXAFS: Physics‐Informed Prediction of EXAFS from Atomic Structure
creator: Javier Heras‐Domingo, Andrea Ruiz‐Ferrando, Adam H Clark, Stephan Pollitt, Sharon Mitchell, Javier Pérez‐Ramírez, Núria López
description: Understanding atomic structure across chemical systems relies heavily on extended X‐ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) because of its sensitivity to local atomic environments. However, quantitative interpretation remains inherently iterative, requiring structural parameters or models to be fitted against experimental spectra using explicit multiple‐scattering calculations.

title: Microbiome structure in healthy and pregnant women and importance of vaginal dysbiosis in spontaneous abortion
creator: Majid Eslami, Ramtin Naderian, Ariyan Ahmadpour, Ali Shushtari, Sahar Maleki, Parham Mohammadian, Arvin Amiri, Maryam Janbazi, Mohammad Memarian, Bahman Yousefi
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The vaginal microbiome of healthy women is dominated by Lactobacillus spp. A variety of illnesses, such as vaginosis, sexually transmitted infections (STIs), failed implantation, premature birth (PTB), and preterm pre-labor membrane rupture, are brought on by an unbalanced microbiota. Pregnancy is associated with a decrease in the metabolic capacity of the vaginal resident microbiome, which is consistent with a change to a less complex Lactobacillus-dominated microbiome.

title: Effects of Citrate Mixture on Gout Flares During Urate-Lowering Therapy Initiation Among Chinese Male Underexcretion-Type Gout Patients: A Prospective Cohort Study
creator: Lingfang Xu, Jidong Cheng, Lingling Cui, Kai Guo, Can Wang, Han Qi, Qian Zhang, Yuwei He, Xinde Li, Lin Han, Xuefeng Wang, Wenyan Sun, Xueyan Zhang, Mingshu Sun, Changgui Li, Zhen Liu
description: PurposeTo evaluate the effect of urine alkalization with citrate mixture on reducing flare incidence during initial urate-lowering therapy period in male gout patients with renal underexcretion-type.Patients and MethodsIn this prospective cohort study, patients with renal underexcretion and urinary pH < 6.2 were enrolled.

title: Activation‐Induced Turbostratic Ordering in pDCPD‐Derived Hard Carbon Enables Stable Carbonate‐Based Sodium‐Ion Storage
creator: David Schuster, Glen J. Smales, Max Schmallegger, Julian M Rosalie, Konstantin Kraushaar, Andreas Lißner, Julia Bohdal, Pia Winter, Bernd Fuchsbichler, Stefan Koller, Sebastijan Kovačič, Christian Slugovc
description: Sodium–ion batteries are widely considered a promising alternative to lithium‐ion batteries, due to the abundance and low cost of their raw materials. However, the development of high‐performance and cost‐effective electrode materials remains a significant challenge, particularly when competing with lithium iron phosphate systems.

title: Oral Astilbin Nanogels Modulate Senescence‐Associated CD4+ T Cells and Promote Treg Induction in Aged Mice with Colitis
creator: Lei Zhao, Xinyun Zhang, Qian Ren, Xue Song, Meifang Zhao, Rongshen Wang, Haocheng Du, Yan Chen, Peigen Xu, Jiangyun Liu, Jian Zhang, Jingjing Ma
description: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) in older individuals is characterized by immune senescence and deteriorating intestinal homeostasis, both of which limit the efficacy of current therapies. Here, we develop fluorinated β‐glucan/pectin nanogels (F2‐Ast@NGs) for oral delivery of astilbin, a natural flavonoid with anti‐inflammatory and immunoregulatory activities. This multifunctional platform integrates gastrointestinal protection, colon‐targeted release, and local immune modulation.

title: Anodal transcranial direct current stimulation (atDCS) and functional transcranial Doppler sonography (fTCD) in healthy elderly and patients with MCI: modulation of age-related changes in word fluency and language lateralization
creator: Florian Heimann, Sabine Weiss, Horst M. Müller
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Introduction: In addition to age-related changes in language, hemispheric lateralization of language functions steadily declines with age. Also, performance on word fluency tasks declines and is sensitive to the expression of dementia-related changes. The aim of this study is to evaluate the effect of anodal tDCS combined with a word fluency training on language lateralization and word fluency performance in healthy elderly subjects and in persons with mild cognitive impairment (MCI).

title: A Micropeptide Component of the OGDH Complex Modulates ATP Production in the TCA Cycle
creator: Xinqiang Yin, Weiyan Qi, Lifen Lin, Huilin Zheng, Guoxiang Zhao, Quan Chen, Guoqiang Shao, Yifan Wu, Jialiang Hu, Hanmei Xu
description: Since its elucidation, the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle has been regarded as a fully defined enzymatic pathway. Here, we report the discovery of a previously unrecognized micropeptide component of this central metabolic system. Through analyzing ribosome profiling data from the mouse sORFs.

title: The Impact of Age and Physical Assessment Measures on Performance Among Non-Weightbearing Walking Aids: A Randomized Clinical Trial
creator: Audrey Zucker-Levin, Lucy Senger
description: Background:Walking aids for non-weightbearing (NWB) ambulation are often arbitrarily provided with no evidence that physical assessment predicts ambulatory performance.Purpose:We sought to determine if convenient physical assessment measures could guide NWB walking aid prescription and to determine how age impacts ambulatory performance.

title: Moral distress and moral injury among nurses in German acute inpatient care – a cross-sectional study
creator: Tobias Mai, Anna-Henrikje Seidlein, Michael Schilder, Iulia Dahmer
description: BackgroundMoral suffering in health care is increasingly a focus of research. The extent of and relationship between two distinct forms of moral suffering, namely, moral injury (MI) and moral distress (MD), has not yet been studied in nurses in acute inpatient care in Germany.

title: Light modulates organ-specific gibberellin–abscisic acid crosstalk during drought response in Arabidopsis thaliana
creator: Tereza Miksteinová, Marek Szecówka, Ivan Petřík, Terezie Urbanová, Tereza Trávníčková, Martina Špundová, Martin Fellner, Peter Hedden
description: Main conclusionContinuous blue light enhances drought tolerance in Arabidopsis by modulating ABA and GA pathways, whilst controlled GA catabolism, especially via GA2ox7/8, is important for stomatal regulation and drought adaptation.AbstractIn response to drought, plants undergo physiological and developmental adjustments to reduce water loss and survive the stress, including reduced shoot growth, altered root architecture, and stomatal closure.

title: Facial emotion recognition of sadness relates to superior parietal gray matter volume in mild cognitive impairment
creator: Rachana Mahadevan, Naomi Kristin Giesers, Thomas Liman, Karsten Witt, Andrea Hildebrandt, Mandy Roheger, Stephanie Rosemann
description: Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) is associated with early, regionally selective neurodegenerative changes that may affect socioemotional functioning before atrophy becomes widespread. This study examined whether structural brain alterations in MCI relate to facial emotion recognition performance. Sixty adults (30 MCI, 30 healthy controls), aged 50–86 years, completed neuropsychological testing, the Facial emotion composite Task, and structural MRI.

title: Covalently silane-bridged e-graphene oxide nanosheets toward year-long dispersion-stable epoxy nanocomposites with superior corrosion protection
creator: Anh-Tuan Pham, Quan-Doan Mai, Ngo Thi Loan, Nguyen Thai Huy, Ngo Thi Phuong Anh, Pham Cong Thanh, Nguyen Thi Trang, Le Minh Quang, Nguyen Van Quyet, Ta Ngoc Bach, Anh-Tuan Le
description: Epoxy resins are extensively used in protective coating applications owing to their excellent adhesion, mechanical strength, and chemical resistance; however, maintaining these properties under prolonged service environments remains challenging. Although nanoscale fillers have been widely explored to enhance the durability of epoxy coatings, the long-term dispersion stability of nanofillers in epoxy matrices remains severely limited by interfacial incompatibility and aggregation.

title: Implementation of a universal psychosocial screening program across the pediatric cancer treatment trajectory: a standard of care
creator: Lamia P Barakat, Susanna Vargo, Shannon N Hammer, Anne Reilly, Charles Phillips, Patricia Burns-Lynch, Lisa A Schwartz, Megan N Perez
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). PurposeGuided by Rapid Evaluation and Assessment Methods (REAM) and using rigorous quality improvement processes, we describe implementation of an evidence-based psychosocial screening program at key transitions in childhood cancer treatment to guide care matched to need.MethodsPediatric cancer patients (≥ 11 years) and caregivers (patients 0–17 years) were offered screening questionnaires electronically at 4–6 months, 18–24 months, and 4–6 years post-diagnosis through a phased implementation across three cancer center sites and in their preferred language (English, Spanish, Arabic).

title: An oxygen-releasing mouthwash shows species-dependent antibacterial and antibiofilm activity against periodontal pathogens
creator: Fatemah M. AlAhmari, Rhodanne Nicole A. Lambarte, Terrence S. Sumague, Mary Grace B. Vigilla, Marwa Y. Shaheen, Sumaiah Ajlan, Lamees Alssum, Amani M. Basudan, Abdurahman A. Niazy
description: ObjectivesThis study evaluated whether an oxygen-releasing mouthwash formulation (O2MW) produces species-dependent antibacterial, antibiofilm, and gene expression responses in Aggregatibacter actinomycetemcomitans and Prevotella intermedia compared with 0.12% chlorhexidine under planktonic and biofilm conditions in vitro.Materials and methodsMinimum inhibitory concentrations (MICs) were determined using a resazurin-based broth microdilution, and minimum bactericidal concentration (MBC) by agar subculture. Agar diffusion assessed growth inhibition.

title: High-performance flexible electronics from organic fluorosilicone/carbon composites for low-temperature wearable sensors
creator: Xiaoyu Ma, Yulu Wang, Hongxia Zhu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Flexible wearable sensors often fail in cold and wet environments due to the embrittlement of polymer substrates and the consequent interfacial delamination. Herein, we present a durable composite electrode material designed to overcome this “low-temperature brittleness” challenge. The material is fabricated by spray-coating a conductive carbon paste onto a substrate of organic fluorosilicone synthetic leather, which is synthesized via platinum-catalyzed hydrosilylation.

title: Spaces for skateboarding in the city–new spatial concepts beyond skateparks
creator: Veith Kilberth
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Since the 1990s, skateboarding has emerged as a significant urban practice, often resulting in spatial conflicts. The predominant response from municipal authorities has been to confine skateboarding to purpose-built skateparks, overlooking more integrated and inclusive spatial solutions. This study critically examines this approach and explores alternative skateboarding spaces within the framework of urban sociological discourse on the creative city phenomenon and the evolving collaboration between skateboarding communities and city authorities.

title: Mapping of quantitative trait loci and mining of candidate genes for seed viability in soybean [Glycine max (L.) Merr.]
creator: Manisha Saini, Raju R. Yadav, Rahul Kumar, Subhash Chandra, N. Krishna Kumar Rathod, Meniari Taku, Manu Yadav, Sudipta Basu, Ambika Rajendran, S. K. Lal, Akshay Talukdar
description: Global oilseed crop soybean [Glycine max (L.) Merrill] contains 18%–20% oil, 40%–45% protein, and countless nutrients vital for human health. It is grown worldwide for food, feed, pharmaceutical, and industrial applications. However, inherent loss of seed viability during ambient storage poses serious bottleneck in the production and maintenance of quality seeds.

title: Highly sensitive and selective electrochemical determination of curcumin using a polyaniline-based molecularly imprinted polymer
creator: Amir Abbas Rafati, Esmaeil Karami
description: A novel and highly selective electrochemical sensor based on a polyaniline molecularly imprinted polymer modified glassy carbon electrode (MIP–PANI/GCE) was developed for the determination of curcumin. The molecularly imprinted polymer was synthesized directly on the electrode surface via electropolymerization of aniline in the presence of curcumin as a template molecule, followed by template extraction to generate specific recognition sites.

title: Oral Radiographic Changes in Severe Sickle Cell Anemia Patients: A Retrospective Comparative Study
creator: Haifa AlKhodier, Fahad Bin Saleh, Abdulmajeed AlRumi, Tariq AlOjaym
description: IntroductionSickle cell disease is caused by a point mutation in the β-globin gene, resulting in the production of abnormal hemoglobin. Various oral radiographic changes have been documented in the literature, though they are less frequently reported in patients with severe disease. This study aimed to evaluate specific radiographic features in pediatric patients with severe sickle cell disease.

title: A Global Study of Skin and Subcutaneous Diseases Among Individuals Under 20 Years of Age
creator: Xiju He, Na Feng, Junjie Chang, Xiaomin Huang, Tao Zhu, Wenrui Min, Xinxin Wang, Zudong Meng, Yulin Zou
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundSkin diseases are chronic and recurrent conditions that impose substantial disability and long-term psychosocial burden. However, the global burden of pediatric skin diseases has been insufficiently studied.MethodsWe extracted age-specific data for individuals younger than 20 years from GBD 2021. A comprehensive analytical framework was applied, including Joinpoint regression analysis, SDI frontier analysis, Bayesian age–period–cohort (BAPC) modeling, and ARIMA time-series forecasting to evaluate temporal trends and predict future disease burden.

title: Safety, Pharmacokinetics, and Efficacy Study of Porcine and Rabbit Antithymocyte Globulin in the Treatment of Patients With Severe Aplastic Anemia: A Multicenter, Prospective, Randomized, Open‐Label Clinical Trial
creator: Yawen Zhang, Yingying Zhang, Yuemin Gong, Yu Sun, Guangsheng He
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Severe aplastic anemia (SAA) is a T lymphocyte‐mediated bone marrow failure disorder. Only porcine ATG (p‐ATG) and rabbit ATG (r‐ATG) are available in mainland China, with the optimal first‐line regimen undetermined. This study compared their pharmacokinetics, efficacy, and safety. Ninety‐three SAA patients ineligible for transplantation or lacking a suitable donor (p‐ATG, n = 55; r‐ATG, n = 38) who were receiving immunosuppressive therapy were prospectively enrolled between 2020 and 2024. The primary endpoint was dynamic changes in lymphocyte subsets.

title: Reciprocal longitudinal effects between sense of school belonging and academic achievement: quasi-experimental estimates using United States primary school data
creator: Chris Sakellariou
description: IntroductionThis study investigates the bidirectional relationship between earlier sense of school belonging and later academic achievement in schoolchildren at grades 4 and 5 in US schools, using ECLS-K:2011 longitudinal data.MethodsTwo alternative estimation methods were used, both addressing biases due to endogenous covariates.

title: Cynaroside: a potential therapeutic agent targeting arachidonate 15-lipoxygenase to mitigate cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury
creator: Wenpeng Cao, Yufeng Hu, Xingyu Yu, Tingting Long, Baofei Sun, Shan Lei, Peng Xie, Wenfeng Yu
description: IntroductionDue to the anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties of cynaroside (Cyn), it may be useful in the treatment of cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury (I/R). This study aims to evaluate the effect of Cyn on cerebral ischemia/reperfusion injury.MethodsTransient middle cerebral artery occlusion model (tMCAO) and oxygen and glucose deprivation/reperfusion (OGD/R) microglia models were used to evaluate the effect of Cyn.

title: Elucidating the Molecular Impact of DA29‐Induced ClpP Chemoactivation on Mitochondrial Function
creator: Francesca Rizzo, Morena Miciaccia, Maria Grazia Perrone, Antonio Scilimati, Paola Loguercio Polosa, Francesco Bruni
description: Cellular function relies on tightly regulated mitochondrial proteolysis, which controls organelle protein quality and specific mitochondrial functions, including gene expression and oxidative phosphorylation. In human mitochondria, one of the main proteolytic machineries is the soluble ClpXP complex, consisting of the protease ClpP and its chaperone ClpX, which degrades misfolded or aggregated proteins to preserve organelle function and integrity.

title: Diffusion of excellence: evaluating a system to identify, replicate, and spread promising innovative practices across the Veterans health administration
creator: George L. Jackson, Gemmae M. Fix, Brandolyn S. White, Sarah L. Cutrona, Caitlin M. Reardon, Laura J. Damschroder, Madison Burns, Kathryn DeLaughter, Marilla A. Opra Widerquist, Maria Arasim, Jennifer Lindquist, Allen L. Gifford, Heather A. King, Jenesse Kaitz, Guneet K. Jasuja, Timothy P. Hogan, Jai
description: IntroductionThe Veterans Health Administration (VHA) Diffusion of Excellence (DoE) program provides a system to identify, replicate, and spread promising practices across the largest integrated healthcare system in the United States. DoE identifies innovations that have been successfully implemented in the VHA through a Shark Tank style competition. VHA facility and regional directors bid resources needed to replicate promising practices.

title: Clarifying Baseline Cognitive Eligibility and Cross-Scale Follow-Up in a Randomized Trial of Remimazolam Tosylate for Laparoscopic Surgery [Response To Letter]
creator: Jingya Liu, Mengyu Li, Huimin Wang, Sheng Wang
description: MoCA scores reported in Table 1 (median [IQR]: 25–26 in Group R, 24–27 in Group P) include values below the exclusion threshold of 26, and questions whether this contradicts the criterion of excluding patients with preoperative MoCA < 26. We wish to clarify that the MoCA values presented in Table 1 are the raw (unadjusted) scores.

title: Why First-Hand Accounts from Nursing Assistants Matter? Methodological Reflections on a Role Theory-Informed Qualitative Study [Letter]
creator: Fei-Yi Zhao, Qiang-Qiang Fu, Jia-Yi Zhu
description: grated medical and elderly care services (IMECS).1 We therefore value the descriptive qualitative study by Song et al that examined the roles and impacts of NAs in IMECS institutions.1 Nonetheless, certain aspects of the study’s methodology and interpretation of results merit further consideration.

title: Clinical potential of sensory neurites in the heart and their role in decision-making
creator: Mugdha Tendulkar, Reshma Tendulkar, Parmdeep Singh Dhanda, Alpa Yadav, Mukul Jain, Prashant Kaushik
description: The process of decision-making is quite complex involving different aspects of logic, emotion, and intuition. The process of decision-making can be summarized as choosing the best alternative among a given plethora of options in order to achieve the desired outcome.

title: EPAS1 and VEGFA Polymorphisms Modulate COPD Susceptibility in a High-Altitude Population: A Case-Control Study
creator: Lin Lin, Yi Zhang, Xiang Fu, Yangjie Zhang, Yunchao Wang, Zhen Yang, Xiaoming Ma, Xinhua Wang
description: BackgroundThe onset and progression of Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease (COPD) are influenced by both environmental and genetic factors. Persistent hypoxia at high altitudes is a major environmental stressor. Under hypoxic conditions, EPAS1 is stably expressed and activates its downstream target gene VEGFA; however, the underlying mechanisms remain unclear.

title: Drug-target identification in COVID-19 disease mechanisms using computational systems biology approaches
creator: Anna Niarakis, Marek Ostaszewski, Alexander Mazein, Inna Kuperstein, Martina Kutmon, Marc E. Gillespie, Akira Funahashi, Marcio Luis Acencio, Ahmed Hemedan, Michael Aichem, Karsten Klein, Tobias Czauderna, Felicia Burtscher, Takahiro G. Yamada, Yusuke Hiki, Noriko F. Hiroi, Finterly Hu, Nhung Pham,
description: IntroductionThe COVID-19 Disease Map project is a large-scale community effort uniting 277 scientists from 130 Institutions around the globe. We use high-quality, mechanistic content describing SARS-CoV-2-host interactions and develop interoperable bioinformatic pipelines for novel target identification and drug repurposing. MethodsExtensive community work allowed an impressive step forward in building interfaces between Systems Biology tools and platforms.

title: Circulating Natural Killer Cells in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes and Peripheral Neuropathy Are Altered in Their Frequency and Exhibit Impaired Functions and Angiogenic Activities
creator: Maria Teresa Palano, Federica Riccio, Luisa Sambado, Elena Tagliabue, Milena Bertolotti, Marzia Campanile, Martina Mutoli, Fiorenza Lotti, Andrea Rampin, Cristian Rubuano, Giorgia Maspero, Antonio Antico, Francesca Pitzalis, Matteo Fassan, Piero Maria Stefani, Paola Ostano, Giovanna Chiorino, Nicolò
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and critical limb‐threatening ischemia (CLTI), a severe vascular complication associated with amputation and high mortality, exhibit chronic inflammation and endothelial dysfunction. We previously reported an increased frequency of natural killer (NK) cells in advanced CLTI; however, whether NK cell alterations are already present in patients with peripheral neuropathy, which often precedes diabetic foot lesions with or without distal macroangiopathy, remains unclear.

title: Arbuscular Mycorrhizal Fungi Inoculation Mediated Changes in Phytohormones Under Drought Stress
creator: Murugesan Chandrasekaran, Iyyakkannu Sivanesan, Se Chul Chun
description: Changes in climatic conditions around the world have increased day by day which leads to droughts in agricultural lands. Nowadays various technologies and methodologies are being used to protect plants from drought stress. Among various methods, arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (AMF) mediated alleviation of drought stress was found to be a more efficient one.

title: Inter- and intra-species interactions between meat plant environmental bacteria and a non-biofilm-forming Escherichia coli O157:H7 strain in co-culture biofilms
creator: Jeyachchandran Visvalingam, Peipei Zhang, Xianqin Yang
description: This study evaluated the impact of meat-processing environmental bacteria (MPB) on biofilm formation by Escherichia coli O157:H7 in dual-species cultures. Biofilm development by 50 MPB and E. coli O157:H7 was assessed using crystal violet staining. Four MPB and E. coli O157:H7 combinations were evaluated further for viable cell numbers.

title: Intratumoral and Peritumoral Functional Connectivity Reveals Network‐Level Signatures of Glioma
creator: Hongbo Bao, Yan Bai, Jie Hu, Wencai Ding, Jiacheng Lai, Andrew Zalesky, Ye Ella Tian, Yanmei Tie, Janet Mei, Shengyu Fang, Xing Fan, Licia P Luna, Craig K Jones, Jianxun Ren, Weigang Cui, Jiadong Yan, Zeya Yan, Zihan Wang, Renwu Zhang, Zhonghua Lv, Yihang Jiao, Tao Jiang, Peng Liang, Haris I Sair, Y
description: Gliomas are recognized as network‐level diseases that remodel functional connectivity across the brain. Using resting‐state functional MRI (rs‐fMRI) data from 306 patients with pathologically confirmed glioma at two hospitals, we delineated individualized intra‐ and peritumoral functional networks to quantify tumor‐related alterations.

title: Prevalence and risk factors of cognitive impairment in Chinese patients with hypertension: a systematic review and meta-analysis
creator: Cheng Xie, Dongling Zhong, Yue Zhang, Xiaobo Liu, Lili Zhang, Xiao Luo, Yimeng Gong, Wei Jiang, Rongjiang Jin, Juan Li
description: BackgroundCognitive impairment is prevalent in Chinese patients with hypertension; however, current evidence on prevalence and risk factors is required to be synthesized.ObjectivesThis systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the prevalence and risk factors of cognitive impairment in Chinese patients with hypertension.

title: Tumour‐proximal deep serum proteomics identifies biomarkers associated with ovarian cancer
creator: Darren Lau, Daniel Pincher, Clifford Young, Nicholas Chappell, Noor A. Lokman, Parul Mittal, Leigh Donnellan, Martin K. Oehler, Doug A. Brooks, Peter Hoffmann
description: Ovarian cancer diagnosis is often delayed due to poorly defined clinical symptoms, underscoring the need for novel biomarkers that enable earlier detection. Protein biomarker discovery in blood samples is analytically challenging using mass spectrometry, as high‐abundance proteins can obscure detection of low‐abundance biomarkers.

title: Exploratory Evaluation of the parkrun Practice Initiative in Australian General Practice: A Cross‐Sectional Survey of Healthcare Professionals and Event Directors
creator: Callum Leese, Ruth Eagles, Anne Grunseit, Benni Whiteley, Lewis Boylen, Robert Mann, Emma Cockcroft, Moira Smith
description: Issue AddressedThe health benefits of physical activity (PA) are overwhelming, yet a high proportion of the Australian population does not meet recommended guidelines. Community‐based initiatives such as parkrun offer a scalable approach to increasing PA. The parkrun practice initiative links general practice with local parkrun events to support people to become more physically active.

title: Optimizing Left-Sided Breast Cancer Radiotherapy: Strategy-Dependent Trade-Offs Among VMAT and Hybrid Techniques
creator: Rocco Mottareale, Francesca Buonanno, Valentina d’Alesio, Sara Falivene, Marcello Serra, Cecilia Arrichiello, Gianluca Ametrano, Piera Ferraioli, Gaetano Gagliardo, Rossella Di Franco, Simona Mercogliano, Paolo Muto, Vincenzo Ravo
description: PurposeTo compare dosimetric trade-offs among two full-VMAT and two hybrid 3D-CRT/VMAT strategies for left-sided whole-breast irradiation (WBI), and to evaluate the influence of planning strategy, introducing a novel tangential hybrid approach (H-tVMAT).Patients and MethodsTwenty patients with left-sided breast cancer treated with WBI (40.05 Gy in 15 fractions) were retrospectively analyzed.

title: A comparison of design algorithms for choosing the training population in genomic models
creator: Alexandra Stadler, Werner G. Müller, Andreas Futschik
description: In contemporary breeding programs, typically genomic best linear unbiased prediction (gBLUP) models are employed to drive decisions on artificial selection. Experiments are performed to obtain responses on the units in the breeding program. Due to restrictions on the size of the experiment, an efficient experimental design must usually be found in order to optimize the training population.

title: Outcomes and risk factors associated with in-hospital mortality in patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting with low ejection fraction
creator: Yang Zhao, Xu Yu, Xiaolong Ma, Liang Zhang, Zehui Wang
description: ObjectiveTo investigate the short-term prognosis and risk factors associated with in-hospital mortality in patients undergoing coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) with low ejection fraction.MethodsClinical data were collected from 765 patients who underwent CABG with an ejection fraction of less than 40% between 2019 and 2023 at Anhui Chest Hospital and Beijing Anzhen Hospital, Capital Medical University.

title: Methodological considerations in interpreting serum galectin‐3 as a predictor of incident type 2 diabetes
creator: Lingyan Chen, Dandan Weng
description: alectin‐3 as a potential metabolic risk marker in a Japanese population. However, we would like to highlight two methodological considerations that may be relevant to the interpretation of the findings. First, loss to follow‐up raises the possibility of selection bias in the longitudinal analysis.

title: Research Progress of Ferrosoferric Oxide Nanoparticles in Bone Regeneration and Disease Treatment
creator: Jia-bin Song, Jin-yao Li, Yi-bing Ding, Shun-zhi Yang, Lu Sun, Ying Yang, Zi-xuan Lin, Yan-chen Feng, Fei-xiang Liu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Ferrosoferric oxide nanoparticles (Fe3O4NPs), with unique magnetic properties and biocompatibility, have shown great promise for application in the treatment of bone regeneration and diseases in recent years. Bone-related diseases, such as osteoporosis, bone defects and bone tumors, seriously affect the health and quality of life of millions of people around the world, and existing treatments have many limitations, such as low bioavailability, significant side effects, and lack of precision in drug delivery.

title: Synthetic study of vic-bromination of diarylacetylenes, easy purification and separation
creator: Akane Togo, Hiyono Suzuki, Yuto Akai, Makoto Matsumoto, Yoshinori Suzuma, Hidehiko Kodama, Kouichi Matsumoto
description: E-Selective bromination for diphenylacetylene was established by using the combination of NBS and FeBr3 in CH2Cl2. In addition, easy purification and separation from the crude product were found. When the crude product was treated with heptane, the E isomer could be recovered as a solid material by utilizing the difference in solubility.

title: Can artificial intelligence bridge critical gaps in hypertension prediction and risk assessment in low- and middle-income countries? A scoping review
creator: David Sasu, Tsatsu Agbettor, Angela Owusu Ansah, William Annoh, Lecia Ackerson, Ayeyi Adjoa Domeyo Ohene-Adu, Roselyn Sackitey-Matey
description: ObjectiveAccording to the WHO, as of 2025, 1.4 billion adults between the ages 30–79 were living with hypertension, with approximately two-thirds of that number from low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). By 2025, the number of individuals with hypertension is expected to have reached 1.5 billion, with sub-Saharan Africa alone projected to have 74.7 million cases.

title: Familial Mediterranean fever in Armenian children with inflammatory bowel disease
creator: Gayane Amaryan, Tamara Sarkisian, Artashes Tadevosyan, Christian Braegger
description: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) and familial Mediterranean fever (FMF) are inflammatory diseases with complex interactions among genetic, immune, and environmental factors. FMF is a monogenic autoinflammatory disease, characterized by recurrent febrile attacks and polyserositis, and is manifested mainly in childhood. FMF is widespread in Armenia. There are reports on the concurrent occurrence of FMF and IBD.

title: Association of haematological cancer drugs recommendation levels in Chinese Society of Clinical Oncology guideline with different approval approaches: a cross-sectional study
creator: Lirong Zhang, Hongbin Yi, Liping Kuai, Sheng Han, Hong Sun, Jiaqin Cai, Xiaoxia Wei
description: IntroductionTo evaluate the associations between approval approaches and the Chinese Society of Clinical Oncology (CSCO) guidelines for haematological cancer drug indications.MethodsHaematological cancer drug indications approved via different approaches between 2015 and 2023 were retrieved from the National Medical Products Administration (NMPA) website, and their CSCO guideline recommendation levels were analysed. Basic characteristics were analysed descriptively.

title: IRP2 contributes to COPD-associated hypoxic epithelial injury through regulation of Sestrin2-related stress responses and ferroptosis
creator: Chunyan Xiong, Min Song, Tianshu He, Yao Ma, Jiang Wang
description: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is characterized by persistent oxidative stress and airway epithelial injury. However, the molecular mechanisms linking iron metabolism and cellular stress responses in COPD remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the role of iron regulatory protein 2 (IRP2) in COPD-associated epithelial injury.

title: An Uncommon Case of Recurring Pulmonary, Lymphatic, and Skeletal Tuberculosis Accompanied by Myositis: Is It Associated with Particular Resistance?
creator: Yani Jane R Sugiri, Kristia Fahmi, Rezki Tantular, Nurima Diyah Puji Hastuti, Nuning Winaris, Loeki Enggar Fitri, Iman P Maksum, Hendy Setyo Yudhanto, Liana Karliasari
description: Tuberculosis (TB) remains one of the primary causes of illness and death worldwide. Indonesia ranks second globally in TB incidence. Recurrent or relapsed TB, especially with multifocal involvement, presents significant diagnostic and therapeutic challenges, often complicated by incomplete treatment and limited molecular diagnostic capacity in developing countries.

title: A nomogram based on clinicopathological and ultrasound characteristics to predict central neck lymph node metastases in papillary thyroid cancer
creator: Fei Chen, Shuiping Jiang, Fan Yao, Yixi Huang, Jiaxi Cai, Jia Wei, Chengxu Li, Yanxuan Wu, Xiaolin Yi, Zhen Zhang
description: PurposePapillary thyroid cancer (PTC) has grown rapidly in prevalence over the past few decades, and central neck lymph node metastasis (CNLNM) is associated with poor prognoses. However, whether to carry out preventive central neck lymph node dissection (CNLND) is still controversial. We aimed to construct a prediction model of CNLNM to facilitate making clinical surgical regimens.

title: Multimodal substrate recruitment enables CTLHMKLN1 E3 ligase to target acetylated N-, C-, and internal degrons
creator: Sara Sepic, Karthik V Gottemukkala, Jiale Du, Samuel A Maiwald, Jakub Chrustowicz, Eleftheria C Papadopoulou, Luca J Stier, Susanne von Gronau, Brenda A Schulman
description: The GID/CTLH family of E3 ubiquitin ligases employs several substrate receptor subunits that recruit distinct degrons, but the substrate recognition mechanisms of the CTLHMKLN1 assembly have largely remained elusive. Here, we reconstitute CTLHMKLN1-dependent ubiquitylation of three biochemically distinct substrates – MKLN1 itself, ZMYND19, and FAM72A-recruited UNG2, and determine cryo-EM structures of each substrate bound to MKLN1.

title: Assessment of Population Immunity to Enteric Hepatitis Viruses in the Population of Belgrade
creator: Anna Yurievna Popova, Alesia Yuryevna Olkhovskaya, Luka Dragačević, Yulia Vladimirovna Ostankova, Svetlana Alexandrovna Egorova, Alexander Nikolaevich Schemelev, Darya Tsibulskaya, Ekaterina Vladimirovna Anufrieva, Anastasiya Romanovna Ivanova, Irina Victorovna Drozd, Ojuna Bayarovna Zhimbaeva, Bran
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background: Hepatitis A (HA) and E (HE) represent a significant global health burden. Despite the development of effective vaccines against hepatitis A virus (HAV) and hepatitis E virus (HEV), outbreaks of acute HA and HE continue to occur worldwide. This study aimed to assess the seroprevalence of anti-HAV and anti-HEV IgG antibodies (Abs) in the population of Belgrade and to analyze their association with socio-demographic and clinical factors.

title: Nomogram model based on preoperative clinical characteristics of unilateral papillary thyroid carcinoma to predict contralateral medium-volume central lymph node metastasis
creator: Fan Wu, Kaiyuan Huang, Xuanwei Huang, Ting Pan, Yuanhui Li, Jingjing Shi, Jinwang Ding, Gang Pan, You Peng, Yueping Teng, Li Zhou, Dingcun Luo, Yu Zhang
description: ObjectivesTo explore the preoperative high-risk clinical factors for contralateral medium-volume central lymph node metastasis (conMVCLNM) in unilateral papillary thyroid carcinoma (uPTC) and the indications for dissection of contralateral central lymph nodes (conCLN).MethodsClinical and pathological data of 204 uPTC patients who underwent thyroid surgery at the Hangzhou First People’s Hospital from September 2010 to October 2022 were collected.

title: The aminoadamantane derivative 3F2 modulates monocyte and NK cell activation and restores immune mediators altered by Monkeypox virus stimuli
creator: Thaís de Fátima da Silva Moraes, Geovane Marques-Ferreira, Ágata Lopes-Ribeiro, Erik Vinicius de Sousa Reis, Gabriela Lorrany Aparecida Azevedo, Victor de Melo Rocha, Marília Bueno da Silva Menegatto, Felipe Alves Clarindo, Caio Wilker-Teixeira, Laura Cardoso Corrêa-Dias, Nathália Evelyn Morais Cost
description: The monkeypox virus (MPV) is known to employ multiple immune evasion strategies that compromise antiviral defenses and disrupt immune homeostasis. Here, we characterized the immune responses induced by stimulation with inactivated MPV and evaluated the ability of aminoadamantane (AMA) and its derivative, 3F2, to restore immune function.

title: Analysis of Upper-Limb Movement Characteristics in Tennis Volleys Based on Skill-Level Differences: Kinematic Features of the Backhand Versus Forehand Volley
creator: Kohei Katsumi, Hitoshi Koda, Noriyuki Kida
description: Background: In tennis, the volley is an important shot; however, studies describing its movement characteristics have been limited to the forehand volley (FV). In this study, we analyzed the characteristics of upper-limb movement during FV and backhand volley (BV) in skilled and less-skilled tennis players.

title: Central Nervous System Reservoirs and HIV Cure: Therapeutic Opportunities and Challenges
creator: Thomas A Angelovich, Michael Roche, Paul R Gorry, Melissa J Churchill
description: Purpose of reviewDespite viral suppression with antiretroviral therapy, people with HIV (PWH) remain at increased risk of neurocognitive impairment, neuroinflammation, and potential viral rebound following therapy interruption. Although the central nervous system (CNS) is a recognised HIV reservoir, it is often not fully considered in cure approaches.

title: Metabolic syndrome before 16 weeks’ gestation: prevalence and haemodynamic profile in a socioeconomically disadvantaged pregnancy cohort: baseline findings from Mother’s Heart Study
creator: A Mohebi, M Arstall, J Dalton, G Dekker, AR Alexander, MM Pathirana, M Wittwer, S Leemaqz, PH Andraweera
description: BackgroundPregnancy provides an opportunity to identify young women at risk of future cardiometabolic diseases. We aimed to determine the prevalence of metabolic syndrome (MetS) and its components, and to assess haemodynamic profiles in early pregnancy.MethodWe recruited pregnant women at Lyell McEwin Hospital before 16 weeks’ gestation. Haemodynamic parameters were measured using USCOM BP+ device.

title: Digital supportive care in prostate cancer: a systematic review
creator: C. Paterson, D. Coro, J. N. Morris, M. R. Turner, N. Perrotta, M. Godfrey, A. Robertson, J. Christina
description: PurposeTo map and synthesise the existing evidence on people’s perspectives and requirements for patient-facing digital health technologies for use in prostate cancer care delivery. Understanding the preferences of people with prostate cancer and understanding the barriers and facilitators to maximising engagement with digital supportive care healthcare landscape.MethodsFour electronic databases were searched to identify suitable studies.

title: The Impact of Ambient Ozone Exposure on Respiratory Health in the U.S. Populations: A Systematic Review
creator: Yoojin Cho, Yu Yu, Xinyu Zhang, Michael Kleeman, Michael Jerrett, Ninez A Ponce
description: Ozone, a photochemically generated air pollutant, continues to pose a major concern for public health in the United States, with some 125 million people living in areas that exceed national ambient air quality standards set by the United States Environmental Protection Agency.

title: Structured postmortem genetic counselling and testing in sudden unexplained death among young adults in the Netherlands: results and implications regarding hereditary risk
creator: Tess M. Wemeijer, Leonie A. Verbaan, Wilma L.J.M. Duijst, Yvonne M. Hoedemaekers, Imke Christiaans
description: IntroductionSudden unexplained death (SUD) in young adults may result from hereditary cardiovascular disorders that remain undetected even after conventional autopsy. Routine postmortem genetic testing may identify these disorders, improving determination of the cause of death while providing diagnostic and preventive opportunities for surviving blood relatives.

title: Adoption of robot-assisted minimally invasive surgery across surgical specialties in France: a nationwide population-based study
creator: Anaïs Havet, François Bettega, Violaine Fernandez, Clara Bouvard, Cécile Payet, Jean-Christophe Lifante, Christophe Tresallet, Laurent Brunaud, Xavier Armoiry, Marie Viprey
description: Robotic minimally invasive surgery has been used in France for nearly two decades, with monitoring enabled by the National Health Data System (SNDS) since March 2020. No French study has comprehensively described robotic procedures, including ENT, at a fine geographical scale.

title: Knowledge predicts agility but not power: the role of injury prevention awareness in the functional performance of female collegiate athletes
creator: Monira I. Aldhahi, Smaher Abdullah Aldawood, Raghad Khalid Alotaibi, Haneen Hamoud Alsahli, Fay Ahmed Faqihi, Rawan Mansour Binsaad, Reem M. Alwhaibi
description: BackgroundInjury prevention is essential for sustaining athletic performance and minimizing risks. Although knowledge and attitudes toward injury prevention are believed to influence outcomes, their relationship with functional performance remains underexplored. This study aimed to assess the association between injury prevention knowledge, attitudes, and performance metrics among female collegiate athletes.MethodsSixty female collegiate athletes were recruited for this study.

title: Correction: Comparison of manual and automated methods in the hematological evaluation of a frugivorous bat captured in urban green areas
creator: Melissa Harumi Sumiyoshi, Eva Munyque da Cruz, Morgana Maira Hennig, Marcela Natacha Aparecida Rocha, Kayana Mota Caribé de Figueiredo, Nathália Soares Lima Rabelo, Gabriel de Mello, Glenda Akimi Ota, Guilherme Ratts de Almeida, Jéssica Inácio Gomes, Jhonathan França Bello, Mylene Karoline da Silva

title: Frequency of SARS-CoV-2 variants identified by real-time PCR in the AUNA healthcare network, Peru
creator: Tamin Ortiz-Gómez, Andrea C. Gomez, Brigitte Chuima, Alejandra Zevallos, Karen Ocampo, Diana Torres, Joseph A. Pinto
description: IntroductionIn Peru, on 11 February 2023, the Ministry of Health registered 4 million patients infected with COVID-19 and around 219,260 deaths. In 2020, the SARS-CoV-2 virus was acquiring mutations that impacted the properties of transmissibility, infectivity, and immune evasion, leading to new lineages.

title: Periodontal Disease and Heart Failure: Current Evidence and Perspectives
creator: Alícia Eliege da Silva, Valéria Duarte de Almeida, Gilson Aquino Cavalcante, Roque Ribeiro da Silva Júnior, Daria Raquel Queiroz de Almeida, José Veríssimo Fernandes, Ellany Gurgel Cosme do Nascimento, Cléber de Mesquita Andrade, Thales Allyrio Araújo de Medeiros Fernandes
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Purpose of ReviewPeriodontal disease has been increasingly recognized as a chronic inflammatory condition with potential systemic implications, particularly in the cardiovascular system. Heart failure (HF), a pro-inflammatory syndrome with multisystem involvement, remains a major public health burden.

title: Modeling freshwater inflow to a tropical estuary using stochastic and neural-network approaches under contrasting hydroclimatic conditions in Brazil
creator: Luísa Maria de Souza Viana, Eloá Corrêa Lessa Tostes, Wendel Dias Constantino, Felipe Henrique Rossi Luze, Marcos Sarmet Moreira de Barros Salomão, Taíse Bonfim de Jesus, Carlos Eduardo Veiga de Carvalho
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Freshwater inflow regulates estuarine circulation, salinity gradients, sediment transport, and biogeochemical fluxes, yet long-term discharge records remain scarce in many tropical coastal basins. We compared linear regression, stochastic time-series models (ARMA, ARIMA, and SARIMA), and multilayer perceptron (MLP) neural networks for reconstructing monthly discharge at the Ituberá gauging station, upstream of the Serinhaém estuary (southern Bahia, Brazil), using records from 1966 to 2019. No model family was uniformly superior across rolling-origin selection and independent validation.

title: Diabetes‐Related Foot Disease as the Principal Reason for Hospital Admission: 5 Years of Data From a Major Tertiary Hospital in Aotearoa New Zealand
creator: Michele Garrett, Rinki Murphy, Arier Lee, Peter A. Lazzarini, Timothy Kenealy
description: ObjectiveTo examine hospitalisations caused by diabetes‐related foot disease (DFD) at the largest tertiary hospital in Aotearoa New Zealand.MethodsWe analysed hospital admission data for DFD‐caused hospitalisations from Auckland City Hospital (ACH), from 1 July 2014 to 30 June 2019, for people 15 years or older, using ICD10‐AM discharge codes and amputation procedure codes.

title: Timing matters: a life-course review of midlife type 2 diabetes, exposure duration, and late-life dementia risk
creator: Mrityunjay Sivakumar, Chakravarthy Marx Sadacharan
description: PurposeThis review synthesizes the evidence regarding Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) as a critical modifiable risk factor for dementia through a life-course lens. The primary purpose is to move beyond the general association and determine how the timing and severity of T2DM, specifically age at onset, duration of disease, and glycemic instability, influence cognitive decline.

title: The associations between optimism, personal growth initiative and the latent classes of social media addiction
creator: Heng Yue, Shiwen Gao, Yufeng Huang, Xuemin Zhang
description: IntroductionMost previous studies have explored the risk antecedents of social media addiction, while few studies have focused on the protective factors that may decrease the risk of this behavioral disorder. By using a person-centered method, the current study focused on the effects of two protective factors (optimism and personal growth initiative) on the latent classes of social media addiction.

title: A dataset on radical and extremist attitudes in Europe
creator: Sebastian Jungkunz, Nina Fadarkhan Osenbrügge, Marc Helbling
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This dataset introduces the first cross-nationally validated measurement scales for left-wing and right-wing radicalism, and general political extremism, along with an implicit association test (IAT) for implicit political extremism in the Western world. It includes data from more than 18,000 participants collected through ten surveys conducted between 2022 and 2024 in France, Germany, Great Britain, Greece, Hungary, the Netherlands, and the United States. The dataset facilitates comparative analyses of the origins and consequences of radical and extremist attitudes across different political systems.

title: Final analysis results from DREAMM-3, a phase 3 study of belantamab mafodotin versus pomalidomide plus dexamethasone in patients with relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma
creator: Meletios Athanasios Dimopoulos, Vania Hungria, Haitao Meng, Atanas Radinoff, Jian Li, Sosana Delimpasi, Ting Niu, Gabor Mikala, Tamas Masszi, Marcelo Capra, Michael Low, Angelo Maiolino, Yan Xu, Xavier Leleu, Vasiliki Pappa, Dominik Chraniuk, Tatiana Konstantinova, Iurii Osipov, Shawn Hakim, Chris B
description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). el, Astrid McKeown, Julia Boyle, Sumita Roy-Ghanta, Katja Weisel
Published: 2026

To the Editor,

Targeting B-cell maturation antigen (BCMA) has transformed the relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma (RRMM) landscape with unprecedented overall survival (OS) outcomes versus standard-of-care triplet regimens. Belantamab mafodotin, an anti-BCMA antibody-drug conjugate, has a multimodal mechanism of action involving minimal immunosuppression and no evidence of induction of T-cell exhaustion [1, 2].

title: Relative muscle mass and grip strength as complementary correlates of metabolic syndrome: a nationwide DXA-based study of Korean adults
creator: Eun Young Lee, Hyun Min Kim
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). PurposeBoth muscle mass and strength relate to metabolic health, but their separate contributions to metabolic syndrome (MetS) are unclear. Using the 2024 Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (KNHANES) with concurrent dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA)–based appendicular skeletal muscle mass (ASM) and handgrip strength (HGS), we examined the independent associations of relative muscle mass and HGS with MetS in Korean adults aged ≥40 years.MethodsWe analyzed 3033 adults from KNHANES. ASM/body weight (ASM/BW) and HGS/body weight (relative HGS) served as primary indicators.

title: The effectiveness of physiotherapy-led non-surgical and perioperative interventions for glenohumeral osteoarthritis: A systematic review
creator: Daha Garba Muhammad, Nadine E Foster, Mickylle Pelaez, Karina O’Leary, Ilana N Ackerman, Jonathan G Quicke
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundPhysiotherapists are commonly involved in the management of adults with glenohumeral osteoarthritis (GHOA), to improve symptoms or restore function after surgery. This systematic review investigated the effectiveness of physiotherapist-led interventions in adults with GHOA including rotator cuff arthropathy (RCA).MethodWe conducted a comprehensive systematic review (PROSPERO Registration: CRD42022318534) searching PubMed, Cochrane, CINAHL, EMBASE and PEDro databases from inception up until June 2025.

title: Vulvar Squamous Cell Carcinoma: Scientific Progress and Impacts to Pathology Practice
creator: Lynn Hoang, Somayah Alsolami, Blake Gilks, Jessica N. McAlpine, Amy Jamieson
description: Despite vulvar cancer’s rarity, meaningful advances have been made to improve the clinical care of affected patients—particularly with respect to vulvar squamous cell carcinoma (VSCC). These advances are reflected in changes to tumor classification, surgical strategies, early detection of precursors, and targeted therapeutic exploration.

title: Interaction between number of formed bubbles, reaction rate and flow velocity of acoustic streaming in the initiation period of power-induced quenching
creator: Ryota Aoki, Takuya Yamamoto
description: To elucidate the detailed process of power-induced quenching in which the rate of sonochemical reactions decreases sharply as ultrasonic power increases, the interaction between the number of formed bubbles, the sonochemical reaction rate, and the flow velocity of acoustic streaming was investigated during the initiation period of ultrasonic irradiation.

title: PSIP1 Orchestrates Immune Escape in Osteosarcoma: Insights From Single‐Cell Analysis and Implications for Immunotherapy Resistance
creator: Simin Liu, Hong Yan, Wei Ku, Guo Liu, Hao Zhang
description: BackgroundOsteosarcoma (OS) is characterized by a highly heterogeneous tumor microenvironment (TME) that frequently limits the efficacy of immunotherapy. Identifying molecular drivers of immune escape (IE) is essential for improving therapeutic outcomes.MethodsWe integrated single‐cell RNA sequencing (scRNA‐seq) and bulk transcriptomic data to dissect the OS immune landscape.

title: Fecal microbiota transplantation unveils sex-specific differences in a controlled cortical impact injury mouse model
creator: Tulasi Pasam, Manoj P. Dandekar
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). IntroductionContusion type of traumatic brain injury (TBI) is a major cause of locomotor disability and mortality worldwide. While post-TBI deleterious consequences are influenced by gender and gut dysbiosis, the sex-specific importance of commensal gut microbiota is underexplored after TBI. In this study, we investigated the impact of controlled cortical impact (CCI) injury on gut microbiota signature in a sex-specific manner in mice.MethodsWe depleted the gut microflora of male and female C57BL/6 mice using antibiotic treatment.

title: Comparison of microbial diversity and community structure in soils managed with organic and chemical fertilization strategies using amplicon sequencing of 16 s and ITS regions
creator: Ajay Kumar Mishra, Poonam Yadav, Sheetal Sharma, Piyush Maurya
description: Soil microbial species diversity and distribution of microbial communities are vital for soil and crop health, nutrient cycling, availability, and subsequent plant growth. These soil dynamics are highly influenced and altered by various soil management practices, inputs, and agricultural techniques.

title: Highlights of the 2026 Korean Society of Hypertension guidelines for the management of hypertension: what’s new and what has changed
creator: Eun Mi Lee, In-Jeong Cho, Hee-Taik Kang, Kwang-Il Kim, Dae-Hee Kim, Ju Han Kim, Hack-Lyoung Kim, Hyeon Chang Kim, Hae Jin Kim, Eun Sil Koh, Sungha Park, Jong-Moo Park, Jeong-Hun Shin, Janghoon Lee, Hae Young Lee, Hokyou Lee, Mi-Hyang Jung, Eun Joo Cho, Seonghoon Choi, Sang-Hyun Ihm, on Behalf of Com
description: The recently released 2026 Korean Society of Hypertension (KSH) guidelines incorporate contemporary advances in the diagnosis and management of hypertension. This highlight summarizes the most important updates, focusing on the underlying evidence and key changes, particularly the newly introduced and revised recommendations.

title: Visual Impairment and Driving in Older Adults: A Narrative Review
creator: Shu Xu, Joshua R Ehrlich, Lindsey B De Lott
description: Purpose of ReviewThis narrative review synthesizes current evidence on the relationship between visual impairment and driving safety in older adults, with a focus on the visual functions required for safe driving, the impact of common visual deficits, and current approaches to clinical evaluation and management.

title: Uncommon Case of Hemophagocytic Lymphohistiocytosis as the First Presentation of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
creator: Swetha Tummala, Andy Wu, Yen-Nan Lin, Tiarra Price, Anthony Demetris, Stela Celaj
description: Hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis secondary to systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a potentially fatal condition that is frequently misdiagnosed, particularly when its occurrence is the first manifestation of SLE. Diagnosis is often delayed due to overlapping clinical and laboratory findings with infections and autoimmune diseases.

title: Pulpotomy of deciduous molars with deep caries using three different hydraulic calcium silicate cements: a short-term pilot randomized controlled split-mouth study
creator: Ulrike Urmann, Isabelle M Schenke, Karl-Anton Hiller, Wolfgang Buchalla, Katrin Bekes, Matthias Widbiller, Frederike Schenke, Fabian Cieplik, Konstantin J Scholz
description: ObjectivesThis randomized, controlled split-mouth study evaluated the short-term clinical survival of three hydraulic calcium silicate cements for pulp capping after pulpotomy in primary molars under general anesthesia.Materials and methodsThirty-three children aged 2 to 6 years, each with three carious primary molars (ICDAS 4–6), were recruited for treatment under general anesthesia.

title: Pulmonary Marginal Zone B‐Cell Lymphoma of Mucosa‐Associated Lymphoid Tissue (PMZL‐MALT) Diagnosed by Radial Probe Endobronchial Ultrasound–Guided Biopsy: A Case Report
creator: Xia Ren, Wenjin Liang, Li Chen, Min Gao, Jing Wang, Nannan Pang, Chao Wu
description: This case report presents a rare case of primary pulmonary marginal zone B‐cell lymphoma of mucosa‐associated lymphoid tissue (PMZL‐MALT). Follow‐up lung imaging performed 17 months after the initial presentation showed persistent pulmonary consolidation. After a radial probe endobronchial ultrasound (RP‐EBUS)–guided transbronchial lung biopsy, histopathological analysis confirmed the diagnosis of primary PMZL‐MALT.

title: Trends in medical debt in the United States by imputed borrower race and ethnicity, 2016-2022
creator: Alexander C Adia, Jenny S Guadamuz, Charleen Hsuan, Hector P Rodriguez
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionMedical debt is a major financial consequence of healthcare in the United States, but there is limited evidence about whether medical debt in collections varies across racial and ethnic groups.MethodsWe analyzed credit report data from 2016 to 2022 for 23,093,888 adults to study medical debt in collections accrued within the past year (flow) and total outstanding medical debt in collections (stock).ResultsBlack borrowers had the highest levels of annual flow of medical debt, with 11.2% of borrowers facing any annual flow of debt

title: Tele-Electrocardiography and Mortality: Clinical Outcomes in Digital Electrocardiography Cohort–Data from Belo Horizonte, Brazil (CODE-BH)
creator: Gabriela Miana de Mattos Paixão, Carla Paula Moreira Soares, Paulo Gomes Rodrigues, Peter W. Macfarlane, Antonio Luiz P. Ribeiro
description: Cardiovascular diseases are the leading cause of mortality in Brazil and around the world. The electrocardiogram (ECG) has a vital diagnostic and prognostic role in cardiovascular diseases. The CODE-BH cohort was established by linking ECG data (2006 to 2018) to hospitalization and mortality data from the public health database of Belo Horizonte, Minas Gerais, Brazil.

title: Ultrasound‐Guided Erector Spinae Plane Block Versus Transversus Abdominis Plane Block for Postoperative Analgesia in Adult Patients Undergoing Laparoscopic Appendectomy
creator: Eman Abdelnaby Mohamed Soliman, Mohsen Abdelgani Basyoni, Amira Fathy Hafni Soliman, Mohamed Abdelmawla Saleh, Engy Sami Attia Sami, Srijoni Sengupta
description: BackgroundEffective postoperative analgesia is essential after laparoscopic appendectomy. This randomized, double‐blind controlled study compared the analgesic efficacy of ultrasound‐guided erector spinae plane block (ESP) and the transversus abdominis plane block (TAP).MethodsThis randomized, double‐blind controlled study included 72 adult patients undergoing laparoscopic appendectomy. The primary outcome was the 24 h postoperative Numerical Rating Scale (NRS) pain score.

title: Crime opportunity theory: the state of the art
creator: Graham Farrell, Nick Tilley
description: The 1976 monograph Crime as Opportunity initiated a paradigm for how crime and criminality should be understood and controlled. Here we define a crime opportunity as any situation in which the benefits of committing crime outweigh the costs, and group crime opportunity-related theories and concepts under the banner of crime opportunity theory.

title: Empowering researchers and healthcare professionals in academic publishing: key insights and practical lessons from the British Society of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy (BSAC) workshop 2025
creator: Godwin Pius Ohemu, Tsitsi Arikana Mufunde, Tracie Muraya, Emmanuel Essonanjo, Peter Zarb, Rasha Abdelsalam Elshenawy, Neil Powell, Virve I Enne, Riina Rautemaa-Richardson
description: The British Society of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy (BSAC) Academic Publishing Workshop, held at the Birmingham City Event Centre in the UK from 19 to 20 March 2025, provided practical guidance for early-career researchers and healthcare professionals seeking to understand and actively engage with the academic publishing process.

title: Tonic dopamine sensing reveals a D2 and D3-mediated dopamine response to raclopride in ClockΔ19 mice model
creator: Bingchen Wu, Elisa Castagnola, Elaine Robbins, Mariya Kaminsky, Subramaniam Sanker, Colleen A McClung, Xinyan Tracy Cui
description: The circadian rhythm regulates physiological and behavioral processes, with disruptions linked to metabolic and neuropsychiatric disorders. Circadian genes play a crucial role in the regulation of dopaminergic signaling, yet the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigates how the Clock gene modulates dopamine (DA) dynamics using in vivo electrochemical DA sensing and molecular profiling.

title: Dietary Bazhen San solid-state fermentation product improves laying performance, immunity and intestinal health in laying hens during the late laying period
creator: Zenghui Zhao, Xiao Wang, Yongzhan Bao, Jiahui Meng, Jinlong Gong, Lu Zhang, Zhaonian Li, Weiyu Yao, Yanan Chuo, Wanyu Shi, Jianxi Li
description: The aim of this study was to investigate the effects of solid-state fermentation products of Bazhen San (FB) on the production performance, immunity, and intestinal health of laying hens during the late laying stage. A total of 150 70-week-old laying hens were randomly assigned to five treatment groups, with five replicates per group and six hens per replicate.

title: Impact of self-control and time perception on intertemporal choices in gain and loss situations
creator: Weiguo Qu, Ying Yang, Mengjie Zhou, Wei Fan
description: Individuals frequently encounter dilemmas in which they must choose between smaller, immediate gains and larger, delayed rewards; this phenomenon is known as intertemporal choice. The present study analyzed the interplay of trait and state self-control and time perception tendencies (time overestimation vs.

title: Paraneoplastic Vasculitis in a Patient With Breast Cancer at an Unusual Age: A Case Report
creator: Angélica Mandujano, Melissa Golubov, Víctor Gutiérrez
description: We report the case of an 87‐year‐old woman whose initial presentation was palpable purpura. Henoch–Schönlein purpura was initially diagnosed, for which she received intravenous methylprednisolone and epinastine, resulting in complete remission of the skin lesions. After discontinuation of corticosteroid therapy, she experienced multiple relapses over the ensuing months with an incomplete response to medical treatment.

title: A deep neural network-enhanced multi-scale coupled model of patient-specific acoustic wave propagation for mechanotransduction stimulation of healthy and osteoarthritic knee articular cartilage
creator: Nuno A. T. C. Fernandes, Betina Hinckel, Ana leal, Óscar Carvalho
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This study presents a multi-scale computational framework to quantify how externally applied acoustic waves propagate through the knee joint and induce mechanotransductive strain at the level of the chondrocyte nucleus. Patient-specific knee geometries (n = 8) were used to simulate acoustic wave transmission through layered tissues, while a representative volume element modelled the coupled solid–shell–acoustic behaviour of the chondrocyte, pericellular matrix, and extracellular matrix. Modal and frequency–response analyses identified the spheroidal s3 mode as the dominant contributor to nuclear deformation.

title: Probiotics and human health: biological activities, nutritional aspects, immunomodulatory properties, applications, and future perspectives - a comprehensive review
creator: Mohamed T. El-Saadony, Ahmed M. Saad, Mahmoud Sitohy, Samar Sami Alkafaas, Mthokozisi Dladla, Soumya Ghosh, Dina Mostafa Mohammed, Essam H. Ibrahim, Mohamed A. Fahmy, Amr Elkelish, Synan F. AbuQamar, Khaled A. El-Tarabily
description: Probiotics, defined as living microorganisms, are widely recognized for their ability to positively influence the gut microbiota, an effect increasingly linked to a wide array of health benefits. They are claimed to treat or prevent conditions ranging from infant colic to cardiovascular disease, respiratory infections, and certain cancers.

title: Surgical resection versus stereotactic body radiotherapy for oligometastatic breast cancer to the liver
creator: Lianjie Niu, Lixu Zhu, Qiang Zhang, Yongtao Bai, Qigen Fang, Xianfu Sun, Wenzhi Guo
description: Comparative evidence for hepatic resection and stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT) in breast cancer liver oligometastases remains limited. We compared survival, progression, and recovery after these treatments. This three-center retrospective study included adults with breast cancer and ≤ 3 liver metastases undergoing hepatic resection or SBRT between 2010 and 2023. Patients with uncontrolled extrahepatic disease were excluded.

title: Serological and molecular assessment of severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus infection in wild boars from two adjacent endemic prefectures in Japan
creator: Hirohisa MEKATA, Kazunori KIMITSUKI, Mari YAMAMOTO, Kazumi UMEKI, Takaaki YAHIRO, Reiko MIYAHARA, Akira NISHIZONO, Tamaki OKABAYASHI
description: Severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome virus (SFTSV) is a tick-borne zoonotic virus endemic to western Japan. Miyazaki and Oita Prefectures are neighboring regions on Kyushu Island; however, the total number of reported human SFTS cases in 2013–2025 was nearly double in Miyazaki compared with Oita.

title: Geographic disparities and temporal trends in aggressive prostate cancer: a SEER population-based analysis (2004–2022)
creator: Yifei Xu, Ayush Singh, Eric Li, Nicholas George Zaorsky, Nathaniel Geyer, Yifan Yang, Yanxu Yang, Alicia C. McDonald, Lijun Zhang, Ming Wang
description: PurposeProstate cancer burden may be amplified in rural regions or Appalachia areas, where access to screening and healthcare may be limited. This study examined geographic disparities and temporal trends in aggressive and metastatic prostate cancer across four groups defined by rurality and Appalachian status, while assessing assessed racial differences.

title: An integrated green strategy based on deep eutectic solvents and ultrasound for efficient polyphenol profiling and antioxidant evaluation of dendrobium officinale
creator: Dong-min Cao, Qian Zeng, Wen-xing Ao, Shuai Zheng, Ying-xin Lu, Xi-cheng Wang, Ming-Hua Xian, Shu-mei Wang
description: Deep eutectic solvents (DESs) combined with ultrasound-assisted extraction (UAE) have emerged as a promising green strategy for efficient recovery of bioactive compounds. In this study, a DES-based UAE system was developed for the extraction of polyphenols from Dendrobium officinale (DO), with particular emphasis on the synergistic effects and underlying mechanisms.

title: Anatomical and radiological analysis of ventricular catheter trajectories: neuronavigation-guided dissection and tractography-based 3D visualization
creator: Caner Fahrettin Kara, Mehmet Emin Akyüz, Muhammet Elveren, Ufuk Temtek, Mete Zeynal, Samet Kapakin, Ahmet Yalçın, Egemen Gök, Hakan Hadi Kadıoğlu, Mehmet Hakan Şahin
description: Ventricular catheter placement (VCP) is a life-saving intervention frequently performed in emergency departments and intensive care units. The free hand technique is the most commonly used approach for placing catheters. This study demonstrates the anatomical and radiological relationship between catheters inserted through the most commonly used access points and the anatomical structures in their path.

title: Symptom duration and postoperative outcomes in degenerative cervical myelopathy: a systematic review and meta-analysis
creator: Michał Szymoniuk, Wojciech Czyżewski, Marek Kochański, Barbara Buchalska, Piotr Kamieniak
description: Background: Surgical decompression is regarded as standard treatment for degenerative cervical myelopathy (DCM). However, the timing of surgery remains a critical yet unresolved issue in clinical practice. Therefore, this meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the impact of symptom duration on surgical outcomes and determine the optimal timing for surgery.

title: From historical dosing to precision dosing: Modernising tobramycin monitoring in people with cystic fibrosis
creator: Ellie Johnson, Michael Williams, Daniel Henderson, Timothy Riddles, David Reid, Daniel Smith, Andrew Burke, Ieuan Edward Shepherd Evans
description: BackgroundHistorical therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) strategies for intravenous tobramycin in people with cystic fibrosis (pwCF) were developed in the pre-CFTR modulator era and relied predominantly on clearance-based monitoring to minimise toxicity. Contemporary pwCF demonstrate greater variability in body composition and clinical phenotype, potentially limiting the applicability of historical dosing approaches.

title: Incorporation of robotic automated transcranial Doppler to screen for patent foramen ovale (PFO) and quantify right-to-left shunt severity in the evaluation of ischemic stroke patients for etiology and PFO management
creator: Ira Chang, Yasaman Pirahanchi, Simon Izaguirre, Richard Rodriguez, Alyssa Wicknick
description: BackgroundRight-to-left shunt (RLS) associated with patent foramen ovale (PFO) is common among cryptogenic strokes. Current diagnostic tools have limitations. Transthoratic echocardiography (TTE) is not as sensitive as Transesophageal echocardiography (TEE), TEE is invasive, and manual transcranial Doppler (TCD) requires trained staff to operate. Robotic automated TCD (raTCD) may be feasible and comparable to manual TCD.

title: Scutellaria baicalensis and Lonicera japonica herbal extracts enhanced the performance and physiological responses of pigs subjected to hot and dry season
creator: Vetriselvi Sampath, Yu Jin Baek, In Ho Kim
description: A 10-week growth trial was conducted using three groups of 70 growing-finishing pigs [210 head (Landrace × Yorkshire ♀ × Duroc ♂) with initial BW 53.92 ± 2.38 kg] to evaluate the effects of herbal extract mixture (HEM), composed of Scutellaria baicalensis and Lonicera japonica on overall performance of growing–finishing pigs.

title: Vitamins A, D, E, and K Intakes, Status, and Breastmilk Concentrations in Breastfeeding Women in Ireland
creator: Malak Ali, Fiona O’Dwyer, Brona Murphy, Heleena Moni Bottu, Martina Rooney, Torres Sweeney, Sharleen L O’ Reilly, Aifric M O’Sullivan
description: BackgroundFat-soluble vitamins A, D, E, and K are critical during the postpartum period for maternal recovery and infant development.ObjectivesTo determine the concentrations of vitamins A, D, E, and K in maternal serum and breastmilk during the early postpartum period in breastfeeding women.MethodsThis was a secondary analysis of the WellFed 4-wk randomized controlled trial.

title: Advances in statistical methods for cancer surveillance research: an age-period-cohort perspective
creator: Philip S. Rosenberg, Adalberto Miranda-Filho
description: BackgroundAnalysis of Lexis diagrams (population-based cancer incidence and mortality rates indexed by age group and calendar period) requires specialized statistical methods. However, existing methods have limitations that can now be overcome using new approaches.MethodsWe assembled a “toolbox” of novel methods to identify trends and patterns by age group, calendar period, and birth cohort.

title: Genome-wide characterisation of leaf rust resistance loci in an Eastern European barley collection
creator: Shiva Azizinia, Md Arifuzzaman, Eden Tongson, Karanjeet Sandhu, Gabriel Keeble-Gagnère, Ghazanfar Abbas Khan, Kerrie Forrest, Matthew Hayden, Dragan Perovic, Davinder Singh, Peter M Dracatos
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Key messageGWAS and inheritance testing uncovered known and potentially new genetic sources of leaf rust resistance in barley, mapping the dominant locus RphCaspian (RphCas) to chromosome 4HL in close physical proximity to Rph21. This study has unravelled the genetic architecture of leaf rust in barley and also provides closely linked SNP markers on the 40k Infinium wheat barley array suitable for marker assisted selection.AbstractBarley leaf rust (BLR) is a damaging foliar disease affecting grain yield and quality.

title: Stratified analysis based on VAS scores to assess the effect of acupoint application therapy in children with chronic coughs of varying severity-a randomized controlled study
creator: Danxia Ni, Liyun Zhong, Xinping Liu, Wenjing Lai, Jingyi Mai, Weiyi Dai, Meifeng Xie, Lifang Lei
description: MethodsIn this randomized controlled trial, one hundred children with chronic cough were allocated to either a control group (n = 50) receiving conventional bronchodilator and inhaled corticosteroid therapy, or an observation group (n = 50) receiving conventional therapy plus acupoint application.

title: “Can Everyone Hear Me?” Lessons on Educating Post-2020
creator: Kathryn Knoop
description: lty could not understand why learners were unwilling to unmute and join in the discussion. Virtual options are now a part of our learning environments as an alternative attendance option; therefore, it is important to reflect on effective teaching strategies.

title: Mannose-binding lectin gene polymorphism in psoriasis and vitiligo: an observational study and computational analysis
creator: Mohammed Y. Behairy, Noha Z. Tawfik, Refaat A. Eid, Dalal Nasser Binjawhar, Dalal Sulaiman Alshaya, Eman Fayad, Walid F. Elkhatib, Hoda Y. Abdallah
description: IntroductionPsoriasis and vitiligo are inflammatory autoimmune skin disorders with remarkable genetic involvement. Mannose-binding lectin (MBL) represents a significant immune molecule with one of its gene variants strongly linked to autoimmune diseases. Therefore, in this study, we investigated the role of the MBL variant, rs1800450, in psoriasis and vitiligo disease susceptibility.

title: BK virus-associated hemorrhagic cystitis in pediatric stem cell transplantation: a case report and scoping review
creator: Julia E. Moss, William J. Muller
description: IntroductionBK virus-associated hemorrhagic cystitis (BK-HC) is a debilitating and poorly understood complication of hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (SCT). Hematuria, dysuria, and other symptoms associated with BK-HC are common in the immediate post-SCT period, making BK-HC difficult to distinguish from other conditions presenting with these symptoms.

title: The unified protocol for transdiagnostic treatment of emotional disorders for misophonia: a pilot trial exploring acceptability and efficacy
creator: Kibby McMahon, Clair Cassiello-Robbins, Anna Greenleaf, Rachel Guetta, Emily Frazer-Abel, Lisalynn Kelley, M. Zachary Rosenthal
description: IntroductionMisophonia is a recently defined disorder characterized by distressing responses to everyday sounds, such as chewing or sniffling. Individuals with misophonia experience significant functional impairment but have limited options for evidenced-based behavioral treatment. To address this gap in the literature, the current pilot trial explored the acceptability and efficacy of a transdiagnostic cognitive-behavioral approach to treating symptoms of misophonia.

title: Timing of Insulin Glargine Administration During Intermittent Ramadan Fasting in patients With Type1 Diabetes: A Randomized Controlled Trial (GLARIF)
creator: Reem Alamoudi, Ali Alqarni, Maram Alsubaiee, Ghofran Khogeer, Yousef Saleh, Abdulrhman Aljawharji, Hawazen Zarif, Salwa Alaidarous, Seham Khashwayn, Mohamed Hassanein
description: Objective:The effect of basal insulin timing on hypoglycemia during Ramadan fasting remains uncertain despite recommendations to administer basal insulin earlier in the evening. We evaluated whether early evening compared with bedtime administration of insulin glargine reduces hypoglycemia and improves glycemic outcomes in individuals with type1 diabetes (T1D) fasting during Ramadan.

title: Glutamate tone in preBötzinger complex rhythmogenesis: ambient extracellular glutamate as a candidate excitability bias
creator: Enrique Vázquez-Mendoza, Carol Alejandra Olmos-Pastoresa, Donají Chí-Castañeda, María Leonor López-Meraz, Luis Beltran-Parrazal, Consuelo Morgado-Valle
description: The preBötzinger complex (preBötC) is essential for inspiratory rhythm generation, yet the biological processes that repeatedly establish the excitability state required for neuronal recruitment remain incompletely understood. This unresolved issue is reflected in computational models of respiratory rhythmogenesis, which rely on a phenomenological baseline excitability parameter, , without a defined biological substrate.

title: Loop Taping for Heel Fat Pad Syndrome: A Crossover Pilot Randomized Controlled Trial
creator: Alison H Chang, Katrine Bruun Skov, Thomas Sørensen, Michael Skovdal Rathleff, Henrik Riel, Kristian Damgaard Lyng, Jens Lykkegaard Olesen, Marianne Christensen
description: ObjectivesHeel fat pad syndrome (HFPS) is a common but under‐investigated cause of plantar heel pain. No randomized controlled trials (RCTs) have evaluated targeted treatments.
