This study evaluated the immediate and short‐term effects of novel loop taping on pain, function, and fat pad thickness in adults with HFPS.DesignTwo‐period crossover pilot RCT.

title: Location of incidental and symptomatic LGGs. A review of comparative studies
creator: Barbara Tomasino, Ilaria Guarracino, Serena D’Agostini, Asgeir S Jakola, Tamara Ius
description: Highlights•We aimed at understanding the anatomical distribution of symptomatic and asymptomatic low grade gliomas.•22 cohort studies and 6 case reports were included.•there is a predominance of iLGGs in the frontal lobes.•there is an equal involvement of the left and right hemisphere.•the number of oligodendroglioma were correlated with the number of frontal lesions.

title: Dual-Access Secure-and-Pull Technique of an Entrapped Left Main Stent With Late Mechanical Failure
creator: Kaïs Ouerghi, Mihai Cocoi, Tahar Lazizi, Victor Mateus
description: BackgroundStent entrapment within a previously implanted left main (LM) scaffold is a rare but high-risk complication. Although snare retrieval is an effective bailout strategy, traction may induce occult structural injury.Case SummaryA 63-year-old man underwent emergent LM-to–left anterior descending (LAD) bifurcation stenting after resuscitated cardiac arrest (day 0).

title: Cryo‐EM structures of multiple‐peptide resistance factor (MprF) from Pseudomonas aeruginosa
creator: Shaileshanand Jha, Kutti R. Vinothkumar
description: Aminoacylation of the lipid head group in many bacteria is carried out by bi‐functional enzymes called MprF, which encode a soluble synthase domain that typically transfers lysine or alanine from a tRNA to lipid head groups. The modified lipid is subsequently translocated across the leaflets by a transmembrane domain.

title: B Cell Deficiency Protects Against the Development of c‐MET and Beta‐Catenin Driven Hepatocellular Carcinoma in Mice
creator: Fang Wang, Eun Bi Lim, Rehan Mehta, Yee Ling Wu
description: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), a lethal form of liver cancer, continues to show rising mortality rates despite advancements in immunotherapies. This highlights the need for more effective treatments. Recent studies linked the presence of B cells within human tumors, including HCC, to improved responses to immunotherapy and better prognoses.

title: Target Trial Emulation or Target Trial Approximation?
creator: Priya Vart
description: Target trial emulation has contributed to improvements in the design and interpretation of observational studies aimed at causal inference. By encouraging researchers to think explicitly about the design of a hypothetical randomized trial, it has helped identify and address avoidable design flaws. However, the framework cannot overcome biases and limitations inherent in observational data.

title: Effects of electrical stimulation on the cardiogenic differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells: A systematic review
creator: Alejandra Sandoval Villarreal, Paola Neuta-Arciniegas, John Jairo Cabrera-López, Álvaro José Rojas Arciniegas
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Electrical stimulation has emerged as a promising strategy for promoting cardiogenic differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells; however, the available evidence remains highly heterogeneous across stimulation parameters, experimental platforms, and outcome measures. This systematic review synthesized the available in vitro evidence regarding the effects of electrical stimulation on MSC cardiogenic differentiation, with particular emphasis on stimulation parameters, experimental platforms and biological outcomes related to early cardiogenic commitment and structural maturation.

title: Prevalence of overweight and obesity among children in Greenland: a growing concern
creator: Emma Vang Frandsen, Ida Hove Christensen, Michael Lynge Pedersen, Stine Byberg
description: To investigate the prevalence of overweight and obesity among children aged 3 to 10 years in Greenland. Further, to describe the prevalence of overweight and obesity according to sex, place of residence and age, including change over time. In a cross-sectional study, we included 4715 children aged 3–10 years, using data from the national electronic medical records.

title: Dose-dependent cardiac autonomic dysregulation under classroom crowding: heart rate variability analysis and machine learning classification
creator: Mohamed Naeem
description: Classroom overcrowding affects hundreds of millions of students globally, yet its physiological impact on cardiac autonomic function remains uncharacterized. This controlled within-subjects experiment enrolled 30 healthy university students who attended standardized 30-min lectures under three calibrated density conditions: low (30 students/150 m2), medium (60/150 m2), and high (100/150 m2), with all environmental parameters held constant.

title: Prevalence and associated factors of subjective cognitive decline (SCD Plus): a cross-sectional analysis of three population-based European cohorts
creator: Andrea E. Zülke, Melanie Luppa, Christian Sander, Ronny Baber, Ronald Biemann, Kerstin Wirkner, Samira Zeynalova, Silke Zachariae, Milica Matijevic, Christoph Engel, Nigar Reyes, Andreas Hinz, Heide Glaesmer, Matthias L. Schroeter, A. Veronica Witte, Arno Villringer, Markus Löffler, Carol Brayne, St
description: BackgroundSubjective cognitive decline (SCD) is considered an early preclinical marker for Alzheimer’s disease (AD). However, prevalence estimates vary widely due to inconsistent definitions. SCD Plus criteria were proposed by experts to improve specificity for preclinical AD. Population-based evidence on the prevalence and correlates of SCD Plus remains limited.

title: Dietary characteristics associated with hemoglobin and anemia among prospective first-time voluntary blood donors in Accra, Ghana
creator: Salmana Mehmood, Susan Telke, Edeghonghon Olayemi, Caitlin Ward, Lucy Asamoah-Akuoko, Bernard Appiah, Alfred Edwin Yawson, Tara Tancred, Amma Anima Benneh-Akwasi Kuma, Reena Ametorwo, Frank Ofori, Philip Baba Adongo, Jerry Daneku, Isaac Danso, Abigail Nana Afua Amegadoe, Catherine Segbefia, Cavan Re
description: BackgroundOptimal dietary intake supports adequate hemoglobin (Hb) levels for blood donation. However, little is known about the dietary characteristics of prospective first-time voluntary blood donors (VBDs) in Ghana and their associations with Hb and anemia. We aimed to identify dietary characteristics associated with Hb concentration and anemia status among prospective first-time VBDs in Accra.

title: Late-onset Graves’ disease after hemithyroidectomy: a case report
creator: Sayaka Mabuchi, Naoko Adachi, Atsushi Nagasawa, Satoshi Nabika, Kazumi Notsu
description: BackgroundAmong hyperthyroidism cases, Graves’ disease is the most common, with incidence peaking between 30 and 60 years of age. Hemithyroidectomy is sometimes performed for conditions such as thyroid tumors, and Graves’ disease may develop from the residual thyroid tissue postoperatively. The occurrence of Graves’ disease in the residual thyroid gland after resection of neoplastic lesions is very rare.

title: Greenness profile assessment of a novel pioneer approach for voltametric sensing of cloperastine fendizoate in a pharmaceutical dosage form
creator: Maha Mahmoud Abou El‑Alamin, Ola Abd Elkhalek, Marwa M. Azab
description: A novel sustainable analytical approach based on an electrochemical sensor has been fabricated for the quantification of Cloperastine Fendizoate (CLP), which has recently been employed in the management of COVID-19. A carbon paste electrode modified with 2% multiwalled carbon nanotubes and 1% chitosan (2%MWCNT/1%Chitosan/CPE) was fabricated to implement the proposed procedure.

title: Paravertebral muscle quality and adjacent facet joint degeneration as significant predictors of ASDis revision after lumbar fusion
creator: Dandan Li, Peng Gao, YingJuan Chang, Xing Tang
description: BackgroundPosterior lumbar interbody fusion (PLIF) combined with pedicle screw internal fixation is widely used to treat lumbar degenerative diseases. However, adjacent segment disease (ASDis) is a severe complication and requires revision surgery, and few studies have focused on this complication.

title: A method of deep network auto-training based on the MTPI auto-transfer learning and a reinforcement learning algorithm for vegetation detection in a dry thermal valley environment
creator: Yayong Chen, Beibei Zhou, Chen Xiaopeng, Changkun Ma, Lei Cui, Feng Lei, Xiaojie Han, Linjie Chen, Shanshan Wu, Dapeng Ye
description: UAV image acquisition and deep learning techniques have been widely used in field hydrological monitoring to meet the increasing data volume demand and refined quality. However, manual parameter training requires trial-and-error costs (T&E), and existing auto-trainings adapt to simple datasets and network structures, which is low practicality in unstructured environments, e.g., dry thermal valley environment (DTV).

title: Study insights in the role of PGC-1α in neurological diseases: mechanisms and therapeutic potential
creator: Mi-bo Tang, Yi-xuan Liu, Zheng-wei Hu, Hai-yang Luo, Shuo Zhang, Chang-he Shi, Yu-ming Xu
description: Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor-γ coactivator-1α (PGC-1α), which is highly expressed in the central nervous system, is known to be involved in the regulation of mitochondrial biosynthesis, metabolic regulation, neuroinflammation, autophagy, and oxidative stress. This knowledge indicates a potential role of PGC-1α in a wide range of functions associated with neurological diseases.

title: Loss of power by degree of heaping in covariables
creator: Matthias Becher, Willi Sauerbrei, Heiko Becher
description: Heaping or digit preference is frequently occurring in health research data as well as in deliberate data masking. We investigate the associated loss of power associated by degree of heaping by simulation and illustrate the effect with a real dataset. Moderate heaping leads to little power loss and may be tolerable.

title: Trajectories of systemic immune inflammation index and mortality risk in patients with moderate-to-severe traumatic brain injury: a retrospective cohort study
creator: Zhiyong Tang, Canlin Liao, Zerui Zhuang, Zhennan Xu, Mingfa Liu, Haixiong Xu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundSome studies have shown a strong link between the central nervous system and peripheral immune system, but the prognostic implications of dynamic peripheral immune-inflammatory responses in patients with traumatic brain injury (TBI) remain unclear. This study aimed to determine the dynamic trajectory patterns of the Systemic Immune Inflammation Index (SII) in patients with TBI and assess its association with all-cause hospital mortality.MethodsThis retrospective cohort study utilized a large public database of patients with TBI sourced from the eICU Collaborative Research Database (eICU-CRD).

title: Wnt signal-dependent antero-posterior specification of early-stage CNS primordia modeled in EpiSC-derived neural stem cells
creator: Kae Nakamura, Yusaku Watanabe, Claire Boitet, Sayaka Satake, Hideaki Iida, Koya Yoshihi, Yasuo Ishii, Kagayaki Kato, Hisato Kondoh
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The specification of the embryonic central nervous system (CNS) into future brain (forebrain, midbrain, or hindbrain) and spinal cord (SC) regions is a critical step of CNS development. A previous chicken embryo study indicated that anterior epiblast cells marked by Sox2 N2 enhancer activity are specified to the respective brain regions during the transition phase of the epiblast to the neural plate-forming neural primordium.

title: Integrative transcriptomic analysis reveals tumor-adjacent mucosal remodeling in colorectal cancer
creator: Sha Wu, Long Wu, Ruoshi Li, Xin Luo, Xueni Zhao, Liangrui Shi, Wei Liu, Lishan Ding, Zhaotong Cong, Zhuohong Li, Chuan Zheng, Chi Song
description: Tumor-adjacent mucosa is commonly used as a normal reference in colorectal cancer (CRC) transcriptomic studies, but its relationship with distant normal mucosa and tumor tissue remains unclear. Here, we performed bulk RNA sequencing of paired distant normal, adjacent, and tumor tissues from 25 patients with CRC and used these three tissue states to construct an ordered normal–adjacent–tumor (N-A-T) expression continuum.

title: Histotype and molecular subtype integration in epithelial ovarian cancer: implications for targeted treatment
creator: Shuyi Liu, Chaoyang Sun
description: Ovarian cancer remains a major global health burden among women, ranking eighth in both cancer incidence and cancer mortality worldwide in 2024, with an estimated 330,731 new cases and 203,850 deaths. Epithelial ovarian cancer (EOC) accounts for more than 90% of ovarian cancers and comprises five major histological subtypes with distinct biological behavior, molecular alterations, and therapeutic vulnerabilities.

title: Tick bite-induced alpha-gal syndrome and immunologic responses in an alpha-gal deficient murine model
creator: Surendra Raj Sharma, Shailesh K. Choudhary, Julia Vorobiov, Scott P. Commins, Shahid Karim
description: IntroductionAlpha-Gal Syndrome (AGS) is a delayed allergic reaction due to specific IgE antibodies targeting galactose-α-1,3-galactose (α-gal), a carbohydrate found in red meat. This condition has gained significant attention globally due to its increasing prevalence, with more than 450,000 cases estimated just in the United States alone.

title: Tackling climate change at the city level: insights from Lighthouse Cities' climate mitigation efforts
creator: Mehmet Efe Biresselioglu, Zehra Funda Savas, Muhittin Hakan Demir, Cigdem Kentmen-Cin
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). IntroductionThe link between lifestyles and Greenhouse Gas (GHG) emissions has prioritized climate mitigation strategies of cities worldwide. As cities have increasingly generated GHG emissions by their industrial and transportation activities, their role in climate mitigation has gained prominence. Cities' climate mitigation policies to reduce the GHG intensity of their residents' daily lives are one of their significant efforts to tackle climate change.

title: Peripheral and cerebrospinal fluid inflammatory markers in sporadic amyotrophic lateral sclerosis an exploratory cross-sectional association study
creator: Agnieszka Wełnicka-Wesołowska, Karolina Łuczkowska, Przemysław Nowacki, Edyta Paczkowska, Agnieszka Meller, Karolina Machowska-Sempruch, Bogusław Machaliński, Monika Gołąb-Janowska
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder with an ambiguous etiology, whose onset may be linked to innate immune system activation outside the central nervous system (CNS). We investigated the association between peripheral blood and CNS inflammatory parameters in 45 sporadic ALS patients compared to 30 controls, analyzing peripheral blood tests (C-reactive protein [CRP], blood count, fibrinogen) and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) immunological measures (Tumor Necrosis Factor alpha [TNF-α], TNF receptor type 1 [TNFR-1], CRP) alongside clinical characteristics.

title: Healthcare under fire: a retrospective analysis of a national ngo response during the 2024 conflict in Lebanon
creator: Rana El Haidari, Adnan Husseini, Kassem Baydoun, Rima Badran, Samir Mansour, Abbas Hoballah
description: BackgroundThe 2024 conflict in Lebanon triggered widespread internal displacement and placed significant strain on the national health system. This study analyzes the emergency healthcare response of the Health Society during Lebanon’s 2024 conflict using a health systems resilience framework and SWOT analysis to inform evidence-based interventions for conflict-affected populations and guide future policy and research.

title: Effects of lifestyle education interventions on quality of life and fbg in women with gestational diabetes: a systematic review and meta-analysis
creator: Mina Shojaee, Mahsa Sharifnejad, Nastaran Safavi Ardabili, Fatemeh Abdi, Mohammadamin Jandaghian-Bidgoli, Mahboubeh Firouz, Solmaz Norouzi
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Introduction: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM) is a prevalent condition with significant maternal and fetal health implications. Lifestyle education is a promising non-pharmacological intervention to improve quality of life (QoL) and fasting blood glucose (FBG) in affected women. For the purposes of this review, lifestyle education interventions are defined as structured programs including dietary counseling, physical activity guidance, and/or self-management education (e.g., blood glucose monitoring), delivered through planned sessions with defined frequency, duration, and content.

title: Effects of experimental ostracism on cortisol, autonomic regulation, and affective states in adolescents with nonsuicidal self-injury
creator: Andreas Goreis, Annika Lozar, Rosa List, Sofia-Marie Oehlke, Diana Klinger, Bettina Pfeffer, Karin Prillinger, Clarissa Laczkovics, Heidi Zesch, Urs M. Nater, Nadine Skoluda, Peter B. Marschik, Laurence Claes, Paul L. Plener, Oswald D. Kothgassner
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundAdolescents who engage in nonsuicidal self-injury (NSSI) show a high sensitivity to ostracism, and its effects may be amplified by dysregulated stress-system function. However, ecologically grounded experimental studies examining multilevel stress responses in adolescent mental health remain scarce.

title: How the adaptation of the human microbiome to harsh space environment can determine the chances of success for a space mission to Mars and beyond
creator: Seyed Mohammad Javad Mortazavi, Ilham Said-Salman, Ali Reza Mortazavi, Sami El Khatib, Lembit Sihver
description: The ability of human cells to adapt to space radiation is essential for the well-being of astronauts during long-distance space expeditions, such as voyages to Mars or other deep space destinations. However, the adaptation of the microbiomes should not be overlooked.

title: Streptomyces chodovensis sp. nov.: a novel candidate for plant growth-promoting actinomycete from bare soil developing on Miocene lacustrine sediment of the Sokolov Coal Basin, Czech Republic
creator: Alper Dede, Vaclav Krištůfek, Lucie Kotrbová, Kateřina Petříčková, Terézia Horváthová, Christopher M Field, Sarah Kirstein, Meina Neumann-Schaal, Imen Nouioui, Alica Chroňáková
description: A novel actinomycete, designated as BCCO 10_0861T, was isolated from overburden Miocene clay sediments undergoing primary succession in Northwest Czechia and characterized by the polyphasic approach. According to 16S rRNA gene sequence similarity, the strain was closely related to Streptomyces turgidiscabies DSM 41838T (99.00%), Streptomyces reticuliscabiei DSM 41804T (98.93%), Streptomyces lacrimifluminis DSM 111125T (98.15%), and Streptomyces geranii JCM 32177T (98.08%).

title: Impact of COVID-19 on the mental health of adolescents and youth in Nairobi, Kenya
creator: Peter B. Gichangi, Meagan E. Byrne, Mary N. Thiongo, Michael Waithaka, Bianca Devoto, Elizabeth Gummerson, Shannon N. Wood, Philip Anglewicz, Michele R. Decker
description: ObjectiveTo report on the mental health status of adolescents and youth in relation to the COVID-19 pandemic in Nairobi County, Kenya.MethodologyThis was a mixed-methods study with cross-sectional quantitative and qualitative components conducted in Nairobi County, Kenya from August to September 2020. The quantitative survey involved phone interviews of n = 1,217 adolescents and youth.

title: Epstein-barr virus-associated hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis after antithymocyte globulin-conditioned allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation: a single-center case series
creator: Ingerid Weum Abrahamsen, Anders Eivind Myhre, Camilla Dao Vo, Tobias Gedde-Dahl, Tor Henrik Tvedt
description: ired conditions such as malignancies, infections, autoimmune diseases and therapies that induce immune dysregulation. A substantial proportion of cases are associated with immune dysregulation in combination with reactivation of the Epstein–Barr virus (EBV) [2]. In allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT), EBV reactivation is a well-recognized complication.

title: Establishment of a reverse genetics system for an epidemic strain of porcine rotavirus JXAY01 type G5P[23]I12
creator: Changjin Liu, Huangsiwu Wei, Xingyi Zhang, Wenjie Wu, Zhengqiao Shen, Feng Luo, Shunzhou Deng
description: Porcine rotavirus is one of the most important pathogens causing diarrhea in newborn piglets, and the genome of this virus contains 11 double-stranded RNA segments, which are easy to be recombined among strains to produce new strains with different antigenic properties. The reverse genetics system is an informative tool for studying virus biology.

title: Vascular plasticity in the gastric cancer environment: mechanisms, prognostic significance, and concepts of therapeutic interventions
creator: Magdalena Chmiela, Patrycja Jaroniek, Juan Carlos Rodríguez Manzaneque, Ewa Balcerczak, Marek Brzeziński, Agnieszka Jeleń, Saravanan Mani, Agnieszka Wosiak, Weronika Gonciarz
description: Gastric cancer (GC) remains a major global health problem because of its aggressive behavior and frequent development of therapeutic resistance. In GC, as in other malignancies, blood vessels are essential for Tumor-cell survival and dissemination, thereby facilitating metastasis to distant organs. As tumors grow, they remodel the surrounding microenvironment, generating hypoxic, acidic, nutrient-poor conditions with elevated interstitial fluid pressure.

title: Hemoptysis caused by Parvimonas micra: case report and literature review
creator: Axue Shao, Qingqing He, Xin Jiao, Jianbo Liu
description: BackgroundParvimonas micra (P. micra), a Gram-positive anaerobic bacterium, exhibits colonization tendencies on oral mucosal and skin surfaces, potentially evolving into a pathogenic entity associated with diverse diseases. The diagnostic trajectory for P. micra-related diseases encounters delays, often with severe consequences, including fatality, attributed to the absence of symptom specificity and challenges in culture.

title: Drug-eluting beads transarterial chemoembolization vs conventional transarterial chemoembolization in the treatment of hepatocellular carcinoma in adult patients: a systematic review and update meta-analysis of observational studies
creator: Tatiana Chernyshenko, Roman Polkin, Ekaterina Dvoinikova, Valeriy Shepelev, Roman Goncharuk
description: Study designSystematic review and update meta-analysis.PurposeThe present systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted to compare the efficacy and safety of the two approaches for HCC in adult patients (DEB-TACE vs cTACE).Overview of literatureThe TACE procedure is indicated for the treatment of HCC with intermediate (BCLC B) and early (BCLC A).

title: Expert consensus on the management of peripheral neuropathy in patients with lymphoma on brentuximab vedotin
creator: Roser Velasco, José A. Sanches, Andreas A. Argyriou, Guido Cavaletti, Eva Domingo-Domenech, Alexander Fosså, Jaime Gállego Pérez-Larraya, Antonia Miranda Ruiz, Alex Molassiotis, André Neder Ramires Abdo, Pablo L. Ortiz-Romero, Susanna B. Park, Julia Scarisbrick, Lauren Urwin, Mian Wang, H. Miles Pri
description: PurposeBrentuximab vedotin (BV) represents a therapeutic advancement in the treatment of CD30-positive lymphomas, yet its clinical utility is often limited by BV-induced peripheral neuropathy (PN). Currently, evidence-based, BV-specific guidelines for the assessment and management of PN are scarce, resulting in variability in clinical practice.

title: A three-player game model for promoting enterprise green technology innovation from the perspective of media coverage
creator: Yan Liu, Yun-ping Chen, Tong-ping Xie, Yi-han Xia
description: ObjectiveThe objective of this study was to explore the game relationship among enterprise, the government, and the public under the new media environment, so as to provide decision-making reference for improving enterprise green technology innovation and promoting economy high-quality development with new media participation.

title: Ghana’s Diagnosis Related Grouping (G-DRG) tariffs versus hospital charges: implications for inpatient care financing at a secondary hospital in Ghana
creator: Peter Gyasi Darkwa, Genevieve Cecilia Aryeetey, Eric Nsiah-Boateng
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundGhana introduced the National Health Insurance Scheme (NHIS) in 2003 as a means of achieving Universal Health Coverage. The Ghana-Diagnosis Related Groupings (G-DRG) is one of the payment mechanisms used to reimburse providers for services and procedures.

title: IFNλ1 is a STING-dependent mediator of DNA damage and induces immune activation in lung cancer
creator: Stine Høvring Godsk, Caroline Maren Stengaard Jensen, Trine Vilsbøll Larsen, Johanne Ahrenfeldt, Kristine Raaby Gammelgaard, Martin Roelsgaard Jakobsen
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). IntroductionThe importance of the cGAS-STING pathway and type I interferon (IFN) in anti-tumor immunity has been widely studied. However, there is limited knowledge about the role of type III IFNs in cancer settings.

title: Postoperative care in conflict-affected northwest Syria: a mixed-methods study assessing the perspectives of patients, health workers, and non-governmental organizations
creator: Camila Polinori, Maia C. Tarnas, Kelli Wagner, Mohammad Darwish, Stefany M. Lazieh, Ahmad Alnasser, Ahmad Ghandour, Ismail Alkhatib, Saverio Bellizzi, Bara Zuhaili, Gilbert Burnham
description: IntroductionThirteen years of conflict have profoundly disrupted Syria’s health system. In northwest Syria, constraints such as deliberate attacks on healthcare, chronic underfunding, and a fragmented health system have created a fragile surgical ecosystem in which health workers operate under extreme resource constraints, patients struggle to access care, and postoperative complications are increasingly likely.

title: Immune mapping of human tuberculosis and sarcoidosis lung granulomas
creator: Berit Carow, Victoria Muliadi, Kristina Skålén, Chika Yokota, Gokul Raj Kathamuthu, Todia Pediatama Setiabudiawan, Christoph Lange, Katrin Scheu, Karoline I. Gaede, Torsten Goldmann, Ankur Pandita, Kiran Iqbal Masood, Shahid Pervez, Johan Grunewald, Zahra Hasan, Max Levin, Martin E. Rottenberg
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Tuberculosis (TB) and sarcoidosis are both granulomatous diseases. Here, we compared the immunological microenvironments of granulomas from TB and sarcoidosis patients using in situ sequencing (ISS) transcriptomic analysis and multiplexed immunolabeling of tissue sections. TB lesions consisted of large necrotic and cellular granulomas, whereas “multifocal” granulomas with macrophages or epitheloid cell core and a T-cell rim were observed in sarcoidosis samples. The necrotic core in TB lesions was surrounded by macrophages and encircled by a dense T-cell layer.

title: Oral_voting_transfer: classification of oral microorganisms’ function proteins with voting transfer model
creator: Wenzheng Bao, Yujun Liu, Baitong Chen
description: IntroductionThe oral microbial group typically represents the human body’s highly complex microbial group ecosystem. Oral microorganisms take part in human diseases, including Oral cavity inflammation, mucosal disease, periodontal disease, tooth decay, and oral cancer. On the other hand, oral microbes can also cause endocrine disorders, digestive function, and nerve function disorders, such as diabetes, digestive system diseases, and Alzheimer’s disease.

title: Neurofilaments in cerebrospinal fluid and/or serum as a possible biomarker of pediatric spinal muscular atrophy
creator: Markéta Kumhera, Eva Vrsčaj, Tanja Loboda, Damjan Osredkar, Petra Holotová, Marie Rohlenová, Barbora Lauerová, Vanesa Jurášová, Jitka Hanzalová, Markéta Pavlíková, Jana Haberlová
description: BackgroundSpinal muscular atrophy (SMA) is a severe, genetically determined neuromuscular disorder characterised by progressive muscle weakness resulting from motor neuron degeneration. Although therapies such as nusinersen have altered disease trajectories, objective biomarkers for treatment monitoring remain lacking. Neurofilament proteins, particularly phosphorylated neurofilament heavy chain (pNFH), are promising candidates for this role.

title: Decoupling of kinetic and kinematic asymmetry in elite sculling: catch slip synchronization is more closely associated with boat speed than force balance
creator: Shuwei Chen, Yingping Zhang, Xiaohua Li, Yang Liu, Sen Yang, Xiubing Zhang, Weibao Liang
description: BackgroundTo investigate the phase-dependent behavior of kinematic and kinetic asymmetry during an on-water incremental 2000-m test and to determine which asymmetry components were independently associated with boat speed in elite scullers.MethodsTwelve elite male single scullers completed a continuous 2000 m on-water incremental test.

title: A tale of two belongings: social and academic belonging differentially shape academic and psychological outcomes among university students
creator: Smaranda Ioana Lawrie, Delwin B. Carter, Karen Nylund-Gibson, Heejung S. Kim
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The benefits of belonging in academic settings are well established; however, past empirical research has for the most part conflated academic and social belonging. This study utilized latent class analysis (LCA) with a sample of undergraduates (N = 837) to determine whether distinct classes or profiles of belonging exist on a college campus and whether class membership predicts academic and psychological outcomes.

title: Impact of COVID-19 on national health screening participation and chronic disease detection: evidence from South Korea’s NHIS database
creator: Sunyoung Kim, Hyejin Lee, Jungha Park, Sujeong Han, Hye Yeon Koo, Eunbyul Cho, Haeung Song, Bumjo Oh
description: BackgroundThe COVID-19 pandemic disrupted preventive healthcare services worldwide, raising concerns about missed diagnoses of chronic diseases. South Korea’s national health screening program experienced a substantial decline in participation during 2020. This study investigated how changes in screening rates influenced chronic disease detection and what these shifts reveal about the resilience of the national health system.

title: Structural Snapshots of F1 ‐ATPase Catalysis in Drug Resistant Acinetobacter baumannii Reveal Novel Therapeutic Targets
creator: Khoa C M Le, Jan K Marzinek, Vikneswaran Mathiyazakan, Peter J Bond, Gerhard Grüber
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Gram‐negative Acinetobacter baumannii , one of the most critical priority pathogens, has developed multiple defense mechanisms, including upregulation of drug efflux pumps powered by the proton‐motive force (pmf) or ATP. As a nonfermenting bacterium, it relies on oxidative phosphorylation, in which the F‐ATP synthase, composed of an F1‐ATPase (α 3:β 3:γ:ε) and FO‐domain (a:b 2 :c 10), synthesizes ATP, the cell's currency of life.

title: No evidence for a causal link between Helicobacter pylori infection and Irritable bowel syndrome: a Mendelian randomization study
creator: Chenchen Wang, Jing Zhang, Fengli Han, Dong Liu, Yuying Han
description: BackgroundAlthough clinical studies have revealed a potential link between Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infection and irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), the causal relationship between them remains unknown. The objective of this study was to investigate whether H. pylori infection is causally associated with IBS.

title: Microbial cell factories for gamma-linolenic acid biosynthesis: metabolic engineering, downstream processing, and future perspectives
creator: Jie Qiao, Wei Wang, Peiyao Duan, Zhili Zhang, Rongrong Yang, Haiyang Cui, Xiujuan Li
description: Gamma-linolenic acid (GLA) is a vital anti-inflammatory polyunsaturated fatty acid, yet its traditional supply from plant seeds such as evening primrose and borage is constrained by low yields and climatic instability. Consequently, microbial cell factories present a sustainable and season-independent alternative for scalable GLA production. This review critically synthesizes recent biotechnological advancements in utilizing oleaginous microorganisms as production platforms.

title: The Serotonergic and Cholinergic Signaling Pathways Drive Gastric Precancerous Lesions and Its Potential Mechanism
creator: Shengli Gao, Xufei Feng, Nana Zhang, Jia Su, Yuyan Wang, Linghan Kong, Jianing Zhou, Hui Dong, Feifei Guo
description: Gastric cancer (GC) is a leading lethal malignancy globally. Gastric precancerous lesion (GPL) represents a critical step in GC, but its neural regulatory mechanisms remain largely unclear. We combined bioinformatics, patch‐clamp recording, immunofluorescence, and chemogenetics to investigate serotonergic and cholinergic signaling in GPL. An N‐methyl‐N‐nitrosourea (MNU) ‐induced mouse model was used for in vivo validation.

title: Tetrandrine-based in situ vaccination via multifunctional Mn²⁺-hyaluronic acid hydrogel loading gelatinase-responsive nanoparticles
creator: Wanru Wang, Shujun Song, Dongliang Han, Yuling Qiu, Dan Lei, Xuxuan Gu, Haoyue Qi, Hanxi Zhang, Lanqi Cen, Jie Shao, Xiaoping Qian, Wenxiu Chen, Lixia Yu, Baorui Liu, Li Xie, Rutian Li
description: In situ tumor vaccination (ISV) has emerged as a promising strategy for converting tumors into endogenous vaccine depots, but its application in breast cancer remains limited by poor intratumoral drug retention and insufficient microenvironment remodeling. Here, we developed an injectable Mn²⁺-coordinated hyaluronic acid hydrogel embedding gelatinase-responsive tetrandrine nanoparticles (TETNPs@Gel) as an MRI-trackable local ISV platform.

title: Eco-friendly biosynthesis of silver nanoparticles by saprophytic Fusarium solani as a sustainable therapeutic approach for the management of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus wound infections
creator: Heba A. Ramadan, Fatma Sonbol, Tarek El‑banna, Ahmed Kassem El-Sayed, Mohamed M. El-Zahed, Engy Elekhnawy
description: The rising prevalence of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) has prompted the exploration of novel, naturally sourced therapeutic alternatives. Here, the saprophytic fungus Fusarium solani was used to biosynthesize silver nanoparticles (AgNPs), which were characterized by UV–visible spectroscopy, transmission electron microscopy (TEM), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), X-ray diffraction (XRD), and Fourier-transform infrared spectroscopy (FTIR).

title: ROS-responsive hydrogel microspheres deliver shTMEM2-loaded liposomes to suppress pyroptosis and ameliorate intervertebral disc degeneration
creator: Zhiqiang Xu, Hanmo Fang, Chengrui Peng, Zhiwei Liao, Guoyu Yang, Hu Qian, Jun Ao, Xinghuo Wu
description: Low back pain (LBP) is a highly prevalent musculoskeletal disorder worldwide. Nucleus pulposus cell (NPC) pyroptosis contributes to intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD), but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. We identified TMEM2, a transmembrane protein not previously linked to IVDD, as markedly upregulated in degenerated NPCs by single‑cell RNA sequencing.

title: Statistical optimization of melanin-like pigment biosynthesis by marine Streptomyces isolate MOE3 and evaluation of its cytotoxic activity against A-431 cells
creator: Moaz M Hamed, Sahar W M Hassan, Eman H Zaghloul
description: Marine actinomycetes represent a promising source of biologically active natural pigments. In the present study, isolate MOE3, recovered from mangrove sediment along the Egyptian Red Sea coast, was provisionally assigned to Streptomyces lateritius based on partial 16 S rRNA gene sequencing and phylogenetic analysis, showing approximately 99% sequence similarity to closely related Streptomyces taxa.

title: Modern teaching for clinical education involving manual therapy: a 6-pillar approach
creator: Kenneth J Young, Roger Kerry, Cecilia Bergström, Sylwia Borowicz, Lisa J Cary, Chad Cook, James Coughlan, David W Evans, Vasileios Georgopoulos, Nathan Hutting, Edward Lee, Anna Maria Mazzieri, Chris McCarthy, Daniel Moore, Firas Mourad, Colette Ridehalgh, Clarice Tang, Nicholas Tripodi, Steven Voge
description: BackgroundMusculoskeletal (MSK) conditions remain a leading source of global disability, and manual therapy (MT) features in multimodal guideline concordant care; however, teaching in clinical programs that involve MT often remains technique-centric and insufficiently aligned with contemporary, person-centred teaching and practice.

title: hUCMSC-exosomes attenuate acute lung injury by inhibiting ferroptosis in pulmonary microvascular endothelial cells through ribosomal protein RPS11 upregulation
creator: Anyun Ding, Mingou Yan, Yunong Li, Zhongyun Bi, Jingchun Song, Lin Zhao, Renyu Ding
description: BackgroundHuman umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cell-derived exosomes (hUCMSC-Exos) are a promising treatment for acute lung injury (ALI)/acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS), but traditional delivery methods have limitations. Therefore, this study presents a noninvasive therapeutic approach for ALI/ARDS, offering new mechanistic insights and identifying potential therapeutic targets.

title: Doublecortin-like kinase 1 promotes fibroblast activation and fibrotic progression through Smad3 binding in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis
creator: Lee-Yuan Lin, Wun-Hao Cheng, Yu-Chih Wu, Heng-Ching Wen, Hsao-Hsun Hsu, Chia-Hao Liu, Jing-Yun Chen, Wen-Shan Chang, Ying-Jung Wu, Jie-Syuan Wu, Fara Silvia Yuliani, Chueh-Yi Wang, Chien-Huang Lin, Bing-Chang Chen
description: BackgroundIdiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a progressive, fatal lung disease with limited treatment options. Although the results of a gene expression analysis revealed that lung tissues in individuals with IPF contain high levels of doublecortin-like kinase 1 (DCLK1), the role of DCLK1 in fibroblast activation remains unclear.

title: Effects and mechanisms of acupuncture analgesia mediated by afferent nerves in acupoint microenvironments
creator: Zezhi Fan, Baomin Dou, Jiangshan Wang, Yongjian Wu, Simin Du, Jiashan Li, Kaifang Yao, Yanwei Li, Shenjun Wang, Yinan Gong, Yi Guo, Zhifang Xu
description: In the past few decades, the use of acupuncture analgesia in clinical practice has increased worldwide. This is due to its various benefits, including natural alleviation of pain without causing various adverse effects associated with non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAID) and opioids.

title: Intelligent diagnosis and prediction of pregnancy induced hypertension in obstetrics and gynecology teaching by integrating GA
creator: Xiaolan Li, Fen Kang, Xiaojing Li
description: TitleAdvanced Diagnosis and Forecasting of Pregnancy-Induced Hypertension in Obstetrics and Gynecology Education through the Integration of Genetic Algorithms.BackgroundPregnancy-induced hypertension represents a critical issue within the fields of obstetrics and gynecology, where precise diagnosis and forecasting are essential for effective management. The potential for misdiagnosis, often stemming from the inexperience of healthcare professionals, underscores the necessity for an advanced diagnostic system.

title: Histological evaluation of three-dimensional rectangular grid plates in treatment of mandibular fractures: an experimental study
creator: Mohamed Mohsen Elbanna, Ibrahim H. Ahmed, Mohamed Hassan Eid, Mohamed Elsholkamy, Mohamed Said Hamed
description: Aim of the workEvaluate the efficacy of 3D rectangular grid plates in treatment of mandibular fractures in comparison to the more commonly used locking plates.Subjects and methodsThis experimental study was conducted on sixteen mature male Mongrel dogs (ranged from 1-2 years old), weighting about 15-20 kg each.

title: Influence of sound levels, secondary school student characteristics, sound types, and audiovisual interactions on the restorative potential of school environment soundscapes
creator: Leyi Zheng, Huanzhen Ren, Shan Shu, Haoyue Gao, Junxi Fan
description: IntroductionSoundscapes can significantly impact individuals’ physical and mental health. However, the factors influencing the perceived restorativeness of soundscapes among secondary school students remain unclear. This study aims to explore the effects of school environment sound levels, individual characteristics, types of sounds, and audiovisual interactions on the perceived restorativeness soundscape (PRS) of secondary school students.

title: Identification of key genes as potential diagnostic and therapeutic targets for comorbidity of myasthenia gravis and COVID-19
creator: Liyan Huang, Yao Zuo, Hui Yang, Xiaofang He, Lin Zhang
description: IntroductionMyasthenia gravis (MG) is a chronic autoimmune neuromuscular disorder. Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) has a significant impact on the health and quality of life of MG patients and may even trigger the onset of MG in some cases. With the worldwide development of the COVID-19 vaccination, several new-onset MG cases and exacerbations following the COVID-19 vaccines have been acknowledged.

title: IL-1β/IL-6 inflammatory crosstalk drives DNA methylation and histone remodeling associated with cytokine induced senescence in luminal breast cancer
creator: Satyajit Dey Pereira, Kanaka Sai Ram Padam, Padival Shruptha, Aditi Atreya, Manjunath B Joshi, Kapaettu Satyamoorthy
description: BackgroundChronic inflammation exerts paradoxical effects in breast cancer, inducing growth arrest while sustaining tumor progression. However, how autocrine and paracrine inflammatory cytokine induced senescence integrates with tumor-promoting behaviour remains unclear. Here, we identify a reciprocal IL-1β/IL-6 circuit that links inflammatory cues, epigenetic remodeling and cytokine induced senescence in luminal breast cancer cells.

title: Factors influencing the use of epidural labor analgesia: a cross-sectional survey analysis
creator: Wei Li, Na Wu, Shuangqiong Zhou, Weijia Du, Zhendong Xu, Zhiqiang Liu
description: IntroductionThis study aimed to explore the personal and organizational factors influencing the lack of implementation of epidural labor analgesia (ELA).MethodsThis study was conducted at the Shanghai First Maternity and Infant Hospital, School of Medicine, Tongji University, Shanghai, China. A total of 451 women who underwent vaginal delivery without ELA between 8 October 2021 and 30 March 2022, were included.

title: Immunologic and inflammatory consequences of SARS-CoV-2 infection and its implications in renal disease
creator: Hiam Naiditch, Michael R. Betts, H. Benjamin Larman, Moshe Levi, Avi Z. Rosenberg
description: The emergence of the COVID-19 pandemic made it critical to understand the immune and inflammatory responses to the SARS-CoV-2 virus. It became increasingly recognized that the immune response was a key mediator of illness severity and that its mechanisms needed to be better understood.

title: Novel (Q)SAR models for prediction of reversible and time-dependent inhibition of cytochrome P450 enzymes
creator: Sadegh Faramarzi, Arianna Bassan, Kevin P. Cross, Xinning Yang, Glenn J. Myatt, Donna A. Volpe, Lidiya Stavitskaya
description: The 2020 FDA drug-drug interaction (DDI) guidance includes a consideration for metabolites with structural alerts for potential mechanism-based inhibition (MBI) and describes how this information may be used to determine whether in vitro studies need to be conducted to evaluate the inhibitory potential of a metabolite on CYP enzymes.

title: Molecular evidence of Bartonella spp. in wild felids from Brazil
creator: Clara Morato Dias, Daniel Antônio Braga Lee, João Vitor dos Santos Alves da Silva, Laura Berger Nunes, Joares Adenilson May Júnior, Vinícius Baggio-Souza, Felipe Bortolotto Peters, Marina Ochoa Favarini, Ana Paula Neuschrank Albano, Suelen Dias Segui, Silvia Resende Terra, Flávia Pereira Tirelli, Jo
description: Among Felidae, domestic cats play a role as reservoirs for Bartonella henselae, Bartonella clarridgeiae, and Bartonella koehlerae. Despite the well-known relationship between Bartonella spp. and domestic cats, to date, there is still a paucity of reports on Bartonella spp. in wild felids. The aim of this study was to molecularly detect and characterize Bartonella spp.

title: Neuronal autoantibodies associated with poorer neuropsychological and motor outcomes 6 months after stroke: results from the PHYS-STROKE trial
creator: Charlotte Pietrock, Konrad Neumann, Kristin Rentzsch, Harald Prüss, Andreas Meisel, Matthias Endres, Alexander Heinrich Nave
description: IntroductionEmerging evidence suggests a role of neuronal autoantibodies (nAbs) for long-term stroke outcomes. However, data remain limited and many domains unexamined. We present a comprehensive analysis of nAbs and their association with a broad range of outcome measures at multiple timepoints in the six months following moderate stroke.

title: Childhood traumatic experiences and postpartum depression: a mixed methods narrative study
creator: Maria McDonald, Richard Jiang, Sahana Gopi, Jennifer L. Payne, Xin Tong
description: PurposePostpartum depression (PPD) is a significant public health concern with profound effects on the health and well-being of women, children, and families. A growing body of research has identified an association between childhood traumatic experiences and an increased risk of PPD.

title: Correction to: Real‑time qPCR coupled with high‑resolution melting curve analysis for the detection of the internal transcribed spacer 1 of Angiostrongylus costaricensis
creator: Joban Quesada, Paula Alfaro‑Segura, Carlos Mata‑Somarribas, Jackeline Alger, Mazlova Toledo, Jucicleide Ramos de Souza, Javier Mora, Carlos Graeff‑Teixeira, Alberto Solano‑Barquero, Alicia Rojas
description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). noticed that the primer sequence of AcosR1 (5′- GTCTATACGAGCGAACGCATAC-3′) reported in the paper was written in its reverse complement. Therefore, the primer sequence should be corrected to AcosR1 (5′-GTATGCGTTCGCTCGTATAGAC-3′). In line with this correction, the text that reads as below in page 2 (Primer design section) needs to be corrected from:

Accordingly, designed primers AcosF2 (5′-GGTAGTATCGTAACACCCGTT-3′) and AcosR1 (5′- GTCTATACGAGCGAACGCATAC-3′) targeted a 125-bp fragment of the ITS1 loci of A. costaricensis and were used in subsequent analyses.

title: Ferroptosis in cancer: molecular mechanisms, tumour microenvironment, therapeutic resistance, and clinical translation
creator: Ghisaram Dewasi, Sakshi Jain
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Ferroptosis is a distinct form of regulated cell death driven by iron-dependent lipid peroxidation and oxidative membrane damage, and it differs fundamentally from apoptosis, necroptosis, and pyroptosis in its molecular mechanisms and execution pathways. Increasing evidence indicates that ferroptosis plays a pivotal role in cancer biology by regulating tumour initiation, progression, metastasis, therapeutic resistance, and interactions within the tumour microenvironment (TME).

title: Longitudinal assessment of age-related changes in antegonial notch depth in untreated individuals
creator: Mohamad Rustom, Balazs J. Denes, Stavros Kiliaridis, Gregory S. Antonarakis
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionThe role of the antegonial notch as an indicator of growth remains controversial in the literature. This study examined how antegonial notch depth changes during growth and whether craniofacial morphology is associated with its depth.MethodsA longitudinal sample of 250 untreated healthy individuals (42% female) from the American Association of Orthodontists Foundation Craniofacial Growth Legacy Collection was analysed at three time points: ages 7–8, 13–14, and 17–18 years. Antegonial notch depth was measured from standardized lateral cephalograms.

title: Algorithmic bias in clinical resource allocation by a large language model: a cross-sectional in-silico evaluation of 13,608 decisions
creator: Siddharth Gandhi, Michael Balas
description: BackgroundLarge language models (LLMs) hold the potential to transform clinical medicine, but their capacity to amplify societal biases is a significant concern, particularly in the ethically sensitive domain of clinical resource allocation. A critical knowledge gap exists in the quantitative understanding of how these models weigh non-clinical factors in forced-choice ethical dilemmas.

title: Lipid Extract from Ulva ohnoi Algae: Chemical Characterization, Antibacterial Potential, and Cytotoxicity in the Search for New Agents Against MDR Infections
creator: Marisa Castro Jara, Diego Serrasol do Amaral, Leonardo Werner, Eduardo Bastos, Luana de Azevedo Aimi, Nathalia Stark Pedra, Vithor Parada Garcia, Matheus Pereira de Albuquerque, Clarissa Piccinin Frizzo, Milena de Nardin, Wellington da Rocha da Silva, Silvia de Oliveira Hübner, Rodrigo de Almeida Va
description: Antimicrobial resistance is a critical global concern. This study explored the lipid extract (LE) of Ulva ohnoi regarding its chemical composition, antibacterial activity, and cytotoxicity against multidrug-resistant (MDR) microorganisms. The LE was characterized by GC–MS, thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), and differential scanning calorimetry (DSC).

title: Allocentric navigation is computationally universal
creator: Gualtiero Piccinini
description: I present three proofs that idealized neurocomputational architectures capable of navigation guided by allocentric maps with landmark structure can be computationally universal. Navigation may occur online, in the environment, or offline, in the animal’s head. The first proof encodes the counters of a two-counter machine as positions of movable markers on orthogonal axes.

title: Red blood cell transfusion is not associated with lymphocyte subpopulation counts in very low birthweight infants
creator: Niclas Oßmann, Mats Ingmar Fortmann, Kirstin Faust, Julia Pagel, Martin Demmert, Christoph Härtel, Alexander Humberg
description: BackgroundVery low birthweight (VLBW) infants frequently require red blood cell (RBC) transfusions. Transfusions may modulate immune responses, but their impact on immune development remains incompletely understood.Methods120 VLBW infants participating in the prospective “Immune Regulation of the Newborn Study” (IRON study) were analyzed during the first 42 postnatal days with serial immune phenotyping. Infants were stratified by RBC transfusion exposure.

title: The recovery of intestinal barrier function and changes in oral microbiota after radiation therapy injury
creator: Kun Wang, Jingjing Zhang, Yihao Zhang, Junze Xue, He Wang, Xiaojie Tan, Xuelong Jiao, Haitao Jiang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). IntroductionColorectal cancer (CRC) is the third most common malignant tumor, and neoadjuvant chemo-radiotherapy is usually recommended for advanced stage colorectal cancer. Radiotherapy can cause damage to intestinal mucosal barrier, which may be related to perioperative complications. Intestinal microbiota is one of the constituents of the intestinal mucosal biological barrier, and literature reports that patients with CRC have changes in corresponding oral microbiota.

title: Impact of matched samples on domain harmonization in cross-cohort NMR metabolomics
creator: A Ottas, L Goldoni, A Armirotti, S Decherchi
description: IntroductionMachine learning models trained on metabolomics data frequently show reduced performance when applied to independent cohorts because of domain shifts introduced by differences in analytical platforms, sample handling, storage conditions, and metabolite quantification procedures. Robust approaches for harmonizing metabolomics datasets across cohorts are therefore needed to improve model transferability and reproducibility.

title: Relative effectiveness of bivalent COVID-19 vaccine: a systematic review and meta-analysis
creator: Meng-qun Cheng, Rong Li, Zhi-ying Weng, Gao Song
description: ObjectiveThe rapid development of COVID-19 bivalent vaccines (BVs) has encompassed both the original virus strains and the variant strain. However, the effectiveness of BVs is largely unknown. Therefore, we conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of the effectiveness of BVs.MethodsLiterature research was conducted through PubMed, Cochrane Library, Embase, and Web of Science up until November 4, 2023.

title: Sexual and gender identity differences in mental health concerns as a function of social media use and cyberbullying among U.S. youth
creator: Yaxin Pu, Jessica N. Fish
description: As adolescents increasingly engage with social media, concerns have emerged about its potential implications for youth mental health and about disparities in digital experiences by sexual orientation (SO) and gender identity (GI). However, the mechanisms linking social media use (SMU) to mental health and SOGI disparities in digital contexts remain unclear.

title: Being human in non-human systems: why nursing leadership needs Artful Intelligence™ alongside artificial intelligence
creator: Marion Lynch
description: is both a help and a hinderance to our future. AI is described as a new frontier in nursing (Tranka, 2025), and a way of transforming and strengthening nursing (Yakusheva et al., 2025). Although replacing some tasks, AI will not be able to replace nurses (Ball Dunlap et al., 2026). Or will it?

title: Targeted pathway mining reveals novel modified hexapeptides from the demiguisin family
creator: Tanya Decker, Marie Dayras, Lena Schweizer, Sari Rasheed, Franziska Fries, Bulisa Iova, Kasun H Bodawatta, Knud Andreas Jønsson, Rolf Müller, Christine Beemelmanns
description: Following the discovery of the piperazic acid (Piz)-containing hexapeptide demiguisin A from a toxic bird-associated Amycolatopsis strain, we aimed to investigate the structural diversity and bioactive potential of this natural product family. Here, we used the dmg biosynthetic gene cluster from Amycolatopsis sp. PS_44_ISF1 as a pathway mining probe to search for alternative demiguisin A producers.

title: Clinical and imaging characterization of ocular toxoplasmosis in a Central-West Brazilian population
creator: Alexsandra Passarelli Giabardo Marques, Luiza Roschel Zaunrith, Danilo Donizete da Silva, Aparecida Perpétuo Silveira Carvalho, Fernando Henrique Antunes Murata, Rubens Camargo Siqueira, Lucas Gazarini, Edis Belini Júnior, Julie Massayo Maeda Oda, Christiane Maria Ayo, Luiz Carlos de Mattos, Cinara
description: ObjectiveTo evaluate and characterize patients with presumed ocular toxoplasmosis using combined clinical and serological approaches in the municipality of Três Lagoas, Mato Grosso do Sul, Brazil.MethodsThis cross-sectional quantitative study included 85 patients with presumed Toxoplasma gondii related retinochoroiditis referred from the public healthcare system. Participants underwent ophthalmologic examination and serological testing for anti-T. gondii IgG and IgM antibodies.

title: Efficacy of artemether-lumefantrine for uncomplicated plasmodium falciparum malaria treatment in Mozambique: a systematic review and meta-analysis
creator: Abel Nhama, Pedro Aide, David Torres-Fernandez, Rosauro Varo, Arsénio Nhacolo, Quique Bassat
description: BackgroundMalaria remains a significant public health concern in Mozambique. Early diagnosis and the prompt use of effective drugs are essential for malaria control in endemic regions. This review aims to synthesize the existing evidence concerning the efficacy of artemether-lumefantrine (AL) in treating uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Mozambique.

title: Assessing financial toxicity with COST-FACIT: experience from a tertiary care cancer center
creator: Mahir Khan, Elizabeth N. Dewey, Colleen Strzalka, Aarushi Bhan, Heather McKee Hurwitz, Holly Stegh, Renata Hurn, Jacqueline Tomer, Sujata Patil, Kim Bell, Betty K. Hamilton
description: PurposeFinancial toxicity (FT) refers to the direct and indirect consequences of cancer diagnosis and treatment and is a key mediator of quality of life (QOL) and survival in cancer patients. To address this, financial navigation (FN) programs have been implemented in many cancer centers.

title: Valorization of Beetroot and Watermelon by-Products as Functional Ingredients Targeting Nitric Oxide Pathways: Implications for Cardiovascular Health
creator: Thiago Silveira Alvares
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Purpose of the ReviewFood loss and waste represent major challenges for food systems, while fruit and vegetable by-products generated during processing are underused sources of bioactive compounds with potential applications in functional food development. The present review aims to examine the valorization of beetroot and watermelon by-products as functional ingredients associated with nitric oxide (NO) bioavailability, vascular function, and cardiovascular health.

title: Optimal insurance coverage and pricing of outpatient drugs in Iran: a cost- and chronicity-based adaptation of the vertical equity model
creator: Shekoofeh Sadat Momahhed, Atefehsadat Haghighathoseini
description: ObjectiveTo estimate welfare-optimal insurance coverage and drug prices in Iran’s NHI outpatient market, using drug cost and chronicity as proxies for patient financial vulnerability in the absence of income data.SettingA complete administrative census of 88,565 outpatient prescription claims across all NHI fund types and provinces in Iran, fiscal year 2023, covering 7,977 unique pharmaceutical products.

title: Short-term surgical outcomes of robotic versus laparoscopic radical gastrectomy for gastric cancer: a propensity score-matched retrospective cohort study
creator: Dongdong Zhang, Ning Ning, Lin Chen
description: Robotic gastrectomy (RG) is increasingly used for gastric cancer, but real-world comparative data from Chinese institutions during the early phase of robotic program implementation remain limited. We retrospectively identified patients who underwent radical gastrectomy between January 2015 and October 2025. The primary comparison included 54 patients who underwent RG and 162 who underwent Laparoscopic gastrectomy (LG).

title: Link between ultra-processed foods and drinks intake, gut microbiota and inflammation: an exploratory analysis in adult volunteers
creator: Laetitia Lengelé, Manon Autuori, Emilie Bosteels, Audrey M. Neyrinck, Marie Rombaux, Patrice D. Cani, Valérie Dormal, Louise Deldicque, Laure B. Bindels, Nathalie M. Delzenne
description: BackgroundUltra-processed foods and drinks (UPFD) have been acknowledged to promote metabolic disturbances and inflammation. Knowing that both events can be associated with gut microbiota alterations, this observational longitudinal analysis aimed to explore the link between UPFD intake, faecal microbiota composition and activity, and inflammatory biomarkers.MethodsMICROBOOST-1 study included 20 adults for 3 study visits spaced at least 7 days apart.

title: Improved executive function and sleep quality in preteens with high-functioning autism following a structured physical activity program
creator: Miriam Richter, Marie K. Taylor, Sofia Åkerlund, Sofia Backman, Sofia Krili, Björn Axel Johansson, Olof Rask, Christine T. Ekdahl
description: PurposeChildren with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) frequently exhibit atypical cognitive profiles, sensory processing challenges, sleep disturbances, and co-occurring psychiatric and somatic conditions. This exploratory prospective study, with a single-arm pre-post design, investigated the effects of a 10-12 weeks structured physical activity program on psychological symptoms, cognitive function, and sleep in children aged 10–14 years with high-functioning ASD.

title: A novel PolyAr87-based cell transfection protocol for nanobody expression optimized via a targeted design of transfection approach
creator: Lautaro Fidel Bracco, Giovanna Lucia Liguori, Antonella Lanati, Juan Manuel Lázaro-Martínez, Mariela Bollini, Leonardo Poggio, Marina Bok, Lorena Itatí Ibañez, Viviana Parreño
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionTransfection is a fundamental technique for introducing foreign nucleic acids into eukaryotic cells, widely used in biotechnology for recombinant protein expression. Nanobodies fused to enzymes are key reagents in the development of diagnostic tests such as ELISA.

title: The potential of N2-modified cap analogues for precise genetic manipulation through mRNA engineering
creator: Karol Kurpiejewski, Anna Stankiewicz-Drogon, Karolina Piecyk, Eliza Rajkowska, Paulina Skrzypczyk, Jingping Geng, Edward Darzynkiewicz, Renata Grzela, Marzena Jankowska-Anyszka
description: The technology of mRNA-based drugs is currently being intensively developed and implemented. Medical products of this type are already being used as viral vaccines and could potentially find application in a wide range of diseases. The tremendous interest in mRNA is due to the relatively easy production process, which can be quickly adapted to meet societal needs.

title: A genome-wide association study of cognitive impairment in a Chinese cohort of 1,040 individuals
creator: Maggie Haitian Wang, Yexian Zhang, Rui Sun, Fudong Li, Tao Zhang, Xue Gu, Jingzhi Lou, Lirong Cao, Shimin Su, Hong Zheng, Caiqi Liu, Marc Ka Chun Chong, William Ka Kei Wu, Jun Yu, Benny Chung-Ying Zee, Junfen Lin
description: While genetic heritability plays a major role in the development of cognitive impairment, most genetic risk factors are identified from studies of European populations. We conducted a genome-wide association study (GWAS) on cognitive impairment in the Chinese population by sequencing 1,040 matched case-control individuals from a longitudinal cohort of Zhejiang Province, China.

title: Baseline Symptom Collection in Elite Rugby Union Players—Limited Clinical Utility? An Investigation of Assessments Across 5879 men and Women Athletes
creator: James Brown, Ross Tucker, Christina Mack, Gordon Ward Fuller, Lindsay Starling, Martin Raftery, Éanna Cian Falvey
description: In World Rugby's Head Injury Assessment (HIA) protocol, a modified Sports Concussion Assessment Tool (SCAT) is completed during the pre‐season (baseline) and when a player has a suspected head injury. The symptom component of the SCAT, which involves comparing current to baseline symptoms, has been shown to be the most predictive component for concussion diagnosis.

title: Accuracy, readability, and content coverage of AI-generated responses to questions on functional appliances
creator: Serene A Badran, Snigdha Pattanaik, Sarah Jumaah, Abdulrahman Salmeh, Meena Al-Saadi, Taiba Al-Mizban, Nadia Al-Zaidi, Abdullah Hanifa, Mahmoud K AL-Omiri
description: BackgroundPatients increasingly rely on Large Language Models (LLMs) for health information, yet the accuracy and readability of AI-generated dental advice remain variable across different clinical domains and Artificial Intelligence (AI) models. This study therefore aimed to compare the readability, accuracy, and comprehensiveness of responses generated by four leading AI models (ChatGPT-4o Mini, ChatGPT-5, Google Gemini 2.

title: Endothelial Matrin‐3 Limits Cellular Senescence and Lipid Dysregulation to Protect Against Murine Atherosclerosis
creator: Xiao Cheng, Fatema Yeasmin Tanni, Rachelle Nelson Zoni, Elham Abdollahi, Eli Childs, Xinghui Sun
description: Matrin‐3 is a DNA‐ and RNA‐binding protein implicated in cardiovascular development. However, the role of endothelial Matrin‐3 in atherosclerosis has not been previously studied. Here, we found that Matrin‐3 silencing induces endothelial senescence, characterized by reduced cell proliferation, increased senescence‐associated β‐galactosidase activity, and impaired mitochondrial function in vitro.

title: Designing an antimicrobial stewardship curriculum for nurses to strengthen knowledge and clinical practice
creator: Fatima Aldawood, Nour Shamas, Majid Alshamrani
description: BackgroundAntimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a public health threat. Antimicrobial stewardship (AMS) provides a promising solution to mitigate AMR risk. Despite the recognition of AMS interventions, educational curricula tailored to nurses are scarce. This study aimed to develop an evidence-based nursing AMS curriculum.

title: Assessing diagnostic performance of multimodal LLMs and a custom convolutional neural network in tooth-level caries detection and localization
creator: Aamna Khalid, Ayesha Nooruddin, Nighat Naved, Syed Muhammad Faizan Ahmed, Niha Adnan, Sarang Suresh, Abhishek Lal, Fahad Umer
description: BackgroundArtificial Intelligence is reshaping dental diagnostics through automated interpretation of images. While Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) demonstrate high accuracy via domain-specific training, multimodal Large Language Models (LLMs) such as ChatGPT-4o and Gemini 2.5 Flash have recently acquired visual-reasoning capabilities without task-specific fine-tuning.

title: Chemical mixtures and birth weight: comparison of multipollutant models in the Maternal-Infant Research on Environmental Chemicals (MIREC) study
creator: Susan MacPherson, Jillian Ashley-Martin, Joseph M. Braun, Youssef Oulhote, Tye E. Arbuckle
description: Fetal growth is a critical health outcome influenced by prenatal exposure to environmental chemicals, particularly endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs). Studies have shown that pregnant women are simultaneously exposed to multiple chemicals, illustrating the need for methods that can examine the health effects of cumulative exposures.

title: Online forecasting for financial time series
creator: Nikolas Michael, Mihai Cucuringu, Sam Howison
description: We introduce OFTER (online forecasting via temporal embedding regression), a time series forecasting pipeline tailored for financial problems centered on mid-sized multivariate time series. OFTER utilizes the non-parametric models of k-nearest neighbors and generalized regression neural networks, integrated with a dimensionality reduction component.

title: Combined effects of heat and rhamnolipids against Listeria monocytogenes: Influence of water activity and pH
creator: Gustavo Vasconcelos Gomes, Marcia Nitschke
description: Foodborne diseases remain a major public health concern, with Listeria monocytogenes being one of the most significant foodborne pathogens due to its high mortality rate and persistence in food-processing environments. This study evaluated the combined effects of heat, pH, and water activity on the antimicrobial activity of rhamnolipids (RL) against L. monocytogenes within the framework of hurdle technology.

title: A SHAP-based machine learning approach to decoding the relationship between running posture features and tibial load in novice runners with MTSS: towards accurate and intelligent rehabilitation strategies
creator: Ting Fan, Xiaomin Wu, Zeyi Zhang, Youping Sun
description: BackgroundThis study systematically investigates the relationship between running posture and tibial load in novice runners using machine learning methods from the field of artificial intelligence. The aim is to provide scientific evidence for the precise prevention and personalized rehabilitation of Medial Tibial Stress Syndrome (MTSS).MethodsA total of 174 novice runners diagnosed with MTSS were included in the study.

title: MR arthrographic examination of the association with glenohumeral instability of posterior labroligamentous i̇nsertion types and posterior labrum anatomical variants
creator: Rodi Ertogrul, Hayri Ogul, Yusuf Yahsi, Zakir Sakci, Yusuf Sulek, Mecit Kantarci
description: ObjectivesThe objective of this study is to evaluate the relationship between posterior labroligamentous morphological variants and abnormal position of the humeral head in the glenoid cavity using MR arthrography (MRA). Additionally, the study seeks to investigate whether these variations act as biomechanical risk factors for subclinical instability.

title: Diabetes Mellitus Is Associated With Increased Risk for Subsequent Hip Arthroscopy After Index Hip Arthroscopy
creator: Nicholas J. Morriss, Justin Harrington, Jacob Waldron, Brian Giordano
description: PurposeTo determine whether diabetes mellitus is associated with higher systemic and hip‐specific complications and to evaluate reoperation rates after hip arthroscopy.MethodsUsing the TriNetX Research Network and Current Procedural Terminology and International Classification of Diseases codes, we identified diabetic and nondiabetic patients aged 12 to 65 years who underwent hip arthroscopy between 2005 and 2025.

title: Double‐Bundle Anterior Cruciate Ligament Reconstruction Provides Superior Short‐to‐Midterm Rotational Stability But Not Clinically Important Functional Gains Over Single‐Bundle: A Systematic Review and Meta‐analysis
creator: Manuel Alberto Gutierrez‐Moreno, Luis Eduardo Arámbula‐Torres, Ramon Alonso Prieto‐Baeza, Carlos Leal‐Contreras, Cristina Alejandra Fuentes‐Flores, Edmundo Berumen‐Nafarrate
description: PurposeTo compare the biomechanical and functional outcomes between single‐bundle and double‐bundle (DB) anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction techniques using the most current evidence, stratified by follow‐up duration.MethodsPubMed, Embase, and Cochrane databases were searched from 2013 to September 2025 for randomized controlled trials comparing single‐bundle versus DB anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction with a minimum follow‐up of 24 months.

title: Personalized medicine in triple-negative breast cancer: combining neoantigen vaccination and genomic profiling in a patient undergoing neoadjuvant chemotherapy
creator: Laura Camila Martinez-Enriquez, David A. Bernal-Estévez, Daniel Alzate, Diego Amaya, Óscar Iván Reyes-Cortés, Carlos A. Parra-López
description: IntroductionTriple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is an aggressive subtype of breast cancer with the poorest prognosis among all breast cancer subtypes. The limited effectiveness of first-line treatments, such as systemic neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC) and surgery, underscores the urgent need for alternative therapeutic strategies.

title: Decompression Sickness Myelopathy: Case Report and Acute Management Review for the Neurologist
creator: Thomas J. Pisano, Brendan Zotter, David S. Lambert, Sashank Prasad
description: Decompression sickness (DCS) is an uncommon but important cause of acute myelopathy that neurologists should recognize in the emergency setting. We report a 43-year-old experienced technical diver who developed acute sensory loss with a thoracic sensory level, gait dysfunction, upper motor neuron signs, and urinary retention after rapid ascent from approximately 90 feet below sea level.

title: The role of nitrogen dioxide in the prevalence of adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases in China: a national multi-pollutant geospatial analysis
creator: Guanmou Li, Shuying Chen, Yu Liu, Aishan Arzuguli, Jiawei Zhang, Shaobin Qiu, Rongjun Zou
description: IntroductionCardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases (CCVDs) pose a severe global health threat, particularly among middle-aged and elderly populations. Ambient air pollution is a well-recognized environmental risk factor for CCVDs, yet existing studies often focus on single pollutants or outcomes, lacking comprehensive evaluations.

title: Congenital hyperinsulinism as part of a multisystem disease caused by a compound heterozygous variant in the YARS1 gene
creator: Anna Bolmasova, Anna Zaretskaia, Sofia Mikhalina, Anna Postrigan, Anna Kolodkina, Valentina Peterkova
description: Tyrosyl-transfer RNA (tRNA) synthetase, encoded by YARS1, is essential for protein synthesis, catalyzing the attachment of tyrosine to its cognate tRNA during translation. Pathogenic biallelic YARS1 variants cause infantile-onset multisystem neurological, endocrine, and pancreatic disease type 2 (IMNEPD2; OMIM #619418), an orphan disorder. Hypoglycemia in IMNEPD2 remains poorly characterized, with few reported cases.

title: Membrane Topology and Oligomerization of Peptaibols by Solid‐State NMR Spectroscopy
creator: Burkhard Bechinger, Evgeniy S. Salnikov
description: Here, we review solid‐state NMR investigations of a variety of peptaibols in phospholipid bilayer environments. The peptides were prepared using different approaches such as microbial expression, solid‐phase peptide synthesis or the chemical synthesis in solution and a modular fragment condensation approach.

title: Psychometric properties of the Japanese version of the standardised assessment of personality abbreviated scale
creator: Issaku Kawashima, Tomoko Hinuma, Masatoshi Nagata, Akio Yoneyama, Masaru Honjo, Hiroaki Kumano, Saori C. Tanaka
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). This study was undertaken to translate the Standardised Assessment of Personality – Abbreviated Scale (SAPAS) into Japanese and to evaluate its validity and reliability. SAPAS is one of the most rapid tools for assessing personality disorder (PD) and has excellent sensitivity and good specificity, whereas other PD assessment tools require such a significant investment of time that they are infeasible for large surveys or routine clinical practice.

title: Male histone deacetylase 6 (HDAC6) knockout mice have enhanced ventilatory responses to hypoxic challenge
creator: Paulina M. Getsy, Gregory A. Coffee, Thomas J. Kelley, Stephen J. Lewis
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Histone deacetylase 6 (HDAC6) is a class II histone deacetylase that is predominantly localized in the cytoplasm of cells. HDAC6 associates with microtubules and regulates acetylation of tubulin and other proteins. The possibility that HDAC6 participates in hypoxic signaling is supported by evidence that 1) hypoxic gas challenges cause microtubule depolymerization, 2) expression of hypoxia inducible factor alpha (HIF-1α) is regulated by microtubule alterations in response to hypoxia, and 3) inhibition of HDAC6 prevents HIF-1α expression and protects tissue from hypoxic/ischemic insults.

title: Role of glutathione disulfide reductase in colorectal cancer: a tumor suppressor
creator: Lilin Lin, Zexiu Chen, Cong-yu Zhang, Jingnian Fang
description: BackgroundGlutathione-disulfide reductase (GSR) was responsible for maintaining the supply of reduced glutathione, and was found to be abnormally expressed in a variety of cancers. There was an incomplete understanding regarding the roles of GSR in colorectal cancer (CRC) today.MethodsWe used colorectal cancer tissues and cell lines to detect the function of GSR in CRC.

title: Bibliometric mapping of research trends and publication growth in cancer sonodynamic therapy from 2001 to 2025
creator: Xiaoting Wang, Bo Zhang, Ke Yang, Peitong Deng
description: BackgroundSonodynamic therapy (SDT) is increasingly investigated for cancer treatment. This study aimed to characterize the knowledge structure, thematic evolution, and publication trajectory of cancer SDT research.MethodsEnglish-language articles and reviews published from January 1, 2001, to December 31, 2025, were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection (WoSCC) on January 16, 2026. CiteSpace 6.4.R1 and VOSviewer 1.6.

title: Synthetic Notch CD123 and CLL1 chimeric antigen receptor T-cells (CAR-T) target acute myeloid leukemia and reduce off-tumor effects associated with CLL1 CAR-T cells
creator: Rui Zhang, Na Chen, Mengnan Li, Qingxi Liu, Mingfeng Zhao
description: Chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (CAR-T) therapy targeting the C-type lectin-like molecule-1 (CLL1) antigen has emerged as a promising therapeutic approach for acute myeloid leukemia (AML). However, its clinical translation is hindered by on-target, off-tumor toxicity, particularly severe neutropenia caused by CLL1 expression on normal neutrophils.

title: Next-generation digital polymerase chain reaction assay for BCR::ABL1 in chronic myeloid leukemia: comprehensive validation for standardized measurable residual disease detection
creator: Yong-Hwi Kim, Min-Sik Jang, Shin-Hyun Kim, In-Young Roh, Bong-Suk Kim, Kyung-Mi Kee, Soo-Hyun Kim, Dong-Wook Kim, Jae-Hoon Kim
description: PurposeThe sensitivity of real-time quantitative reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) for detecting measurable residual disease (MRD) in patients with chronic myeloid leukemia (CML) who have achieved a deep molecular response is limited. We validated a digital PCR (dPCR) assay (LQ Check BCR::ABL1 Major %IS Kit) for MRD quantification.

title: Valuable interaction with cognitive remediation and optimal antipsychotics for recovery in schizophrenia (VICTORY-S): study protocol for an interventional, open-label, randomized comparison of combined treatment with cognitive remediation and lurasidone or paliperidone
creator: Ryotaro Kubota, Satoru Ikezawa, Hideki Oi, Mari S Oba, Shoki Izumi, Ryoko Tsuno, Leona Adachi, Mako Miwa, Shunji Toya, Yohei Nishizato, Daisuke Haga, Tatsuro Iwane, Kazuyuki Nakagome
description: BackgroundCognitive impairment, a core feature of schizophrenia, is associated with poor outcomes. Pharmacotherapy and psychosocial treatment, when used alone, have inadequate effect sizes for cognitive impairment, leading to recent interest in combination interventions. A previous study examined the additive effect of cognitive remediation on lurasidone in patients with schizophrenia, which was negative.

title: Modulator therapy: rates and stages of respiratory bacteriome restoration in cystic fibrosis patients chronically infected with Pseudomonadota
creator: Olga L. Voronina, Natalia N. Ryzhova, Marina S. Kunda, Ekaterina I. Ermolova, Elena L. Amelina, Rezuan U. Kagazezhev, Alexander L. Gintsburg
description: BackgroundChronic lung infection caused by Pseudomonadota (PCH) in patients with cystic fibrosis (pwCF) is difficult to eradicate. CFTR modulators have a potential role in the prevention of airway infections, but their ability to eradicate chronic infection remains to be investigated.

title: Leadership Education for Doctors—A Scoping Review
creator: Naja Vaaben, Alberte Nielsen, Constance Thyra Giertz Christiansen, Nikoline Svensson, Peter Dieckmann, Ann Merete Møller
description: IntroductionClinical leadership is essential for patient safety and effective healthcare delivery. While leadership training is increasingly integrated into medical education, there is no consensus on how to define, teach, or evaluate these skills. This scoping review aimed to map the existing literature on medical clinical leadership training and identify gaps.

title: Modelling the multidimensional structure of workplace violence against emergency medical technicians and mitigation strategies in Ghana: a confirmatory factor analysis
creator: Yenube Clement Kunkuaboor, Azudaa R Atandigre, Jones Opoku-Ware, Godwin Armstrong Duku, Miilon Sommik Duut, Isaac Adjei Mensah, Adusei Bofa
