description: BackgroundEmergency Medical Technicians (EMTs) are routinely exposed to workplace violence, yet empirical evidence from low- and middle-income countries remains limited. This study examined the multidimensional structure of workplace violence against EMTs in Ghana, evaluated perceived mitigation strategies using a confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) approach and explored EMTs’ perceptions of workplace violence mitigation strategies.

title: The stories of the ageing population in Luton, United Kingdom on their experience of periodontal diseases healthcare
creator: Karuna Preethi Velpula, Enemona Jacob
description: BackgroundOral health is an important part of general wellbeing, but in the United Kingdom there are substantive inequalities, especially based on ethnic minority and ageing. There is a poor quality of life, a lack of awareness and preventive measures, and periodontal disease contributes to loss of teeth, poor nutrition, and poor quality of life.

title: Prevalence of Hepatitis C Infection and Treatment Initiation Following Dried Blood Spot Testing in New South Wales, Australia
creator: Annabelle Stevens, Anna Conway, Nigel Carrington, Evan B. Cunningham, Alison D. Marshall, Janaki Amin, Phillip Read, Tracey Brown, Rick Varma, Bianca Prain, Philip Cunningham, Gregory J. Dore, Jason Grebely
description: Background and AimsTo achieve hepatitis C (HCV) elimination by 2030, testing and treatment must reach people most at risk. Dried blood spot (DBS) testing offers an alternative to venepuncture, suitable for community and prison settings. This study evaluated HCV infection prevalence and treatment initiation among people receiving DBS testing in New South Wales (NSW), Australia.

title: New biomarker in the early diagnosis of breast cancer: adiponectin, asprosin, adropin, and resistin
creator: Ömer Çelik, Halit Özgül, Sibel Kulaksızoğlu, Osman Zekai Öner, Barış Rafet Karakaş, Remzi Can Çakır, Zinet Asuman Arslan Onuk, Uğur Bilge
description: BackgroundEarly diagnosis of breast cancer remains difficult despite advances in imaging because false-positive and false-negative findings still occur. Circulating biomarkers reflecting metabolic and inflammatory changes may provide complementary information. Adiponectin, adropin, asprosin, and resistin have been suggested as candidates, yet their comparative diagnostic performance in breast cancer has not been adequately defined.

title: Methyltransferase RsmB chaperones E. coli ribosome assembly by orchestrating the recruitment of ribosomal proteins
creator: Qilan Wei, Sarah A. Woodson
description: Ribosomal RNA modification enzymes increase cellular fitness, but it’s little known whether this benefit arises from rRNA modification or a chaperone function of the modification enzyme. Here, we show that E. coli methyltransferase RsmB chaperones the initial recruitment of ribosomal proteins to the 16S 3′ domain rRNA, a key step in assembly of the 30S subunit.

title: Vascular endothelial growth factor A: friend or foe in the pathogenesis of HIV and SARS-CoV-2 infections?
creator: Mieke A. van der Mescht, Helen C. Steel, Ronald Anderson, Theresa M. Rossouw
description: This review article discusses the role of vascular endothelial growth factor A (VEGF-A) in the pathogenesis of SARS-CoV-2 and HIV infection, both conditions being renowned for their impact on the vascular endothelium. The processes involved in vascular homeostasis and angiogenesis are reviewed briefly before exploring the interplay between hypoxia, VEGF-A, neuropilin-1 (NRP-1), and inflammatory pathways.

title: (Un)aware of change? Objective and subjective reactivity to the sensor‐based measurement of physical activity and sedentary behaviour
creator: Alea Ruf, Judith R. Gruber, Ulrich W. Ebner‐Priemer, Andreas Reif, Laura M. König, Silke Matura
description: ObjectivesDespite being the gold standard for assessing physical activity (PA) under free‐living conditions, accelerometer‐based assessments are prone to measurement reactivity, that is, changes in people's cognitions, emotions or behaviour due to being measured. Little is known about whether participants are aware of these changes.

title: Data linkage studies on veteran suicidality: a scoping review of the field, knowledge gaps and evidence appraisal
creator: Nicolas Rivero Weidemüller, Shannon Dias, Emilia Janca, Luke T. Bayliss, Ed Heffernan, Carla Meurk
description: Background and aimsSuicidality among veterans is a serious issue that impacts veterans, their families, friends, and communities. Using data linkage to examine suicidality among veterans remains an emerging area. This review examines the application of data linkage to questions on suicidality among veterans from within the Five Eyes alliance to generate learnings that can be applied to the Australian context.

title: Longitudinal evaluation of cervical length for the prediction of mid-trimester cervical length in low-risk population
creator: Bilge Cetinkaya Demir, Murat Deniz Celenk, Gokhan Ocakoglu
description: BackgroundPreterm birth (PTB) remains a leading cause of perinatal mortality and long-term morbidity. While screening strategies primarily target high-risk populations, a substantial proportion of PTBs occur in low-risk women. Mid-trimester cervical length (CL) assessment may be implemented too late for effective prevention. Earlier evaluation in the first trimester may improve risk stratification.

title: MFN2-associated astrocyte dysfunction contributes to neuronal hyperexcitability and depressive-like behaviors
creator: Feng-xia Ma, Min Wang, Shuo-yan Fang, Xiao-xin Wang, Shen-han Xu, Xin-xin Zhao, Yu-xiao Liu, Cong Wang, Chen Qiao, Qiu-ling Wang, Lei Cao
description: Astrocyte pathology is increasingly recognized as a key factor in the pathogenesis of major depressive disorder (MDD), where disrupted glutamate clearance and impaired neuron-glia interactions contribute to synaptic dysfunction. However, the molecular mechanisms leading to astrocyte loss remain largely undefined.

title: Evaluation of dose-response relationships between smoking tobacco, alcohol consumption and oral cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis
creator: G. Aswathi, Andre Carvalho, Sathishrajaa Palaniraja, M. Shivacharan, Bhukya Nom Kumar Naik, Saman Warnakulasuriya, Kishore Chaudhry, Muralidhar Kulkarni, Ranjitha S. Shetty, Shirley Lewis, Vijay Shree Dhyani, Suzanne Tanya Nethan, Ravivarman Lakshmanasamy, Vasudeva Guddattu, K. Devaraja
description: BackgroundTobacco smoking and alcohol consumption are established independent risk factors for oral carcinogenesis, yet the quantitative dose-response relationships for key exposure variables remain unclear.MethodsA systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis (PROSPERO registration number: CRD42024531040) was conducted following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines.

title: Identification and validation of CNTNAP2/PAX1 hypermethylation as an epigenetic biomarker panel for detection of cervical cancer and precancerous lesions in hrHPV-positive women
creator: Yuying He, Haiyan Yang, Chuang Zhang, Ruiwei Jiang, Kai Kang, Yuxue Wang, Dixian Luo, Dan Xiong
description: BackgroundCervical cancer remains a significant global health burden, and effective triage strategies are urgently needed for high-risk human papillomavirus (hrHPV)-positive women in screening programs. This study aimed to identify and validate DNA methylation markers for detecting cervical precancerous lesions in hrHPV-positive women.

title: Thickness‐Gradient Liquid Metal Connectors for Seamless Electrophysiological Sensors
creator: Jinyoung Kim, Jaejun Lee, Christopher E Tabor, Vladimir V Tsukruk
description: High‐fidelity electrophysiological monitoring requires wearable bioelectronic devices with mechanical properties closely matched to human skin. However, current approaches focus primarily on electrode design and performance, while overlooking mechanical compliance and interfacial continuity with complex and dynamic human skin. Mechanical mismatches across electrodes, connectors, and interconnects often lead to interfacial noise, motion artifacts, and electrical instability.

title: Adrenal hormones in the maintenance of glucose homeostasis during prolonged fasting in male glucagon‐deficient mice
creator: Sayumi Kanie, Koki Nishida, Yusuke Seino, Shihomi Hidaka, Shinji Ueno, Hiroaki Sumioki, Eisuke Tomatsu, Takuya Haraguchi, Naoya Murao, Haruki Fujisawa, Takeshi Takayanagi, Yoshihisa Sugimura, Yoshitaka Hayashi, Atsushi Suzuki
description: Aims/IntroductionGlucagon is a key regulator of fasting glucose homeostasis, but the contribution of adrenal hormones during prolonged fasting remains unclear. We investigated the complementary roles of glucagon and adrenal hormones in hepatic glucose metabolism during prolonged fasting.Materials and MethodsMale proglucagon‐deficient (GCGKO) mice and adrenalectomized (ADX) mice were studied after a 36‐h fast.

title: Benefit-risk assessment of the use of toxic botanical drugs in superiority field: a case study on Aconitum carmichaeli Debx
creator: Xiaomeng Zhang, Congcong Qu, Bing Zhang, Jintao Lyv, Zhijian Lin, Xinlong Liu
description: ObjectiveThe study aimed to establish a benefit-risk assessment (BRA) model utilizing multi-criteria decision analysis (MCDA), in order to evaluate the benefit-risk relationship of decoctions containing Aconitum carmichaeli Debx. (Fuzi) in the treatment of rheumatoid arthritis (RA), laying the foundation for the decision-making on the use of clinical toxic botanical drugs and facilitating their rational application.

title: Review of the effect of atrazine on the HPG axes and steroidogenic pathways in males: relevance for testicular and prostate cancer
creator: Ralph L. Cooper, James W. Simpkins, Charles Breckenridge
description: Subacute, subchronic, and chronic rodent studies on atrazine were evaluated to determine the no observed adverse effect levels (NOAEL) for male reproductive toxicity and carcinogenicity. In vitro studies were also evaluated for the effect of atrazine on molecular pathways related to male reproductive function and potential mechanisms for cancer. Gestational exposure to high doses of atrazine delayed male development post-partum.

title: A meta-analytic review of Mandarin tone perception: tone height and tone contour, prosodic background, and L2 experience
creator: Xin Cui, Hong Zhao
description: This meta-analysis synthesizes data from 18 empirical studies to examine how tonal features of height and contour, native prosodic background, and second language (L2) experience affect the perception of Mandarin lexical tones. Results revealed overall large effect sizes, indicating that variability in tone perception is statistically robust and theoretically significant.

title: Clinician perspectives on the feasibility of a pain management protocol in kidney transplant
creator: Cassandra B Iroz, Julie K Johnson, Vinayak S Rohan
description: BackgroundOpioids are often prescribed to treat pain after kidney transplant (KT) but pose significant risks to patients as well as the risk of diversion of unused opioids into the community. While there is growing interest, only 18% of KT programs in the United States have a pain management protocol.

title: A caprine mammary infection model for highly pathogenic avian influenza H5N1
creator: Lauren Aubrey, Nathalie Berube, Natalia Pessoa, Cynthia Swan, M. Afzal Javed, Claire Bertens, Erin Scruten, Rob Stevens, Carla Norleen, Kyla Cutts, Yanyun Huang, Yohannes Berhane, Bryce Warner, Antonio Facciuolo, Yan Zhou
description: Highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 virus spillover into dairy cows represents the emergence of a mammalian host capable of sustaining a panzootic and creates a transmission pathway to humans. HPAI research involving dairy cows is constrained by the space requirements needed to house large animals in high biocontainment.

title: Freezing stress response of wild and cultivated chickpeas
creator: Shweta Kalve, Megan Alexandra House, Bunyamin Tar’an
description: Chickpea is an economically and nutritionally important grain legume globally, however, cold stress has adverse effects on its growth. In cold countries, like Canada where the growing season is short, having cold stress-tolerant varieties is crucial. Crop wild relatives of chickpea, especially Cicer reticulatum, can survive in suboptimal environments and are an important resource for crop improvement.

title: Diagnostic ultrasound enhances, then reduces, exogenously induced brain activity of mice
creator: Henry Tan, Devon J. Griggs, Lucas Chen, Kahte Adele Culevski, Kathryn Floerchinger, Alissa Phutirat, Gabe Koh, Nels Schimek, Pierre D. Mourad
description: Transcranially delivered diagnostic ultrasound (tDUS) applied to the human brain can modulate those brains such that they became more receptive to external stimulation relative to sham ultrasound exposure. Here, we sought to directly measure the effect of tDUS on mouse brain activity subjected to an external stimulation—a blinking light.

title: Policy paper: “Nudging for better nutrition: behavioral strategies to address childhood obesity in Arab communities” policy recommendations for action
creator: Duaa Mohamed Suliman, Immanuel Azaad Moonesar, Leena A. A. Mohammed
description: IntroductionChildhood obesity is a growing public health crisis globally, particularly in Arab countries, due to changing dietary habits, sedentary lifestyles, and cultural factors. Prevention efforts focus on behavioral change strategies that promote healthy eating, physical activity, and sleep to balance energy intake and expenditure. However, the effectiveness of interventions remains uncertain, prompting ongoing research.

title: Molecular and developmental insights into proprioceptive identity in the mesencephalic trigeminal nucleus neurons
creator: Pa Reum Lee, Seog Bae Oh
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The mesencephalic trigeminal nucleus (MTN) contains trigeminal proprioceptive neurons, a unique class of primary sensory neurons with centrally located cell bodies and a developmental origin distinct from that of peripheral ganglion-derived spinal proprioceptors. MTN neurons have long been recognized for their morphological heterogeneity, but their functions were traditionally viewed as confined to the jaw jerk reflex and oromotor control, reflecting their predominant innervation of jaw-closing muscles.

title: Exploring the role of trained surgical care nurses in cricothyrotomy and other emergency procedures: a systematic review and meta-analysis
creator: Chao Zhang, Feng Jiang, Junrong Li, Haiyan Shen, Huiping Wang, Yanfen Huang
description: BackgroundThere is a severe shortage of healthcare professionals, emphasized in a stark manner by the recent COVID-19 pandemic, where the mortality rate was primarily a consequence of medical professionals lacking the technical know-how for conducting specialized procedures. Therefore, this systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the success rates of nurse-performed emergency surgeries, focusing on trauma care (e.g.

title: Prognostic predictors in HIV-negative neurosyphilis: a retrospective cohort study with prospective follow-up
creator: Wei-Yang Cheng, Jian-Feng Qu, Xiao-Wen Liu, Ming-Zi Wang, Run-Xiong Li, Xue-Xin Chen, Yang-Kun Chen
description: BackgroundThe prognosis and its predictors in human immunodeficiency virus (HIV)-negative neurosyphilis remain poorly characterized.ObjectiveTo identify clinical, laboratory, and neuroimaging predictors of poor long-term outcomes of HIV-Negative Neurosyphilis.MethodsWe conducted a retrospective cohort study with prospective follow-up in 128 newly diagnosed HIV-negative neurosyphilis patients at a single tertiary center.

title: Dual Nd isotopic archives in fossil teeth reveal bottom-current control of rare-earth element enrichment in deep-sea sediments
creator: Zongqi Zou, Shengping Qian, Qiong Wu, Xuran Liang, Fan Yang, Le Zhang, Pengli He, Yi-Gang Xu
description: The global emergence of deep-sea sediments enriched in rare-earth elements and yttrium (REY) after the Late Eocene cooling coincides spatiotemporally with Antarctic bottom water (AABW) expansion, yet the underlying mechanism remains unresolved. Here, we present in situ elemental and neodymium isotopic analyses of apatites extracted from Oligocene-Miocene sediments along the North Pacific AABW pathway.

title: Neighborhood-level sleep health and childhood opportunities
creator: Suzanne Gorovoy, Sydney Phan, Tommy K. Begay, Dora Valencia, Lauren Hale, Rebecca Robbins, William D. S. Killgore, Ariel A. Williamson, Michael Grandner
description: ObjectivesRegional sleep differences may reflect other important indicators of health and well-being. Examining sleep health at the regional level can help inform policies to improve population health. We examined the relationship between neighborhood-level adult sleep health (modeled in this study via adult sleep duration) and other health metrics and multiple indicators of child-relevant opportunity.

title: Molecular Prevalence and Antimicrobial Resistance Patterns of Methicillin‐Resistant Staphylococcus aureus in Buffaloes from Bangladesh
creator: Piash Kumer Ghosh, Masud Ali, Hemayet Hossain, Md Monjur‐e‐Alahi Tuha, Milton Roy, Tufayel Ahmed, Asikur Rahman, Md Shahidur Rahman Chowdhury, Md Masudur Rahman, Md Bashir Uddin, Md Mahfujur Rahman, Md Mukter Hossain
description: BackgroundMethicillin‐resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) is an emerging zoonotic pathogen in livestock and poses a potential public health threat.ObjectiveThis cross‐sectional study investigated the prevalence, antimicrobial resistance profiles and molecular characteristics of S. aureus and MRSA isolated from buffalo nasal swabs in the Sylhet and Noakhali districts of Bangladesh.

title: Jejunal and pancreatic transcriptomic adaptations underpin enhanced performance in broilers fed sugarcane bagasse-supplemented diets
creator: Collins Amponsah Asiamah, Sarbast K. Kheravii, Sosthene Musigwa, Shu-Biao Wu, Sara de las Heras-Saldana
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundThis study investigated the transcriptomic changes in the jejunum and pancreas of broiler chickens fed a diet supplemented with sugarcane bagasse (SB) to elucidate the physiological response of broilers to insoluble dietary fiber.ResultsA total of 168 0-day-old Ross 308 male broiler chicks were randomly allocated to two dietary treatments: a control diet or a diet supplemented with 2% SB, each consisting of six replicate pens (14 broilers/pen).

title: Diagnostic efficacy and necessity of 18F-FDG PET/CT in fever of unknown origin: insights from a retrospective cohort study
creator: Xiaoman Yu, Shuang Wang, Na Du, Hongguang Zhao, Haiying Chen
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundDespite advancements in medical examination equipment and techniques, fever of unknown origin (FUO) remains challenging in internal medicine.PurposeThis study evaluates the diagnostic efficacy and necessity of 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography (18F-FDG PET/CT) in patients with FUO.MethodsWe retrospectively analyzed the results of 18F-FDG PET/CT in a cohort of 284 patients with FUO admitted to the Department of Infection at the First Hospital of Jilin University between January 2018 and March 2024.

title: Realignment of ferroelectric nematic by photoinduced electric field
creator: Sathyanarayana Paladugu, Oleksandr Kurochkin, Ruslan Kravchuk, Mykola Kravets, Volodymyr Sashuk, Bijaya Basnet, Vassili G. Nazarenko, Sergij V. Shiyanovskii, Oleg D. Lavrentovich
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Liquid crystal displays (LCDs) use thin pixels of a paraelectric nematic, confined between two glass plates with transparent indium tin oxide (ITO) electrodes. A voltage applied to the electrodes realigns the molecules, changing optical appearance of the pixel. Here, we demonstrate that a similar molecular realignment can be triggered by a low-power light irradiation when the paraelectric nematic in the cell with ITO electrodes is replaced with a ferroelectric nematic (NF).

title: Staphylococcus aureus carriage among hemodialysis outpatients: risk factors, antimicrobial resistance, and molecular characterization
creator: Agnė Kirkliauskienė, Monika Vitkauskaitė, Karolina Vankevičienė, Maksim Bratchikov, Marius Miglinas, Laurynas Rimševičius
description: BackgroundStaphylococcus aureus (S. aureus) carriage is prevalent among hemodialysis outpatients and may be associated with frequent healthcare contact and vascular access use. The aim of the study was to determine the prevalence of S. aureus carriage, factors associated with carriage, antimicrobial resistance patterns, and selected resistance and virulence genes among hemodialysis outpatients.MethodsA cross-sectional observational study was conducted in 2018–2021.

title: Co-opted CHIP E3 Ub-ligase provides protein quality control by regulating molecular properties of condensates formed by a positive-strand RNA virus
creator: Wenwu Lin, Yuyan Liu, Peter D. Nagy
description: Positive-strand RNA viruses are important pathogens that built viral replication organelles (VROs) via exploiting co-opted host proteins and intracellular membranes in infected cells. Tomato bushy stunt virus (TBSV) membranous VROs are associated with dynamic virus-induced replication (vir)–condensate substructures driven by TBSV p33 replication protein. We targeted micropeptide “killswitch” to VROs to enhance p33 self-association and remodel vir-condensates.

title: Whole-genome sequencing revealed the genomic origin of Solanum demissum Lindl., a Mexican hexaploid wild potato species
creator: Awie J Hosaka, Kazuyoshi Hosaka
description: BackgroundSolanum demissum Lindl. (2n = 6x = 72) is the most popular wild species in potato breeding because of its resistance to late blight, caused by Phytophthora infestans (Mont.) de Bary. Regular meiosis with 36 bivalents indicates that S. demissum has three distinct genomes, but their origin remains unknown.ResultsWe constructed a chromosome-scale assembly of S.

title: Hyperinvasive and quinolone-resistant meningococci cc4821 achieved immune evasion through capsule switching
creator: Jiebin Huang, Panpan Lv, Yue Jiang, Youxing Shao, Mei Zeng, Qinglan Guo, Mingliang Chen
description: BackgroundNeisseria meningitidis stands as one of the predominant etiological agents of bacterial meningitis worldwide. Sequence type (ST) 4821 clonal complex (cc4821), notably linked to the hyperinvasive and quinolone-resistant clone ChinaCC4821−R1−C/B, has emerged and caused the epidemiological shift from serogroup A (MenA, mostly cc5 and cc1) to MenC in China since 2003 and the subsequent introduction of MenA + C vaccination.

title: Association between low‐carbohydrate diet scores and macrovascular events or all‐cause mortality in adults with type 1 diabetes in Japan
creator: Junko Sato, Tomoya Mita, Takuya Negami, Shohei Fujikawa, Haruki Nagashima, Eri Takagi, Shuhei Aoyama, Emi Otani, Yuya Nishida, Fuki Ikeda, Katsumi Aso, Hirotaka Watada
description: Aims/IntroductionThe effects of lifestyle factors on macrovascular events or all‐cause mortality remain unclear in type 1 diabetes. We examined the associations of diet, physical activity, and sleep with these outcomes among adults with type 1 diabetes living in Japan.Materials and MethodsThis multicenter prospective cohort included 352 adults with type 1 diabetes from the Juntendo–Aso Type 1 Diabetes cohort.

title: The value of a risk model combining specific risk factors for predicting postoperative severe morbidity in biliary tract cancer
creator: BaoLong Ye, JunFeng Xie, KeXing Xi, ZhiShun Huang, YanNian Liao, ZiWen Chen, Wu Ji
description: PurposeSeveral surgical risk models are widely utilized in general surgery to predict postoperative morbidity. However, no studies have been undertaken to examine the predictive efficacy of these models in biliary tract cancer patients, and other perioperative variables can also influence morbidity.

title: Osteoporosis risk in alpha and beta thalassemia: An age- and sex-specific retrospective cohort study
creator: Yuan-Sheng Hsu, Sheng-Chieh Tseng, Tze-Fan Chao, Kun-Hui Chen
description: SummaryRationale: Differential skeletal risks between alpha- and beta-thalassemia subtypes remain unclear. Main result: Beta-thalassemia correlates with higher fracture risk than alpha-thalassemia. Notably, males aged 18–50 with beta-thalassemia show a 14-fold increase in osteoporosis. Significance: Identifies a notably elevated osteoporosis risk in young males, supporting consideration of earlier skeletal surveillance.

title: Charge-mediated remote epitaxy of Ga2O3 via MoS2
creator: Gyeong Ryul Lee, Dong-Gwan Kim, Wonwoo Suh, Yoonho Choi, Donghan Kim, Mohammad M. Afandi, Juhui Oh, Hongsik Park, Celesta S. Chang, Hyun S. Kum, Taehoon Lee, Roy B. Chung
description: Remote epitaxy of the corundum phase α-Ga2O3 is demonstrated through a domain-free, transfer-free monolayer of MoS2 template synthesized on sapphire. Despite the intrinsic nonidealities of MoS2—specifically its thickness and polar bonding characteristics—for remote epitaxy, single-crystalline α-Ga2O3 films are epitaxially grown on polycrystalline MoS2 with crystallographic fidelity comparable to those grown directly on bare sapphire.

title: Intelligent predictive neural network analysis on LTNE impacts on thermophoretic particle deposition in HFE 7100 nanofluid with Co3O4 nanoparticle
creator: Saba Liaqat, Bouthaina Dammak, Muhammad Sabaoon Khan, Walid Abdelfattah, Joy Djuansjah, Ilyas Khan, Munawar Abbas, Nidhal Ben Khedher
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This study examines the outcome of heat generation on thermophoretic particle deposition in Co3O4/HFE-7100 nanofluid flowing past a vertical cylinder in a permeable media under local thermal non-equilibrium conditions employing an ANN coupled with a Bayesian-regularized back-propagation algorithm. For contrast, a simplified mathematical formulation is also used to examine the thermal behavior without local thermal equilibrium assumptions, that is, without LTNE limitations.

title: Rice tiller number estimation based on an improved Swin-UNet model and multi-feature fusion
creator: Xiao Liang, Junnuo Wu, Cheng Zhang, Lielie Qin, Xingcheng Liu, Yingli Cao
description: Rice early tillering characteristics are key indicators for high-yield breeding, with tiller number and tillering rate as core parameters. High-throughput, temporal, and precise monitoring of tiller numbers via drone digital imagery provides quantitative support for tillering trait screening in breeding, serving as an important auxiliary tool for smart breeding. However, during the early tillering stage, complex backgrounds (e.g.

title: GJA5 and ATP1A1 perturbations recapitulate inflammation-related beat irregularities in iPSC-based atrial myocardium tissue model
creator: Thomas Hutschalik, Albert Dasí, Leto L. Riebel, Maury Wiendels, Frederikus Bakker, Lucas J. A. M. Beckers, Koen C. Kriege, Susanne M. Valster, Roland C. M. Vulders, Ozan Özgül, Rémi Peyronnet, Blanca Rodriguez, Mariana Argenziano, Ulrich Schotten, Elena Matsa
description: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common cardiac arrhythmia, linked to greater risk of heart failure, stroke and death. Inflammation has been connected to AF emergence, however mechanisms of inflammation-caused AF remain thus far elusive, leading to a lack of mechanism-based treatments.

title: Can they touch? A novel mental motor imagery task for the assessment of back pain
creator: H. Branch Coslett, Jared Medina, Daria Kliot Goodman, Yuchao Wang, Adam Burkey
description: IntroductionAs motor imagery is informed by the anticipated sensory consequences of action, including pain, we reasoned that motor imagery could provide a useful indicator of chronic back pain. We tested the hypothesis that mental motor imagery regarding body movements can provide a reliable assessment of low back pain.

title: Antimicrobial drug use and its association with antimicrobial resistance in fecal commensals from cows on California dairies
creator: Essam M. Abdelfattah, Pius S. Ekong, Emmanuel Okello, Tapakorn Chamchoy, Betsy M. Karle, Randi A. Black, Wagdy ElAshmawy, David Sheedy, Deniece R. Williams, Terry W. Lehenbauer, Barbara A. Byrne, Sharif S. Aly
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The current study objective was to investigate the risk factors associated with the isolation of antimicrobial-resistant Escherichia coli, Enterococcus spp., and Streptococcus spp. (ES) from the feces of dairy cows in California (CA).

title: Akinetopsia: a systematic review on visual motion blindness
creator: Johanna L. Browne, Lydia Krabbendam, Jan Dirk Blom
description: BackgroundAkinetopsia, or visual motion blindness, is a perceptual distortion characteristic of Alice in Wonderland syndrome in which people see moving objects as disjointed ‘jumps’ or ‘freeze frames.’ Despite its profound impact, the condition remains poorly understood beyond the established centrality of cortical area V5/MT in visual motion perception.

title: An inspiration-off attractor supports the robust and flexible control of breathing
creator: Nicholas E. Bush, Luiz M. Oliveira, Zachary T. Glovak, Jan-Marino Ramirez
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Breathing is a fundamental motor rhythm necessary to sustain life. The rhythm and pattern of breathing arises from the coordination of a rostrocaudally extended ventral respiratory column (VRC) in the medulla. Although recurrent excitation is sufficient for rhythmic bursting in reduced in vitro preparations, comparatively less is understood about how inhibition and excitation interact with feedback circuits to generate the breathing rhythm in vivo.

title: Nanoconfinement-cooperated catalysis enables rapid tandem redox kinetics for wide-temperature lithium-sulfur batteries
creator: Tianli Li, Tao Chen, Pu Hu, Congcong Cai, Juntao Wang, Chaoqun Shang, Liwei Xiong, Yajie Li, Hanxing Liu, Jian Wang, Yaobing Wang
description: The slow kinetics of sulfur cathodes caused by the high energy barriers of Li+ desolvation stem primarily from the structure of the inner Helmholtz plane (IHP). Herein, a synergistic strategy combining electrochemical tandem catalysis with spatial nanoconfinement is proposed to regulate the Li(solvent)x+ dynamics.

title: Multi-hierarchical biofunctional polymeric biomaterial to promote wound closure
creator: Zacharie Deruyver, Naïma Ahmed Omar, Claire de Lartigue, Noémie Petit, Louise Hosty, Aline Echalard, Chloé Eudier, Shane Browne, Christophe Egles, Anthony C. Duncan
description: Chronic wounds constitute a significant medical, societal, and economic issue due to the significant delay in wound closure, leading to the increased risk of infection, which extends patients’ time spent in the hospital and negatively impacts overall health. Biofunctional biomaterials have emerged as powerful tools to promote tissue regeneration by mimicking extracellular matrix properties and delivering therapeutic agents.

title: Direct electrical stimulation of the human amygdala enhances recognition memory for objects but not scenes
creator: Krista L. Wahlstrom, Justin M. Campbell, Martina K. Hollearn, James Swift, Markus Adamek, Gansheng Tan, Lou Blanpain, Tao Xie, Tyler Davis, Peter Brunner, Stephan B. Hamann, Amir Arain, Lawrence N. Eisenman, John D. Rolston, Shervin Rahimpour, Joseph R. Manns, Jon T. Willie, Cory S. Inman
description: Research from studies using invasive neuroanatomy-inspired direct manipulations suggests the basolateral amygdala (BLA) mediates a generalized modulation of many different types of memory. In contrast, noninvasive indirect correlations suggest that specificity exists in how the BLA prioritizes experiences in memory. We used direct electrical stimulation of the BLA to investigate the specificity of the memory enhancement in the human brain.

title: Scaling up production of recombinant human basic fibroblast growth factor in an Escherichia coli BL21(DE3) plysS strain and evaluation of its pro-wound healing efficacy
creator: Le Li, Bingjie Yu, Yingji Lai, Siyuan Shen, Yawei Yan, Guojun Dong, Xiangyun Gao, Yanrong Cao, Caojie Ge, Liqin Zhu, Huan Liu, Shanhui Tao, Zhiang Yao, Shijun Li, Xiaojie Wang, Qi Hui
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Introduction: Human basic fibroblast growth factor (hbFGF) is a highly valuable multifunctional protein that plays a crucial role in various biological processes. In this study, we aim to accomplish the scaling-up production of mature hbFGF (146aa) by implementing a high cell-density fermentation and purification process on a 500-L scale, thereby satisfying the escalating demands for both experimental research and clinical applications.

title: Proximity labelling suggests association of the nonhost receptor PSS1 protein with enzymes of multiple defense pathways in Arabidopsis
creator: Oluwatoyosi F. Akintayo, Christian Montes Serey, Justin W. Walley, Madan K. Bhattacharyya
description: IntroductionPSS1 encoding a glycine-rich integral plasma membrane protein plays a pivotal role in nonhost resistance of Arabidopsis against the soybean pathogens, Phytophthora sojae and Fusarium virguliforme. Notably, P. sojae fails to penetrate the wildtype Col-0 ecotype but not the pss1 mutant. To elucidate the molecular basis of PSS1-mediated nonhost immunity, we employed a miniTurbo-based proximity labeling approach.

title: Radiotherapy quality assurance in the TROG 12.01 randomised trial and its impact on loco-regional failure
creator: June Corry, Alisha Moore, Liz Kenny, Chris Wratten, Tsien Fua, Charles Lin, Sandro Porceddu, Chen Liu, Michael Ruemelin, Amy Sharkey, Lachlan McDowell, Dean Wilkinson, Albert Tiong, Danny Rischin
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). IntroductionThere is no consensus as to what specifically constitutes head and neck cancer radiotherapy quality assurance (HNC RT QA). The aims of this study are to (1) describe the RT QA processes used in the TROG 12.01 study, (2) review the RT QA processes undertaken for all patients with loco-regional failure (LRF), and (3) provide prospective data to propose a consensus statement regarding the minimal components and optimal timing of HNC RT QA.Materials and methodsAll patients undergoing RT QA in the original

title: Homage to James Feeney, a pioneer of biological NMR – Part II
creator: Gordon C. Roberts
description: the Medical Research Council (MRC) Molecular Pharmacology Unit in Cambridge, as part of which in 1972 he moved to the MRC National Institute for Medical Research (NIMR) at Mill Hill in London where he worked until retirement, rising to become Head of the Molecular Structure Division and Controller of the Biomedical NMR Centre.

title: Lipid biomarkers reveal dominance of aerobic methanotrophy in a continental serpentinizing system
creator: Cybele R. Collins, Mary N. Parenteau, Linda L. Jahnke, Michael D. Kubo, Serena Moseman-Valtierra, Kyle Young, Dawn Cardace
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Sources and sinks of methane within an advanced serpentinization-influenced system were investigated at the Coast Range Ophiolite Microbial Observatory (CROMO) in Lower Lake, California. Subsurface water-rock reactions at CROMO contribute to unique, high pH groundwaters and substantial methane emissions. We performed lipid analysis on biomass and measured radiocarbon and stable carbon isotopic composition of groundwater to trace the origins and fate of methane. Specific groups of microorganisms involved in methane cycling were identified through analysis of membrane lipid components.

title: Fostering therapeutic relationships in brief interventions: an exploratory qualitative study of the Ensemble program for informal caregivers of adults with psychiatric disorders
creator: Hélène Wilquin, Léa Plessis, Elora Bourgade, Shyhrete Rexhaj
description: IntroductionInformal caregivers play a crucial and multifaceted role in the recovery of individuals with psychiatric disorders, but this role can negatively impact their own quality of life. Therefore, targeted interventions that address caregivers’ specific needs are essential. The Ensemble program is a brief, targeted intervention designed to enhance caregivers’ psychological well-being through a helping relationship centered on their lived experience.

title: Harnessing generative AI for predicting and optimizing antimicrobial peptides against drug-resistant infections
creator: Sandra Clemens, Hannah Franziska Löchel, Nico Häußer, Felix Wannemacher, Wilhelm Bertrams, Bernd Schmeck, Dominik Heider
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) poses a major global health threat that demands the discovery of new antimicrobial agents. Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) offer a promising therapeutic alternative due to their broad-spectrum activity and reduced likelihood of resistance development. In the current study, we developed COMPASS, a comprehensive database aggregating 75,381 unique AMP sequences from nine public repositories, and created AmpGPT2, a transformer-based generative model specifically fine-tuned for AMP sequence generation.

title: Morphological changes and lateralization of the thalamic nuclei in children with growth hormone deficiency
creator: Joo Young Lee, Sung-min Lim, Jung Hwan Oh, Hyuna Kim, Gang Yi Lee, Bong Gun Lee, Jeong-Kyu Hoh, Seung Yang, Hyun Ju Lee
description: IntroductionChildhood growth hormone deficiency (GHD) is an endocrine disorder characterized by reduced secretion of growth hormone (GH), leading to impaired linear growth and delayed developmental milestones. Recent studies suggest that GHD is associated with cognitive, socio-emotional, and behavioral impairments, potentially via altered neurodevelopment, with neuroimaging studies revealing changes in brain morphology and broader GH-related effects on the central nervous system.

title: Assessment of adherence to dietary recommendations and associated factors among type 2 diabetic patients in selected hospitals in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia
creator: Wabi Temesgen Atinafu, Kefyalew Naniye Tilahun
description: BackgroundIn Ethiopia, diabetes and its complications are significant causes of morbidity and mortality, with huge economic implications. Despite the high dietary non-adherence that has been reported in limited studies in Ethiopia. Moreover, there is a gap from the perspective of patients in the area of this topic.

title: Evaluating the relative predictive validity of measures of self-referential processing for depressive symptom severity
creator: Ethel Siew Ee Tan, Hong Ming Tan, Kah Vui Fong, Sheryl Yu Xuan Tey, Nikita Rane, Chong Wei Ho, Zhao Yuan Tan, Rachel Jing Min Ong, Chloe Teo, Jerall Yu, Maxine Lee, An Rae Teo, Sin Kee Ong, Xin Ying Lim, Jin Lin Kee, Jussi Keppo, Geoffrey Chern-Yee Tan
description: IntroductionThe self-referential encoding task (SRET) has a number of implicit measures which are associated with various facets of depression, including depressive symptoms. While some measures have proven robust in predicting depressive symptoms, their effectiveness can vary depending on the methodology used.

title: Prioritized nonlinear modeling of shared dynamics across neural populations
creator: Trisha Jha, Dong Song, Maryam M Shanechi
description: Objective. Advances in neural recording technology enable simultaneous measurements across multiple brain regions, providing new opportunities to study inter-regional interactions. However, several challenges arise when developing nonlinear dynamical models of cross-region interactions. In particular, we identify three key desired properties for a nonlinear framework. First, it should prioritize extraction of cross-region dynamics to avoid confounds from within-region dynamics.

title: A unified framework for characterizing response quality in surveys with multi-item scales
creator: Nivedita Bhaktha, Henning Silber, Clemens M Lechner
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Self-administered surveys are widely used but the quality of the survey responses have been a major concern. Low-quality responses threaten the validity and replicability of studies. To detect potentially problematic responses, many data quality indicators have been proposed. We propose a unifying conceptual framework for response quality issues in multi-item surveys as literature is scattered and suffers from a lack of conceptual and terminological clarity.

title: FAO laboratory mapping tool results analysis for veterinary laboratories from 2012 to 2020: highlights of the gaps, the strengths across Southeast Asia and implications for capacity building activities
creator: Morgane Gourlaouen, Stuart D. Blacksell, Khanh Kim Le, Christopher J. Morrissy, Wantanee Kalpravidh, Kachen Wongsathapornchai, Paolo Motta, Asfri Rangkuti, Gwenaelle Dauphin, Lidewij Wiersma, Thao Tran, Luca Porfiri, Beatrice Mouillé, Filip Claes
description: IntroductionThe Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) developed the Laboratory Mapping Tool (FAO-LMT) Core module in 2010 to assess the general activities and capacities of central veterinary laboratories. Indeed, the FAO-LMT Core can determine strengths and gaps in laboratory functionality to define mechanisms and targets for capacity building to fill the measured gaps.

title: Influence of dual stratification on the magnetohydrodynamic flow of Jeffrey nanofluid over an exponentially stretching permeable sheet with viscous dissipation and Joule heating
creator: M. Siva Sankari, M. Eswara Rao, Fuad A. Awwad, Emad A. A. Ismail, O. D. Makinde, Waris Khan
description: Nanoparticles show superior potential for enhancing thermal properties compared to conventional particle–liquid suspensions. This investigation delves into magnetohydrodynamics (MHD) drift, heat, and mass transfer effects within a Jeffery nanoparticle liquid. The study includes transference equations that consider the influences of thermophoresis and Brownian motion on particle deposition.

title: Outcome after vacuum-assisted closure in patients with anorectal malformations—a multi-center comparative study
creator: L.-M. Borsch, M. Bouzidi, B. Ludwikowski, M. Bottländer, L. Wennemann, J. Dingemann, N. Schukfeh
description: PurposeIn patients with anorectal malformations (ARM), perineal wound complications following posterior sagittal anorectoplasty (PSARP) remain a challenge with an occurrence of 22%-43%. In adults, vacuum-assisted closure (VAC) aims to support wound healing after colorectal procedures. In children evidence is limited, suggesting a potential benefit of VAC therapy after PSARP.

title: Genomic evolution and climate related drivers of cholera surges in Dhaka Bangladesh between 1996 and 2024
creator: Md Mamun Monir, Khalilur Rahman, Mohammad Tarequl Islam, Marzia Sultana, Wali Ullah, Sardar Muhammad Osail, Md Alimul Islam Ridoy, Abdullah Al-Mamun, Shirajum Monira, Kimberley D Seed, Andrew Camilli, Carla Mavian, Nicholas Thomson, Rita R Colwell, ASG Faruque, Tahmeed Ahmed, Munirul Alam
description: BackgroundCholera, a climate-associated diarrhea occurs endemically in Dhaka city, Bangladesh, often turning into large epidemics. In 2022, a massive outbreak struck Dhaka city, resulting in a very high number of cholera cases. Although extensive studies have focused on climate and cholera, including genomic evolution of the causative agent, Vibrio cholerae, their association with the case surges remains poorly understood.

title: Glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis is prevented by dietary prune in female mice
creator: Nicholas J. Chargo, Kerri Neugebauer, Douglas V. Guzior, Robert A. Quinn, Narayanan Parameswaran, Laura R. McCabe
description: Glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis (GIO) is a significant side effect of prolonged glucocorticoid (GC) treatment. Chronic GC treatment also leads to trabecular bone loss and gut microbiota dysbiosis in mice. The gut dysbiosis is mechanistically linked to GIO, which indicates that the microbiota can be targeted to prevent GIO.

title: Cognitive reserve and the risk of postoperative neurocognitive disorders in older age
creator: Friedrich Borchers, Miriam Rumpel, Jochen Laubrock, Claudia Spies, Petra Kozma, Arjen Slooter, Simone J. T. van Montfort, Sophie K. Piper, Janine Wiebach, Georg Winterer, Tobias Pischon, Insa Feinkohl
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundPostoperative delirium (POD) and postoperative cognitive dysfunction (POCD) are postoperative neurocognitive disorders (PNDs) that frequently occur in the aftermath of a surgical intervention. Cognitive reserve (CR) is a concept posited to explain why cognitive health varies between individuals.

title: Across preclinical and clinical platforms, approved and investigational psychiatric drugs share pathways and associate with similar molecular functions
creator: Emily Su, Nico Matthew S. Valencia, Jarod Le, Emily Liu, Jennifer L. Wilson
description: Introduction:Translating findings from cell and animal models to the clinic is difficult because these systems insufficiently capture human disease biology. Computational approaches, notably pathways modeling, have overcome interspecies differences by mapping shared signaling pathways between species. We considered whether this approach could be generalized to bridge animal and virtual drug screening data to effects measured in patients.

title: The role and underlying mechanisms of Qi Gong Wan in enhancing the endometrial receptivity of a rat model with polycystic ovary syndrome
creator: Chun Ding, Qinhua Li, Yiwen Deng, Yuhan Liu, Lei Liu, ChunYu Cao, Siwei Li, Tingting Zheng, Liangqun Xie, Jing Zhao, Hong Ye, Junkui Li
description: BackgroundQi Gong Wan (QGW) is a herbal formula which is used for treating infertility associated with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS). However, the mechanism of action remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate whether QGW enhances endometrial receptivity in a PCOS with insulin resistance (PCOS-IR) rat model and to explore the underlying molecular mechanisms and primary active constituents.

title: Sustainable dye removal using fish scale-derived biosorbent: performance and mechanisms
creator: Fatima Ezzahra Atmani, Zouhair Jemali, Safaa Adim, Meriem Kasbaji, Morad Kaddouri, Nadia Anter, Mohammed Al-zharani, Fahd A. Nasr, Ashraf Ahmed Qurtam, Reda El kacmi, Abdelali Bouli, Aziz Hasib
description: Introduction: In the context of sustainable methodologies for wastewater remediation, this study focuses on the development of an efficient and low-cost biosorbent derived from Sardina pilchardus fish scales (SPFS) for dye removal applications. Methods: The prepared biosorbent was characterized using physicochemical and morphological analyses to evaluate its surface properties and porosity.

title: Bibliometric analysis of targeted immunotherapy for osteosarcoma-current knowledge, hotspots and future perspectives
creator: Yunxiang Hu, Rui Yang, Shuai Ni, Zefeng Song
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). ObjectiveThe objective of this study is to conduct a bibliometric analysis on examining the current condition, areas of interest, and rising trends of immunotherapy for osteosarcoma (ITFOS), as well as its importance in associated research domains.MethodsAn extensive collection of academic papers on the use of ITFOS was obtained from the Web of Science between January 1, 2000 and October 20, 2023. Then, using a variety of tools like HisCite, VOSviewer, CiteSpace, and the bibliometrix package, a bibliometric study was carried out.

title: Correlation between gut microbiota and their metabolites and the efficacy of chemotherapy combined with immunotherapy for extensive-stage small cell lung cancer
creator: Wenjing Song, Shiwei Liu, Dan Zang, Wenjuan Meng, Chenguang Liu, Jun Chen
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionGut microbiota has been reported to be associated with the host’s immune system and immunotherapy response, as well as immune-related adverse events (irAEs). Additionally, gut microbial metabolites have various immunomodulatory effects. Our study focused on the differences in gut microbiota and their metabolites between long progression-free survival (PFS) and short PFS in patients with small cell lung cancer before and after chemotherapy combined with immunotherapy.MethodsThe enrolled patients collected in our department were divided into long PFS and short PFS groups according to

title: Immune-related gene expression links anxiety, depression, and pain outcomes in adolescence
creator: Anh Cong Tuan Le, Tobias Banaschewski, Arun L W Bokde, Rüdiger Brühl, Sylvane Desrivières, Hugh Garavan, Penny Gowland, Antoine Grigis, Andreas Heinz, Jean-Luc Martinot, Marie-Laure Paillère Martinot, Eric Artiges, Dimitri Papadopoulos Orfanos, Luise Poustka, Michael N Smolka, Nathalie Holz, Nilaksh
description: Background:Chronic pain and internalising disorders such as anxiety and depression frequently co-occur during adolescence. Although prospective associations between internalising symptoms and later pain have been reported previously, the biological mechanisms underlying individual differences in this relationship remain poorly understood. Immune- and oxidative stress-related pathways, including the NRF2 gene, may contribute to such variability.

title: Genomic, transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses of Amorphophallus albus provides insights into the evolution and resistance to southern blight pathogen
creator: Longfei Duan, Jianfeng Qin, Gaoxin Zhou, Chuan Shen, Baofu Qin
description: Introduction Amorphophallus albus, a perennial herb in the Araceae family, is a valuable cash crop known for its high production of konjac glucomannan and high disease resistance.MethodsIn this study, we present a high-quality, chromosome-scale genome assembly of A. albus using a combination of PacBio HiFi sequencing, DNBSEQ short-read sequencing, and Hi-C technology.

title: Reconstructing the aqueous environment of the Ryugu parent body through the speciation of multiple elements
creator: Takahiro Kawai, Keisuke Fukushi, Tomohiro Ohno, Hiroki Suga, Masayuki Uesugi, Ayu Takemoto, Akiko Yamaguchi, Takaaki Itai, Yuta Ijichi, Shohei Yamashita, Yasuhiro Niwa, Ryoichi Nakada, Mizuho Koike, Hideto Yoshida, Masaki Oura, Megumi Matsumoto, Tomohiro Usui, Yoko Kebukawa, Takazo Shibuya, Shogo Ta
description: The parent body of the C-type asteroid Ryugu experienced aqueous alteration. The past aqueous environments have been reconstructed using mineralogies and geochemical modeling, often assuming Na-Cl-rich fluid compositions. Here, we reconstruct Ryugu’s aqueous environment using chemical equilibrium modeling constrained by Electron Probe Microanalyzer (EPMA) and X-ray absorption near-edge structure spectroscopy.

title: Mortality risk prediction model in AIDS patients with pneumocystis pneumonia in China
creator: Xi Wang, Letian Liu, Wen Wang, Yang Zhang, Hui Chen, Zhangli Wang, Jianwei Li, Yue Gao, Yanqun Huang, Lijun Sun, Tong Zhang, Aixin Li
description: IntroductionPneumocystis pneumonia (PCP) is a common and serious complication of HIV/AIDS, with a higher prevalence in patients not receiving antiretroviral therapy. Due to the high mortality rate of PCP, accurate prediction of its case fatality rate is very important for clinical treatment.

title: Negligible impact of UV-curable resist shrinkage on NIL pattern fidelity
creator: Guiyan Yang, Xinhe Cao, Jiabing Wang, Jiahong Chen, Ruiyang Chen, Bo Xu, Xinyu Wang, Xiaofeng Chen, Mengmeng Deng, Zongbin Hao, Yushuang Cui, Haixiong Ge
description: Shrinkage of UV-curable resists during nanoimprint lithography (NIL) has long been regarded as a potential source of pattern distortion; however, direct experimental validation of this effect remains scarce. Here, we systematically investigate the influence of resist shrinkage on the imprinted pattern fidelity using two UV-curable resins with distinct volumetric shrinkage ratios (6.8% and 2.6%).

title: Sequencing whole genomes of the West Javanese population in Indonesia reveals novel variants and improves imputation accuracy
creator: Edwin Ardiansyah, Anca-Lelia Riza, Sofiati Dian, Ahmad Rizal Ganiem, Bachti Alisjahbana, Todia P. Setiabudiawan, Arjan van Laarhoven, Reinout van Crevel, Vinod Kumar
description: Existing genotype imputation reference panels are mainly derived from European populations, limiting their accuracy in non-European populations. To improve imputation accuracy for Indonesians, the world’s fourth most populous country, we combined Whole Genome Sequencing (WGS) data from 227 West Javanese individuals with East Asian data from the 1,000 Genomes Project.

title: Prioritizing competencies for soldier’s mental resilience: an application of integrative fuzzy-trapezoidal decision-making trial and evaluation laboratory in updating training program
creator: Svajone Bekesiene, Rasa Smaliukienė, Ramutė Vaičaitienė, Dalia Bagdžiūnienė, Rosita Kanapeckaitė, Olena Kapustian, Oleksandr Nakonechnyi
description: BackgroundThe development of resilience is of the utmost importance in military training due to the demanding and high-stress nature of combat situations. Although there have been numerous studies on resilience competencies in the military, there is a research gap when it comes to identifying the most essential competencies that should be prioritized in training programs, particularly within compressed timeframes.

title: A cross-sectional study of the prevalence and correlates of post-traumatic stress among people attending acceptance and commitment therapy for chronic pain
creator: Kezia Kadri, Cara Keating, Madeleine Anderson, David Novelli, Emily McBride, Whitney Scott
description: ObjectiveExperiences of trauma are common among people with chronic pain, although estimates of comorbid post-traumatic stress vary widely across contexts. Acceptance and commitment therapy (ACT), which targets psychological flexibility to improve pain-related functioning, is increasingly delivered for people with pain.

title: Wives with long and high-quality hair have more frequent sex
creator: Jeong Eun Cheon, Jeongwoo John Kim, Young-Hoon Kim
description: The image of an ideal woman often involves her having long, silky hair. However, the dearth of psychological research on hair limits the understanding of how women’s hair functions in romantic relationships. While some scholars have found that the appearance of women’s hair signals reproductive potential to men, whether women’s hair may affect their sexual lives remains unknown.

title: Human immunodeficiency virus infection mimicking very early onset inflammatory bowel disease
creator: Rasha Abi Radi Abou Jaoudeh, Cary Sauer, Teresa Oh
description: Very early onset inflammatory bowel disease (VEO‐IBD), defined as diagnosis before 6 years of age, is often associated with immune dysregulation and monogenic etiologies; however, infectious mimics may be overlooked in low‐prevalence regions. We report a 4‐year‐old male with poor weight gain, intermittent diarrhea, elevated fecal calprotectin, and persistently elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate.

title: Magnetic Resonance Imaging Does Not Accurately Estimate the Size of Glenoid Labrum Tears in Patients With Shoulder Instability
creator: Samuel K. Gerak, Antonia S. Caldwell, William A. Crites, Cameron Crasto, Benjamin E. Jevnikar, Ronak J. Mahatme, Shawn A. Moore, Susan E. Braley, Brian M. Grawe
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). PurposeTo compare magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)‐based measurements of glenoid labral tears with intraoperative measurements.MethodsA retrospective review was performed of patients that underwent shoulder capsulorrhaphy between 2019 and 2024 at a single academic medical center. All patients with a single labrum tear, an MRI within 6 months of surgery, and historical tear measurements or measurable intraoperative photographs were included in the study.

title: Associations of mindful eating and physical activity with mental workload and sleep quality in medical interns
creator: Mina Babashahi, Niloofar Rahgoshay, Najme Setoude, Hadi Daneshmandi
description: This study aimed to investigate mindful eating practices and physical activity levels among medical interns and to examine their associations with mental workload and sleep quality. This cross-sectional study was conducted in 2025 among 165 medical interns at Shiraz University of Medical Sciences, Iran. Participants were recruited through convenience sampling.

title: Lactobacillus derived small RNAs protect against Klebsiella pneumoniae infection
creator: Tingting Xu, Xiuying Tao, Dan Fang, Haijie Zhang, Zhiqiang Wang, Yuan Liu
description: Carbapenem‐resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CRKP) is a major multidrug‐resistant pathogen with limited treatment options. Plant‐derived natural products have broad biological activities, but their protective effects against extraintestinal multidrug‐resistant bacterial infections remain poorly understood. Herein, we show that selected plant‐derived natural products protect mice against CRKP pulmonary infection by remodeling the gut microbiota.

title: Expert perspectives on the ecosystem of medical AI oversight in the GenAI era
creator: Stephen Gilbert, Tinglong Dai
description: In this third article of a three-article series on interviews with Dr Shantanu Nundy, an advisor in the office of the Commissioner of the US FDA on AI governance and digital health policy, we explore how the oversight of generative AI (GenAI) and large language model (LLM)-enabled medical devices extends beyond the remit of any single regulator, requiring coordination among

title: Implicit bias in referrals to relational psychological therapies: review and recommendations for mental health services
creator: Chenai Mandangu, Anne Millicent Ramos, Mohona Sengupta, Rosslyn Bender, Reem El-Hayani, Ifrah Hasan, Hannah Okechukwu, Shafeena Anas, Dominik Havsteen-Franklin
description: IntroductionTimely and appropriate psychological treatment is an essential element required to address the growing burden of mental health issues, which has significant implications for individuals, society, and healthcare systems. However, research indicates that implicit biases among mental health professionals may influence referral decisions, potentially leading to disparities in access to relational psychological therapies.

title: Early parathyroid hormone elevation after denosumab therapy following parathyroidectomy: a diagnostic pitfall
creator: Hiroyuki Yamashita, Hisakazu Shindo, Daisuke Tatsushima, Yusuke Mori, Kento Katsuyama, Shinya Sato
description: Persistently elevated parathyroid hormone (PTH) after parathyroidectomy is often attributed to residual disease but may reflect altered calcium (Ca) homeostasis. The impact of denosumab on perioperative PTH interpretation remains unclear. A 77-year-old woman presented with a hypercalcemic crisis and was initially managed at another hospital.

title: Monoclonal antibody development against the Hepatitis C virus core protein enables rapid antigen detection
creator: Prince Baffour Tonto, Bobby Brooke Herrera
description: Hepatitis C virus (HCV) remains a major global health burden, with limited access to affordable diagnostics impeding progress toward the World Health Organization target elimination by 2030. While HCV ribonucleic acid (RNA) testing is the gold standard, it requires costly infrastructure and technical expertise.

title: Impacts of non-native invertebrates and plants on polar soil systems
creator: Octavia D M Brayley, Peter Convey, Sami Ullah, Scott A L Hayward
description: Invasive non-native species are amongst the most serious threats to biodiversity at local and global scales. Due to their geographical remoteness, extreme conditions and lower levels of human activity, the Earth’s polar regions have seen fewer invasions to date compared to temperate and tropical areas.

title: Optimization of treatment strategies based on preoperative imaging features and local recurrence areas for locally advanced lower rectal cancer after lateral pelvic lymph node dissection
creator: Zhao Xu, Mandula Bao, Qiang Cai, Qian Wang, Wei Xing, Qian Liu
description: PurposeLocal recurrence (LR) is the main cause of treatment failure in locally advanced lower rectal cancer (LALRC). This study evaluated the preoperative risk factors for LR in patients with LALRC to improve the therapeutic strategies.Patients and MethodsLALRC patients who underwent total mesorectal excision (TME) with lateral pelvic lymph node (LPN) dissection (LPND) from January 2012 to December 2019 were reviewed.

title: Assessing the stability and adaptability of wheat genotypes in well-watered and rainfed conditions using AMMI, BLUP, GGE biplot and MTSI approaches
creator: Nishtman Abdi, Hadi Alipour, Reza Darvishzadeh, Ehsan Rabieyan
description: This study aimed to analyze genotype × environment interaction (GEI), assess yield stability and adaptability, and identify superior Iranian wheat genotypes using multiple statistical approaches. A total of 266 genotypes, comprising 86 cultivars and 180 landraces, were evaluated under rainfed (S2017-2020) and well-watered (N2016-2020) conditions using a lattice design with two replications.

title: The first and second zinc finger domains from Poly-ADP-ribose polymerase 1 (PARP1) are modified by hydrogen sulfide
creator: Ayanna J. Williams, Sarah L. J. Michel
description: Poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase 1 (PARP1) is a Zinc Finger (ZF) protein that is involved in DNA damage response. PARP1 contains three zinc finger (ZF) domains, two with a Cys2HisCys (CCHC) ligand set and one with a Cys4 (CCCC) ligand set that coordinate zinc.

title: Countermovement jump peak force discriminates low hip bone mineral density in postmenopausal women
creator: Raphael Gonçalves de Oliveira, Mariana Machado Signoreti, Larissa Victória Branco, Andreo Fernando Aguiar, Laís Campos de Oliveira
description: Postmenopausal women are at increased risk of low bone mineral density (BMD) and osteoporotic fractures, yet access to dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA) remains limited in many settings. This study evaluated the diagnostic accuracy of countermovement jump (CMJ)-derived variables for identifying low BMD in postmenopausal women.

title: Synergistic fusion of a multilevel visual transformer in CNN for variable-length volumetric radiographic data analysis and content-based retrieval
creator: Muhammad Owais, Muhammad Zubair, Taimur Hassan, Divya Velayudhan, Naoufel Werghi, Irfan Hussain
description: Volumetric radiographic data analysis poses significant challenges due to its 3D structure and variable input lengths. Moreover, the unpredictable distribution of diseased regions, often spanning multiple slices and interspersed with normal tissue within abnormal volumes, further complicates the analysis. Despite advancements, existing 3D volumetric analysis methods predominantly rely on 2D slice selection and expert intervention, limiting scalability and efficiency.

title: Autoimmune hepatitis following long-term denosumab therapy in a patient with Hashimoto thyroiditis
creator: Jacob Maniattu, McAnto Antony, Alvin Maliakal
description: Denosumab, a receptor activator of nuclear factor-κB ligand (RANKL) inhibitor, is widely used to treat osteoporosis. Its role as a trigger for autoimmune hepatitis (AIH) remains uncertain. We report a 68-year-old woman with osteoporosis and Hashimoto thyroiditis who developed jaundice and severe hepatocellular liver injury after 3 years of denosumab therapy. Alternative viral, obstructive, and metabolic causes were excluded.

title: Editome profiling and cross-cohort validation reveal A-to-I RNA editing dysregulation in the hippocampus and prefrontal cortex of sepsis patients
creator: Jie Shen, Jia-Qi Pan, Tian-Yue Yu, Le-Wen Liu, Yu-Nuo Li, Yun-Yun Jin, Minmin Zhu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionSepsis is a severe systemic inflammatory response to infection, potentially resulting in serious neurological complications. Adenosine-to-inosine (A-to-I) RNA editing is a critical epitranscriptomic process, yet its clinical involvement in different brain regions during sepsis remains to be elucidated.MethodsWe conducted a comprehensive editome analysis and experimental validation to characterize A-to-I RNA editing in hippocampal and prefrontal cortical tissues from a sepsis cohort, as well as in brain tissues from a validation cohort.ResultsOur findings revealed diverse dysregulation of RNA editing in these brain regions,

title: Caring in crisis: family dynamics and child wellbeing in Rohingya refugee camps
creator: Bree Akesson, Ashley Stewart-Tufescu, Cindy Sousa, Karen Frensch
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). For Rohingya families living in the world’s largest refugee camps, the perinatal period unfolds under conditions of profound insecurity and deprivation, despite being a critical developmental window that reshapes family dynamics and lays the foundation for child outcomes.

title: Monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio as a predictor of left ventricular aneurysm in acute STEMI patients
creator: Dong Hu, Dongyang Wu, Ting Huang, Guangji Wang, Xin Guo, Qinshuo Zhao, Man-Hua Chen, Yi Zhou
description: BackgroundThe monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratio (MLR) has emerged as a novel marker of inflammation. Nevertheless, its potential utility in predicting the development of left ventricular aneurysm (LVA) remains unexplored. This study aims to investigate the association between MLR and the risk of LVA in patients presenting with acute ST segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI).

title: Neurotoxicity-sparing radiotherapy for brain metastases in breast cancer: a narrative review
creator: Dagmara Buczek, Renata Zaucha, Jacek Jassem
description: Breast cancer brain metastasis (BCBM) has a devastating impact on patient survival, cognitive function and quality of life. Radiotherapy remains the standard management of BM but may result in considerable neurotoxicity. Herein, we describe the current knowledge on methods for reducing radiation-induced cognitive dysfunction in patients with BCBM.

title: The role of systemic inflammatory response index in predicting myocardial infarction in patients with unstable angina
creator: Zhengwen Yang, Shuiquan Li, Tianlu Wang, Xiangyu Zhao, Fang Wang, Xueqian Zhang, Yangang Chen
description: BackgroundUnstable angina (UA) is a high-risk presentation of acute coronary syndrome (ACS) that can rapidly progress to myocardial infarction (MI) if not identified and managed promptly. Inflammation plays a key role in plaque instability and thrombotic events, making inflammatory biomarkers useful tools for early risk assessment.

title: The interplay between gingival crevicular fluid microbiome and metabolomic profile in intensively treated people with type 1 diabetes - a combined metagenomic/metabolomic approach cross-sectional study
creator: Iwona Gregorczyk-Maga, Michał Kania, Michalina Dąbrowska, Emilia Samborowska, Natalia Żeber-Lubecka, Maria Kulecka, Tomasz Klupa
description: AimsThis study aimed to assess the gingival crevicular fluid (GCF) microbiome and metabolome of adults with type 1 diabetes (T1D) treated with continuous subcutaneous insulin infusion (CSII).MethodsIn this cross-sectional study, the GCF of adults with T1D treated with CSII and non-diabetic controls were sampled, and metagenomic/metabolomic analyses were performed.

title: Mental health literacy among older adults in Shanghai: a descriptive qualitative study
creator: Rongjing Xu, Mingrui Jing, Aining Zhang, Liqi Zha, Yan Wang, Anni Wang, Jun Tang, Biyun Xia, Shoumei Jia
description: BackgroundThe aging population in China is surging rapidly, and elderly individuals are at higher risk of multiple mental health issues. Improving the mental health literacy of older adults can help them recognize mental illness and adopt proactive measures, potentially improving their mental health status and supporting the goal of healthy aging.

title: Comparative Pharmacokinetics and Safety of Orally Disintegrating and Conventional Tablet Formulations of Zastaprazan in Healthy Subjects
creator: Hyung‐Gun Kim, Seunghyun Kang, Sunyoung Min, Heejoo Hong, Moonjung Bae
description: Zastaprazan, a potassium‐competitive acid blocker, has been developed as an orally disintegrating tablet (ODT) to improve administration flexibility. This study evaluated the pharmacokinetics and safety of a single 20 mg dose of Zastaprazan ODT administered with or without water compared with the conventional tablet in healthy volunteers.

title: Changes in hepatic L-carnitine levels in people with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) assessed by magnetic resonance techniques
creator: Dragana Savic, Michael Pavlides, Mette Skalshøi Kjær, Sher May Ng, Katharine Thomas, Tim James, Gabrielle Allen, Claire Hart, Stefan Neubauer, Leanne Hodson, Ladislav Valkovič, Ferenc E Mózes
description: L-carnitine is critical for metabolism of some fatty acids therefore different carnitine species may play a role in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) pathogenesis. Until recently, hepatic acetylcarnitine could not be quantified non-invasively. Now new technical developments in magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS) enable quantification of hepatic acetylcarnitine content in vivo.

title: Ferroptosis-related proteins orchestrate aortic dissection: unveiling novel molecular signatures and therapeutic avenues
creator: Guohua Cai, Xueying Wu, Rong Guan, Xuemei Qian, Kexin Ren, Xue Guan, Yi Feng, Junquan Li
description: AD (Aortic dissection) is a life-threatening cardiovascular emergency. Initially, through integrated bioinformatics analysis, we screened proteomic data from AD and control samples. By combining this with a ferroptosis-related database, 22 key ferroptosis-associated proteins were identified. Multidimensional analyses (including heatmaps and volcano plots) were used to visualize differences in protein abundance and pathway disruptions.

title: Correction: Inclusion of patient-centered, non-microbiological endpoints and biomarkers in tuberculosis drug trials
creator: Andrew R. DiNardo, Wilbert Sabiiti, Stephen H. Gillespie, Sophia B. Georghiou, Norbert Heinrich, Norbert Hittel, Sami Taghlabi, Danna Carrero Longlax, Mikashmi Kohli, Ursula Panzner, Collins Musia, Christoph Lange, Anca Vasiliu, Rob J. W. Arts, Anna M. Mandalakas, Morten Ruhwald, Lieven J. Stuyver,
description: ided. The correct Funding statement reads: “This project has received funding from the Innovative Medicines Initiative 2 Joint Undertaking (JU) under grant agreement No 101007873. The JU receives support from the European Union’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme and EFPIA, Deutsches Zentrum für Infektionsforschung e. V. (DZIF), and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München (LMU).

title: Artificial intelligence models and combined scoring approaches for endometrial receptivity assessment in in vitro fertilization
creator: Teymur Bornaun
description: This retrospective study evaluates the effectiveness of artificial intelligence (AI) models and integrated scoring systems in assessing endometrial receptivity during in vitro fertilization (IVF). We combine AI-driven image analysis for automated endometrial segmentation (U-Net with VGG16 encoder) and embryo quality classification (VGG16) with a patient-specific clinical probability metric (SART) to generate a composite score.

title: Diagnostic accuracy of a modified non-contrast O-RADS MRI scoring system: a retrospective study
creator: Yan Ren, Can Cui, Zhijing Zhang, Wei Liao, Chen Zhang, Yue Cheng, Wen Shen
description: ObjectiveTo develop a modified non-contrast O-RADS MRI scoring system and validate its diagnostic performance.Materials and methodsThe modified non-contrast O-RADS MRI scoring system was developed by incorporating the significant signs from the standard O-RADS MRI system. This study retrospectively enrolled the 176 adnexal masses in cohort A. MRI imaging features were compared between benign and malignant tumors within this cohort.

title: Clinical, neurophysiological evaluation and genetic features of axonal Charcot–Marie–Tooth disease in a Chinese family
creator: Li Cao, Jie Yang, Xiaohuan Zhang, Xu Wang, Zhangyuwei Chen, Song Tan, Jiyun Yang
description: Charcot–Marie–Tooth disease (CMT) is a group of inherited peripheral neuropathies related to variants in the mitochondrial transfer RNA (mt-tRNAval) gene. Here, we report a Chinese family harboring the m.1661A>G variant in the mt-tRNAval gene. Clinical evaluation, neuroelectrodiagnostic testing, and nerve biopsy were performed on four affected family members.

title: Temporal and production-related determinants of microbial counts in pingo, the natural starter culture of minas artisanal cheese
creator: Gustavo Augusto Lacorte, Daniel Arantes Pereira, Joao Paulo Andrade de Araújo, Danielle Stornino de Freitas, Gabriel Henrique Oliveira Silva, Jaqueline Flaviana Oliveira de Sá, Jonas e Silva Guimarães, Milene Therezinha das Dores, Fernanda Faria Quadros
description: Minas Artisanal Cheese (MAC) is among the most widely consumed and recognized artisanal cheeses in Brazil, produced from raw milk, rennet, salt, and a natural starter culture known locally as pingo. Pingo is an endogenous starter culture generated by backslopping, which carries into MAC cheese both technologically beneficial microorganisms and spoilage contaminants.

title: Enhanced detection of network intrusions and anomalies in internet of things applications using a hybrid artificial intelligence model combining CNN and LSTM
creator: Bharathi Subramaniam, Sudhakar Sengan, Julian L. Webber, Abolfazl Mehbodniya, Meshal Ghalib Alharbi, Majed Alsafyani, Ahmed Emara
description: The rapid development of the internet of things (IoT) has made an increasing number of large-scale, interconnected networks more vulnerable to advanced attacks. There are increased risks of hidden intrusions and compromised security in IoT environments, resulting from class imbalance in network traffic datasets, high-dimensional feature spaces, and the requirement for spatial and temporal anomaly detection.

title: Maternal deaths and severe maternal morbidity in the Nordic countries—Time to build collaborative routine surveillance and shared learning to improve healthcare
creator: Hilde Marie Engjom, Outi Äyräs, Anna Aabakke, Eva Jonasdottir, Teresia Svanvik, Lill Nyfløt
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ans and epidemiologists in the five Nordic countries: Denmark, Finland, Iceland, Norway, and Sweden and aim to describe causes of maternal deaths and severe morbidity and facilitate joint learning to improve clinical obstetric care in the Nordic countries. The Nordic collaborations participate jointly in the International Network of Obstetric Survey Systems (INOSS) with other countries in Europe, North America, Africa, and Asia.

title: Chewing lice of wild birds in Iran: new data and a checklist of avian louse species reported in Iran
creator: Zahra Bahiraei, Alireza Sazmand, Javad Khedri, Mohammad Babaei, Erfan Moeinifard, Bilal Dik
description: Between September 2019 and December 2023, a total of 612 wild birds representing 16 orders, 33 families, 60 genera, and 78 species from nine provinces of Iran with different climates namely Hamedan (n = 54), Sistan-va-Baluchestan (n = 372), Kerman (n = 73), South Khorasan (n = 52), Mazandaran (n = 7), Chaharmahal-va-Bakhtiari (n = 2), Gilan (n = 2),

title: Correction: Lactic acid bacteria, potentially probiotic, in whole-grain pet biscuits: survival and technological potential of millet-based formulations (Pennisetum glaucum)
creator: Wendy Carla Dantas Rocha, Isabel Luísa Ribeiro de Abreu Teixeira, Maria Eduarda Costa Campos, Taynan Jonatha Neves Costa, Isabella Maciel Costa, Debora Cristina Sampaio de Assis, Felipe Machado Trombete, Washington Azevedo da Silva, Erika Ramos de Alvarenga, Fabiola de Oliveira Paes Leme, Verônica O

title: Transformer enhanced based YOLOv8 integration: a hybrid deep learning framework for intelligent insulator defect detection in high-voltage transmission systems
creator: Umer Farooq, Fan Yang, Jamshed Ali Shaikh
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Insulators are vital components of high-voltage power transmission systems, where undetected defects can lead to catastrophic failures and significant economic losses. Accurate and timely detection of insulator defects (IDs) under diverse environmental conditions is critical for ensuring system reliability. This study presents Transformer-Enhanced YOLOv8 (TE-YOLOv8), a novel hybrid deep learning framework designed to address the challenges of detecting small, complex defects in transmission line inspections.

title: Identifying the 50 most productive researchers in top-tier, broad-scope educational psychology journals (2017–2022): a new perspective with a focus on publication trends and diversity
creator: Veit Kubik, Lena Keller, Lea Jaspers, Annika Koch, Vincent Hoogerheide, Julian Roelle
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The present study identified the most productive researchers in educational psychology by analyzing the number of published articles in top-tier and broad-scope educational psychology journals from 2017 to 2022. Building on prior productivity research, we extended the scope of the analysis in three distinct ways: (1) we expanded the sample to include the 50 most productive researchers; (2) we applied three different scoring methods to assess productivity; and (3) we used a broader and more objectively defined set of journals, based on

title: Effects of postmortem interval on myelin integrity in rhesus macaque brain tissue
creator: Anna Novoseltseva, Rhiannon Robinson, Peter Niziolek, Allen Jang, Ting Xie, Ankita Tiwari, Ayman Abdelhakeem, Raymond Nicks, Yvonne Lucas, Qiong Yang, Farzad Mortazavi, David Boas, Hui Wang, Tara L. Moore, Douglas L. Rosene, Irving J. Bigio
description: When conducting microscopy of human brain sections, the postmortem interval (PMI) introduces myelin‐related artifacts that can confound neuropathological interpretation, yet the extent and detectability of these changes remain poorly characterized. This study examined the impact of controlled PMI on myelin integrity in rhesus macaque brain tissue using advanced optical imaging approaches. Brains from five aged rhesus macaques (20.5–28.

title: Continuous DNA methylation deconvolution-based surrogate for B-cell differentiation state in chronic lymphocytic leukemia
creator: Jeffrey Hage, Lauren Wainman, Fiyinfoluwa Kolawole, Fred Kolling IV, Pauline Patzke, Daniel Schoolcraft, Sarah Spracklin, Prabhjot Kaur, Brock Christensen
description: BackgroundChronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) is clinically divided categorically into IGHV mutated (M-CLL) and IGHV unmutated (U-CLL) subtypes.
