Its low incidence and broad range of clinical signs and symptoms may mimic more common inflammatory and/or infectious processes, causing delays in accurate diagnosis and management with a resultant negative impact on clinical outcomes.

title: Co-inoculation of Trichoderma viride with Azospirillum brasilense could suppress the development of Harpophora maydis-infected maize in Egypt
creator: Rasha M. Elmeihy, Omar A. Hewedy, Maryam S. Alhumaidi, Khadijah A. Altammar, Eman O. Hassan, Samah A. El-Debaiky
description: Plant diseases caused by fungal pathogens are responsible for severe damage to strategic crops worldwide. Late wilt disease (LWD) is a vascular disease that occurs late in maize development. Harpophora maydis, the causative agent of maize LWD, is responsible for significant economic losses in Egypt.

title: The effects of pH on cortex and condensate formation
creator: Brooke E Waechtler, Chujun Liu, Bethany A Todd, Oiza Dimowo, Emma P Morin, Jasmine Barraza, Mashal Nawabi, Constance Campbell, Douglas N Robinson
description: Waechtler et al. discover that a pH differential between the actin cortical and cytoplasmic phases of the cell serves as one mechanism that controls actin cytoskeletal reorganization. Specifically, a pH gradient between these two phases may mediate the transition between cortex construction beneath the membrane and cytoskeletal protein condensate formation throughout the cytoplasm.

title: Comparing Real and Virtual Nature Exposure on Cognition, Well-Being, and Brain Activity in Adults With and Without Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder: Protocol for a Randomized Experimental Study
creator: Tianran Zhang, Dimitrios Adamis, Natasha Langan, Martin O’Neill, Javad Sarvestan, Jose Ferrer Costa, Nabi Nazari
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundNatural environments are associated with improved cognitive functioning and psychological well-being, potentially through attentional restoration and stress reduction. Virtual reality (VR) offers an accessible way to simulate natural settings; however, it remains unclear whether VR nature engages the brain and cognition in the same way as real nature, particularly in adults with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), who show atypical neural oscillations and heightened sensitivity to environmental demands.ObjectiveThis protocol describes a randomized experimental study designed to compare the effects of a single exposure to

title: Reporting of Telehealth Implementation in Cystic Fibrosis: Scoping Review Using a Novel Theory-Based Evaluation Lens
creator: Tamara Vagg, Robyn Doherty, Sarath C Ranganathan, Barry J Plant
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Specifically, dynamic covalent bonds trigger network reconstruction after thermal activation and enhance chain disentanglement, which promotes chain translocation in nanochannels.

creator: Catherine Wilkinson

Building flexibility into the research design of a study allows for responsiveness to the embodied and fluctuating nature of participants’ chronic illnesses, which may be shaped, for instance, by flare-ups and periods of remission of acute pain. Whilst the methodology literature has, to some extent, considered how to accommodate the pain of research participants when designing a study, consideration of how methodological choices are responsive to the researcher's pain needs has not to date been foregrounded.

title: Identification of key genes and signaling pathways associated with acute pancreatitis and acute lung injury by bioinformatics analysis
creator: Lingfeng Chen, Fengzhu Guo, Chunlin Hong

Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were screened.

Systemic autoinflammatory diseases (SAIDs) are disorders of innate immunity, which are characterized by unprovoked recurrent flares of systemic inflammation often characterized by fever associated with clinical manifestations mainly involving the musculoskeletal, mucocutaneous, gastrointestinal, and nervous systems. Several conditions also present with varied, sometimes prominent, involvement of the vascular system, with features of vasculitis characterized by variable target vessel involvement and organ damage. Here, we report a systematic review of vasculitis and vasculopathy associated with inborn errors of immunity.

title: Machine learning prediction of obesity-associated gut microbiota: identifying Bifidobacterium pseudocatenulatum as a potential therapeutic target

title: TIME FOR COFFEE coordinates phase separation and chromatin regulation for salt tolerance
creator: Wenwen Tian, Xinheng Lyu, Grace R. Qian, Xuehua Zhong
description: The circadian clock enhances plant fitness by aligning internal timing with the external photoperiod, but how it coordinates spatiotemporal regulation with chromatin dynamics to improve salt tolerance is not well understood. Here, we show that the clock component TIME FOR COFFEE (TIC) forms biomolecular condensates in response to salt stress, but not to osmotic stress alone.

title: Local control of Cre-regulated genetic modeling in vivo using wireless implantable optoelectronics
creator: Trisha Bansal, Min-Kyu Lee, Courtney Coleman, Young-Mee Kim, Dane Hintermueller, Yaner Chen, Varsha Sreekanth, Chad R. Haney, Olga A. Karginova, Raudel Avila, Jacob Matsche, Shaluah Vijeth, Farah Yousef, Kento Yamagishi, Jiheon Kang, Kaitlyn Mowry, Minsung Kim, Sophianne Loh, Sachin Clark, Huong Huy
description: Effective modeling of chronic human diseases in vivo requires precise spatiotemporal regulation of molecular processes at defined tissue locations. Optogenetic and optoelectronic tools can provide such control but targeting internal organs such as the lungs remain challenging. To address this, we developed E-LightR-Cre recombinase, enabling precise, spatially restricted gene activation with no dark-state activity and robust blue light responsiveness.

title: Exploratory research on drugs after lung surgery based on real-world data from the FDA adverse event reporting system database
creator: Qiaoling Pan, Hang Chen, Hanbo Pan, Zeyang Hu, Keyue Qiu, Jiaheng Zhang, Ni Li, Yinyu Mu, Keyun Zhu, Guodong Xu, Yiming Shen
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundsLung surgery is the most common surgery in thoracic surgery, but postoperative dyspnea, cough, palpitations, and chest pain seriously affect the quality of life of patients and hinder their postoperative recovery.MethodsTo reveal the potential correlation between drugs and adverse events, we used disproportionation analysis to calculate the ROR and PRR values of the top 30 reported cases of dyspnea, cough, palpitations, and chest pain, respectively.

title: Social determinants of mental health in asthma: an exploratory study
creator: Sarah A. Hiles, Hayley Lewthwaite, Vanessa L. Clark, Anne E. Vertigan, Amber Smith, Vanessa M. McDonald
description: IntroductionAsthma and mental health problems co-occur at high rates. In context of a holistic approach to health, considering the extent to which social determinants relate to mental health in people with asthma helps identify health inequity and inform population-level preventative strategies.

title: Rising global population coexposure to heatwaves and landscape fire-sourced air pollution
creator: Yao Wu, Rongbin Xu, Bo Wen, Lidia Morawska, Michael J Abramson, Fay H. Johnston, Wenhua Yu, Gongbo Chen, Yiwen Zhang, Zhihu Xu, Wenzhong Huang, Zhengyu Yang, Pei Yu, Shuang Zhou, Yanming Liu, Tingting Ye, Xu Yue, Shanshan Li, Yuming Guo
description: Landscape fires are increasingly threatening public health by causing substantial fire-sourced air pollution (SFAP), with risks amplified during heatwaves. We investigated the global spatial, temporal, and sociodemographic distribution of the population coexposure to heatwaves and SFAP from 2000 to 2019. We found that 52.4% of populated areas and 55.9% of the global population experienced increasing coexposure.

title: Distinct early-life mechanisms of quantity discrimination in domestic chicks
creator: Maria Loconsole, Elisa Tedaldi, Lucia Regolin, Lesley Rogers, Lesley Rogers, Lesley Rogers, Lesley Rogers
description: In research on animal numerical cognition, newly hatched domestic chicks have been shown to rely on distinct strategies when confronted with quantitative choices. In some conditions, such as after imprinting on a specific set of objects, chicks preferentially approach the larger set of familiar items, indicating sensitivity to magnitude.

title: False memories and biased judgments for physical touch: the role of misinformation on eyewitness reports
creator: Fabiana Battista, Tiziana Lanciano, Pasquale Zappimpulso, Federico Puleo, Ivan Mangiulli, Antonietta Curci
description: IntroductionMemory is a reconstructive process susceptible to external influences. The misinformation effect, extensively studied in eyewitness testimony, refers to the distortion of post-event information upon memory recall. However, limited research has examined how misinformation influences memory along with evaluation of an event involving physical touch.

title: Editorial Note: Detection of relapsing fever Borrelia spp., Bartonella spp. and Anaplasmataceae bacteria in argasid ticks in Algeria
creator: The
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). opical Diseases’ research ethics policies. Specifically, the Materials and methods section of [1] reports that ticks were collected between May 2012 and October 2015. Furthermore, the article reports that the sampling locations involved a variety of natural and human-impacted habitats, and included rodent burrows in farms, yellow-legged gull nests (after the nesting period ended), and “other animal shelters,” located in Mostaganem, Algiers, El Tarf, and M’sil (Algeria).

title: A B1 SINE element within the mouse Malat1 long noncoding RNA acts as an internal ribosome entry site mediating micropeptide translation
creator: Wen Xiao, Tanja Hann, Zion Perry, Vijaya Pandey, Jeffrey Cheng, James Wohlschlegel, Anna Marie Pyle, Douglas L. Black
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). In most cells, Malat1 long noncoding RNA localizes to the nucleus where it affects splicing and chromatin function. In mouse neurons, Malat1 is exported to the cytoplasm where it is translated to generate the M1 micropeptide. Here, we characterize an internal ribosome entry site (IRES) required for M1 translation that is sufficient to induce cap-independent expression of a downstream open reading frame.

title: Cytogenetics of Neotropical fishes: Patterns, advances and prospects after five decades of research
creator: Mauro Nirchio, Claudio Oliveira
description: This review synthesizes the most significant advances and innovations in the cytogenetic study of Neotropical fishes, with emphasis on recurrent chromosomal patterns, evolutionary mechanisms, and the integration of modern genomic tools. The Neotropical region, which harbors more than 12,000 fish species, exhibits not only extraordinary taxonomic richness but also remarkable chromosomal diversity.

title: Context association in pyramidal neurons through local synaptic plasticity in apical dendrites
creator: Maximilian Baronig, Robert Legenstein
description: The unique characteristics of neocortical pyramidal neurons are thought to be crucial for many aspects of information processing and learning in the brain. Experimental data suggests that their segregation into two distinct compartments, the basal dendrites close to the soma and the apical dendrites branching out from the thick apical dendritic tuft, plays an essential role in cortical organization.

title: 3D-printed hip prostheses with regenerative integration: a state-of-the-art comprehensive review
creator: Sebastián Giraldo Gallego, Luis Eduardo Rodríguez Cheu
description: This article offers an in-depth review of the design and modeling of 3D-printed hip prostheses, emphasizing the integration of regenerative medicine, especially in the context of custom Rapidly Destructive Osteoarthritis implants. It traces the history of Total hip arthroplasty and current implant materials, along with recent advances in tissue engineering strategies and biofunctionalization methods to enhance biological integration.

title: A new taxonomy of neuroprotective agents for stroke appropriate for the reperfusion era
creator: Mersedeh Bahr-Hosseini, Jeffrey L. Saver
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The advent of the era of highly effective reperfusion therapy for acute ischemic stroke has reawakened interest in neuroprotective treatments as they are far more likely to be efficacious as synergistic complements to reperfusion rather than standalone interventions. However, testing neuroprotective agents combined with reperfusion mandates not only renewed conduct of trials but also a fundamental reconceptualization of the subclasses of neuroprotection therapies.

title: The influence of age and gender on self-assessment of piano competencies
creator: Chen Chen, Wen Lin
description: IntroductionThis study examined how pianists assess their own abilities in four areas: technical proficiency, musical understanding, expressive control, and presentation skills.MethodsParticipants included piano students and professional pianists, all with at least ten years of experience. Results were compared across age and gender groups. The study involved 600 participants divided into three age groups: 13- to 15-year-olds (M = 14.

title: Fecal bacteria-free filtrate transplantation is proved as an effective way for the recovery of radiation-induced individuals in mice
creator: Hang Zhang, Miaomiao Dong, Jixia Zheng, Yapeng Yang, Jinhui He, Tianhao Liu, Hong Wei
description: BackgroundIonizing radiation can cause intestinal microecological dysbiosis, resulting in changes in the composition and function of gut microbiota. Altered gut microbiota is closely related to the development and progression of radiation-induced intestinal damage. Although microbiota-oriented therapeutic options such as fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) have shown some efficacy in treating radiation toxicity, safety concerns endure.

title: Design and Development of ‘Building Opportunities for Optimal physical activity Skills Training in children with Down Syndrome (BOOST‐DS)’ Programme and its Content Validation through Consensus using Modified Delphi method
creator: V. Megha Jain, Bhamini K. Rao, Selvam Ramachandran, Delphi Expert Panel, B. S. Santhosh Kanna, Deepalaxmi Paresh Poojari, Deepa Metgud, Kirti Joshi, Mithula Vijaykumar, Radhika Attal, Rajitha Alva, Sanjay Tejraj Parmar, Shreekanth D. Karnad, Smitha Elizabeth Joseph, Tanochni Mohanty
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundChildren with Down syndrome (DS) often do not meet daily physical activity requirements, which affects their participation in daily activities and overall quality of life. Structured physical activity programmes could address these issues, but accessible, participation‐based activities are limited.MethodThe Building Opportunities for Optimal physical activity Skills Training in children with Down Syndrome (BOOST‐DS) programme was designed, developed and content validated in three phases.

title: The principles of tactical formation identification in association football (soccer) — a survey
creator: Hadi Sotudeh
description: This paper reviews the principles employed to identify team tactical formations in association football, covering over two decades of research based on event and tracking data. It first defines formations and discusses their history and importance. It then introduces the preprocessing and team/position-level principles.

title: Targeting health-related quality of life issues not found with functional outcome measures a year after aneurysm subarachnoid hemorrhage in a Swedish national cohort
creator: Helena Aineskog, Bryndís Baldvinsdóttir, Ola G Nilsson, Asgeir S Jakola, Erik Kronvall, Elisabeth Ronne Engström, Paula Klurfan, Peter Alpkvist, Mikael Svensson, Jan Hillman, Peter Lindvall
description: PurposeOutcome after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH) is often devastating with life time issues also for independent survivors. We aimed to identify health related quality of life (HRQoL) issues in this favorable functional outcome group compared to a sex and age matched general population.

title: Developing national meta-accreditation standards for medical education accreditation bodies in Iran: a mixed-methods standards development and consensus study
creator: Tahereh Sabouri Aghbolagh Rostam Khan, Tahereh Changiz, Azim Mirzazadeh, Marta van Zanten, Nikoo Yamani
description: Ensuring the quality and credibility of medical education systems increasingly depends on robust accreditation mechanisms, yet the performance of accreditation bodies themselves often remains insufficiently evaluated. Addressing this gap, this study developed and validated the first national meta-accreditation standards for Iran’s Ministry of Health and Medical Education.

title: Ustekinumab in the Management of Perianal Fistulizing Crohn’s Disease: Current Evidence and Practical Strategies
creator: Bolin Yang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Perianal fistulizing Crohn’s disease (PFCD) is a severe and complex manifestation associated with high morbidity and limited treatment durability. Ustekinumab is a monoclonal antibody targeting the interleukin-12/23 pathway, which is involved in the pathogenesis of PFCD. Evidence from post hoc analyses and real-world studies has shown the therapeutic potential of ustekinumab in both anti-tumor necrosis factor-experienced and selected biologic-naïve patients with PFCD.

title: Machine learning uncovers previously undetectable genetic deletions in cancer panel sequencing
creator: Irina A Kerle, Oleksandr Husak, Thomas Gross, Andreas Hartig, Rebecca Prause, Daniela Richter, Sascha Brückmann, Maximilian Werner, Anja Kögler, Dorothea Hanf, Lino Möhrmann, Doreen William, Karsten Wendt, Nicole Pfarr, Carolin Mogler, Daniela E Aust, Evelin Schröck, Christoph Heining, Hanno Glimm
description: Missed genetic deletions can prevent cancer patients from receiving effective targeted therapy. Standard pipelines, such as TSO500, use bin count averaging for copy number variation detection but often overlook focal events. To address this, we developed a machine learning (ML) pipeline for deletion detection and zygosity evaluation within the MASTERsg precision oncology program.

title: Phylogenetic and functional analysis of tiller angle control homeologs in allotetraploid cotton
creator: Foster Kangben, Sonika Kumar, Zhigang Li, Avinash Sreedasyam, Chris Dardick, Don Jones, Christopher A. Saski
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). IntroductionPlants can adapt their growth to optimize light capture in competitive environments, with branch angle being a crucial factor influencing plant phenotype and physiology. Decreased branch angles in cereal crops have been shown to enhance productivity in high-density plantings. The Tiller Angle Control (TAC1) gene, known for regulating tiller inclination in rice and corn, has been found to control branch angle in eudicots.

title: The endogenous hydrogen gas (H2) drives women’s health: a comment on “Gut bacteria convert glucocorticoids into progestins in the presence of hydrogen gas”
creator: Shuangling Yang, Jiongshan Zhang, Luyao Xu, Yajie Guan, Chun Fang, Shuhui Zheng, Hongzhi Yang, Haimei Liu, Yaxing Zhang
description: ological significance of endogenous H2 is not clear. In the recent issue of Cell, McCurry et al. reveal that endogenous H2 drives 21-dehydroxylation for transforming glucocorticoids to progestins, which may further influence female health, such as postpartum depression (1). We are very interested in this milestone study that reveals the physiological effects of endogenous H2.

title: Viral load kinetics and the clinical consequences of cytomegalovirus in kidney transplantation
creator: Sabina Dobrer, Karen R. Sherwood, Ishan Hirji, James Lan, John Gill, Nancy Matic, Paul A. Keown
description: BackgroundDespite advances in clinical management, cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection remains a serious complication and an important cause of morbidity and mortality following kidney transplantation. Here, we explore the importance of viral load kinetics as predictors of risk and potential guides to therapy to reduce transplant failure in a large longitudinal Genome Canada Transplant Consortium (GCTC) kidney transplant cohort.

title: Drivers of invertebrate community structure in a high-volume Neotropical cave system: a newly recognized subterranean biodiversity hotspot
creator: Gabriel Augusto Silva Vaz, Rodrigo Lopes Ferreira, Marconi Souza-Silva
description: Understanding how niche-based and neutral processes shape biological communities is a central objective in ecology, particularly in extreme and poorly explored environments such as large subterranean systems. Here, we investigated the mechanisms structuring terrestrial invertebrate communities in the one of the most extensive and voluminous cave systems in South America.

title: Long-term effects of voice training and swallowing function exercises on postoperative functional recovery in laryngeal cancer patients: a retrospective cohort study
creator: Jing Liu, Gaiping Fan, Wenjuan Li
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveTo investigate the long-term effects of combined voice training and swallowing function exercises on functional recovery, quality of life, and complications in patients after laryngeal cancer surgery.MethodsIn this retrospective cohort study, 120 patients who underwent laryngeal cancer surgery between June 2019 and June 2023 were divided into a rehabilitation group (n = 60, receiving systematic voice and swallowing training) and a routine care group (n = 60).

title: Genome-wide genetic architecture for plant maturity and drought tolerance in diploid potatoes
creator: Bourlaye Fofana, Braulio Soto-Cerda, Moshin Zaidi, David Main, Sherry Fillmore
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Cultivated potato (Solanum tuberosum) is known to be highly susceptible to drought. With climate change and its frequent episodes of drought, potato growers will face increased challenges to achieving their yield goals. Currently, a high proportion of untapped potato germplasm remains within the diploid potato relatives, and the genetic architecture of the drought tolerance and maturity traits of diploid potatoes is still unknown.

title: Local endoreduplication of the host is a conserved process during Phytomyxea–host interaction
creator: Michaela Hittorf, Andrea Garvetto, Marianne Magauer, Martin Kirchmair, Willibald Salvenmoser, Pedro Murúa, Sigrid Neuhauser
description: BackgroundEndoreduplication, a modified cell cycle, involves cells duplicating DNA without undergoing mitosis. This phenomenon is frequently observed in plants, algae, and animals. Biotrophic pathogens have been demonstrated to induce endoreduplication in plants to secure more space or nutrients.MethodsIn this study, we investigated the endoreduplication process triggered by two phylogenetically distant Rhizaria organisms—Maullinia spp.

title: Primary gastrinoma of the gallbladder: a case report and review of the literature
creator: Yao-Ge Liu, Shi-Tao Jiang, Yang Zhou, Jun-Wei Zhang, Xin-Ting Sang, Lei Zhang, Xin Lu, Yi-Yao Xu
description: BackgroundPrimary gallbladder gastrinoma is an exceptionally uncommon tumor and is a rare form of neuroendocrine neoplasm. Until now, no cases of primary gallbladder gastrinoma and rare cases of primary gastrinoma from the biliary system have been reported.Case presentationWe report a case of a 50-year-old woman with watery diarrhea who intermittently received proton pump inhibitors (PPIs) as treatment.

title: Effects of a cardiac rehabilitation program on anthropometric and functional parameters: an observational pre-post study
creator: Estrella García-Sánchez, Mirian Santamaría-Peláez, Jerónimo J González-Bernal, Josefa González-Santos, Jessica Fernández-Solana, Rodrigo Vélez-Santamaría
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionCardiac rehabilitation is a multidisciplinary intervention designed to improve functional capacity and quality of life in patients with cardiovascular diseases. However, its impact on anthropometric and functional parameters remains an important area of study.

title: Racial disparities in metastatic colorectal cancer outcomes revealed by tumor microbiome and transcriptome analysis with bevacizumab treatment
creator: Lei Feng, Rui Wang, Qian Zhao, Jun Wang, Gang Luo, Chongwen Xu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background: Metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) is a heterogeneous disease, often associated with poor outcomes and resistance to therapies. The racial variations in the molecular and microbiological profiles of mCRC patients, however, remain under-explored. Methods: Using RNA-SEQ data, we extracted and analyzed actively transcribing microbiota within the tumor milieu, ensuring that the identified bacteria were not merely transient inhabitants but engaged in the tumor ecosystem.

title: A functional SNP of the core promoter region within goat CDC25A gene affects litter size
creator: Taiyuan Zhang, Jingxuan Wang, Yangyang Bai, Qian Wang, Ke Wang, Haijing Zhu, Lei Qu, Zhengang Guo, Chuanying Pan, Xianyong Lan
description: The Cell division cycle 25A (CDC25A) gene has been considered as a candidate gene associated with reproductive traits for goat breeding. In this study, five truncated fragments divided at position-2285 nt to +198 nt were amplified and cloned into the luciferase reporter vectors to identify the core promoter.

title: Obesity- and lipid-related indices as a predictor of type 2 diabetes in a national cohort study
creator: Ying Wang, Xiaoyun Zhang, Yuqing Li, Jiaofeng Gui, Yujin Mei, Xue Yang, Haiyang Liu, Lei-lei Guo, Jinlong Li, Yunxiao Lei, Xiaoping Li, Lu Sun, Liu Yang, Ting Yuan, Congzhi Wang, Dongmei Zhang, Jing Li, Mingming Liu, Ying Hua, Lin Zhang
description: ObjectiveType 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) remains a major and widespread public health concern throughout the world. The prevalence of T2DM in the elderly has risen to the top of the list of public health concerns. In this study, obesity- and lipid-related indices were used to predict T2DM in middle-aged and elderly Chinese adults.

title: Identifying natural inhibitors against FUS protein in dementia through machine learning, molecular docking, and dynamics simulation
creator: Darwin Li
description: Dementia, a complex and debilitating spectrum of neurodegenerative diseases, presents a profound challenge in the quest for effective treatments. The FUS protein is well at the center of this problem, as it is frequently dysregulated in the various disorders. We chose a route of computational work that involves targeting natural inhibitors of the FUS protein, offering a novel treatment strategy.

title: Diagnostic challenges of masked arginine vasopressin deficiency in neurosarcoidosis complicated by sodium–glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitor use
creator: Ryohei Nonaka, Katsuhiro Tanaka, Akemi Tomimoto, Yukie Nagai, Takuya Nomura, Hirotaka Shibata
description: A wide variety of endocrine disorders caused by sarcoidosis have been reported to date. We report the case of an 82-year-old male patient who presented with hypercalcemia and anterior pituitary hormone deficiency at the time of his sarcoidosis diagnosis and was subsequently diagnosed with arginine vasopressin deficiency (AVP-D) 6 months after the initiation of glucocorticoid therapy.

title: The role of bovine colostrum in feeding intolerance in preterm neonates: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
creator: Jia Yao, Bo Zheng, Jie Zhang, Fen Xu, Jianbo Zhuang
description: BackgroundFeeding intolerance is common in preterm infants and may lead to poor weight gain and prolonged hospitalization. Bovine colostrum, owing to its rich content of bioactive components such as immunoglobulins, lactoferrin, and growth factors, has been suggested to reduce feeding intolerance and promote gut maturation in preterm infants; however, available clinical trials provide inconsistent evidence regarding its efficacy.

title: Preoperative Total Iron‐Binding Capacity Is a Potential Surrogate Marker of Long‐Term Outcomes After Pancreatectomy for Pancreatic Cancer
creator: Taishi Yamane, Hiromitsu Hayashi, Hiroshi Sawayama, Takashi Matsumoto, Toru Takematsu, Takanobu Yamao, Yuki Kitano, Tatsunori Miyata, Hirohisa Okabe, Masaaki Iwatsuki
description: BackgroundThis study aimed to examine whether preoperative serum total iron‐binding capacity (TIBC), which is directly proportional to transferrin level, correlates with long‐term outcomes after pancreatectomy.MethodsPreoperative TIBC levels, calculated by summing serum iron and unsaturated iron binding capacity, were evaluated in 158 patients who underwent pancreatectomy for pancreatic cancer.

title: Dietary supplementation with microbially fermented rice bran promotes lactation performance in dairy cows by increasing rumen fermentation performance and nutrient digestibility
creator: Zixiao Zhang, Wanhao Cai, Xiaoshi Wei, Bo He, Yanze Liu, Xiaowei Zhang, Jinyong Yang, Fusheng Li, Zhefeng Li, Chong Wang
description: IntroductionMicrobial fermentation effectively addresses the issue of rice bran rancidity also enhances its nutritional value as animal feed. This study aimed to explore the effects of dietary microbially fermented rice bran feed (MFRB) supplementation on lactation performance, nutrient digestibility, plasma biochemical indicators, rumen fermentation parameters and microbiota of lactating dairy cows.MethodsThirty Holstein cows with similar milk yield (38.1 ± 1.

title: Finerenone in Cardiorenal Disease: A Narrative Review of Molecular Mechanisms, Clinical Evidence, and Emerging Therapeutic Roles
creator: Giulio Geraci, Nicola Sinatra, Valentina Paternò, Vincenzo Calabrese, Giuliano Cassataro, Giuseppe Cuttone, Calogero Geraci, Roberta Esposito, Costantino Mancusi, Giacomo Pucci, Luca Zanoli, Giuseppe Mulè, Riccardo Polosa, Pietro Ferrara, Caterina Carollo
description: Cardiorenal disease reflects a tightly interconnected pathophysiological continuum driven by neurohormonal activation, inflammation, oxidative stress, and progressive fibrosis. Among these mechanisms, mineralocorticoid receptor (MR) overactivation has emerged as a central mediator of cardiac and renal injury independent of blood pressure effects.

title: What Keeps Older Adults Moving? An Analysis of Barriers and Motivation Across Different Exercise Settings
creator: Bruno Fernando de Souza Tavares, Eduardo Quadros da Silva, Grazieli Covre da Silva, Sonia Maria Marques Gomes Bertolini, José Roberto Andrade do Nascimento, Daniel Vicentini de Oliveira
description: Perceived barriers and motivational factors may influence the adherence of older adults to physical exercise. Considering these variables, this study investigated the association between barriers and motivation for physical exercise among older adults. This cross-sectional study included 225 older adults engaged in physical exercise at private gyms, senior fitness centers, and sports centers in Maringá, Paraná, Brazil.

title: Dual-attention bidirectional LSTM with feature genomic analysis improves prognostic survival prediction in colorectal cancer patients
creator: Zhuochao Wu, Xueping Tan, Dinghui Wu, Min Tao, Chaoqun Li, Rongrui Liang
description: The increasing incidence and mortality rates of colorectal cancer necessitate accurate prediction of patients’ prognostic survival time for better management, early screening, and extended lifespan. This study uses the TCGA public dataset to conduct differential analysis on lncRNAs in 39 diseased tissues and their normal counterparts from 413 colorectal cancer patient samples, identifying 458 differentially expressed lncRNAs (DELncRNAs).

title: Astragaloside IV and Ferroptosis Modulation in Pathological Cardiac Hypertrophy: Current Evidence, an Integrative Hypothesis, and Future Directions
creator: Pengbo Liu, Yongzhi Deng
description: Pathological cardiac hypertrophy is initially an adaptive response to sustained mechanical, neurohormonal, or metabolic stress; however, it can progress to fibrosis, contractile dysfunction, arrhythmia, and heart failure. Ferroptosis is a type of regulated cell death caused by iron‐dependent phospholipid peroxidation.

title: Brachial artery access for endovascular procedures: how safe is it?
creator: Lucy Rose Howroyd, Arjan Singh Khattar, Hoi-Ying Claudia Tam, Robert Morgan, Joo-Young Chun
description: PurposeWhile femoral and radial artery access are routine for endovascular procedures, brachial artery access remains an important alternative in selected cases. This study aimed to evaluate the complication rate of percutaneous brachial artery access at a tertiary centre and identify potential risk factors for access-site complications.

title: RPRD1A drives lenvatinib resistance in hepatocellular carcinoma via the ITGA5-FAK signaling axis
creator: Xiaomeng Yao, Yunkai Lin, Pingping Chen, Mengyou Xu, Mengmiao Pei, Xinru Fan, Huibo Feng, Xinhao Xing, Jiaqi Guo, Yang Liu, Xinzhu Quan, Yufei Pan, Yexiong Tan, Huabang Zhou, Liwei Dong, Hui Wang, Heping Hu
description: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) constitutes a formidable global health challenge. Lenvatinib, a multi-targeted tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI), has gradually become a cornerstone therapeutic agent for advanced HCC; however, the emergence of drug resistance severely compromises its clinical efficacy and remains a major obstacle to improving patient outcomes.

title: Radiomics in sporadic microsatellite instable, mismatch repair deficient and Lynch syndrome-associated pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma: a pilot study
creator: Ellis L. Eikenboom, Joséphine Magnin, Remo Alessandris, Natally Horvat, Mithat Gonen, William R. Jarnagin, Jeffrey Drebin, Michael I. D’Angelica, T. Peter Kingham, Vinod P. Balachandran, Kevin C. Soares, Anja Wagner, Manon C. W. Spaander, Jayasree Chakraborty, Alice C. Wei
description: IntroductionPancreatic cancer, mostly presenting as pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), has a poor prognosis. The microsatellite-instable (MSI-H)/mismatch repair deficient (MMRd) subtype, however, is more susceptible to immune therapy and is expected to have a better prognosis. Presently, MSI-testing is not routinely performed on PDAC. We assessed whether quantitative imaging features (radiomics) of pretreatment computed tomography (CT) scans could diagnose MSI-H/MMRd.

title: Exploration of the anti-inflammatory potential of Polygonum bistorta L.: protection against LPS-induced acute lung injury in rats via NF-ĸβ pathway inhibition
creator: Sajida Parveen, Kashif ur Rehman Khan, Shahid Muhammad Iqbal, Hanan Y. Aati, Areej M. Al-taweel, Liaqat Hussain, Musaddique Hussain
description: Traditional medicine uses the roots and rhizomes of Polygonum bistorta L. (Polygonaceae) to treat cough, bronchitis, and other respiratory infections. Our goal was to gain insights into the lung protective effects of the roots of P. bistorta L. against lipopolysaccharide-induced acute lung injury in rats, along with the possible mechanism(s).

title: Estimating marginal effects with zero-inflated models: A tutorial with the R package mzim
creator: Chendong Li, Oi-Man Kwok, Timothy Lawrence
description: Count data in the psychological and health sciences are often characterized by an excess of zero values, a feature known as zero inflation. While traditional zero-inflated models, such as the zero-inflated Poisson (ZIP) and zero-inflated negative binomial (ZINB), were developed to handle such data, they present challenges for applied researchers.

title: Immuno-neural mechanisms in gastrointestinal tumorigenesis: bridging inflammation, neural regulation, and therapeutic innovation
creator: Yan Zhao, Ji-feng Sui, Dong-ning Wu, Min Chen, Jin-xia Ni, Yue Zhang, Shi-yong Xin, Meng-Nan Fan
description: Gastrointestinal (GI) tumors remain a leading cause of global cancer mortality, with late-stage diagnosis and metastatic dissemination posing major clinical challenges. This review synthesizes current understanding of the intricate interplay between immune regulation, neural signaling, and tumor microenvironment dynamics in GI malignancies. We highlight how chronic inflammation, driven by pathogens like H.

title: Who you gonna call? Examining police reports involving people with psychosis to improve front line management
creator: George Karystianis, Freya Stephenson, Patricia Taflan, Sharon Reutens, Ed Heffernan, Tony Butler
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundIn New South Wales (NSW), Australia, police respond to mental health related events every nine minutes, sometimes resulting in negative outcomes, including arrest, use of force and death.MethodsIn this exploratory study, we manually analyzed 100 “patient” narratives (i.e., narratives with the involvement type for the suspected individual set by police as “patient”) to describe police encounters with individuals reported to have psychotic disorders in NSW from 2017 to 2021 to identify the reasons for police involvement, arrest circumstances, and outcomes.ResultsOf 100 events,

title: Clinical profile of microsporidial keratoconjunctivitis in healthy individuals of China —new species and neglected risk factors
creator: Yingnan Xu, Xuguang Sun, Shanshan Xu, Shijing Deng, Yang Zhang
description: ObjectiveTo characterize microsporidial keratoconjunctivitis (MKC) in immunocompetent individuals in Mainland China, including novel etiologies and risk factors.MethodsA prospective analysis of 20 MKC patients in 2025, including clinical features, pathogens (via corneal scrapings and metagenomic sequencing), risk factors and etc.ResultsAll patients were misdiagnosed for a median of 1 month. Patients (mean age 28.5 years, 13 F) showed Encephalitozoon hellem (65.0%), E.

title: Disruption of the thyroid hormone system and patterns of altered thyroid hormones after gestational chemical exposures in rodents – a systematic review
creator: Isabel Forner-Piquer, Asma H. Baig, Andreas Kortenkamp
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). We present a comprehensive overview of changes in thyroxine (T4) and thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH) serum concentrations after pre-gestational, gestational and/or lactation exposures of rodents to various chemicals that affect the thyroid hormone system. We show that T4 and TSH changes consistent with the idealized view of the hypothalamic-pituitary-thyroid (HPT) feedback loop (T4 decrements accompanied by TSH increases) are observed with only a relatively small set of chemicals. Most substances affect concentrations of various thyroid hormones without increasing TSH.

title: Combined Karyotyping, Copy Number Variation Sequencing, and Whole Exome Sequencing in the Prenatal Diagnosis of Congenital Heart Disease: Detection Rates and Phenotypic Associations
creator: Jieqiong Xie, Yanru Huang, Xingmei Yao, Lutan Zhang, Yixi Zhou, Wenbo Wang, Jian Zhang, Yunsheng Ge
description: ObjectiveThis study aimed to assess the value of genetic testing in the prenatal congenital heart disease (CHD) diagnosis and evaluate the relationship between genetic variants and prenatal phenotypes.MethodsA total of 235 fetuses with CHD were classified into three groups: A: isolated simple CHD, B: isolated complex CHD, and C: non‐isolated CHD.

title: Investigating synovial trace elements as diagnostic markers in acute septic arthritis: an exploratory study
creator: Alexia Leloix, Martine Ropert-Bouchet, Théau Cavillon, Marie-Laure Island, Olivier Loreal, Pascal Guggenbuhl, François Robin
description: ObjectivesAcute arthritis requires a precise and rapid diagnosis, particularly to rule out an infectious cause, which constitutes a rheumatologic emergency. Cytological, bacteriological, and microcrystal analyses do not always clearly differentiate causes. We hypothesized that variation in metal concentrations in synovial fluid could provide additional clues for etiological orientation. Our objective was to evaluate their diagnostic value in acute arthritis.

title: Ethnic and racial differences in self-reported symptoms, health status, activity level, and missed work at 3 and 6 months following SARS-CoV-2 infection
creator: Kelli N. O’Laughlin, Robin E. Klabbers, Imtiaz Ebna Mannan, Nicole L. Gentile, Rachel E. Geyer, Zihan Zheng, Huihui Yu, Shu-Xia Li, Kwun C. G. Chan, Erica S. Spatz, Ralph C. Wang, Michelle L’Hommedieu, Robert A. Weinstein, Ian D. Plumb, Michael Gottlieb, Ryan M. Huebinger, Melissa Hagen, Joann G. El
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). IntroductionData on ethnic and racial differences in symptoms and health-related impacts following SARS-CoV-2 infection are limited. We aimed to estimate the ethnic and racial differences in symptoms and health-related impacts 3 and 6 months after the first SARS-CoV-2 infection.MethodsParticipants included adults with SARS-CoV-2 infection enrolled in a prospective multicenter US study between 12/11/2020 and 7/4/2022 as the primary cohort of interest, as well as a SARS-CoV-2-negative cohort to account for non-SARS-CoV-2-infection impacts, who completed enrollment and 3-month surveys (N = 3,161; 2,402

title: Rehabilitation and Return to Play Protocols Following Osteochondral Autograft and Allograft Transplantation for Knee Chondral Lesions in Athletic Populations
creator: S Ryan Pierson, Richard M Silverman, Brock Knapp, Robert H Brophy
description: Purpose of ReviewOsteochondral autograft transplantation (OATS) and osteochondral allograft transplantation (OCA) are established cartilage restoration procedures for symptomatic chondral and osteochondral defects of the knee in athletes. Postoperative rehabilitation is central to graft healing and incorporation, functional recovery, and safe return to play (RTP).

title: Remote Video Assessment of Ataxia via SARAhome : Correlation of Pose‐Derived Endpoints with Clinician Severity Ratings
creator: Rabia Aziza, Elisa Ferrer, Fereshteh Poursaeed, Vivian Maas, Jennifer Faber, Arian Taheri Amin, Katharina Hill, Matthis Synofzik, Lisa H Graf, Dagmar Timmann, Andreas Thieme, Paola Giunti, Hector Garcia‐Moreno, Magda M Santana, Jeannette Hübener‐Schmid, Elin H Davies, Thomas Klockgether, Marcus Grob
description: BackgroundRemote assessment of ataxia is increasingly important for patient‐centered care and clinical research. SARAhome, a validated video‐based adaptation of the Scale for the Assessment and Rating of Ataxia (SARA), enables self‐administration of key motor tasks at home.ObjectiveThe aim was to evaluate the correlation of pose‐derived gait and stance endpoints from SARAhome videos with clinician‐rated severity.

title: Scalable network emulation on analog neuromorphic hardware
creator: Elias Arnold, Philipp Spilger, Jan V. Straub, Eric Müller, Dominik Dold, Gabriele Meoni, Johannes Schemmel
description: We present a novel software feature for the BrainScaleS-2 accelerated neuromorphic platform that facilitates the partitioned emulation of large-scale spiking neural networks. This approach is well suited for deep spiking neural networks and allows for sequential model emulation on undersized neuromorphic resources if the largest recurrent subnetwork and the required neuron fan-in fit on the substrate.

title: Health-related quality of life instruments in pediatric disorders of gut–brain interaction: a COSMIN-based systematic review
creator: Zehui Zhao, Yueyue Chen, Huiyu Zeng, Yuqi Fang, Siyuan Hu
description: BackgroundFunctional gastrointestinal disorders, now referred to as disorders of gut–brain interaction (DGBI), impose substantial functional and psychosocial burdens on affected children and their families. Health-related quality of life (HRQoL) has become an important patient-reported outcome in this field. This review aimed to systematically evaluate the measurement properties of instruments used to assess HRQoL in pediatric DGBI.

title: Cross-domain signal grammars of transcription termination
creator: Shouqing Hou, Hongru Ma, Xuye Lang, Yuan Yao
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Transcription termination establishes gene boundaries, recycles RNA polymerase, and prevents interference between neighboring transcription units. Termination depends on cis-acting elements, trans-acting factors, and the susceptibility of the elongation complex to pausing, cleavage, destabilization, or release. Predicted motifs, stable RNA ends, processing sites, readthrough regions, and polymerase-release regions are nevertheless often treated as measurements of the same event, which complicates mechanistic comparison and model development.

title: Multiple diffusion metrics in differentiating solid glioma from brain inflammation
creator: Kai Zhao, Ankang Gao, Eryuan Gao, Jinbo Qi, Ting Chen, Guohua Zhao, Gaoyang Zhao, Peipei Wang, Weijian Wang, Jie Bai, Yong Zhang, Huiting Zhang, Guang Yang, Xiaoyue Ma, Jingliang Cheng
description: Background and purposeThe differential diagnosis between solid glioma and brain inflammation is necessary but sometimes difficult. We assessed the effectiveness of multiple diffusion metrics of diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) in differentiating solid glioma from brain inflammation and compared the diagnostic performance of different DWI models.

title: Psoas Muscle Trajectory and Survival After Liver Transplantation for Steatotic Liver Disease in Severe Obesity
creator: Baila Elkin, Mohammad Alabbas, Qijun Yang, Blake Brandon, Christopher Coppa, Manal Abdelmalek, Omar T. Sims, Jamile Wakim-Fleming
description: BackgroundSarcopenia after liver transplantation is poorly characterized in recipients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and severe obesity. We evaluated longitudinal changes in psoas muscle index (PMI) after transplantation and examined whether PMI trajectory was associated with post-transplant survival.

title: Gross total resection and survival outcomes in elderly patients with spinal chordoma: a SEER-based analysis
creator: John Pham, Elias Shaaya, Ben Rhee, Anna Kimata, Evrim E. Ozcan, Katie M. Pham, Tianyi Niu, Patricia Sullivan, Ziya L. Gokaslan
description: ObjectiveThe association between aggressive resection and improved survival for adult spinal chordoma patients has not been well characterized in the geriatric population. Thus, the present study aimed to elucidate the relationship between gross total resection (GTR) and survival outcomes for patients across different age groups.

title: TFPI2 expression predicts resistance to immunotherapy plus tyrosine kinase inhibitor and informs first-line therapy selection in metastatic renal cell carcinoma
creator: Jiajun Wang, Lingzhi Du, Ying Wang, Hang Wang, Yanjun Zhu, Xianglai Xu
description: PurposeCombinations of anti-PD-1/PD-L1 immunotherapy (IO) and anti-VEGF tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) are recommended as first-line therapy for metastatic renal cell carcinoma (RCC). We aimed to evaluate the predictive value of tissue factor pathway inhibitor 2 (TFPI2) for IO + TKI response.

title: Validation of the immersion in digital life and quality of digital experience scales in German, French, Spanish, Polish and Czech
creator: Joanna Witowska, Christine Schoetensack, Katarzyna Goncikowska, Sébastien Chappuis, Mónica Fernández Boente, Tereza Klegr, Julie Papastamatelou, Rafael Valenzuela, Vanda Černohorská, Nuria Codina, Chantal Martin-Soelch, Marc Wittmann, José V. Pestana, Georgina Giner, Quentin Meteier, Ruth Ogden
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The Quality of Digital Experience Scale (QDES) and the Immersion in Digital Life Scale (IDLS) were developed to measure positive and negative experiences of digital technology use and the extent to which different facets of life were digital. Critically, the QDES and ILDS were developed to be independent of digital device or platform, thus providing a more holistic account of digital technology use than previous measures.

title: Observation of a supersolid phase in a spin-orbit coupled exciton-polariton Bose-Einstein condensate
creator: Marcin Muszyński, Pavel Kokhanchik, Rafał Mirek, Darius Urbonas, Pietro Tassan, Piotr Kapuściński, Przemysław Oliwa, Ioannis Georgakilas, Thilo Stöferle, Rainer F. Mahrt, Michael Forster, Ullrich Scherf, Dmitriy Dovzhenko, Rafał Mazur, Przemysław Morawiak, Wiktor Piecek, Przemysław Kula, Barbara Pię
description: In Bose-Einstein condensates, spin-orbit coupling (SOC) produces supersolidity. It is a peculiar state of matter, which, in addition to the superfluid behavior, shows periodic density modulation typical for crystals. Here, we report the fabrication of an original type of optical microcavity, allowing the achievement of room-temperature supersolidity for a quantum fluid of light.

title: Endometrial transcriptome profiling of patients with recurrent implantation failure during hormone replacement therapy cycles
creator: Wen-bi Zhang, Jue Li, Qing Li, Xiang Lu, Jun-ling Chen, Lu Li, Hua Chen, Wei Fu, Jiu-cheng Chen, Bing-jie Lu, Han Wu, Xiao-xi Sun
description: BackgroundThe molecular mechanisms underlying window of implantation (WOI) displacement in patients with recurrent implantation failure (RIF) remain unclear. This study aims to explore the transcriptomic signatures of endometrium with normal and displaced WOIs and to identify the causes of endometrial receptivity (ER) abnormalities and WOI displacement in RIF patients.

title: Automating data extraction in meta-research: A multi-model benchmark in network psychometrics papers
creator: Benjamin Simsa, Artem Buts, Ivan Ropovik, Matúš Adamkovič
description: Manual data extraction in meta-research is often tedious, time-consuming, and error-prone. In this paper, we investigate whether the current generation of large language models (LLMs) can be used to extract accurate information from scientific papers. Across the meta-research literature, these tasks usually range from extracting verbatim information (e.g.

title: Use of a wearable device to improve sleep quality
creator: Susan L. Moore, Evan P. Carey, Kristyna Finikiotis, Kelsey L. Ford, Richard D. Zane, Katherine K. Green
description: ObjectivesThe present study aimed to analyze the effects of the use of a digital wellness device on improving sleep through reducing environmental noise.MethodsFifty-five self-reported light or moderate sleepers with difficulty falling or staying asleep due to environmental noise participated in the study.

title: Inside the ‘Black Box’ of Pharmaceuticalisation: NICE, the Permissive Principle and the Case of Anticoagulants
creator: John Abraham, Gowree Balendran
description: Sociological interest in pharmaceuticalisation continues to grow, especially regarding the expansion of pharmaceutical use in society. This article presents the first major empirical study focusing on the directionality of pharmaceuticalisation by taking cost‐effectiveness assessment and regulation of anticoagulants in England by the National Institute of Health and Care Excellence (NICE) as a case study.

title: Comprehensive bioinformatics analysis of EXOSC family genes in lung adenocarcinoma
creator: Ning Li, Xiaolei Wang, Tingting Chu, Yongxin Pan, Xuezhong Zhang
description: The RNA exosome complex (EXOSC1-10) orchestrates 3’-5’ RNA processing and decay, yet its family-wide landscape and clinical relevance in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remain incompletely defined. Here, we conducted an integrative multi-omics analysis of EXOSC family members in LUAD using public transcriptomic and proteomic resources, external validation cohorts, and single-cell data. Across TCGA (59 normal vs.

title: Analytic attributes of the 16S rRNA gene sequencing methodology for human gut microbiota characterization
creator: Diego A. Rivera, Oscar J. Lara-Guzmán, N. Andrea Villota-Salazar, Jelver A. Sierra, Katalina Muñoz-Durango, Juan S. Escobar
description: Gut microbiota is crucial for human health. While 16S rRNA gene sequencing is most used for characterizing this community, the validation and standardization of the technique are often overlooked. This study analyzes critical factors influencing the repeatability and intermediate precision of 16S rRNA gene sequencing methodology for human gut microbiota characterization, examining the impact of key analytical factors.

title: Transcriptional control of meiotic recombination by DREAM complex components
creator: Hasibe Tunçay, Xing Ma, Katja Müller, Yuxuan Guo, Valerio Filippo Toccaceli, Huiqi Fu, Franziska Böwer, Lucas Lang, David Latrasse, Yingxiang Wang, Moussa Benhamed, Arp Schnittger
description: Meiotic chromosome segregation and recombination, essential for sexual reproduction and evolution, require a specialized gene set. Despite its importance, the transcriptional regulators that directly orchestrate meiotic gene expression remain unidentified in plants. We identify the MuvB core components known from the DREAM complex as key transcriptional regulators of meiotic recombination in Arabidopsis.

title: Novel mitochondrial-targeted alkyl chains act as fungal specific inhibitors of C. neoformans
creator: Elizabeth S. M. Edrich, Luke Young, John Spencer, Andrew McGown, Anthony L. Moore, Campbell W. Gourlay
description: Cryptococcus neoformans is the causal agent of cryptococcal meningitis in immunocompromised patients and increasing instances of anti-fungal resistance have led to investigations into new alternative antifungal targets. For example, C. neoformans possesses an Alternative Oxidase enzyme (Aox) that has been implicated in stress resistance and virulence that may represent a viable antifungal target.

title: Thermo-hygrometric dynamics reveal divergent adaptive strategies in africanized and buckfast honey bees
creator: Leandro Alves da Silva, Mateus Rodrigues Oliveira, Tasyely Daylhany Freire de Lima, Herica Girlane Tertulino Domingos, Genevile Carife Bergamo, Robson Mateus Freitas Silveira, Tamiles Araujo Lima, Débora Andrea Evangelista Façanha, Katia Peres Gramacho
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The present study investigated the adaptive strategies of Africanized and Buckfast honey bee colonies in a dry tropical environment, considering the thermohygrometric dynamics of the colonies. The internal temperature (IT) and internal relative humidity (IRH) were continuously recorded 24 h a day for seven months, yielding 36,360 observations in ten Africanized colonies and 22,680 observations in eight Buckfast colonies for each variable. Canonical discriminant analysis captured 100% of the data variance (P < 0.05) and revealed two significant functions (p < 0.001).

title: Long-term quality of life in adult craniopharyngioma patients: correlation with pituitary stalk section after endoscopic endonasal surgery
creator: Irene Portonero, Enrico Lo Bue, Alessandro Pesaresi, Alice Antico, Silvia Sgambetterra, Raffaele De Marco, Federica Penner, Diego Garbossa, Michele M R Lanotte, Francesco Zenga
description: PurposeCraniopharyngiomas are benign but locally aggressive tumors whose surgical treatment poses a challenge due to their proximity to critical structures. While gross total resection (GTR) may reduce recurrence risk, it often leads to significant long-term morbidity, especially when the pituitary stalk is sacrificed.

title: Establishment of titration-based control of DNA replication in Escherichia coli
creator: Belén Adiego-Pérez, Christina Ludwig, Demian Fluit, Mareike Berger, Alejandra Alonso Santirso, Johannes Hohlbein, Raymond H. J. Staals, Pieter Rein ten Wolde, John van der Oost, Nico J. Claassens, Lorenzo Olivi
description: Escherichia coli couples the initiation of DNA replication with cell size by modulating the activity of the replication initiator protein DnaA. The activity of DnaA is regulated both by its interconversion between an active and inactive form and by its titration on chromosomal binding sites.

title: Pharmacological potential of Chinese botanical drugs in managing chronic kidney disease by targeting mitochondrial quality control
creator: Hongyu Liu, Shumin Huang, Shichun Chen, Shuzhen Liang, Minying Huang, Shiyu Li, Yongxiang Xu, Baocheng Xie
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a multifactorial health issue characterized by structural and functional impairments of the kidneys, with significant incidence and mortality rates in global populations. Mitochondrial quality control (MQC) comprises cellular mechanisms that maintain mitochondrial health, and imbalances in the MQC system, including abnormalities in mitochondrial oxidative stress, dynamics, biogenesis, autophagy, and apoptosis, have been implicated in the onset and progression of CKD.

title: Overheating ocean: understanding thermal stress responses in seagrasses
creator: Lillian R Aoki, Fiona Tomas, Ryan S Mueller
description: This article comments on: Vivanco-Bercovich M, Bonet-Melià P, Schubert N, Marín-Guirao L, Muñiz-Salazar R, Cabello-Pasini A, Ferreria-Arrieta A, Garcia-Pantoja JA, Guzmán-Calderón JM, Procaccini G, Samperio-Ramos G, Sandoval-Gil JM. 2026. Crossing thermal limits: functional collapse of the surfgrass Phyllospadix scouleri under simulated extreme marine heatwave. Journal of Experimental Botany 77, 6642–6659. https://doi.org/10.

title: Toward efficient screening systems for sunflower drought tolerance: a comparative and molecular perspective
creator: Malin Alf, Alessia Ronchi, Aleksandra Radanović, Florian Schilling, Kimon Ionas, Boško Dedić, Srđan Bursać, Siniša Jocić, Zeena D. Costa Rodriguez, Serena Varotto, Dragana Miladinović, Renate Horn
description: The observed longer and more frequent periods of drought in recent years have drawn more focus on efficient breeding techniques for drought-tolerant crops. Several systems have been used to simulate drought conditions in order to select drought-tolerant lines. However, little is known about the comparability of different screening methods.

title: Death and chemotaxis: Bacterial chemotaxis enables collective escape from phage predation
creator: Victoria G. Muir, Alejandro Martínez-Calvo, Ned S. Wingreen, Sujit S. Datta
description: Bacteriophages (“phage”) are viruses that prey on bacteria in diverse environments, from biological tissues to soils. In many of these environments, bacterial hosts are constantly migrating, yet how bacterial migration is influenced by phage predation remains poorly understood. Using transparent granular hydrogels that mimic natural habitats, we directly visualize populations of motile Escherichia coli encountering lytic T4 phage.

title: The effect of unemployment on suicidal ideation among men: evidence from Australia during the COVID-19 pandemic
creator: Andrew R. Timming
description: IntroductionThe COVID-19 pandemic presented governments with unprecedented choices that had to be made under conditions of imperfect information. One of the key trade-offs pertains to decision-making around social distancing mandates to reduce the risk of infection, resulting in high levels of joblessness.

title: Neuroprotective effects of cell-free supernatant from Pediococcus pentosaceus TAP041 against glycation- and inflammation-associated stress responses
creator: Huijin Jeong, Young Seo Jang, Chaeeun Lee, Hak-Jong Choi, Young-Seo Park
description: Neurodegenerative diseases are increasingly associated with the convergence of oxidative, inflammatory, and glycation-associated stress pathways. The present study evaluated the stress-modulatory activity and probiotic-related characteristics of Pediococcus pentosaceus TAP041, a lactic acid bacterium isolated from citrus fruit. cell-free supernatant from P. pentosaceus TAP041 (TAP041 CFS) was assessed in in vitro models of neuronal and glial stress.

title: Glucose metabolic dysregulation of diabetes and Its role in atrial fibrillation pathogenesis
creator: Yuqi Chen, Min Xu, Ke Wei, Nan Ma
description: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is the most prevalent persistent arrhythmia in clinical practice, with a complex pathogenesis that remains incompletely understood. Emerging evidence underscores a strong association between diabetes and the occurrence of AF, highlighting a significantly elevated risk among diabetic patients.

title: Critical analysis of withdrawn drug applications in marketing authorization procedures of the European Medicines Agency (EMA) 2006–2024
creator: Florian Hitsch, Roland Seifert
description: Withdrawn drug applications (WDAs) are drug approval applications withdrawn by the applicant before the European Medicines Agency (EMA) has made a final decision. To better understand the main reasons for the emergence of WDAs, this study critically analyzes all WDAs in the period from 2006 to 2024.

title: Secretion systems shaping host–pathogen interactions in Burkholderia species
creator: Sparsha Pallen, Aishwariya Madhavan, Sivakumar Subhashree, Varshith MR, Piyush Behari Lal, Chiranjay Mukhopadhyay, Roberto Herai, Somasish Ghosh Dastidar, Ranita Ghosh Dastidar
description: AbstractUnderstanding the virulence mechanisms of pathogenic bacteria is crucial for elucidating their ability to cause disease. Among these, type secretion systems (TSS) are important for mediating host-pathogen interactions. This review focuses on the TSS in Burkholderia species, emphasizing their molecular structures, mechanisms, and their role in virulence. Burkholderia spp. employ a variety of TSS, each contributing distinctly to pathogenicity.

title: Alzheimer's Disease Biomarkers Measured by Capillary Blood Collection Versus Venous Plasma and Cerebrospinal Fluid
creator: Sara Ho, Ziling Shen, Alexandria Lewis, Megha Patel, Anny Zheng, Gianna Proscino, Thaovy Ho, Jiangxia Wang, Marilyn Albert, Abhay Moghekar
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveBlood biomarkers are increasingly critical for non‐invasive Alzheimer's Disease (AD) diagnostics and research but typically require on‐site processing. Remote point‐of‐care collection methods could enhance biomarker testing in clinical and research settings. We evaluated the safety and accuracy of blood collection via venous blood and two capillary blood collection devices (Tasso+ and TAPII) for measurements of amyloid‐beta 42/40 ratio (Aβ42/40), phosphorylated‐tau‐217 (pTau217), neurofilament‐light (NfL), and glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) from capillary plasma to simultaneously collected venous plasma and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF).MethodsPatients seen

title: Mesh placement and patient-reported outcomes in primary ventral hernia repair: a nationwide survey- and register-based study
creator: Usamah Ahmed, Hugin Reistrup, Anders Gram-Hanssen, Jacob Rosenberg, Laus Wolsing Wullum, Jason Joe Baker
description: BackgroundMesh repair reduces recurrence risk, but evidence regarding patient-reported outcomes (PROs) across mesh placements remains limited. This study aimed to investigate the association between mesh placement and PROs in primary ventral hernia repair, and secondarily the prevalence of severe chronic pain and foreign body sensation.

title: Association between weekend catch-up sleep and hypertension of the United States population from 2017 to 2020: a cross-sectional study
creator: Yan Luo, Qingyuan Li, Tong Feng, Shasha Meng, Ran Duan
description: BackgroundHypertension is a prevalent cardiovascular risk factor that significantly contributes to morbidity and mortality worldwide. Previous studies have highlighted the role of inadequate sleep during weekdays in the development of hypertension. However, the potential mitigative effects of weekend catch-up sleep (WCS) on hypertension have been less explored.

title: Cell–cell heterogeneity in phosphoenolpyruvate carboxylase biases early cell fate priming in Dictyostelium discoideum
creator: Kenichi Abe, Hidenori Hashimura, Haruka Hiraoka, Shoko Fujishiro, Narufumi Kameya, Kazuteru Taoka, Satoshi Kuwana, Masashi Fukuzawa, Satoshi Sawai
description: Glucose metabolism is a key factor characterizing the cellular state during multicellular development. In metazoans, the metabolic state of undifferentiated cells correlates with growth/differentiation transition and cell fate determination. Notably, the cell fate of the Amoebozoa species Dictyostelium discoideum is biased by the presence of glucose and is also correlated with early differences in intracellular ATP.

title: Occupational therapy improves functional recovery and reduces delirium in critically ill adults with and without stroke: a systematic review and meta-analysis
creator: Shuting Hua, Kunpeng Qiu, Shumin Zeng, Hui Wang, Tong Liu
description: BackgroundPost-intensive care syndrome (PICS), encompassing physical, psychological, and cognitive impairments, significantly compromises recovery in critical illness survivors. Although occupational therapy (OT) may mitigate functional decline, its efficacy in the intensive care unit (ICU) remains inadequately established. This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated the impact of OT on clinical outcomes in critically ill adults.

title: Polyglycine Strands Within a Collagen Triple Helix
creator: Wasin Tiarawut, Gabriel Saenz, Jinyi Yang, Ronald T Raines
description: The collagen triple helix is the most abundant protein structural motif in animals. It tolerates any amino acid in its Xaa and Yaa positions but demands glycine (Gly) at every third position, where the residue packs into the sterically forbidding core of the triple helix and donates the recurring interstrand N–H⋯O=C hydrogen bond that stitches the three strands together.

title: Surface-termination control of nonlinear dynamics in functionalized 2D NEMS
creator: Massoud Malaki
description: Surface functionalization provides an important route for tuning the properties of two-dimensional (2D) materials, yet its implications for nonlinear nanomechanical behavior remain insufficiently understood. Here, we examine how surface termination may influence the mechanical and nonlinear response of functionalized 2D nanoelectromechanical systems (NEMS), with emphasis on MXenes and comparison with graphene oxide and MoS₂.

title: Non‐Relapse Mortality With Bispecific Antibodies in Hematologic Malignancies: A Dual Systematic Review and Pharmacovigilance Analysis
creator: Sohaib Irfan, Harshit Khosla, Saad Nasir, Manmeet Kaur, Tyler J Varisco, Onyebuchi Ononogbu, Sharda Singh, Muhammad Bilal Abid
description: Bispecific antibodies (BsAbs) redirect T‐cells to tumor antigens in an MHC‐independent manner. These universally available, off‐the‐shelf products have demonstrated unprecedented efficacy in heavily pretreated patients with relapsed/refractory (R/R) hematological malignancies (HMs). The indefinite treatment duration associated with most BsAb products, coupled with neutropenia, B‐cell aplasia, and hypogammaglobulinemia result in significant immune‐related toxicities and infections.

title: Historical texts as a potential resource for plant-based antiviral agents against SARS-CoV-2: the example of the Receptarium of Burkhard III von Hallwyl from 16th-century Switzerland
creator: Nina Vahekeni, Jonas Stehlin, Corinna Urmann, Evelyn Wolfram, Yannick Geissmann, Yelena Ruedin, Samuel Peter, Olivier Engler, Andreas Lardos
description: BackgroundIn search for effective prophylactic and possibly curative therapeutics against SARS-CoV-2, an historical-ethnopharmacological approach was used to select plants described in the Receptarium of Burkhard III von Hallwyl (RBH), a recipe text from 16th century Switzerland. Ten plant species were selected from the pre-established RBH database based on specific historical uses presumably linked with the treatment of viral infections.

title: Emerging biomimetic biopolymer-based composites: advancing accessible and sustainable neural disease models and therapeutics
creator: Daniela Duc, Jacob Pattem, Benjamin Gambrill, Polina Prokopovich, Aybike Kocatürkmen, Matthew Church, Amber Mays, Akash Bedi, Emmanuel Brousseau, Oommen P. Oommen
description: Neurological diseases are leading causes of death globally and disability-adjusted life years (DALYs) globally. Because of this, urgency in providing technologies and essential medicines to tackle this issue is currently recognized as key in reversing this trend. Global health strategies have recognized tissue engineering as a pillar element in progressing both neurological disease research and therapy discovery.

title: Vagus nerve stimulation allows to cease maintenance electroconvulsive therapy in treatment-resistant depression: a retrospective monocentric case series
creator: Oumaima Aboubakr, Philippe Domenech, Isabelle Heurtebise, Raphaël Gaillard, Aurore Guy-Rubin, Romain Carron, Philibert Duriez, Philip Gorwood, Fabien Vinckier, Johan Pallud, Marc Zanello
description: ContextThe use of vagus nerve stimulation (VNS) to reduce or stop electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) in treatment-resistant depression seems promising. The aim of this study was to investigate the efficacy of VNS on the reduction of ECT sessions and mood stabilization.

title: Could AAV-vectored delivery of broadly neutralizing antibodies (bNAbs) reduce virologic failure in children diagnosed with perinatal HIV?
creator: Kaiya L Pringle, Mauricio A Martins
description: Antiretroviral therapy (ART) has transformed HIV infection into a manageable chronic condition, but its success depends on lifelong adherence, which can be challenging for children living with HIV (CLWH) and their caregivers, particularly in resource-limited settings. Passive immunization with HIV-1 broadly neutralizing antibodies (bNAbs) can maintain virologic suppression in CLWH after ART withdrawal and offers a promising complementary strategy.

title: A Systematic Intracranial Exposure‐Response Evaluation of Brain‐Penetrant Inhibitors: Informing Dose Selection for Brain Metastases
creator: Yuqian Zhao, Weize Huang
description: Brain metastases (BMs) represent a major clinical challenge due to their high incidence in cancers such as non‐small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and breast cancer, and the limited efficacy of systemic therapies resulting from inadequate drug penetration across the blood–brain barrier.

title: Dyslipidemias associated with endocrine disorders: a position statement of the working group of the nutrition hormones and metabolism club of the italian society of endocrinology (SIE)
creator: Giovanna Muscogiuri, Manuela Albertelli, Giorgio Arnaldi, Luigi Barrea, Giuseppe Bellastella, Marco Bonomi, Marina Caputo, Massimiliano Caprio, Angelo Cignarelli, Ludovico Di Gioia, Francesco Frasca, Davide Ferrari, Alessandra Gambineri, Valentina Gasco, Federico Gatto, Annalisa Giandalia, Roberta G
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). PurposeDyslipidemias are highly prevalent metabolic disturbances and represent a major driver of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. Beyond primary forms, numerous endocrine diseases induce secondary dyslipidemias that substantially modify lipid metabolism and contribute to cardiometabolic risk.

title: Beyond MRI: Unveiling metabolic signatures of primary hypophysitis with 18F-FDG PET
creator: Serdar Sahin, Betul Banu Kocaman, Mehmet Ufuk Yanmaz, Said Erkam Biyikoglu, Ozge Polat Korkmaz, Emre Durcan, Sertac Asa, Haluk Burcak Sayman, Hande Mefkure Ozkaya, Necmettin Tanriover, Pinar Kadioglu
description: AimsHypophysitis is a heterogeneous clinical entity originating from different anatomical compartments of the pituitary gland and driven by diverse pathophysiological mechanisms. This study aims to explore the potential diagnostic and clinical value of 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography in the evaluation of primary hypophysitis.Materials and methodsThis single-center retrospective study was conducted at the pituitary referral unit of a tertiary university hospital.

title: Distinct immune landscapes characterize highly versus minimally invasive brain metastases
creator: Sarah M Maritan, Elham Karimi, Matthew Dankner, Aldo Hernandez-Corchado, Miranda W Yu, Matthew G Annis, Yashar Aghazadeh Habashi, Morteza Rezanejad, Bridget Liu, Nebras Koudieh, Emilie Pichette, Parvaneh Fallah, Benoit Fiset, Yuhong Wei, Ali Nehme, Chun Geun Lee, Jack A Elias, Morag Park, Yasser Ria
description: Brain metastases (BrMs) occur in approximately 30% of cancer patients, causing nearly one-fifth of cancer deaths. While immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) benefit some BrM patients, responses remain highly variable. This variability partly reflects distinct histopathological growth patterns that include minimally invasive (MI) and highly invasive (HI) brain BrMs.

title: CD11c+ CD8 T cells cause IFN-γ–dependent autoimmune neuroinflammation that is restrained by PD-1 signaling
creator: Daniel Hwang, Gholamreza Azizi, Larissa Lumi Watanabe Ishikawa, Maryam Seyedsadr, Arin Cox, Soohwa Jang, Ezgi Kasimoglu, Abdolmohamad Rostami, Guang-Xian Zhang, Bogoljub Ciric
description: In multiple sclerosis (MS) lesions, CD8 T cells outnumber CD4 T cells, suggesting that they contribute to MS pathology. However, little is known about the role of CD8 T cells in MS, partly due to the prevalent use of experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis (EAE) models mediated by CD4 T cells, which have limited involvement of CD8 T cells.

title: First Reported Extravascular-ICD Insertion in a Patient With Prior Sternotomy for Valvular Surgery
creator: Guillaume Serzian, Fiona Ecarnot, Marc Badoz
description: BackgroundThe extravascular implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (EV-ICD) is a novel nontransvenous system designed to prevent sudden cardiac death while avoiding complications associated with transvenous leads. Insertion after prior sternotomy is currently considered contraindicated and to our knowledge has not previously been reported.Case SummaryA 68-year-old man with prior Bentall procedure developed anthracycline-induced cardiomyopathy requiring ICD insertion for primary prevention.

title: MS care: integrating advanced therapies and holistic management
creator: Gavin Giovannoni, Helen L. Ford, Klaus Schmierer, Rod Middleton, Andrea M. Stennett, Ian Pomeroy, Leonora Fisniku, Antonio Scalfari, Colin Bannon, Ruth Stross, Sarah Hughes, Adam Williams, Samantha Josephs, Charlie Peel, Agne Straukiene
description: Lifestyle and environmental factors are key determinants in disease causality and progression in neurological conditions, including multiple sclerosis (MS). Lack of exercise, poor diet, tobacco smoking, excessive alcohol intake, social determinants of health, concomitant medications, poor sleep and comorbidities can exacerbate MS pathological processes by impacting brain health and depleting neurological reserves, resulting in more rapid disease worsening.

title: Research on the evaluation model of pilots’ in-flight stress state based on flight critical events
creator: Lamei Shang, Manting Lu, Chunying Qian, Xiaoru Wanyan, Yubin Zhou, Shuang Liu
description: BackgroundStress refers to the non - specific response that occurs in an organism when it is subjected to stressful stimuli. When fighter pilots execute high-stress missions, they are likely to experience stress responses. These responses may have a negative impact on the cognitive decision-making processes of the pilots, subsequently undermining the mission effectiveness.

title: Hybrid Perventricular Venus P-Valve Implantation Via Mini-Thoracotomy in a Patient With Mechanical Tricuspid Valve
creator: Alper Guzeltas, Selman Gokalp, Sertac Haydin
description: BackgroundChronic severe pulmonary regurgitation following repair of right ventricular outflow dysfunction may result in progressive right ventricular dilatation, heart failure, and arrhythmias. In patients with a complex surgical history, particularly those with mechanical tricuspid valve prostheses, standard transvenous access for pulmonary valve implantation can be technically challenging and carries risks for prosthetic valve injury.

title: Postoperative radiotherapy improves survival in completely resected non-small cell lung cancer with pathologic N2 stage IIIA and positive lymph node count greater than one: a SEER-based retrospective cohort study
creator: Diyang Zhu, Yuanyuan Xiao, Shancheng He, Baochang Xie, Wenqi Zhao, Yuhui Xu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). ObjectiveNon-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) constitutes approximately 85% of lung cancer cases, with 20%–30% of patients diagnosed at stage III. While multimodal therapy is the standard for treating locally advanced NSCLC, the role of PORT remains controversial. This study seeks to evaluate the effect of postoperative radiotherapy (PORT) on overall survival (OS) and cancer-specific survival (CSS) in patients with resected pathologic N2 (pN2) stage IIIA NSCLC.MethodsData from the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results Program (SEER) 17 registry (2010–2019) were analyzed.

title: Ultrasound-Guided Extraluminal Venous Valve Functional Remodeling
creator: Weipu Zou, Meijia Xu, Qianqian Jia, Yuefeng Zhu
description: BackgroundEndovenous treatment for varicose veins is predominantly ablative, whereas vein-preserving approaches remain limited.Case SummaryA 60-year-old man with left lower extremity varicose veins and pruritus underwent ultrasound-guided extraluminal circumferential hyaluronic acid injection around the incompetent terminal valve at the left saphenofemoral junction after duplex ultrasound confirmed primary superficial venous valve incompetence.

title: The Challenges of Hyperparameter Tuning for Accurate Causal Effect Estimation
creator: Damian Machlanski, Spyridon Samothrakis, Paul Clarke
description: ML is playing an increasingly crucial role in estimating causal effects of treatments on outcomes from observational data. Many ML methods (‘causal estimators’) have been proposed for this task. All of these methods, as with any ML approach, require extensive hyperparameter tuning. For non-causal predictive tasks, there is a consensus on the choice of tuning metrics (e.g.

title: Novel variant and enteroendocrine hormone deficiency in a patient with proline and glutamate‐rich protein with a coiled coil domain 1 (PERCC1) associated enteropathy: New diagnostic and therapeutic insights
creator: Teresa Di Chio, Daniela Gattini, Christina Belza, Iram Siddiqui, Bolette Hartmann, Meghan Zoe Benchimol, Shiqi Zhang, Neil E Warner, Aleixo M Muise, Yaron Avitzur
description: Proline and glutamate‐rich protein with a coiled coil domain 1 (PERCC1)‐associated enteropathy is a rare monogenic congenital diarrhea due to defective enteroendocrine cells (EECs). We describe a 6‐year‐old female with intestinal failure since birth. Biopsies demonstrated normal appearing gastric mucosa on hematoxylin and eosin stains. Commercial whole‐exome sequencing did not reveal clinically relevant variants.

title: SEMbeddings: how to evaluate model misfit before data collection using large-language models
creator: Tommaso Feraco, Enrico Toffalini
