description: IntroductionRecent developments suggest that Large Language Models (LLMs) provide a promising approach for approximating empirical correlation matrices of item responses by utilizing item embeddings and their cosine similarities. In this paper, we introduce a novel tool, which we label SEMbeddings.

title: Average annual occupational radiation exposure among dental staff: a 3-years retrospective observational study
creator: Erada Almotiri, Sarra Alsabr, Amal Aljehani, Ebtesam Alsumairi, Sharifah Alharthi, Farrah Alnajjar, Fahad Khalifa
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Diagnostic radiography is indispensable in modern dentistry for its diagnostic and therapeutic value, yet it presents potential health risks to healthcare providers from long-term occupational radiation exposure. This retrospective study aimed to quantify the average annual occupational radiation doses received by dental staff members at King Fahad Armed Forces Hospital (KFAFH) from 2022 to 2024, evaluate exposure variations across clinical specialties, and assess personnel compliance regarding Thermoluminescent Dosimeter (TLD) badge utilization.

title: The underestimated risk of additional ipsilateral BI-RADS 3 lesions identified by preoperative ultrasound in breast cancer patients
creator: Yue Hu, Hongli Wang, Mengzi Wu, Wei Zheng, Jingsi Mei, Xiaofang Jiang, Queran Lin, Ran Gu, Fengtao Liu, Jinna Lin, Chang Gong, Jun Shen, Qiang Liu
description: ObjectiveTo determine the prevalence of malignancy of additional ultrasound BI-RADS category 3 lesions in women with newly diagnosed breast cancer.Materials and methodsBetween July 2014 and June 2022, women with newly diagnosed breast cancer and additional ultrasound BI-RADS 3 lesions were retrospectively included. Malignancy was confirmed by pathology, and malignancy rates were assessed at both the patient and lesion levels.

title: The Impact of Anaesthesia Method on the Use of Anaesthesia Department Resources in Total Knee Arthroplasty
creator: Katarina Lahtinen, Elina Reponen, Noora Skants
description: BackgroundSpinal and general anaesthesia seem to lead to similar health‐related outcomes in total knee arthroplasty. However, to produce economically and environmentally sustainable health care, we should also consider other factors. Current guidelines recommend preferring regional anaesthesia and total intravenous anaesthesia to reduce environmental impact.

title: Knowledge, attitude, and perception of Pakistani populations toward monkeypox: a cross-section study
creator: Humayun Yousaf, Abdul Qadeer, Muhammad Sohail, Maqbool Khan, Muhammad Farooq, Zakir Khan, Dalia Fouad, Yu-Chia Liu, Chien-Chin Chen
description: ObjectiveThe reappearance of monkeypox in non-endemic countries has preceded critical public health concerns. The public’s adherence to preventative measures is influenced by their understanding of the infectious monkeypox virus (Mpox), attitude toward it, and perceptions of it. We conducted this study to evaluate the general population’s knowledge, attitude, and perceptions of Mpox in Pakistan.

title: Factors influencing trust in algorithmic decision-making: an indirect scenario-based experiment
creator: Fernando Marmolejo-Ramos, Rebecca Marrone, Malgorzata Korolkiewicz, Florence Gabriel, George Siemens, Srecko Joksimovic, Yuki Yamada, Yuki Mori, Talal Rahwan, Maria Sahakyan, Belona Sonna, Assylbek Meirmanov, Aidos Bolatov, Bidisha Som, Izuchukwu Ndukaihe, Nwadiogo C. Arinze, Josef Kundrát, Lenka Sk
description: Algorithms are involved in decisions ranging from trivial to significant, but people often express distrust toward them. Research suggests that educational efforts to explain how algorithms work may help mitigate this distrust. In a study of 1,921 participants from 20 countries, we examined differences in algorithmic trust for low-stakes and high-stakes decisions.

title: Profiling the diversity of the village chicken faecal microbiota using 16S rRNA gene and metagenomic sequencing data to reveal patterns of gut microbiome signatures
creator: Mxolisi Nene, Nokuthula Winfred Kunene, Rian Pierneef, Khanyisile Hadebe
description: IntroductionThe production environment of extensively raised village chickens necessitates their adaptability to low-resource systems. The gut microbiome plays a critical role in supporting this adaptability by influencing health and productivity. This study aimed to investigate the diversity and functional capacities of the faecal microbiome in village chickens from Limpopo and KwaZulu-Natal provinces of South Africa.

title: Compressive Coronary Hematoma Treated With Stenting
creator: Kaïs Ouerghi, Clément Fabre, Tahar Lazizi, Victor Mateus, Alain Furber, Serge Willoteaux, Loïc Bière, Fabrice Prunier
description: BackgroundSpontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD) may require revascularization when severe ischemia results from compressive intramural hematoma.Case SummaryA 38-year-old woman presented with anterior ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction caused by a long compressive intramural hematoma of the left anterior descending artery. Optical coherence tomography (OCT) demonstrated a 41-mm Type 2a SCAD with severe true lumen compression (minimal lumen area 0.6 mm2).

title: Physiological-immune resilience risk assessment model for predicting adverse cardiac outcomes in patients with acute myocardial infarction
creator: Ling Zhang, Qiuyue Wang, Yunying Ji, Chunya Sha, Qiuping Zhang
description: BackgroundAdverse cardiac events have been identified as a major determinant of poor prognosis in patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI), directly increasing mortality risk. Therefore, this study aimed to establish a physio-immune resilience risk assessment model to identify, at an early stage, the influencing factors of adverse cardiac outcomes in AMI patients, thereby providing clinical guidance for subsequent interventions.

title: Saphenous Vein Graft Kinking Secondary to Left Atrial Appendage Clip Causing Type 5 Myocardial Infarction
creator: Rashid Alhusain, Mohamed Ibrahim, Artur Schneider, Abdallah El Sabbagh, John Haney, Riyaz Bashir
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundLeft atrial appendage (LAA) clip placement is increasingly used for stroke prophylaxis in atrial fibrillation during cardiac surgery. Rare mechanical interactions with adjacent grafts may cause graft failure and type 5 myocardial infarction.Case SummaryA 75-year-old man underwent coronary artery bypass grafting with left internal mammary artery to left anterior descending artery and saphenous vein grafts to posterior descending artery and second obtuse marginal branch, with LAA clip placement. On postoperative day 2, he suffered pulseless electrical activity arrest and cardiogenic shock.

title: Long-term inactivation mediated by different FGF-A homologues on heterologously expressed NaV1.2 currents
creator: Yenisleidy Lorenzo-Ceballos, Pedro L. Martinez-Espinosa, Xiao-Ming Xia, Christopher J. Lingle
description: Lorenzo-Ceballos et al. show that long-term inactivation (LTI) of NaV1.2 channels mediated by A-isoforms of different FGF homologues (FGF11–FGF14) differ both in intrinsic rates of onset and rates of recovery from LTI. Furthermore, FGF’s allosterically mediate slowing of fast inactivation. Specific effects of each FGF-A result in homologue-specific use-dependent changes in NaV availability.

title: Self‐Care Experiences of Psychiatric Nurses: A Phenomenological Study
creator: Sibel Çaynak, Yeliz Karaçar, Buket Şimşek Arslan, Ahmet Göktaş, Halil İbrahim Karaçar
description: IntroductionSelf‐care is both a personal and professional responsibility for nurses; however, academic evidence in this area remains limited.AimPsychiatric nurses' self‐care experiences were examined.MethodThis descriptive phenomenological study included 18 psychiatric nurses from a public hospital, using purposive sampling. Data were collected via semi‐structured, individual, and in‐depth face‐to‐face interviews conducted between May and June 2025.

title: Performance of the LIAISON PLEX gram-negative blood culture assay for identifying bacterial pathogens and resistance genes in blood cultures
creator: Neelam Dhiman, Christopher L. Emery, Siu-Kei Chow, Dooil Ho, Paul Granato, Brian Bernier, Janet Farhang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Gram-negative bacteria cause potentially life-threatening bloodstream infections worldwide. Delayed initiation of optimal antimicrobial therapy worsens health outcomes. Molecular assays characterize bloodstream pathogens and their antimicrobial resistance (AMR) genes faster than gold-standard culture-based methods. This multi-site study evaluated the performance of the automated multiplex LIAISON PLEX Gram-Negative Blood Culture (BCN) Assay (Luminex Corporation), which tests positive blood cultures for 19 gram-negative bacteria and 8 AMR genes, in approximately 2 h. Samples included 351 prospectively collected, 231 pre-selected, and 746 contrived specimens.

title: Timing of Earliest Documented Positive Hepatitis C Laboratory Result Relative to Delivery Among Pregnant Persons With Active Infection in West Virginia, 2022–2023
creator: Kady Pack, Mamoon Yousaf, Rachel A Wattick, Brett Armstrong, Birgit Shanholtzer, Tonya Chaney, Shannon McBee, Alana G Hudson
description: Direct‐acting antiviral therapy can cure hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection; however, because treatment is not recommended during pregnancy, preconception treatment remains the primary strategy to prevent perinatal HCV exposure. West Virginia birth records from 2022 to 2023 were linked with statewide HCV laboratory surveillance data.

title: From HPV infection to cervical precancer: Molecular mechanisms, immune microenvironment and emerging technologies
creator: Yubing Zhou, Yunxiao Ge, Kangdong Liu, Hui Liu, Zigang Dong
description: Cervical cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality among women globally, with persistent high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) infection as the primary etiological factor. Cervical precancerous lesions, including high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesions and adenocarcinoma in situ, represent the critical window for intervention prior to invasive cancer development.

title: Asmeton minimizes dry cough and diaphragmatic contraction during pulsed-field ablation of atrial fibrillation: a clinical prospective randomized study
creator: Huixing Liu, Yan Zhang, Huafen Liu, Wei Liu, Zhuo Wang, Can Leng, Gangjie Xie, Jiahao Zhao, Jinlin Huang, Lei Huang, Yuzhi Lu, Hongwei Zhang, Songyun Wang, Hong Jiang
description: PurposePulsed-field ablation (PFA) is a novel ablation modality with promising outcomes for atrial fibrillation therapy. However, PFA might lead to dry cough and diaphragmatic contraction, especially under conscious sedation. We aim to explore a novel approach to reduce dry cough and diaphragmatic contraction during PFA procedures performed under conscious sedation.

title: Predictive value of matrix metalloproteinase-9 combined with magnetic resonance spectroscopy for delayed cerebral edema after spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage
creator: Jing Sun, Lei Chen
description: ObjectiveThe aim of this paper was to evaluate the predictive value of matrix metalloproteinase (MMP)-9 combined with magnetic resonance spectroscopy (MRS) for delayed cerebral edema after spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage (SICH).MethodsPatients with head computed tomography (CT) suggestive of SICH were retrospectively included.

title: Association between hearing aid use and cognitive function among Chinese middle-aged and older adults with hearing impairment: the mediating effect of social activity
creator: Xinyi Wang, Xianger Gu, Sunxi Mao, Zinan Zhang, Zhonghua Wang
description: BackgroundIn China’s ageing population, hearing-impaired middle-aged and older adults face cognitive vulnerability. We aimed to explore the effects of hearing aid use on cognitive function and to examine the mediating role of social activity in this relationship.MethodsWe sourced data from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study for the years 2011, 2013, 2015, 2018, and 2020.

title: Handgrip strength in young recreational skiers: is it related to the risk of falling?
creator: Verena Menz, Marc Philippe, Elena Pocecco, Johannes Burtscher, Barbara Strasser, Gerhard Ruedl, Martin Kopp, Martin Burtscher
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Handgrip Strength (HGS) is correlated with general health and fitness throughout the lifespan. However, the relationship between HGS and the frequency of sports accidents is not well understood. The aim of the present survey was twofold. Firstly, to collect HGS data from young skiers and compare them with existing normative values; secondly, to investigate whether the frequency of falls during a day of skiing is correlated with HGS.

title: Hepatitis A Virus (HAV) Recurrence and De Novo Hepatitis A Acquired at Time of Liver Transplantation: Comparison of Graft HAV Infection and Viral Kinetics
creator: David Mutimer, Elinor Latham, Sowsan F. Atabani, Samreen Ijaz
description: Hepatitis A virus (HAV) infection is an uncommon indication for liver transplantation, and donor‐derived or transfusion‐associated HAV infection is rare. Data describing HAV recurrence or early acquisition following liver transplantation, particularly with longitudinal quantitative viral kinetics, are limited. We describe two liver transplant recipients with graft HAV infection occurring in different immunological contexts.

title: Harnessing fungal bio-electricity: a promising path to a cleaner environment
creator: Aisha Umar, Mustansar Mubeen, Iftikhar Ali, Yasir Iftikhar, Muhammad Aamir Sohail, Ashara Sajid, Ajay Kumar, Manoj Kumar Solanki, Praveen Kumar Divvela, Lei Zhou
description: Integrating fungi into fuel cell systems presents a promising opportunity to address environmental pollution while simultaneously generating energy. This review explores the innovative concept of constructing wetlands as fuel cells for pollutant degradation, offering a practical and eco-friendly solution to pollution challenges.

title: Distinct Responses of Estrogen Receptor α and β in Chondrocytes Under Excessive Mechanical Stress
creator: Saki Takesue, Naoto Hirose, Makoto Yanoshita, Sayuri Nishiyama, Eri Tsuboi, Naoki Kubo, Daiki Kita, Yuki Asakawa, Kotaro Tanimoto
description: IntroductionOsteoarthritis (OA) is more common in women, suggesting a link to estrogen. Estrogen supports cartilage homeostasis and metabolism via two receptors: ERα and ERβ. Mechanical stress is the primary cause of OA and affects cellular functions, including receptor activity. The link between excessive mechanical stress and ERs in cartilage is poorly understood.

title: Diagnostic performance of dual-energy CT for differentiating acute intracranial hemorrhage from contrast staining: a systematic review and meta-analysis
creator: Wenbin Ji, Yaosheng Shi
description: BackgroundAccurate differentiation between acute intracranial hemorrhage (AIH) and contrast staining (CS) on follow-up computed tomography (CT) scans in patients with acute stroke, particularly after endovascular thrombectomy, is a critical clinical challenge. Dual-energy CT (DECT), with its capability for material decomposition, has emerged as a promising solution.

title: SOX10 Expression in Primary Salivary Gland Tumors: A Meta-Analysis
creator: Otto Tahvanainen, Henri Lagerstam, David Kalfert, Ivana Kholová
description: PurposePrimary salivary gland tumors form a heterogeneous group with diagnostic challenges. Sex-determining region Y-related homeobox 10 (SOX10) is a transcription factor studied in primary salivary gland tumors for over a decade. To date, no systematic review or meta-analysis has been conducted on its expression in salivary gland tumors.

title: Invalid Nucleic Acid Test Results May Limit Deceased Donor Organ Utilization
creator: Sara Dionne, Hillary Akana, Kaitlin Logue, Brenden O'Neale, Chris Curran, Sean VanSlyck
description: BackgroundNucleic acid testing (NAT) is essential for detecting transmissible viral infections in deceased organ donors and guiding safe organ allocation. However, invalid discriminatory NAT (dNAT) results may lead to unnecessary donor exclusion and reduced organ availability.MethodsWe performed a retrospective analysis of HIV‐1/2, HBV, and HCV NAT results from deceased organ donors in the United States.

title: Case report: Successful laparoscopic management of early abdominal pregnancy
creator: Haixia Li, Limin Feng, Shengpeng Zhang
description: BackgroundAbdominal pregnancy is characterized by the implantation of the gestational sac within the peritoneal cavity, specifically outside the fallopian tubes, ovaries, and cervix. This exceedingly rare form of ectopic pregnancy accounts for about 1% of all ectopic pregnancies. When rupture occurs, it can result in a life-threatening situation for the patient, necessitating immediate medical intervention.

title: Early‐Life Betaine Supplementation Drives Sex‐Specific Metabolic Programming in Rats, Affecting FGF21 Signaling and Energy Balance
creator: Rocío A Martín‐Chamorro, Catalina A Pomar, Andreu Palou, Catalina Picó, Ana M Rodríguez
description: We aimed to evaluate the effects of maternal diet and betaine supplementation during the suckling period on Fgf21 expression and metabolic pathways related to FGF21 signaling and metabolic programming. Offspring of Wistar rats fed either a chow diet (CD) or a Western diet (WD) were studied at postnatal day 22 and at 7 months.

title: High throughput single cell metagenomic sequencing with semi-permeable capsules: unraveling microbial diversity at the single-cell level in sewage and fecal microbiomes
creator: Meilee Ling, Judit Szarvas, Vaida Kurmauskaitė, Vaidotas Kiseliovas, Rapolas Žilionis, Baptiste Avot, Patrick Munk, Frank M. Aarestrup
description: Single-cell sequencing may serve as a powerful complementary technique to shotgun metagenomics to study microbiomes. This emerging technology allows the separation of complex microbial communities into individual bacterial cells, enabling high-throughput sequencing of genetic material from thousands of singular bacterial cells in parallel.

title: Dapagliflozin does not impair microvascular hemorheology in type 2 diabetes mellitus: A multicenter randomized controlled trial (D‐PATH study)
creator: Yuki Nakatani, Nobuyuki Banba, Shoya Ono, Tomoki Turumi, Megumi Hoshiai, Takushi Sugiyama, Takashi Tomoe, Hajime Tamiya, Naoyuki Otani, Hiroyuki Sugimura, Hidekazu Ikemiyagi, Yusuke Ohya, Koji Yokokawa, Shinichiro Ueda, Yoshimasa Aso, Yasuhiro Maejima, Takanori Yasu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). AimsSodium–glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors reduce cardiovascular and renal events beyond glucose lowering, but their hematocrit‐raising effects raise concerns about increased blood viscosity and microvascular impairment. We investigated whether dapagliflozin adversely affects microvascular hemorheology in patients with type 2 diabetes.Materials and MethodsIn this multicenter, open‐label, randomized controlled trial, 82 adults with type 2 diabetes received dapagliflozin (5 mg/day) or conventional therapy for 16 weeks.

title: Association of body mass index with the risk of rheumatoid arthritis: a systematic review and meta-analysis
creator: Fei Cao, Xiaohong Kang, Weizhuo Wang, Shengli Huang
description: BackgroundRheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic systemic autoimmune disease of unknown etiology. Numerous studies have investigated the association between body mass index (BMI) and RA risk, but findings have been inconsistent.ObjectiveThis study aims to comprehensively evaluate the association between different BMI categories and RA risk using a meta-analytic approach.

title: Correction to “Baseline podocyte‐associated state and persistent cell–matrix transcriptional programs are associated with BALB/c substrain differences in adriamycin nephropathy”
creator: Unknown
description: igure 1B, the label “AJcl” was inadvertently retained within the representative periodic acid–Schiff (PAS)‐stained image for the ByJcl group during figure preparation. The corrected Figure 1 is provided below, with the unintended label removed. No other elements of Figure 1 have been changed. This correction does not affect the data, statistical analyses, results, interpretation, or conclusions of the article.

title: Questionnaire survey of risk factors for recurrence of ocular inflammation in patients with uveitis after SARS-CoV-2 infection
creator: Zonghui Ma, Ying Chi, Chunying Guo, Jing Zhang, Liu Yang
description: IntroductionDuring the COVID-19 pandemic in China, the proportion of patients with uveitis who were infected with SARS-CoV-2 increased greatly. The impact of SARS-CoV-2 infection on patients with uveitis has not been fully described.MethodsA questionnaire on SARS-CoV-2 infection was sent to patients with uveitis to assess ocular and systemic conditions before and after infection.

title: Probiotics as a Strategy for Mitigating Viral Infections in Poultry: Immunomodulatory Mechanisms and Therapeutic Potential
creator: Elmer Nayra Ametefe, Daniel Saka, Juliet Nuerkie Anang, Lourraine Sena Doh, Leonard Kofi Adjorlolo
description: Poultry viral infections remain a persistent challenge for the poultry industry, causing significant economic losses and posing potential threats to human health. The escalating frequency of outbreaks involving pathogens, such as infectious bronchitis virus (IBV), Newcastle disease virus (NDV) and avian influenza virus (AIV), underscores the urgent need for effective interventions.

title: Aflatoxin M1 in Milk and Aflatoxin B1 in Animal Feed in Bangladesh: A Systematic Review, Meta‐Analysis and Literature‐Based Dietary Risk Assessment
creator: MD. Al Fattah, Md. Ahsan Habib
description: BackgroundAflatoxin M1 (AFM1), the carcinogenic metabolite of aflatoxin B1 (AFB1), passes into the milk of animals fed mould‐contaminated feed. Bangladeshi feed and milk surveillance have developed separately, and integrated dietary‐risk estimates are scarce.Objective and designTo pool AFM1 occurrence in Bangladeshi milk, summarise feed AFB1 and characterise age‐stratified dietary risk.

title: Association between love breakup and suicidal ideation in Peruvian medical students: a cross-sectional study during the COVID-19 pandemic
creator: Danai Valladares-Garrido, J. Pierre Zila-Velasque, Flor M. Santander-Hernández, Miguel A. Guevara-Morales, Noelia Morocho-Alburqueque, Virgilio E. Failoc-Rojas, César Johan Pereira-Victorio, Víctor J. Vera-Ponce, Darwin A. León-Figueroa, Mario J. Valladares-Garrido
description: ObjectiveWe aimed to determine the association between a major romantic breakup and suicidal ideation in medical students from three universities in Peru.MethodsA cross-sectional study was conducted during the first pandemic wave in 2021 on medical students from three universities in northern Peru. The outcome was suicidal ideation, measured with question nine of the Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9).

title: Co‐ and Multi‐Pathologies in Parkinson's Disease: An International Parkinson and Movement Disorder Society Scientific Issues Committee Review
creator: Michele Matarazzo, Per Borghammer, Inas Elsayed, Jennifer G. Goldman, Yue Huang, Katja Lohmann, Per Svenningsson, Lorraine V. Kalia, Daniela Berg, Jeffrey H. Kordower, the MDS Scientific Issues Committee
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Parkinson's disease (PD) has been historically defined as a disease of striatal dopamine deficiency secondary to degeneration of dopaminergic neurons in the substantia nigra pars compacta, related to the presence of Lewy bodies and Lewy neurites. Since the discovery of pathogenic variants in the gene encoding α‐synuclein, as well as the finding that α‐synuclein is a major constituent of Lewy pathology, PD is considered as a prototypical synucleinopathy.

title: An Energy Autonomous Microneedle Array‐Based Sensing System for Continuous Biomarker Monitoring
creator: Arnab Pal, Kai‐Po Fan, Sheng‐Chun Hung, Jaba Roy Chowdhury, Jun‐Hsun Chung, Meenakshi Ray, Hsiang‐Yun Hsu, Fu‐Cheng Kao, Kuei‐Lin Liu, Zong‐Hong Lin
description: Wearable bioelectronics are revolutionizing personalized healthcare by enabling continuous monitoring of physiochemical indicators. Despite significant advancements, challenges remain in creating platforms that can accurately detect multiple biomarkers while being energy autonomous. This study introduces a wearable, minimally invasive microneedle array platform for real‐time monitoring of clinically relevant biomarkers during exercise.

title: Nonlinear Relations Between Resting Heart Rate Measures and Health Risk Behavior in Emerging Adulthood
creator: Derek P Spangler, Nina Lauharatanahirun
description: IntroductionResting heart rate (HR) measures reflect autonomic processes that could predict health risk behavior (HRB) in emerging adulthood when risky behavior is prominent. However, prior studies and extant theories are inconsistent, such that the relationships between HR measures and HRB could be positive or negative in direction.

title: Experimental evaluation of the healing potential of Sesuvium portulacastrum in excisional wounds in wistar rats
creator: Kelly Kercy Nogueira Da Silva, Gislainy Luciana Gomes Câmara, Salvador Viana Gomes Júnior, Camila Gomes Fernandes De Souza, Kizzy Millenn De Freitas, Amália Cinthia Meneses Do Rego, Irami Araújo Filho, Roque Ribeiro da Silva Júnior, Thales Allyrio Araújo De Medeiros Fernandes, José Rodolfo Lopes de
description: Background Sesuvium portulacastrum (“Pirrixiu”) is a halophytic plant adapted to saline environments with potential wound-healing properties.ObjectiveTo evaluate the wound-healing efficacy of a 10% macerated S. portulacastrum gel compared with the topical antibiotic Nebacetin in Wistar rats with standardized excisional wounds.MethodsExperimental, completely randomized study in Wistar rats. Wound area reduction was measured daily.

title: Aloe-emodin exhibits growth-suppressive effects on androgen-independent human prostate cancer DU145 cells via inhibiting the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway: an in vitro and in silico study
creator: Talib Hussain, Ahmed Alafnan, Ibrahim Abdullah Almazni, Nawal Helmi, Afrasim Moin, Hanadi M. Baeissa, Amir Mahgoub Awadelkareem, AbdElmoneim O. Elkhalifa, Tahani Bakhsh, Abdulrahman Alzahrani, Rashed Mohammed Alghamdi, Mohammad Khalid, Rohit Kumar Tiwari, Syed Mohd Danish Rizvi
description: At the molecular level, several developmental signaling pathways, such as Wnt/β-catenin, have been associated with the initiation and subsequent progression of prostate carcinomas. The present report elucidated the anti-cancerous attributes of an anthraquinone, aloe-emodin (AE), against androgen-independent human prostate cancer DU145 cells.

title: Prevalence of malnutrition and associated factors among the elderly population in Jiaxing City, China
creator: Yangming Sun, Zirui Wang, Yikang Wu, Yun Lin
description: ObjectiveAnalysis on the nutritional status and its influencing factors of the elderly in care institutions in Jiaxing.MethodThe Mini Nutritional Assessment (MNA) was employed to screen the risk of malnutrition among individuals aged 60 years and older residing in these institutions. The single-factor and multi-factor logistic regression models were utilized to analyze the influencing factors.

title: Acupuncture therapy for Parkinson’s disease: a case report demonstrating symptomatic improvement without medication
creator: Suying Lei, Qing Liu, IanI Leong, Jingqi Fan, YauKeung Tsang, Xin Liu, Xiaoyan Xu, Lixing Zhuang
description: BackgroundParkinson’s disease (PD) often necessitates immediate medical intervention following diagnosis. In recent years, there has been a noticeable increase in clinical investigations assessing the efficacy of acupuncture in PD, with many studies reporting positive outcomes. Ethical guidelines commonly endorse pharmaceutical therapies for PD, leading ongoing research to combine acupuncture with standard drug-based treatments.

title: Human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells alleviate brain injury and promote neuroregeneration via BDNF/TrkB/CREB/PI3K-Akt pathway in preterm rats with intraventricular hemorrhage
creator: Mingyou Yu, Ziyi Zhang, Xuxian Wu, Baoying Zhang, Yang Hu, Changge Wei, Miao Ran, Manni Cao, Jinhui Zhang, Xueli Ding, Yan Wang, Can Liu, Maoqiong Chen, Jianwei Xu
description: ObjectiveTo explore the neuroprotective effect and molecular mechanism of human umbilical cord mesenchymal stem cells (hUC-MSCs) in preterm rats with intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH), and provide experimental basis for clinical treatment of neonatal IVH.MethodsTissue block adherence method was used to isolate and culture hUC-MSCs, and P4 Sprague-Dawley premature rats were divided into sham, IVH model, and hUC-MSC treatment groups.

title: Mechanisms of traditional Chinese medicine in enhancing the efficacy and reducing the toxicity of immune checkpoint inhibitors via regulation of the tumor microenvironment and gut microbiota
creator: Junying Pan, Liying Yang, Haoyu Wang, Yinghua Chen
description: Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) face challenges of drug resistance and immune-related adverse events (irAEs). Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM)—including single herbs, compounds, and active monomers—enhances ICI efficacy and reduces toxicity by remodeling the tumor immune microenvironment, regulating gut microbiota, and modulating key immune pathways. TCM also alleviates ICI-induced colitis and myocarditis, demonstrating the value of holistic and syndrome-differentiated therapy.

title: Perceptions and lived experiences with abemaciclib and endocrine therapy for early breast cancer: a rapid communication
creator: Helena Harder, Val Jenkins, Lesley Fallowfield
description: AimsThis study explored perceptions and initial experiences of abemaciclib, a CDK4/6 inhibitor, plus endocrine therapy (ET) as adjuvant targeted therapy for early breast cancer with high risk of recurrence (EBC). Early onset diarrhea is the most common side-effect, but its impact is often under-recognized and may affect treatment adherence.

title: Glioinflammation: disease-associated microglia and astrocytes in psychiatric disorders, neurodegeneration, and senescence
creator: Kumiko Uemura, Shunya Hiro, Suthinee Attachaipanich, Ruixue Du, Nur Intan Saidaah Mohamed Yusof, Miyu Kinoshita, Momoka Hikosaka, Gen Ohtsuki
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). In this review, we synthesize recent conceptual and experimental advances in neuroscience, highlighting selected studies that delineate the roles of reactive microglia and astrocytes in the contexts of developmental inflammatory stress, neurodegenerative diseases, and cellular senescence. Since the characterization of disease-associated glial phenotypes in 2017, building on earlier pioneering discoveries, we focus here on disease-associated microglia (DAM) and disease-associated astrocyte (DAA) to reassess their contributions to glio-inflammation.

title: Patricia Goldman-Rakic: a pioneer and leader in frontal lobe research
creator: Bryan Kolb
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Our understanding of the organization of the frontal cortex can be traced back to the experimental studies in the late 1800s by Fritsch and Hitzig on the frontal cortex of dogs and the frontal cortex of monkeys by Ferrier.

title: An Anti‐Amyloidogenic Approach to Specifically Block Memory Consolidation in Mice for Therapeutic Intervention
creator: Paula López‐García, Kerry R. McGreevy, Maria Eugenia Vaquero, Juan M. Suarez‐Rivero, Antonio Moreno‐Rodríguez, Antonio J. Pérez‐Pulido, Daniel Ramírez de Mingo, Anna Pallé, Helena Akiko Popiel, Andrea Santi, Mario D. Cordero, José Luis Trejo, Yoshitaka Nagai, Mariano Carrión‐Vázquez
description: Post‐traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is a mental health disorder triggered by exposure to a traumatic event, which manifests with anguish, intrusive memories, and negative mood changes. So far, there is no efficient treatment for PTSD other than symptomatic palliative care. However, the cytoplasmic polyadenylation element binding protein‐3 (CPEB3) has been recently associated with a potential risk gene for PTSD.

title: Effects of open-skill exercise on executive functions in children and adolescents: a systematic review and meta-analysis
creator: Shunding Hu, Peng Shi, Ziyun Zhang, Xiaosu Feng, Kai Zhang, Teng Jin
description: BackgroundThe research on the intervention of open-skill exercise on the executive functions of children and adolescents still requires quantitative synthesis, and there is inconsistency in the effects of intervention by strategic and interceptive skills, which are sub-divided from open-skill exercise.

title: Adaptive spatial-channel feature fusion and self-calibrated convolution for early maize seedlings counting in UAV images
creator: Zhenyuan Sun, Zhi Yang, Yimin Ding, Boyan Sun, Saiju Li, Zhen Guo, Lei Zhu
description: Accurate counting of crop plants is essential for agricultural science, particularly for yield forecasting, field management, and experimental studies. Traditional methods are labor-intensive and prone to errors. Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) technology offers a promising alternative; however, varying UAV altitudes can impact image quality, leading to blurred features and reduced accuracy in early maize seedling counts.

title: Specific endophenotypes in EEG microstates for methamphetamine use disorder
creator: Xurong Gao, Yun-Hsuan Chen, Ziyi Zeng, Wenyao Zheng, Chengpeng Chai, Hemmings Wu, Zhoule Zhu, Jie Yang, Lihua Zhong, Hua Shen, Mohamad Sawan
description: BackgroundElectroencephalogram (EEG) microstates, which reflect large-scale resting-state networks of the brain, have been proposed as potential endophenotypes for methamphetamine use disorder (MUD). However, current endophenotypes lack refinement at the frequency band level, limiting their precision in identifying key frequency bands associated with MUD.

title: Sleep patterns and smartphone use among left-behind children: a latent class analysis and its association with depressive symptoms
creator: Xue Han, Cheng-Han Li, Heng Miao, Su Xu, Wen-Jing Yan, Juan Chen
description: BackgroundLeft-behind children in China face challenges in sleep patterns, technology use, and mental health. This study uses an individual-centered approach to derive behavioral profiles associated with depressive symptoms.MethodsData from 131,586 left-behind children aged 8 to 18 years from the Chinese Psychological Health Guard for Children and Adolescents Project were analyzed.

title: Deep reinforcement learning for time-critical wilderness search and rescue using drones
creator: Jan-Hendrik Ewers, David Anderson, Douglas Thomson
description: Traditional search and rescue methods in wilderness areas can be time-consuming and have limited coverage. Drones offer a faster and more flexible solution, but optimizing their search paths is crucial for effective operations. This paper proposes a novel algorithm using deep reinforcement learning to create efficient search paths for drones in wilderness environments.

title: Therapeutic alliance with psychotherapist versus dietician: a pilot study of eating disorder treatment in a multidisciplinary team during the COVID-19 pandemic
creator: Roni Elran-Barak, Rinat Grundman-Shem Tov, Eynat Zubery, Yael D. Lewis
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Little is known about the therapeutic alliance (TA) formed with different professionals in multidisciplinary eating disorder (ED) treatment, particularly in the context of online treatment during the COVID-19 pandemic. We aimed to conduct a pilot study during the COVID-19 pandemic examining characteristics of patients’ TA with their dieticians and psychotherapists, associations between patients’ and therapists’ views of the TA, and relationships between psychological characteristics and TAs.

title: Mechanisms underlying the therapeutic effects of cinobufagin in treating melanoma based on network pharmacology, single-cell RNA sequencing data, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulation
creator: Jiansheng Yang, Chunchao Cheng, Zhuolin Wu
description: Malignant melanoma is one of the most aggressive of cancers; if not treated early, it can metastasize rapidly. Therefore, drug therapy plays an important role in the treatment of melanoma. Cinobufagin, an active ingredient derived from Venenum bufonis, can inhibit the growth and development of melanoma. However, the mechanism underlying its therapeutic effects is unclear.

title: Effect of pretransplant spleen volume on the prognosis of acute myeloid leukemia treated with allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation
creator: Weiwei Liu, Bingjie Liu, Lihou Pang, Lixia Zhou, Fuxu Wang, Xuejun Zhang, Ying Wang
description: ObjectiveThis study aimed to evaluate the influence of pre-transplant spleen volume on the prognosis of patients with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) undergoing allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (allo-HSCT).MethodsWe evaluated 58 patients diagnosed with AML and who have undergone first allogeneic stem cell transplant at the Department of Hematology, Second Hospital of Hebei Medical University from 2017 to 2022.

title: CTRP3 alleviates neuropathic pain by improving mitochondrial biogenesis and mitochondrial unfolded protein response via spinal SIRT1 in rats
creator: Tianzhu Liu, Longqing Zhang, Wei Mei
description: Neuropathic pain arises from an intricate network of interconnected pathophysiological mechanisms, yet the arsenal of effective therapeutic strategies remains frustratingly limited. Accumulating evidence has linked mitochondrial dysfunction to the progression of neuropathic pain. C1q-tumor necrosis factor-related protein-3 (CTRP3), a newly identified adipokine with diverse cytoprotective capacities, has not been previously explored for its role in nociceptive processing.

title: Higher serum sCD14 is an independent biomarker for porto-sinusoidal vascular disease risk in CVID
creator: Laure Delaval, Karim Dorgham, Jehane Fadlallah, Emilie Corvilain, Pierre-Emmanuel Rautou, Eric Oksenhendler, Claire Fieschi, Guy Gorochov, Marion Malphettes
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2027). demonstrate in this study that higher serum soluble CD14, a surrogate marker for bacterial translocation, and IgA deficiency are independent and early predictive biomarkers for porto-sinusoidal vascular disease risk in patients with common variable immunodeficiency. Introduction Porto-sinusoidal vascular disorder (PSVD) is the main liver complication in patients with common variable immunodeficiency (CVID) and is associated with high morbimortality.

title: An application of the Theory of Planned Behavior within a living organ donation education intervention for American Muslim communities: a pre–post evaluation
creator: Rosie Duivenbode, Milda Saunders, Raudah Yunus, Michael T Quinn, Aasim I Padela
description: The disparity between supply and demand for life-saving and life-sustaining donor organs disproportionally affects ethnic and racial minorities, which is partly due to negative attitudes and beliefs regarding transplantation. One way to address these disparities is to implement targeted and tailored behavioral interventions among minority communities, such as the American Muslim population.

title: Biomarkers of radioresistance in lung cancer: Current insights and future directions (Review)
creator: Fatima Zohra Attouahri, Imane Chaoui, Abdelilah Laraqui, Mohamed Rida Tagajdid, Mohammed Oukabli, Mohammed El Marjany, Meriem Khyatti, Mohammed Attaleb, Mouna Ababou, Khalid Ennibi, Khaoula Errafii, Mohammed El Mzibri
description: Radiotherapy (RT) remains a cornerstone of lung cancer (LC) management, serving as either a definitive treatment or an adjuvant modality following surgical resection. Nevertheless, a major challenge for radiation oncologists is the emergence of radioresistance, whether intrinsic or acquired, which contributes to therapeutic failure, tumor recurrence, metastasis and ultimately to increased patient mortality.

title: The Maternal Blood Transcriptome Reflects Molecular Signatures Associated With Large Offspring Syndrome and Other Adverse Pregnancy Outcomes in Cattle
creator: Tatiane S Maia, Maria B Rabaglino, Rebecca Krisher, Paula Rodriguez‐Villamil, Jeniffer Pamela J Laguna, Jeniffer F Escoto, Yanping Zhang, Abigail J Sproull, Peter J Hansen
description: Large offspring syndrome (LOS) in cattle is a phenomenon characterized by fetal overgrowth that is largely associated with calves derived from in vitro produced embryos. Here it was tested whether occurrence of LOS as well as two other adverse pregnancy outcomes, stillbirth and abortion, could be predicted using changes in the maternal blood transcriptome early in gestation.

title: School mental health promotion in Indonesia: a quantitative survey from Surabaya
creator: Margaretha Margaretha, Peter S. Azzopardi, Jane Fisher, Susan M. Sawyer
description: IntroductionMost young people live in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), yet little is known about the implementation of school mental health promotion strategies in resource-poor settings. This study describes the extent of school mental health promotion and its drivers in junior high schools in Surabaya, Indonesia.

title: Biofortification of baby corn: Integrating agronomic and genetic approaches to address zinc micronutrient deficiencies - global perspectives and future challenges
creator: Saikrishna Mallipeddi, Venkateswarlu B, Sree Rekha M
description: The central dilemma of the 21st century lies in sustaining nutrient-rich production under the pressures of rapid urbanization, weather abnormalities, and intensified agronomic practices. These factors have collectively heightened the burden on the remaining cropland to produce nutritionally dense food per unit area, while using the same amount of inputs.

title: Adrenergic Contraction of Human Prostate Tissues Is Maintained Under the Rab GTPase Inhibitors Nexhinib20 and CID1067700
creator: Luca Troffer, Peibin Cen, Michael Brandstetter, Yajie Xu, Patrick Keller, Leo Stadelmeier, Philipp Weinhold, Alexander Tamalunas, Christian G Stief, Martin Hennenberg
description: α1‐Adrenoceptors are an important drug target in benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) and have been intensively studied at the expression level, but their posttranslational regulation in the prostate is widely unknown. Here we examined modulation of prostate smooth muscle contractions by inhibitors for RabGTPases, which are involved in intracellular transport of internalized receptors and in vesicle function.

title: Orchestral maneuvers: integrated cytokinin and gibberellin signals regulate flowering
creator: Grace A Johnston, Cristiana T Argueso
description: This article comments on: Werner S, Bartrina I, Tarkowská D, Werner T, Schmülling T. 2026. Cytokinin regulates flowering time in Arabidopsis thaliana through the gibberellin pathway. Journal of Experimental Botany 77, 6510–6521. https://doi.org/10.1093/jxb/erag284 This article comments on: Werner S, Bartrina I, Tarkowská D, Werner T, Schmülling T. 2026. Cytokinin regulates flowering time in Arabidopsis thaliana through the gibberellin pathway.

title: Mapping the global threat of Mythimna separata (Walker) and its economic implications for Brazil's agriculture
creator: Gabriel Dorotel da Silva Ferreira, Cesar Augusto Marchioro
description: BACKGROUNDIdentifying high‐risk areas for the introduction of invasive alien species is particularly important for agricultural pests with a broad host range that attack widely cultivated crops, such as the oriental armyworm, Mythimna separata (Walker, 1865) (Lepidoptera: Noctuidae). This study aimed to assess the global climatic suitability for M.

title: Molecular characterization and lineage analysis of canine astrovirus strains from dogs with gastrointestinal disease in Ecuador based on ORF-2 gene analysis
creator: Anthony Loor-Giler, Silvana Santander-Parra, Sara Castillo-Reyes, Martín Campos, Renan Mena-Perez, Santiago Prado-Chiriboga, Luis Nunez
description: Canine Astrovirus (CaAstV) part of the Astroviridae family and genus Mamastrovirus, is a linear RNA virus with a genome of approximately 6.6 kb with three open reading frames (ORF): ORF1a and ORF1b, which code for the most conserved non-structural proteins, and ORF2, which code for the capsid protein, the most variable region of the genome.

title: Thiolated Polymers in 3D Bioprinting: Control of Gelation
creator: Soheil Haddadzadegan, Flavia Laffleur, Andreas Bernkop‐Schnürch
description: Thiolated polymers represent a versatile class of bioinks for extrusion‐based 3D bioprinting, combining cytocompatibility with tunable crosslinking chemistry and dynamic redox‐responsive behaviour. This review consolidates recent advances in thiomer chemistry, focusing on synthetic strategies that modulate thiol reactivity through pKa adjustment, neighboring‐group interactions, and redox control.

title: Deletion of dltD gene modulates biofilm matrix and acid metabolism to attenuate Streptococcus mutans cariogenicity
creator: Jingyun Du, Shan Huang, Yijun Li, Zhoucheng Qiu, Yujia Hao, Jing Huang, Ling Zhan, Shuai Chen, Xiaojing Huang
description: IntroductionStreptococcus mutans (SM) is one of the key pathogenic bacteria in the occurrence and development of dental caries. Its complex virulence regulation network has become an important target in current ecological caries prevention research. This study explored how dltD attenuates SM cariogenicity using standard strain SMUA159, high-cariogenic clinical strain SM593, and their dltD deletion/complemented strains.

title: Therapeutic-scale CAR-NK microrobots with programmable swarm navigation for targeted solid tumor therapy
creator: Zhiguang Wu, Yalin Wang, Hongyue Zhang, Xinjian Fan, Mingtong Li, Zesheng Li, Gongzi Zhang, Jialin Wang, Yumeng Lu, Hongda Wang, Yuxin Jia, Hongri Gu, He Tan, Jiawei Tian, Ximing Sun, Hui Xie, Lihai Zhang, Metin Sitti, Jie Zhao
description: An urgent requirement in chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) immune cell therapy [e.g., CAR–natural killer (NK) cells] for solid tumors is to engineer the cells for precise tumor targeting. Meanwhile, medical microrobots can be navigated toward specific target sites using external magnetic fields.

title: Target‐Engagement Prediction From Molecular Structure, In Vitro and Animal Data: A Tutorial for Early Assessment of Clinical Drug Exposure and Therapeutic/Adverse Potential Using the ANDROMEDA and PLATO Software on the InSilicoTrials Platform
creator: Niccolò Totis, Fianne Sips, Simona Catozzi, Marc‐Antonio Bisotti, Pauline Bambury, Sofia Stathopoulos, Vincenzo Carbone, Luca Emili, Mario Torchia, Valentina Belgiovine, Fulvio Ciriaco, Orazio Nicolotti, Urban Fagerholm, Candice N Baker, J Matthew Mahoney, Daniel Röshammar, the CARDIOVERSE Project
description: The target‐engagement predictor, implemented within the InSilicoTrials cloud‐based, AI‐powered platform for model‐informed drug discovery and development, enables early exploration of time‐dependent pharmacological responses. Predictions can be generated using inputs ranging from molecular structure to in vitro, animal, and clinical data. Scaling and translation across species are supported, accounting for differences in body size and plasma protein binding.

title: Associations Between Perceived Knowledge, Interprofessional Collaboration, Autonomy and the Frequency of Nursing Activities in Paediatric Extracorporeal Membrane Oxygenation: A Cross‐Sectional Study
creator: Semyon Melnikov, Reem Abed Elhai, Nashaat Hijazi, Nagah Zaid, Alex Furmanov
description: BackgroundExtracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO) requires coordinated multidisciplinary care. Although registered nurses (RNs) play a critical role, evidence on factors associated with the frequency of ECMO‐related nursing activities in paediatric settings remains limited.AimTo examine associations between perceived ECMO knowledge, interprofessional collaboration, nursing autonomy and the frequency of ECMO‐related nursing activities.Study DesignA multicentre cross‐sectional study was conducted.

title: Revisiting suicide prevention in later life: mixed-methods study protocol
creator: M Isabela Troya, Paul Corcoran, Derek Chambers, Anne M Doherty, Donagh Hennebry, Katerina Kavalidou, Caoimhe Lonergan, Sally Ann Lovejoy, Faraz Mughal, Michael Norton, Emma Wallace, Ella Arensman
description: BackgroundGlobally, suicide is more prevalent in older adults compared with any other age group. Although some research has identified risk and protective factors for suicidal behaviour in older adults, further research is needed to provide an up-to-date overview to inform service delivery.

title: Quantified fat fraction as biomarker assessing disease severity in rare Charcot–Marie–Tooth subtypes
creator: Xingwen Sun, Xiaoxuan Liu, Qiang Zhao, Lihua Zhang, Huishu Yuan
description: ObjectiveCharcot–Marie–Tooth (CMT) disease is the most common inherited neuromuscular disorder. Multi-echo Dixon MRI technique is a highly sensitive method for quantifying muscle fatty infiltration, which may provide excellent value for the assessment of CMT. Due to the rareness of the disease, its use in CMT disease has been rarely evaluated, especially in subtypes.

title: Signed motif analysis of the Caenorhabditis elegans neuronal network reveals positive feedforward and negative feedback loops
creator: Gabor S Szilagyi, Attila Gulyas, Zsolt Vassy, Peter Csermely, Bank G Fenyves
description: BackgroundNervous systems are complex biological networks with largely unknown structural and functional characteristics. Motif analysis is a robust tool that can reveal the unique aspects of connectivity in a complex network. An ideal candidate for motif analysis is the connectome of the nematode Caenorhabditis elegans, which is the first fully reconstructed nervous system.

title: Radical-induced autoxidation dominates squalene oxidative aging under environmental conditions
creator: Xinke Wang, Jillian P. Downey, Giulia Gobbi, William D. Fahy, Wanqi Wu, Linna Xie, Xingwang Hou, Hui Peng, Jonathan P. D. Abbatt
description: Ozone has been viewed as the principal oxidant of skin oils and other unsaturated surface films, but their fate under realistic indoor conditions remains poorly constrained. Here, we use squalene (SQ), a major component of skin lipids, to investigate the dominant oxidation pathways in occupied indoor environments and laboratory flow reactors.

title: Phase I clinical trial of lobaplatin combined with image-guided volume-modulated arc radiation therapy in locally advanced cervical cancer
creator: Jing You, Danning Wu, Jian Tie, Junyue Shen, Yidi Yuan, Xiaoxuan Gu, Weihu Wang, Xiaofan Li
description: BackgroundWe aimed to determine the maximum tolerable dose (MTD) and dose-limiting toxicities (DLTs) of weekly lobaplatin chemotherapy concurrent with external beam radiotherapy (EBRT) using image-guided volumetric-modulated arc therapy (VMAT) and brachytherapy in locally advanced cervical cancer (LACC).MethodsPatients with clinical stage IB3-IVA cervical cancer were enrolled following a standard 3 + 3 dose escalation design.

title: Using Machine Learning Methodology to Identify Predictors of Non-Response to MTSS-B: a Focus on Discipline Problems and Juvenile Justice Involvement
creator: Kate Somerville, Ali Ünlü, Angela K. Henneberger, Bess A. Rose, Elise T. Pas, Catherine P. Bradshaw
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Multi-tiered systems of support for behavior (MTSS-B) is a widely-used tiered preventive intervention currently used in over 25,000 schools across the USA. This study leveraged data from 16,907 elementary students across 42 schools that participated in a prior randomized controlled trial (RCT) of MTSS-B, where schools were randomly assigned to implement Tier 1 + 2 (intervention) supports or Tier 1 only (comparison).

title: Risk and protection of different rare protein-coding variants of complement component C4A in age-related macular degeneration
creator: Johanna M. Seddon, Dikha De, William Casazza, Shun-Yun Cheng, Claudio Punzo, Mark Daly, Danlei Zhou, Samantha L. Coss, John P. Atkinson, Chack-Yung Yu
description: Introduction: Age-related macular degeneration (AMD) is the leading cause of central vision loss in the elderly. One-third of the genetic contribution to this disease remains unexplained. Methods: We analyzed targeted sequencing data from two independent cohorts (4,245 cases, 1,668 controls) which included genomic regions of known AMD loci in 49 genes. Results: At a false discovery rate of <0.

title: Case Report: Dominant deafness-onychodystrophy syndrome and hypokalemic periodic paralysis in a single patient: a rare syndromic overlap
creator: Dong-Lan Luo, Rui-Ping Liu, Xin-Yi Hou, Zhi Liu, Bin Lu
description: Dominant deafness-onychodystrophy syndrome (DDOD) and hypokalemic periodic paralysis (HypoPP) are distinct autosomal dominant disorders caused by mutations in ATP6V1B2 and CACNA1S, respectively. We describe an eight-year-old female with congenital deafness, nail dysplasia, enamel hypoplasia, and recurrent episodes of hypokalemia-induced muscle weakness. Whole-exome sequencing (WES) revealed a de novo ATP6V1B2 nonsense variant (c.1516C>T, p.

title: International multi-center study to quantify the effect of deep venous drainage after surgical resection of Spetzler-Martin Grade II-III brain arteriovenous malformations
creator: Avi A. Gajjar, Rashad Jabarkheel, Mohamed M. Salem, Basel Musmar, Sandeep Kandregula, Hammam Abdalrazeq, Nimer Adeeb, Assala Aslan, Nathan Ramachandran, Stavropoula I Tjoumakaris, Hamza Adel Salim, Adam A. Dmytriw, Christopher S. Ogilvy, Mustafa K. Baskaya, Douglas Kondziolka, Jason Sheehan, Howard
description: Deep venous drainage (DVD) is considered a negative prognostic factor in AVM surgery, yet its effect on postoperative functional decline remains incompletely defined. This study evaluates whether DVD predicts worsened functional status after surgical resection of Spetzler-Martin Grade II-III AVMs.

title: Tumor absorbed dose and outcomes after Y-90 glass radioembolization for colorectal liver metastases: does dose escalation improve survival in real-world practice?
creator: Osman Melih Topcuoglu, Betul Uzunoglu, Tolga Orhan, Ismail Necim Yucel, Ayşegul Gormez, Turkay Toklu, Nalan Alan Selcuk
description: PurposeTo assess the dose-response and dose-survival outcomes of yttrium-90 (Y90) transarterial radioembolization (TARE) using Therasphere microspheres in patients with colorectal cancer liver metastases (CRCLM).Material and methodsBetween May 2014 and December 2024, patients with chemorefractory CRCLM who underwent Y90 TARE using glass microspheres were retrospectively included.

title: Course of well-being and mental health in Switzerland during the COVID-19 pandemic: results of a national survey within the framework of the COH-FIT study
creator: Christian G. Huber, Janina Billian, Tiziana Ziltener, Philippe Conus, Roland von Känel, Gregor Hasler, Jihed Sehli, Anna Mosina, Damir Krinitski, Erich Seifritz, Eva Kowalinski, Isabelle Gothuey, Jennifer Marian, Undine E. Lang, Trevor Thompson, Marco Solmi, Christoph U. Correll, Sabina C. Heuss, An
description: IntroductionThe COVID-19 pandemic significantly impacted the mental health of the Swiss population.MethodsThis study analyzed data from the Collaborative Outcome study on Health and Functioning during Infection Times (COH-FIT) across three pandemic waves: T1 (April–June 2020), T2 (July–December 2020) or T3 (January–June 2021). Each participant participated only once, during one of these three waves.

title: Attenuation of acute kidney injury in a murine model of neonatal Escherichia coli sepsis
creator: Esther M. Speer, Atilade A. Adedeji, Joyce Lin, Alexandra Khorasanchi, Asma Rasheed, Maya Bhat, Kelly Mackenzie, Randolph Hennigar, Kimberly J. Reidy, Robert P. Woroniecki
description: IntroductionSepsis is a risk factor for acute kidney injury (AKI) in neonates, for which no effective treatment exists. The phosphodiesterase inhibitor pentoxifylline (PTX) has demonstrated renal protection from ischemia and inflammation in adult rodents. We hypothesized that addition of PTX to antibiotics may attenuate immune and histological AKI in a murine neonatal sepsis model.

title: Flower development and morphoanatomy of Dendrophthora costaricensis Urb. (Viscaceae) and its implications in the taxonomy of Phoradendreae
creator: Alejandro V Yañez-Macias, Emmanuel Martínez-Ambriz, Sonia Vázquez-Santana
description: Dendrophthora is a genus of stem-parasitic plants that are commonly known as mistletoes. It exhibits a notable morphological similarity to Phoradendron, which makes differentiation difficult. Traditionally, the two genera are grouped within the tribe Phoradendreae. Molecular analyses have called into question the monophyly of each genus but confirm the monophyly of Phoradendreae.

title: Dietary calcium intake in primary hyperparathyroidism and in its normocalcemic variant: a case-control study
creator: Nicolò Bisceglia, Matteo Malagrinò, Anna Piazza, Giulia Vandi, Andrea Repaci, Uberto Pagotto, Guido Zavatta
description: IntroductionNormocalcemic primary hyperparathyroidism (NHPT) is considered to be an early stage in the evolution of primary hyperparathyroidism (PHPT). To formulate a correct diagnosis, secondary hyperparathyroidism due to low calcium intake must be excluded. Whether dietary calcium intake might affect the clinical presentation of PHPT or NHPT has never been addressed consistently.

title: Culture-based and culture-independent approach for the study of the methanogens and obligate anaerobes from different landfill sites
creator: Om Prakash, Sahab Ram Dewala, Yogesh Nimonkar, Shalaka K. Patil, Ashvini Chauhan, Amit Yadav, Dheeraj P. Dhotre, Dilip R. Ranade
description: The landfill is a cheap way of solid waste management in developing countries. The majority of landfills are non-sanitary and work as open garbage dumping sites and pose threats to public and environmental health. Therefore, an in-depth understanding of the chemistry and microbiology of landfills is imperative to develop the right policies for landfill management.

title: Terroir and farming practices drive arbuscular mycorrhizal fungal communities in French vineyards
creator: Patricia Battie-Laclau, Adrien Taudière, Mathilde Bernard, Lucas Bodénan, Myriam Duchemin, Yvan de Roman, Azimê Yol, Dominique Barry-Etienne
description: BackgroundNature-based management of vineyards is at the heart of a sustainable development for the next decades. Although much is known about grapevine benefits from Arbuscular Mycorrhizal Fungi (AMF), little is known about the influence of vineyard terroir and farming practices on AMF communities.

title: SDA: a data-driven algorithm that detects functional states applied to the EEG of Guhyasamaja meditation
creator: Ekaterina Mikhaylets, Alexandra M. Razorenova, Vsevolod Chernyshev, Nikolay Syrov, Lev Yakovlev, Julia Boytsova, Elena Kokurina, Yulia Zhironkina, Svyatoslav Medvedev, Alexander Kaplan
description: The study presents a novel approach designed to detect time-continuous states in time-series data, called the State-Detecting Algorithm (SDA). The SDA operates on unlabeled data and detects optimal change-points among intrinsic functional states in time-series data based on an ensemble of Ward's hierarchical clustering with time-connectivity constraint.

title: The prevalence of E198A and F200Y single nucleotide polymorphism in Haemonchus contortus populations from Polish goat herds
creator: Zofia Nowek, Marcin Mickiewicz, Michał Czopowicz, Agata Moroz-Fik, Adrian-Valentin Potărniche, Kinga Biernacka, Tomasz Nalbert, Olga Szaluś-Jordanow, Paweł Górski, Alistair Antonopoulos, Iwona Markowska-Daniel, Emilia Bagnicka, Marián Várady, Jarosław Kaba
description: A cross-sectional descriptive study was carried out on a study population of 81 goat herds to investigate the prevalence and frequency of two single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs; E198A and F200Y) associated with resistance to benzimidazoles (BZ) in Haemonchus contortus populations of goats in Poland.

title: Description and biomechanical evaluation of the modified laparoscopic-assisted percutaneous gastropexy technique in dogs
creator: Dong Woo Kim, Ho Hyun Kwak, Junhyung Kim, Heung Myong Woo
description: BackgroundTotal laparoscopic gastropexy (TLG) has become increasingly popular due to its minimally invasive nature, requiring only three ports and no additional skin incisions aside from those for port placement. However, a notable limitation of TLG is the difficulty and time required for intracorporeal suturing. To address this challenge, we investigated a new technique—modified laparoscopic-assisted percutaneous gastropexy (mLAPG)—in canine cadavers.

title: Formation of hydroxyapatite on tooth surfaces by calcium hypophosphite in saliva
creator: Pascal Fandrich, Erik Schulze zur Wiesche, Bennett Tochukwu Amaechi, Joachim Enax
description: AimThis in vitro study aimed to investigate whether calcium hypophosphite (CaP) mediates hydroxyapatite (HAP) formation in artificial and human saliva and, in a proof-of-principle toothbrushing model, promotes mineral deposition and occlusion of dentinal tubules.MethodsA CaP solution was added to artificial saliva and human saliva, respectively. The resulting precipitate was analyzed using X-ray powder diffraction (XRD).

title: Delayed diagnosis leading to severe complications in primary hyperparathyroidism caused by atypical parathyroid tumor
creator: Francesca Lacchè, Alessandro Ciarloni, Monia Bordoni, Gianmaria Salvio, Giancarlo Balercia, Gilberta Giacchetti
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Severe skeletal complications at the onset of primary hyperparathyroidism are uncommon in contemporary Western clinical practice because routine serum calcium measurement usually allows early diagnosis. We describe a case of primary hyperparathyroidism in which delayed diagnosis, despite suggestive symptoms, led to an extremely severe presentation characterized by multiple fractures, osteolytic lesions, and prolonged postsurgical hungry bone syndrome requiring several months of intensive treatments and hospitalization. During hospitalization, the patient developed potentially life-threatening infectious and thrombotic complications.

title: Impact of Preoperative Chronic Opioid Use on Postoperative Outcomes Following Lumbar Fusion: A Nationwide Analysis
creator: Atef F Hulliel, Dana Saleh, Ahmad Zayd Alkadri, David J Boughanem, Rafal Chociej, Freddie Rodriguez Beato, Srujan Kopparapu, Patrick Kim, Mohsen Rostami, Puya Alikhani
description: Study DesignRetrospective cohort study.ObjectivesChronic opioid use is common among patients undergoing lumbar fusion, and preoperative use has been linked to worse postoperative outcomes. However, much of this evidence derives from administrative datasets with limited ability to adjust for mental health.

title: A curved-beam piezoelectric MEMS resonator featuring multiple temperature plateaus with enhanced stability
creator: Yancheng Lian, Yueyang Li, Fangzhou Chen, Zhuoyue Zheng, Jinuo Zhou, Junchen Liu, Fengzhe Xu, Jinbo Yang, Jianlin Chen, Chen Wang, Michael Kraft, Ka-Meng Lei, R P Martins, Pui-In Mak, Yuan Wang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Silicon-based Micro-electromechanical Systems (MEMS) resonators face stability challenges due to their temperature susceptibility, which impedes the advancement towards high-precision applications. This work reports a multi-modal curved-beam piezoelectric resonator that enhances frequency stability through engineered irregular geometry and mechanical nonlinearity. Utilizing a standard Silicon-On-Insulator (SOI) - Aluminum Nitride (AlN) process, the proposed device engenders 17 vibration modes within 5 MHz, addressing the detection constraints and information extraction of non-inplane modes for capacitive counterparts and circumventing the needs of vacuum encapsulation.

title: Competency-based training in anaesthesiology: train the trainers first. A descriptive cross-sectional survey by the committee of the European Society of Anaesthesiology and Intensive Care (ESAIC) Teach the Teachers Masterclass
creator: Vojislava Neskovic, Carmen Oliveira, Aeyal Raz, Lesley Bromley, Gordana Jovanovic
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). IntroductionThe level of competence in teaching among trainers expected to deliver training according to the European Training Requirement in anaesthesiology is unknown. The aim of this descriptive cross-sectional survey, performed from 1 September 2021 until 31 October 2021, and promoted by the European Society of Anaesthesiology and Intensive Care (ESAIC) was to establish the current level of knowledge and faculty development among European countries regarding competency-based education and training (CBMET) in anesthesia and intensive care.ResultsA total of 711 responses of anaesthesiologists working

title: Mechanical ventilation–associated AKI: toward a multimodal and kidney-protective ventilatory framework
creator: Ying Gao, Yipeng Fang, Silvia De Rosa, Michele Salvagno, Lina Zhao, Keliang Xie, Fabio Silvio Taccone
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Mechanical ventilation–associated acute kidney injury (AKI) represents a complex manifestation of lung–kidney cross-talk driven by hemodynamic alterations, neurohumoral activation, systemic inflammation and disturbances in gas exchange and acid–base homeostasis. Beyond static ventilatory settings, increasing evidence suggests that dynamic fluctuations in airway and perfusion parameters, including static driving pressure (ΔP), positive end-expiratory pressure (PEEP), mean airway pressure (Pmean), and effective renal perfusion pressure (eRPP) may substantially influence renal vulnerability during mechanical ventilation.

title: Evaluation of host-immune biomarker signatures as multiplex qPCR diagnostic assays: a pilot study toward meeting WHO target product profiles for TB diagnosis in India
creator: Harriet N. Garlant, Kalaiarasan Ellappan, Noyal Mariya Joseph, Carrie Turner, Vishnukanth Govindaraj, Saka Vinod Kumar, Sanjeev Kumar, Seshadri Vasan, Karen E. Kempsell
description: BackgroundTuberculosis (TB) remains the leading cause of death from a single infectious agent. Current diagnostic tools are limited, especially in low-resource settings. The World Health Organization's (WHO) Target Product Profiles (TPPs) call for rapid, non-sputum-based diagnostics with high sensitivity and specificity.

title: Parental involvement, self-efficacy, and learning motivation of hearing-impaired students: insights from Savelugu, Ghana
creator: Isaac Nyame, Mary Nyeyem Issah, Sampson Mante, Christiana Nyarko Adjei, Diana Baapeng
description: The educational development of learners with Hearing Impairment (HI) remains a significant concern within inclusive education systems, especially in low-resource countries. The influence of parental involvement and academic self-efficacy on motivation to learn is considered important, but their relationship has not been thoroughly examined in Sub-Saharan Africa.

title: Persistent Hypoxia After Tricuspid Valve Replacement
creator: John Nguyen, Thomas Merino, Vijay Kandula, Leticia Castillo Kontak, Raul Mercado Garcia, Angel Caldera, Aditi Shankar, Rafael Gonzalez, Soumya Neravetla, Jose F Condado
description: BackgroundTranscatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR) is a novel therapy for symptomatic severe tricuspid regurgitation in high-risk surgical patients. Platypnea-orthopnea syndrome has not previously been described as a complication of TTVR.Case SummaryA 76-year-old woman with symptomatic severe tricuspid regurgitation underwent successful TTVR but developed persistent hypoxia despite negative pulmonary work-up. Her hypoxia followed a platypnea-orthodeoxia pattern.

title: Risk factors for multiple bronchoalveolar lavage procedures in children with severe or refractory Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia
creator: Chaolei Yang, Guitao Li, Ying Zhu, Yong Wang, Lei Zhang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveTo identify factors influencing how often bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) is performed in children with severe or refractory Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia (MPP) and provide evidence to guide early intervention.MethodsClinical data for 271 children with severe or refractory MPP who underwent BAL at the studied institution between May 1, 2023, and April 30, 2024, were retrospectively divided according to the number of BAL procedures into a single-treatment group (STG, n = 219) and a multiple-treatment group (≥ 2 times; MTG, n = 52).

title: Depression and anxiety symptoms among women in post-conflict Somalia: a cross-sectional study in maternal and child health centres
creator: Gallad D. Hassan, Juweria N. L. Abshir, Fatumo Osman
description: ObjectiveMental health issues can be regarded as a severe public health problem that affects low-, middle-, and high-income countries worldwide. However, certain populations in post-conflict countries may have particularly vulnerable mental health, such as women of childbearing age in Somalia.

title: Pediatric oncology drug development and dosage optimization
creator: S. Y. Amy Cheung, Justin L. Hay, Yu-Wei Lin, Rik de Greef, Julie Bullock
description: Oncology drug discovery and development has always been an area facing many challenges. Phase 1 oncology studies are typically small, open-label, sequential studies enrolling a small sample of adult patients (i.e., 3-6 patients/cohort) in dose escalation. Pediatric evaluations typically lag behind the adult development program.

title: Cancer Treatment During Pregnancy and Maternal and Infant Outcomes: A Descriptive Cohort Study Using a Japanese Claims Database
creator: Masami Tsuchiya, Tomofumi Ishikawa, Takamasa Sakai, Satoko Hori, Taku Obara
description: PurposeTo characterize cancer treatment during pregnancy and maternal and infant outcomes among women with cancer identified during pregnancy in Japan.MethodsIn this descriptive cohort study, we used mother‐infant linkage data from the JMDC claims database from 2005 to 2024. Live‐birth pregnancies were considered eligible when a malignant neoplasm (ICD‐10 C00–C97) was recorded between the estimated pregnancy onset and delivery.

title: Impact of Incidental Durotomy on Health Care Resource Utilization Following Posterior Cervical Decompression and Fusion
creator: Mitchell K Ng, Leonidas E Mastrokostas, Paul G Mastrokostas, Eli Berglas, Matthew W Xie, Masataka Mizuno, Imran Kyeso, Avi Gupta, Jesse M Galina, Arie Monas, Jorden Xavier, Sarah Brauer, Pemla Jagtiani, Jad Bou Monsef, Afshin E Razi, Daniel R Fassett, Andrew P Alvarez, Nicholas U Ahn, Mark F Kurd, I
description: Study DesignRetrospective cohort study.ObjectivesTo evaluate the national incidence and hospitalization impact of incidental durotomy following elective posterior cervical decompression and fusion (PCDF), with respect to complications, length of stay (LOS), costs, and discharge disposition.MethodsAdults undergoing elective PCDF were identified in the 2016–2022 National Inpatient Sample.

title: Maize STEM BENDING1 controls plant architecture through cell wall and auxin pathways
creator: Shiya Zhao, Babar Farid, Xintong Liu, Liang Dong, Fang Yang
description: Crop yield is largely determined by plant architecture. Identifying the key genes responsible for maize architecture can help optimize plant architecture for high-density planting. Here, we characterized a dominant stem bending mutant (Stb1) in maize, which exhibited bent stems and curved leaves leading to a slanted architecture. Genetic mapping delimited Stb1 to a 3.7 Mb interval on chromosome 1.

title: Fully automated diaphragm segmentation on routine 2D-cine and 3D thoracic MRI: multireader validation
creator: Samia Boussouar, Alexiane Pasquier, Damien Vaurs, Arthur Dilane Douho Kamta, Anna Reitmann, Nicoletta Pasi, Victoria Donciu, Sara Benchara, Tatiana Wong, Myriam Belghiti, Ithar Gharmaoui, Rose-Marie Dubuisson, Angéline Nemeth, Vincent Lebon, Claire Pellot-Barakat, Marie Poirier-Quinot, Xavier Maître
description: ObjectiveThe diaphragm is central to respiratory mechanics and may be impaired in various diseases. Parametric magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) assessment is limited by time-consuming manual segmentation. We developed and validated fully automated diaphragm segmentation on two-dimensional (2D)-cine and three-dimensional (3D) thoracic MRI.Materials and methodsIn this single-center study, eligible adults without known diaphragmatic disorders underwent 2D-cine MRI, 3D MRI, or both.

title: Relevance theory and the social realities of communication
creator: Marilynn Johnson
description: A central tenet of theories of meaning in the Gricean tradition—such as Relevance Theory—is that others will come to believe certain things simply by recognizing our intentions to communicate. In this article I demonstrate that this is not equally the case for all interlocutors; some bear additional burdens. In particular, I argue that this can happen in two ways.

title: Expanded characterization of the valproic acid zebrafish larval model of autism spectrum disorder: Insights into dysregulation in the gut
creator: Lesha Pretorius, Johanna Adriana Coetzee, Alexio Pedro dos Santos, Carine Smith
description: BackgroundRelative lack of data on mechanisms underpinning poor gastrointestinal (GI) health in autism spectrum disorder (ASD) limits patient management strategies. Although the valproic acid (VPA) model of ASD is widely used, a comprehensive profile of the model in zebrafish is still lacking, and almost no data are available on ASD‐like GI symptomology or underlying mechanisms.

title: Neurodiversity: post-cognitivist foundations of the 3E approach for educational inclusion of autistic students with technology
creator: Ronnie Videla, May Britt Aros, Francisco Parada, Leonie Kausel, Eduardo Sandoval-Obando, Daniela Jorquera, David Ibacache, Sebastián Maluenda, Pablo Rodríguez-Herrero, Carola Cerpa, María Jesús González, Marcelo Chávez, Paola Ramírez
description: The concept of neurodiversity has gained strength in the last years to highlight the value of individual differences based on relevant variations in brain functioning. Inclusive education has embraced neurodiversity to promote a culture centered on valuing diversity, in response to clinical models based on deficits or disorders.

title: A Comprehensive Self-Medication Management System to Reduce Medication Errors Among People Living With Dementia: Mixed Methods Feasibility and Usability Study
creator: Santosh Basapur, Charles Gellman, Jamie B Plenge, Amelia Troutman, Erin Yurko, Brandon Woolsey, Justin McClendon, Lisa Marceau, Neelum T Aggarwal
description: BackgroundMedication adherence is a critical challenge for people living with dementia and their caregivers. Standard care relies on appropriate medication management, yet there are few effective options beyond manual pill-counting and caregiver-administered dosing. These methods are prone to errors and impose a significant burden.

title: Pathways to the development of purpose in life among ethnic minority adolescents
creator: Rosa Kim, Meeyoung O Min, Sarah L Canham, Morgan Williams
description: Purpose in life has been defined as a sense of meaning, direction, and commitment to valued long‐term goals. Developing a sense of purpose in life is an important task during adolescence and considered an essential developmental asset. However, current understandings of how adolescents, particularly those with an ethnic minority background, develop their life purpose remain limited.

title: Application of next-generation sequencing to identify different pathogens
creator: Aljuboori M. Nafea, Yuer Wang, Duanyang Wang, Ahmed M. Salama, Manal A. Aziz, Shan Xu, Yigang Tong
description: Early and precise detection and identification of various pathogens are essential for epidemiological monitoring, disease management, and reducing the prevalence of clinical infectious diseases. Traditional pathogen detection techniques, which include mass spectrometry, biochemical tests, molecular testing, and culture-based methods, are limited in application and are time-consuming. Next generation sequencing (NGS) has emerged as an essential technology for identifying pathogens.

title: Design of an implementation research study for a digital omnichannel community engagement and risk communication intervention for the prevention and control of vector-borne diseases in India: the OMNIVEC-India study protocol
creator: Rashmi Rodrigues, Amey Dhatrak, Madhusmita Bal, Melari Shisha Nongrum, Neeraj Kumar, Rajiv Sarkar, Twinkle Agrawal, Anuj Mundra, Ira Praharaj, Jyoti Singh, Mrunali Zode, Sudipto Roy, Vani Kandpal, Tanica Lyngdoh, Omnivec Study Team
description: IntroductionVector-borne diseases (VBDs), such as malaria, dengue, and lymphatic filariasis, pose significant public health challenges in India, contributing significantly to the nation’s morbidity and mortality. In this scenario, digital technology promises scalable, contextual, and user-centric interventions for behavior change. However, systematic and comprehensive community-based digital approaches for VBD prevention in India are limited.

title: Clinical, social, molecular, and genetic predictors of cognitive resilience in long-living adults without dementia
creator: Ekaterina Spektor, Aleksandra Mamchur, Mariia Bruttan, Liliya Artemieva, Antonina Rumyantseva, Lorena Matkava, Mikhail Ivanov, Veronika Daniel, Sergey Igorevich Mitrofanov, Irina Strazhesko, Vladimir Yudin, Valentin Makarov, Anton Keskinov, Olga Tkacheva, Daria Kashtanova, Sergey Yudin, Veronika Skv
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundLong-living adults often maintain cognitive function despite neuropathological changes, which is often attributed to cognitive resilience (CR)—a combined effect of cognitive and cerebral reserves. CR is influenced by genetic, clinical, sociodemographic, and environmental factors.Materials and methodsWe investigated genetic, clinical, and environmental predictors of CR in 198 dementia-free long-living adults via two neuropsychological examinations over a 2-year period, a geriatric assessment, and a genome-wide association study (GWAS).ResultsLimited mobility, reduced walking, hearing impairment, depression, anemia, lower quality of life, and decreased BMI were key

title: Factors affecting equitable access and uptake of COVID-19 vaccines in Ghana: a scoping review
creator: James Akazili, Dominic Anaseba, Samuel Chatio, Michel Adurayi Amenah, Daniel Malik Achala, Senait Aleamyehu Beshah, Chijioke O. Nwosu, Nyasha Masuka, John Thato Tlhakanelo, Ifeanyi Chikezie, Elizabeth Naa Adukwei Adote, Grace Njeri Muriithi, John Ele-Ojo Ataguba
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundThe coronavirus disease (COVID-19) emerged as one of the most serious pandemics that impacted health systems and world economies.
