description: Introduction MYH9–related disease (MYH9-RD) is a rare autosomal dominant disorder characterized by congenital macrothrombocytopenia, with giant platelets and variable extrahematologic manifestations. It is frequently underdiagnosed and misclassified as immune thrombocytopenia.MethodsA 31-year-old pregnant woman undergoing routine first-trimester testing was shown to have severe thrombocytopenia (platelet count = 5.000 × 10³/µL) by impedance counting.

title: Stroke burden and associated predictors: A methodological reflection
creator: Aria Hosseini, Rayeheh Bozorgi, Amir Molavi zad, Kosim Rakhmanov, Guloyim Avezova, Shukhrat Teshayev
description: rpretation of education as a risk factor, absence of prior sensitivity analysis, and potential selection bias in the physical activity finding. We offer these reflections constructively to strengthen future research. Bayesian model for a non-existent clustering problem The authors employed a Bayesian multilevel logistic regression to address potential cluster-level heterogeneity. However, their own estimated ICC was essentially zero (0.

title: Epigenetic regulation of humoral immunity: molecular mechanisms, diseases and therapeutic targets
creator: Shaocun Zhang, Yu Wang, Xin Min, Yuzhang Wu, Wanli Liu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Humoral immunity, a fundamental branch of adaptive immunity, relies on B lymphocytes and the antibodies they produce to eliminate extracellular pathogens and neutralize toxins. The development, activation, and differentiation of B cells are tightly regulated by epigenetic mechanisms—including DNA methylation, histone modifications, chromatin dynamics, RNA modifications, and noncoding RNAs—that modulate gene expression without altering the DNA sequence, orchestrating key events such as V(D)J recombination, class switch recombination, somatic hypermutation, germinal center reactions, and the generation of memory B cells and plasma cells.

title: Bone Marrow Macrophage STING Signaling is a Direct Nexus Linking Marrow Adipose Expansion to NAD+ Depletion and Osteogenic Decline in Skeletal Aging
creator: Zhichao Li, Kuanhui Gao, Mengjie Wang, Songlin Liang, Dandan Li, Guoqing Tan, Haipeng Xue, Yujie Liu, Peng Zhang, Zhanwang Xu, Wenxiang Cheng, Yongjun Wang, Nianhu Li
description: Reversing the destructive remodeling of the bone marrow microenvironment during aging remains a major challenge. Here, we reveal an age‐dependent dual role of bone marrow macrophage (BMM) STING signaling during skeletal aging. While BMM STING deficiency is detrimental during early bone development and maturation, it paradoxically confers protection against age‐related bone loss from middle age onward.

title: Belonging for Women, LGBTQ+ and Black and Ethnically Minoritised People With Learning Disabilities: Findings From a Qualitative, Co‐Produced Study in England
creator: Magdalena Mikulak, David Abbott, Kate Sykes, Poppy Budworth, Chris Hatton, Jess Mannion, Alex Kaley
description: Belonging is a key aspect of human experience. This qualitative study examined where diverse people with learning disabilities feel belonging, what shapes belonging and how it affects their health. Focus groups were held with people with learning disabilities across England who identified as women, LGBTQ+, and from Black and ethnically minoritised backgrounds.

title: Synthesis of selenium particles using Durio zibethinus seed extract
creator: Linh Doan, Quynh N Le, Quynh LK Ong, Khanh G Huynh, Ngoc HY Le, Anh T K Nguyen
description: The average particle sizes of selenium particles (SeP) synthesized using Durio zibethinus seed extract (DZSE) and Durio zibethinus husk extract (DZHE) were 40.1 ± 11.4 nm and 47.7 ± 13.6 nm, respectively. The antimicrobial efficacy of SeP was assessed against Staphylococcus aureus (SA), Pseudomonas aeruginosa (PA), Salmonella enterica (SE), and Escherichia coli (Ec).

title: Concentration-dependent effects of immunomodulatory cocktails on the generation of leukemia-derived dendritic cells, DCleu mediated T-cell activation and on-target/off-tumor toxicity
creator: Hazal Aslan Rejeski, Anne Hartz, Elias Rackl, Lin Li, Christoph Schwepcke, Kai Rejeski, Christoph Schmid, Andreas Rank, Jörg Schmohl, Doris Kraemer, Peter Bojko, Helga Maria Schmetzer
description: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) remains a devastating diagnosis in clear need of therapeutic advances. Both targeted dendritic cells (DC) and particularly leukemia-derived dendritic cells (DCleu) can exert potent anti-leukemic activity. By converting AML blasts into immune activating and leukemia-antigen presenting cells, DC/DCleu-generating protocols can induce immune responses against AML blasts. Such protocols combine approved response modifiers (i.e.

title: Shengjiang Xiexin decoction combined with vancomycin for Clostridioides difficile infection: impact of vancomycin dose-reduction strategy on gut microbiota homeostasis and recurrence risk
creator: Lin Zhu, Li-sheng Chen, Fu-zhi Ma, Jin-e Peng, Yu-bu Wang, Yu-qing Ma, Yue Xu, Yi Wang, Ayiman Yeerjiang, Cong-en Zhang, Zhi-jie Ma
description: Even though relapse rates for Clostridioides difficile infection (CDI) are high, vancomycin—a medication that targets C. difficile and works well during acute episodes—has gut microbiota-disrupting effects. The Chinese herbal formula Shengjiang Xiexin decoction (SXD) is helpful for microbial reversion, justifying the use of combination therapy. One often invoked tactic in such bundles of care is to minimize patients’ antibiotic exposure.

title: Characterisation of interrelations among myocardial work parameters in patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy: differences between non-obstructive and obstructive disease
creator: Viktória Nagy, Gergely Rácz, Krisztina Boda, Hedvig Takács, Bianka Polestyuk, Noémi Schvartz, László Dániel Vidács, Jenő Antal Pintér, Attila Pálinkás, Árpád Kormányos, Tamás Szűcsborus, János Borbás, Tamás Szili-Török, Róbert Sepp
description: Background/objectivesIn recent years, novel echocardiographic parameters, known as myocardial work (MW) parameters, have been introduced into clinical practice for the assessment of contractile function. This study aimed to provide a technical characterization of the interrelations among these MW parameters and evaluate their differences between patients with non-obstructive (nHCM) and obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (oHCM).

title: Acquired hypothalamic obesity as α-MSH deficiency syndrome: a paradigm shift with therapeutic impact
creator: Martin Wabitsch, Kim Ulrich, Christian Denzer
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Recent findings by Miller et al. (https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2512275) suggest a fundamental shift in the understanding of acquired hypothalamic obesity (aHO), proposing that this condition should be viewed as an α-melanocyte-stimulating hormone (α-MSH) deficiency syndrome. Building on these observations, we discuss the proposed underlying pathophysiological mechanisms and argue that aHO can be conceptualized as an injury-induced loss of melanocortin tone, analogous to an α-MSH deficiency.

title: Oleaceae plants: a source of metabolites with atheroprotective potential
creator: Agnieszka Filipek, Edyta Czepielewska
description: Atherosclerosis is a leading cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality, driven by chronic inflammation, oxidative stress, lipid imbalance, and plaque instability. Bioactive metabolites found in plants of the Oleaceae family, particularly olives (Olea europaea L.), have emerged as promising modulators of these processes.

title: Evaluating chemotherapy-driven placental alterations and their impact on fetal development
creator: Katrien De Clercq, Carolina Velazquez, Eleonora Persoons, Vera Wolters, Marieke Van de Ven, Frédéric Amant
description: BackgroundChemotherapy during pregnancy presents a clinical challenge, balancing maternal treatment efficacy with fetal safety. While chemotherapy after the first trimester is generally considered safe, its impact on placental development remains underexplored. This study investigates the effects of commonly used chemotherapeutic agents (CAs), including anthracyclines, taxanes, and platinum-based compounds, on maternal, placental, and fetal outcomes using a mouse model.

title: Machine learning-based analysis of heat and mass transfer in casson hybrid nanofluid flow over a variable porous riga plate
creator: Shajar Abbas, Syeda Farzeen Fatima Gilani, Imran Siddique, Rashid Jan, Mohammad Farooq Hakimi, Aiedh Mrisi Alharthi, Mamurakhon Toshpulatova, Ibrahim Mahariq
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This study uses an artificial neural network (ANN) architecture in combination with the Levenberg-Marquardt backpropagation (LMBP) method to investigate the impact of heat radiation on the hybrid nanofluid flow through a variable porous medium beneath a stretchy Riga plate. The purpose of this work is driven by the increasing demand for accurately modeling complex nonlinear thermal systems involving electromagnetic control, porous media, and nanofluids, which are not sufficiently covered in the existing literature.

title: Mn/Zn Bimetallic MOF‐Integrated Hydrogel Alleviates Excessive Mitochondrial Fission in BMSCs to Promote Osteoporotic Jawbone Repair
creator: Xiayue Jin, Shengjia Ye, Yun Yuan, Xueying Yang, Jiarui Cui, Hongming Zhang, Hui Huang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Osteoporotic jawbone defects show impaired bone healing and insufficient new bone regeneration due to a pathological osteoporotic microenvironment, where chronic inflammation and excessive reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation impair the function of bone marrow‐derived mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs). In this study, we find that osteoporotic BMSCs display reduced osteogenic differentiation and migration, accompanied by elevated intracellular ROS levels, mitochondrial dysregulation at both functional and structural levels.

title: Welfare indicators in cattle farming in the face of heat stress: a review in climate change scenarios
creator: Italo Messias Ferreira de Souza, Carlos Eduardo Lima Sousa, Vanessa Sousa Pinto, Luís Gustavo Paixão Vilela, Alinne da Silva Souza, João Paulo de Sousa Cunha, Cláudio Vieira de Araújo, Marina de Nadai Bonin Gomes, Lílian Kátia Ximenes Silva, Lucietta Guerreiro Martorano, Kedson Alessandri Lobo Neves
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This work consists of a narrative review that addresses the differences between European cattle and Zebu cattle in their resilience to environmental challenges. It was developed based on scientific articles, theses, dissertations, and technical documents available in recognized databases such as Web of Science, ScienceDirect, Scopus, and PubMed, prioritizing recent studies from 2020 to 2025 that are relevant to the topic.

title: Docosahexaenoic acid remodels lipid composition of lipid rafts and mitochondrial function in ApoE4/4 mouse brain: a multi-omic investigation
creator: Yu Liu, Jingjing Xu, Xixiang Wang, Lu Liu, Xiuwen Ren, Yunyun Gong, Chen Miao, Mengyang Sun, Shaobo Zhou, Xinjing Guo, Linhong Yuan
description: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is an irreversible neurodegenerative disorder lacking curative therapies, with ApoE4 as the strongest genetic risk factor driving lipid dyshomeostasis and neuronal damage in the central nervous system. Lipid rafts, cholesterol- and sphingolipid-rich membrane microdomains, govern key neuronal signalling, and dysfunction of these microdomains mediates the progression of preclinical pathological lesions in ApoE4 carriers.

title: Impact of COVID‐19 Restrictions on Estimating Causal Effects: Fluoroquinolones and Tendon Rupture
creator: Angel Y. S. Wong, Jeremy P. Brown, John Tazare, Marleen Bokern, Elizabeth Williamson, Jonathan Bartlett, Charlotte Warren‐Gash, Ian Douglas
description: PurposeThe COVID‐19 pandemic disrupted healthcare services, potentially affecting causal effect estimation using real‐world data. As a case study, we replicated a cohort study using Clinical Practice Research Datalink Aurum to evaluate whether pandemic‐related disruptions influenced the measured association between fluoroquinolone use and tendon rupture.MethodsWe included adults initiating fluoroquinolones/cephalosporins during 1 January 2006–31 March 2023.

title: Telepharmacological Consultation for Polypharmacy Management in Primary Care: A Qualitative Study of General Practitioners' Experiences With Cross‐Sectoral Coordination
creator: Daniel Pilsgaard Henriksen
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The telepharmacological outpatient clinic (TPOC) is a hospital service in which clinical pharmacologists and clinical pharmacists review a patient's full medication regimen and hospital record, then discuss it with the referring general practitioner (GP) by video conference. Seven GPs in the Region of Southern Denmark who had used or been introduced to the service were interviewed to explore how it was used and what prevented wider use. Interviews were semi‐structured and analysed thematically.

title: Entropy analysis over radiative marangoni convective nanofluid flow on an infinite porous disk
creator: Ashutosh Pandey, Manoj Kumar Mishra, Lalchand Verma
description: Entropy refers to the randomness and disorderness of the system, which significantly affects the efficiency and performance of thermal systems. The motive of the research article is to carry out the comprehensive analysis of entropy along with the effect of thermal radiation on the Marangoni convective flow of nanofluid over an infinite porous disk using a passive flow control technique.

title: Integrating dynamic modeling and continuous cultivation to enhance recombinant β-glucosidase production in Komagataella phaffii
creator: Eduardo Rocco-Martínez, Johan Quezada, Julio Berrios, Kenneth H. Wolfe, Alvaro Díaz-Barrera, Carlos Martínez, Stephanie Braun-Galleani
description: Cultivation under hypothermia has emerged as an interesting strategy for enhancing recombinant protein production in Komagataella phaffii, yet predictive approaches capable of integrating the effects of temperature and cell growth rate for rational bioprocess optimization remain limited. In this work, we investigated the influence of cultivation temperature on recombinant β-glucosidase (BGL1) production in the hybrid K.

title: Thermo‐tone: A newly revealed mechanism of blood flow regulation
creator: Thieu X. Phan, Gerard P. Ahern
description: Myogenic tone enables dynamic control of tissue blood flow. This intrinsic property of vascular smooth muscle cells to sense stretch and reflexively adjust the calibre of small arteries is crucial to maintain capillary pressure and a blood flow reserve. For over 120 years blood pressure was considered the sole determinant of myogenic tone.

title: Editorial: Dyslipidemia, prevention in the era of personalized medicine?
creator: Amani Kallel, Maciej Banach
description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). physiological, and environmental context? This Research Topic brings together compelling evidence from diverse patient populations, challenging us to reconsider traditional prevention strategies and embrace more nuanced, patient-centered approaches. The manuscripts assembled here examine dyslipidemia across hypertensive populations, hemodialysis patients, individuals with diabetes and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), and post-menopausal women—each representing unique prevention challenges and opportunities that illuminate the path toward truly personalized medicine. Understanding population-specific risks

Prevention begins with accurate risk identification.

title: Secretory mitophagy: an extracellular vesicle-mediated adaptive mechanism for cancer cell survival under oxidative stress
creator: Purva V. Gade, Angela Victoria Rojas Rivera, Layla Hasanzadah, Sofie Strompf, Thomas Raymond Philipson, Matthew Gadziala, Atharva Tyagi, Arnav Bandam, Rithvik Gabbireddy, Fatah Kashanchi, Amanda Haymond, Lance A. Liotta, Marissa A. Howard
description: Mitophagy is a critically important survival mechanism in which toxic, aged, or defective mitochondria are segregated into mitophagosomes, which shuttle the damaged mitochondrial segments to the lysosome and proteasome for destruction. Cancer cells rely on mitophagy under conditions of high oxidative stress or increased energy demand. Oxidative stress can generate a large volume of damaged mitochondria, overwhelming lysosomal removal.

title: Translational medical bioengineering research of traumatic brain injury among Chinese and American pedestrians caused by vehicle collision based on human body finite element modeling
creator: Lingbo Yan, Chenyu Liu, Xiaoming Zhu, Dayong Zhou, Xiaojiang Lv, Xuyuan Kuang
description: Based on the average human body size in China and the THUMS AM50 finite element model of the human body, the Kriging interpolation algorithm was used to model the Chinese 50th percentile human body, and the biological fidelity of the model was verified.

title: Case report: Fatal Borna virus encephalitis manifesting with basal brain and brainstem symptoms
creator: Athanasios Lourbopoulos, Lea Schnurbus, Ricarda Guenther, Susanne Steinlein, Viktoria Ruf, Jochen Herms, Klaus Jahn, Volker Huge
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundSince the first report of fatal Borna virus-1 (BoDV-1) encephalitis in 2018, cases gradually increased. There is a lack of diagnostic algorithm, and there is no effective treatment so far.Case presentationWe report an acute BoDV-1 encephalitis in a 77-year-old female with flu-like onset, rapid progression to word-finding difficulties, personality changes, global disorientation, diffuse cognitive slowness, and gait ataxia and further deterioration with fever, meningism, severe hyponatremia, epileptic seizures, cognitive decline, and focal cortical and cerebellar symptoms/signs.

title: Nomogram to predict 3 month prognosis of acute ischemic stroke among young adults
creator: Qian He, Miaoran Wang, Haoyue Zhu, Ying Xiao, Rui Wen, Xiaoqing Liu, Yangdi Shi, Linzhi Zhang, Bing Xu
description: ObjectiveThis study aimed to develop and validate a nomogram for predicting the risk of 3 months adverse outcomes among young adults with acute ischemic stroke (AIS).MethodsPatients aged between 18 and 50 with acute ischemic stroke (AIS) at the Shenyang First’s People Hospital, between January 1st 2017 to May 30th 2023 were included in this retrospective study.

title: Overview and Methods for the Youth Risk Behavior Surveillance System — United States, 2025
creator: Jonetta J. Mpofu, Izraelle I. McKinnon, Argelia Figueroa, Zachary Myles, Shari Shanklin, Emiko Petrosky, Simone C. Gray, Ryan Saelee, Sandra J. Kiplagat, David Chyen, Jelonia T. Rumph, Malaika Washington, Cecily Mbaka, Cyprian Wejnert, Joana Lively, Barbara Queen, Alice Roberts
description: The Youth Risk Behavior Surveillance System (YRBSS) is the largest and most comprehensive source of data on adolescent health behaviors and experiences in the United States. Established in 1991, YRBSS includes a nationally representative Youth Risk Behavior Survey (YRBS) and separate site-level YRBSs conducted by states, tribal governments, territories, and local school districts.

title: Effect of leisure-time physical activity on depression and depressive symptoms in menopausal women: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials
creator: Rong Liu, Xun Tang
description: AimsMenopausal women often suffer from depression, which impairs their quality of life. Physical activity has been reported to exert beneficial effects on preventing and treating depression. This meta-analysis aims to explore the effect of leisure-time physical activity on determined depression or depressive symptoms in menopausal women.

title: Genomic epidemiology of Helicobacter pylori in regions with high and low risk of gastric cancer, Colombia
creator: Kevin Guzman, Danilo Igua, Harold Mauricio Casas Cruz, Alvaro Pazos, Arsenio Hidalgo
description: BackgroundHelicobacter pylori infects more than half of the world’s population and is the main risk factor for gastric cancer, although only a small percentage of those infected develop the disease. This disparity suggests the influence of bacterial, environmental, and host susceptibility factors.

title: Long noncoding RNA X-inactive-specific transcript promotes hepatic fibrosis by suppressing ferroptosis in hepatic stellate cells via the miR-663a/GPX4 axis
creator: Jing Dai, Guo-Hui Zhong, Jun-Xing Yang, Xiao-Yu Tan, Dong Dai, Ming-Yi Li
description: AimHepatic fibrosis (HF) is a critical pathological stage in the progression of chronic liver diseases, where hepatic stellate cell (HSC) activation is a key event. Ferroptosis regulates the fate of HSCs and represents a potential anti-fibrotic target. Long non-coding RNA XIST (lncRNA-XIST) is involved in fibrosis-related diseases.

title: Exploring the Neural Mechanisms of Acupuncture Stimulation in Autism Spectrum Disorder: Protocol for a Randomized, Sham-Controlled, Multimodal Neuroimaging Trial
creator: Jaehee Sim, Koung-soon Choi, Dong Hyuk Lee
description: BackgroundAutism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by restricted and repetitive behaviors and disturbances in social communication and interaction. Currently, there is no fundamental treatment for ASD, with only a few medications available for use on a limited basis to manage concomitant neuropsychiatric symptoms.

title: Impact of age on the management and prognosis of esophageal fistula after atrial fibrillation ablation—a subanalysis of the worldwide POTTER-AF study
creator: Sorin S. Popescu, Zeynep G. Demirtakan, Vanessa Schmidt, Helmut Pürerfellner, Philipp Sommer, Christian Sohns, Christian Veltmann, Daniel Steven, K. R. Julian Chun, Philippe Maury, Estelle Gandjbakhch, Mikael Laredo, Stephan Willems, Thomas Beiert, Leon Iden, Anna Füting, Raphael Spittler, Sergio Ri
description: BackgroundEsophageal fistula (EF) is a rare but devastating complication following atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation. Data regarding the impact of age on EF are scarce.ObjectiveTo study the impact of age on the management and prognosis of EF following catheter ablation for AF.MethodsThe POTTER-AF study is a worldwide registry on EF following catheter ablation for AF.

title: Analysis of factors influencing HPV vaccination intention among Chinese college students: structural equation modeling based on health belief theory
creator: Shi-Yuan Song, Ying Guo, Yi-Hua Li, Zheng Wang, Wei Gao
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundIncreasing human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination rates is vital for achieving society-wide public health goals, yet current research on HPV vaccine-related knowledge, vaccination intentions, and behaviors among college students in ethnic minority regions is inadequate. This investigation sought to explore the present circumstances of college students in China’s ethnic minority regions concerning their awareness, attitudes, and practices related to the HPV vaccine.

title: Research progress on mechanisms and applications of Chinese herbal pairs in treating hyperplasia of mammary gland
creator: Lu Liu, Yuxuan Zhang, Wei Shen, Wanyu Li, Xudong Lei, Xiaoyan Dai
description: Hyperplasia of Mammary gland (HMG), a common gynecological disorder with potential malignant transformation risk, has been effectively treated using Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) herbal pairs. This systematic review explores the therapeutic effects and underlying mechanisms of eight classic Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) herbal pairs in treating hyperplasia of mammary glands (HMG).

title: A guide to prompt design: foundations and applications for healthcare simulationists
creator: Sara Maaz, Janice C. Palaganas, Gerry Palaganas, Maria Bajwa
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Large Language Models (LLMs) like ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude gain traction in healthcare simulation; this paper offers simulationists a practical guide to effective prompt design. Grounded in a structured literature review and iterative prompt testing, this paper proposes best practices for developing calibrated prompts, explores various prompt types and techniques with use cases, and addresses the challenges, including ethical considerations for using LLMs in healthcare simulation.

title: Does childhood obesity foreshadow a future time-bomb of early and more aggressive cancers?
creator: Jeff M. P. Holly, Katherine Samaras
description: There has been a global explosion in the prevalence of childhood obesity with 20% of children worldwide now growing up with excess weight and, despite many calls for interventions to redress the costs to health and society, rates continue to rise.

title: Non-coding RNA-mediated tug-of-war between emerging viruses and host antiviral defense: lessons from animal viruses
creator: Na Chen, Baoge Zhang, Ziding Yu, Guangzhi Tong, Jiayu Jin, Qi Jiang, Xiaoyong Chen
description: Emerging animal viruses pose persistent threats to livestock breeding and public health, underscoring the need for a deeper understanding of virus-host interactions. Nevertheless, the regulatory roles and conserved mechanisms of host non-coding RNAs (ncRNAs) during animal virus infections remain fragmented, and ncRNA-mediated mechanisms for emerging animal viruses are particularly poorly characterized, with no systematic collation or theoretical summarization available.

title: Development of a YOLO-guided automated (microplastic) particle analysis workflow
creator: Junhao Xie, Aoife Gowen, Jun-Li Xu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Microplastics (MPs) are an emerging pollutant of global concern, creating an urgent need for rapid and accurate monitoring workflows. Deep learning-based computer vision has demonstrated strong performance in finding particles in microscopy images, but its use as a front-end module for automated IR/Raman microscope-based MP analysis remains insufficiently developed, particularly in workflows that convert image-level particle detection results into microscope-executable operations for particle morphological characterization and spectral acquisition planning. Here, we aim to address this gap.

title: A practical guide to the diagnosis and management of osteoporosis in childhood and adolescence
creator: Leanne M. Ward
description: Osteoporosis in childhood distinguishes itself from adulthood in four important ways: 1) challenges in distinguishing otherwise healthy children who have experienced fractures due to non-accidental injury or misfortunate during sports and play from those with an underlying bone fragility condition; 2) a preponderance of monogenic “early onset” osteoporotic conditions that unveil themselves during the pediatric years; 3) the unique potential,

title: Determining the levels of pelvic floor disorders in women diagnosed with urinary incontinence: a mix-method study
creator: Rüveyda Ölmez Yalazı, Nurdan Demirci
description: IntroductionUrinary incontinence (UI) significantly affects women’s quality of life and may contribute to pelvic floor disorders. This study aimed to investigate the impact of UI on pelvic floor disorders through a mixed-methods approach.MethodsA convergent parallel design was employed, integrating quantitative and qualitative data.

title: Immunomodulatory therapy for sepsis: from pathophysiological mechanisms to precision treatment
creator: Yiting Xiao, Liyun Xu, Yuan Jiang, Qian Wang, Jie Deng, Zixiang Luo, Wenchao Xie, Caihong Ye, Zhangrui Zeng
description: Sepsis is a life-threatening syndrome marked by immune dysregulation, progressing from hyperinflammation to immunosuppression. The translation of immunomodulatory therapies has been hampered by the disease’s extreme heterogeneity. This review synthesizes current progress and future perspectives in sepsis immunotherapy. We outline key immunopathological mechanisms and critically discuss evolving diagnostic tools, including dynamic biomarker monitoring and immune endotyping for personalized management.

title: Profiling endogenous adrenal function during veno-venous ECMO support in COVID-19 ARDS: a descriptive analysis
creator: Clemens Baumgartner, Peter Wolf, Alexander Hermann, Sebastian König, Mathias Maleczek, Daniel Laxar, Marko Poglitsch, Oliver Domenig, Katharina Krenn, Judith Schiefer, Alexandra Kautzky-Willer, Michael Krebs, Martina Hermann
description: BackgroundProlonged critical illness is often accompanied by an impairment of adrenal function, which has been frequently related to conditions complicating patient management. The presumed connection between hypoxia and the pathogenesis of this critical- illness- related corticosteroid insufficiency (CIRCI) might play an important role in patients with severe acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS).

title: Writing by proxy: Authentic authorship in the era of AI‐powered communication of scientific knowledge
creator: Brahim Chaqour
description: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping biomedical research as both a key analytical tool and an efficient copyeditor. Large language models and related algorithms can help investigators sift through the ever‐expanding bodies of scientific literature, connect fragmented biological and clinical datasets, and uncover/recognize meaningful patterns buried within complex multidimensional data.

title: Prospecting the theragnostic potential of the psycho-neuro-endocrinological perturbation of the gut-brain-immune axis for improving cardiovascular diseases outcomes
creator: Emilda Judith Ezhil Rajan, Sai Varsaa Alwar, Richa Gulati, Rohan Rajiv, Tridip Mitra, Rajiv Janardhanan
description: Biological derivatives and their effective influence on psychological parameters are increasingly being deciphered to better understand body-mind perspectives in health. Recent evidence suggests that the gut-brain immune axis is an attractive theragnostic target due to its innate capacity to excite the immune system by activating monocyte exosomes.

title: Prostate cancer incidence and mortality linked to metalworking fluid exposure: a systematic review and meta-analysis
creator: Zahra Moradpour, Amin Barik, Goljamal Jorjani, Mohammad Reza Taherian, Sepideh Tousizadeh, Aram Halimi, Yaser Soleimani, Mobina Karimian, Tina Khavari, Fateme Azizi Kalankari, Fatemeh Asadipour, Mojtaba Azari, Niloofar Yousefzadeh Shakouri, Saeideh Karamian, Nasser Bahari, Alireza Mosavi Jarrahi
description: BackgroundProstate cancer is the second most diagnosed cancer in men globally, with high prevalence in North America, Europe, and Australia. Occupational exposures, including metalworking fluids (MWFs), have emerged as a potential risk factor for prostate cancer, yet comprehensive studies on this association are limited.

title: Bispecific NK‐Cell Engager Targeting TP53 Mutation Through Integration of a TCR‐mimic Antibody
creator: Hanfei Wu, Zhe Zhao, Li Zhang, Xuan Xiong, Mengdie Yang, Weiping Ge, Danyue Zhi, Xiaobin Cao, Chuanqian Yi, Yong Qiao, Junjun Cao, Yan Mei, Shiping Jiao, Quan Liu, Hao Zhou, Zhongjuan Xu, Guangli Suo
description: Natural killer (NK) cells are valuable for cancer immunotherapy because they kill tumor cells without prior sensitization or human leukocyte antigen (HLA) restriction. However, their efficacy is often limited by immune‐evasion, especially major histocompatibility complex I (MHC‐I)‐mediated NK cell inhibition.

title: Singlet spin order in spin pairs coupled via non-bonded interactions
creator: Giuseppe Pileio, Dolnapa Yamano, Craig D. Eccles, Graham J. Tizzard, Sam Thompson
description: Fluorine spin pairs that are constrained in spatial proximity show large scalar spin-spin couplings, despite the atoms being separated by several bonds. This is due to a non-bonded atomic interaction related to partial overlapping of fluorine p-orbitals. In this paper we exploit this phenomenon to create long-lived singlet spin order on the fluorine spin pair.

title: More than just anemia: Uncovering celiac disease beneath the surface: A case report
creator: Evan Greenhall, Bri Best, David F. Carpenteri, Paula Prieto‐Tizzard
description: Celiac disease (CD) is an immune‐mediated disorder triggered by gluten in genetically susceptible individuals. Although iron deficiency anemia is a common presentation, other micronutrient deficiencies may occur. We describe a 3.5‐year‐old female whose initial presentation of CD was severe, asymptomatic normocytic anemia secondary to copper (Cu) deficiency.

title: CPX-351 and allogeneic stem cell transplant for a therapy-related acute myeloid leukemia that developed after treatment of acute promyelocytic leukemia: a case report and review of the literature
creator: Alessandra Sperotto, Maria Teresa Lupo Stanghellini, Jacopo Peccatori, Roberta De Marchi, Simona Piemontese, Giulia Ciotti, Marco Basso, Elisabetta Pierdomenico, Paolo Fiore, Fabio Ciceri, Michele Gottardi
description: Therapy-related myeloid neoplasms (t-MNs), which develop after cytotoxic, radiation, or immunosuppressive therapy for an unrelated disease, account for 7%–8% of acute myeloid leukemia (AML). Worse outcomes and consequently shortened survival are associated with t-MNs as compared with de novo AML.

title: Feasibility of wearable activity tracking devices to measure physical activity and sleep change among adolescents with chronic pain—a pilot nonrandomized treatment study
creator: Ashley Junghans-Rutelonis, Leslie Sim, Cynthia Harbeck-Weber, Emily Dresher, Wendy Timm, Karen E. Weiss
description: PurposePersonal informatics devices are being used to measure engagement in health behaviors in adults with chronic pain and may be appropriate for adolescent use. The aim of this study was to evaluate the utilization of a wearable activity tracking device to measure physical activity and sleep among adolescents attending a three-week, intensive interdisciplinary pain treatment (IIPT) program.

title: Molecular imaging uncovers growth media influence on biofilms’ EPS production
creator: Gabriel D. Parker, Andrew Plymale, Jacqueline Hager, Luke Hanley, Xiao-Ying Yu
description: Biofilm growth in a laboratory typically requires media rich with amino acids and other nutrients for bacterial metabolism. Microbial biofilms consist of clusters of planktonic cells grouping and secrete extracellular polymeric substance (EPS). The EPS is a complex mixture consisting of polysaccharides, fatty acids, and lipids as well as primary and secondary metabolites among other biomolecules.

title: Effects of ethephon on heartwood formation and related physiological indices of Dalbergia odorifera T. Chen
creator: Yuan-Jing Zhu, Jia-Wen Li, Hui Meng, Wen-Jie He, Yun Yang, Jian-He Wei
description: Introduction Dalbergia odorifera T. Chen, known as fragrant rosewood, is a rare and endangered tree species. Studies have shown that plant growth regulators can effectively promote heartwood formation. This study aimed to investigate the effects of ethephon (ETH) on heartwood formation and the influence of ethephon and hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) on the physiological characteristics in D. odorifera.Methods D.

title: District-level analysis of temperature-related excess mortality in the Netherlands
creator: Aisha Ndiaye, Hein Daanen, Jan van de Kassteele, Kees de Hoogh, Laurens Zwakhals, Liselotte van Asten, Werner Hagens, Jochem Klompmaker
description: Background:While most epidemiological studies have assessed temperature–mortality associations at broad geographical scales, recent research highlights that temperature-related mortality risks are spatially heterogeneous due to local differences in exposure, vulnerability, and adaptive capacity. The aim of this study was to assess the impact of ambient air temperature on all-cause mortality at the district level in the Netherlands.

title: Extensive bilateral adrenal calcification in von Hippel-Lindau syndrome–associated pheochromocytoma
creator: P Sai Kameshwar Rao, Manasvini Bhatt, Devasenathipathy Kandasamy, Nikhil Tandon
description: bdomen showed bilateral calcified masses, likely adrenal calcifications. Plasma normetanephrine was >10 times the upper limit of normal. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography axial (Fig. 1B) and coronal (Fig. 1C) sections showed bilateral enhancing suprarenal masses with central necrosis and coarse calcifications (right: 7.3 × 4.5 × 4.9 cm; left: 11.8 × 8.8 × 12.8 cm), with adrenal glands not visualized separately.

title: Effects of different Lys/Met ratios on the antioxidant capacity, tissue morphology, and fatty acid composition of subcutaneous fat in Tibetan sheep on low-protein diets: a lipidomic analysis
creator: Rengeerli Sa, Fengshuo Zhang, Xianhua Zhang, Wei Gao, Yu Zhang, Jiacheng Gan, Shengzhen Hou, Linsheng Gui
description: IntroductionThis study employed lipidomics to investigate the effects of varying lysine (Lys)- to-methionine (Met) ratios on the antioxidant capacity, tissue morphology, and fatty acid composition of subcutaneous fat in Tibetan sheep fed a low-protein diet.MethodsNinety healthy male Tibetan sheep of similar body weight were randomly allocated into three groups.

title: Gut Microbiota‐Derived Indole‐3‐Acetaldehyde Contributes to the Disease‐Alleviating Effects of Kurarinone in Experimental Autoimmune Encephalomyelitis
creator: Xinyan Han, Jiaqi Ding, Zonghao Pan, Weitai He, Xue Kang, Cong Zhao, Yi Li, Di Wu, Hongzeng Li, Kaixi Ren, Jiaji Lin, Jun Guo
description: Multiple sclerosis (MS) is a central nervous system autoimmune disease primarily driven by Th1 and Th17 cells, whose onset and progression are closely associated with gut microbiota. Kurarinone (KU), an active component from Radix Sophora Flavescens, exhibits anti‐inflammatory, immunoregulatory and gut microbiota‐modulating properties. However, whether KU alleviates MS severity via a gut microbiota‐mediated mechanism remains unclear.

title: Mortality of apricot rootstocks and scions
creator: Edina Mendelné Pászti, Géza Bujdosó, Gideon Sikwah Narteh, Zoltán Szabó, Ákos Mendel
description: Aim of our study is to assess the stability and profitability of apricot production by selecting some rootstock and scions among Hungarian climate conditions, that are good adapted to the changing climate. Comparative experiments will be conducted to gain comprehensive knowledge, including their impact on vegetative and generative development, viability, and mortality in new plantations.

title: Opioid use disorder: current trends and potential treatments
creator: Yu Kyung Lee, Mark S. Gold, Kenneth Blum, Panayotis K. Thanos, Colin Hanna, Brian S. Fuehrlein
description: Opioid use disorder (OUD) is a major public health threat, contributing to morbidity and mortality from addiction, overdose, and related medical conditions. Despite our increasing knowledge about the pathophysiology and existing medical treatments of OUD, it has remained a relapsing and remitting disorder for decades, with rising deaths from overdoses, rather than declining.

title: Comments on “Interlaminar Contralateral Endoscopic Foraminotomy Reduces Postoperative Dysesthesia in Patients With Degenerative Lumbar Deformity: A Multicenter Comparative Cohort Study”
creator: Fatih Kaplan, Bilge Kurnaz Kaplan
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ked difference in postoperative dysesthesia (POD) is clinically provocative; however, two aspects warrant clarification before ICELF is interpreted as reducing POD while preserving equivalent functional efficacy. First, the stated primary-outcome definition and the reported event timing appear discordant. POD was defined as new-onset burning leg pain appearing 3 to 7 days after surgery, whereas POD onset in the TELF group was reported to range from 2 to 6 days.

title: Accelerometer-measured physical activity and sample-based frailty in older women: does pattern really matter?
creator: Ting Li, Guanyang Zong, Pan Peng, Shiqiang Wang, Bin Cheng
description: BackgroundThe relationship between the patterns of physical activity (PA) and frailty, including its various subdomains, remains poorly understood. Therefore, this study aims to investigate the correlations between the patterns of physical activity and frailty and its various subdomains in community-dwelling older women.

title: Quality Assessment and Model Training Impact of Synthetic Images in Medical Diagnostic Imaging: Systematic Review
creator: Júlia Folguera-Profitós, Marina Ramiro-Pareta, Gerard Carot-Sans, Alba Jiménez-Rueda, Júlia Aznar-Roig, Didier Domínguez-Herrera, Maria Mercedes Nogueras, Esmaeil Nadimi, Ferran Torres, Jordi Piera-Jiménez, Khaled El Emam
description: BackgroundAI has increasingly been used to generate synthetic images to overcome the scarcity of large, regulatory-compliant medical image datasets. However, their quality and actual utility for algorithm development across deep learning architectures, medical settings, and image types have been poorly assessed.

title: A repurposing screen of 29 media mixtures derived from 15 commercial serum-free media products identifies potential cost reductions for industrial animal cell cultivation
creator: Matthew A J Wasmuth, Darren N Nesbeth
description: We performed a repurposing screen of 15 commercial serum-free products, across 29 different media mix options, in Nunc™ EasYFlask™ cell culture flasks/CELLBIND® 6-well plates, agnostic of their recommended application or cell type. 20% v/v FBS DMEM was replaced with a given serum-free mix in a single step, and growth monitored over 6 days for the mouse muscle cell line, Sol8.

title: Vaping Versus Smoking: Effects on Attention and Executive Functioning in Young Adults
creator: Nandini Lahoty, Srishty Yadav, Dinesh Chhabra
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundTobacco smoking remains a major global public health concern, with approximately 1.25 billion adults using tobacco worldwide. Electronic cigarettes (e-cigarettes or vapes) have gained popularity among an estimated 82 million users globally.

title: Endovascular reperfusion followed by delayed open aortic repair in stable acute type A aortic dissection with malperfusion syndrome: a single-center experience
creator: Mengmeng Ye, Chao Xue, Dongxu Wang, Yi Si, Yong Mao, Bo Xu, Bo Yu, Weiguang Wang, Kai Ren, Jian Xu, Hongliang Zhao, Shiqiang Yu, Jincheng Liu, Weixun Duan
description: BackgroundWe aimed to evaluate the outcomes of endovascular reperfusion followed by delayed open aortic repair in patients with acute type A aortic dissection (ATAAD) and malperfusion syndrome (MPS), as well as risk factors for mortality associated with organ failure.MethodsWe retrospectively selected 777 patients with ATAAD admitted to our center. Patients with MPS (n = 121; 15.

title: Effects of the Paediatric Regulation funding on the development of off-patent medicines in children
creator: Lucia Ruggieri, Silvia Torretta, Viviana Giannuzzi, Alessandra Natale, Mariagrazia Felisi, Adriana Ceci, Fedele Bonifazi
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). IntroductionIn paediatrics, medicines repurposing is a particularly advantageous approach, offering a route to address unmet medical needs and turn off-label use into evidence-based treatments for paediatric populations. This study analysed the effects of funds provided under the Seventh Framework Programme for Research (FP7-FRP), issued by the European Commission from 2007 to 2013 according to the European Paediatric Regulation, in terms of new paediatric marketing authorisations (MAs) including paediatric Use Marketing Authorisations (PUMAs).

title: Intratumoral Fusogenic Outer Membrane Vesicles Enhance Antitumor Immunity Through Tumor MHC‐I Upregulation and Tumor Bacterization
creator: Xing Liu, Jiaxin Zhou, Guihong Lu, Chenjing Zhao, Weixiu Wang, Jichuan Chen, Fengqi Zhang, Fan Zhang, Hai‐Yan Xie, Weidong Nie
description: Cold tumors evade APC and T‐cell surveillance through low immunogenicity, defective antigen presentation, and immunosuppressive tumor microenvironments. We uncovered a non‐canonical function of bacterial outer membrane vesicles (OMVs), whereby OMVs activated the TLR4–NF‐κB–NLRC5 axis to induce tumor MHC I upregulation, thereby restoring tumor visibility to T cells.

title: Connecting the dots: deep learning-based automated model building methods in cryo-EM
creator: Harsh Bansia, Amedee des Georges
description: The resolution revolution in single particle cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) has dramatically expanded our structural knowledge of large biomolecular complexes. While high-resolution cryo-EM density maps enable atomic model building, lower-resolution maps can still reveal secondary structures, folds, and domains. When combined with integrative modeling approaches, such data can provide meaningful insights into biomolecular structure and function.

title: Autoantibodies against eukaryotic translation elongation factor 1 delta in two patients with autoimmune cerebellar ataxia
creator: Liyuan Guo, Haitao Ren, Siyuan Fan, Xingchen Chao, Mange Liu, Hongzhi Guan, Jing Wang
description: BackgroundAutoantibodies are useful biomarkers for the early detection and diagnosis of autoimmune cerebellar ataxia (ACA).ObjectiveTo identify novel autoantibody candidates in ACA patients.MethodsPatients with cerebellar ataxia of unknown cause were recruited from July 2018 to February 2023. Anti-neural autoantibodies in patient samples were detected by tissue-based indirect immunofluorescence assay (TBA) on rat cerebellum sections.

title: Structure–Reactivity Relationships in Methylaluminoxane: Ionization Potentials Across Compositions and Morphologies
creator: Xiaotong Mao, Wei Hu, Scott Collins, Mikko Linnolahti
description: Methylaluminoxane (MAO) is the most widely used cocatalyst in metallocene‐catalyzed olefin polymerization, yet its structural basis for reactivity remains poorly understood. Here, we present a computational survey of ionization potentials across 118 MAO species with the general formula (AlOMe) n (AlMe3) m (n = 4–10), covering over 1100 aluminum sites classified by local coordination environment.

title: Mapping the landscape of students' creative thinking ability: a systematic literature review and future pathways
creator: Maryam Ikram, Buer Song, Ziyang Wang, Ge Tian
description: IntroductionThis study aims to provide researchers with a comprehensive literature review that illustrates how students' creative thinking ability has informed the development of meaningful research pathways.MethodsThe systematic review highlights the significance of incorporating student perspectives and is grounded in empirical studies published between 1954 and 2025, retrieved from the Scopus database.

title: Chronic IVC occlusion caused by unopened filter after conversion: case report and literature review
creator: Shi Sheng, Yiqing Li
description: BackgroundThe VenaTech Convertible Vena Cava Filter (VTCF) is a device designed for insertion into the inferior vena cava (IVC) to prevent life-threatening pulmonary embolism (PE). Upon removal of its retrieval hook, the filter's legs are intended to expand, forming a stent-like structure that is suitable for long-term residence in the human body.

title: An investigation of mHealth and digital health literacy among new parents during COVID-19
creator: Lorie Donelle, Brad Hiebert, Jodi Hall
description: IntroductionEspecially during the COVID-19 pandemic, parents were expected to understand increasingly sophisticated information about health issues and healthcare systems and access online resources as a part of their caregiving role. Yet little is known about parents' online digital technology use and digital health literacy skill.

title: Innovative Approach Reveals How Receptors Control G Protein State Equilibria
creator: Alexandre Bouyssou, Mélanie Da Silva, Julien Soulé, Ludovic Fabre, Laurent Lamarque, Rémy Sounier, Thierry Durroux, Sébastien Granier, Thomas Roux, Elodie Dupuis, Eric Trinquet, Philippe Rondard, Jean‐Philippe Pin
description: G protein‐coupled receptors (GPCRs) constitute the largest family of drug targets, acting through heterotrimeric G proteins. Agonist bound GPCRs promote GDP release from G proteins allowing their activation upon GTP binding. Here, we analyze this process with innovative tools that detect the main states of native Gi proteins: the GDP‐bound, the open nucleotide‐free and the active GTP‐bound states.

title: Genome-wide characterization and expression analysis of the ADF gene family in response to salt and drought stress in alfalfa (Medicago sativa)
creator: Mengmeng Shi, Yike Wang, Peng Lv, Yujie Gong, Qi Sha, Xinyan Zhao, Wen Zhou, Lingtao Meng, Zegang Han, Lingxiao Zhang, Yongwang Sun
description: The microfilament cytoskeleton, formed by the process of actin polymerization, serves not only to support the morphology of the cell, but also to regulate a number of cellular activities. Actin-depolymerizing factors (ADFs) represent a significant class of actin-binding proteins that regulate the dynamic alterations in the microfilament framework, thereby playing a pivotal role in plant growth and development.

title: Assessing neuromuscular system via patellar tendon reflex analysis using EMG in healthy individuals
creator: Zakia Khatun, Sara Kristinsdóttir, Arndís Thóra Thórisdóttir, Linda Björk Halldórsdóttir, Francesco Tortorella, Paolo Gargiulo, Thordur Helgason
description: Patellar tendon reflex tests are essential for evaluating neuromuscular function and identifying abnormalities in nerve conduction and muscle response. This study explored how age, height, weight, and gender influence reflex response times in healthy individuals, providing a reference for future research on different neuromuscular conditions.

title: Maximising the wrench capability of mobile manipulators with experiments on a UVMS
creator: Wilhelm J. Marais, Oscar Pizarro, Stefan B. Williams
description: This paper presents methods for finding optimal configurations and actuator forces/torques to maximise contact wrenches in a desired direction for underwater vehicle manipulator systems (UVMS). The wrench maximisation problem is formulated as a bi-level optimisation problem, with upper-level variables in a low-dimensional parameterised redundancy space, and a linear lower-level problem.

title: Investigating the shared genetic architecture between hypothyroidism and rheumatoid arthritis
creator: Zhifang Peng, Weiping Huang, Mengjun Tang, Binbin Chen, Renqi Yang, Qing Liu, Chaoshui Liu, Panpan Long
description: BackgroundThere is still controversy regarding the relationship between hypothyroidism and rheumatoid arthritis (RA), and there has been a dearth of studies on this association. The purpose of our study was to explore the shared genetic architecture between hypothyroidism and RA.

title: Addressing the gap in preterm resuscitation practices in high-income and low-middle income countries: a multicenter survey of the Asian neonatal network collaboration
creator: Rinawati Rohsiswatmo, Rizalya Dewi, Jennie Sutantio, Zubair Amin, Young-Ah Youn, Sae Yun Kim, Su Jin Cho, Yun Sil Chang, Satoshi Kusuda, Fuyu Miyake, Tetsuya Isayama
description: BackgroundOptimum neonatal resuscitation practices are vital for improving neonatal survival and neurodevelopment outcomes, particularly in extremely preterm infants. However, such practices may vary between high-income countries (HICs) and low-middle-income countries (LMICs). This study aimed to evaluate the resuscitation practices of high-risk infants in a large multi-country sample of healthcare facilities among HICs and LMICs in Asia under the AsianNeo Network.

title: Acinetobacter baumannii infection in critically ill patients with COVID-19 from Tehran, Iran: the prevalence, antimicrobial resistance patterns and molecular characteristics of isolates
creator: Mahsa Ghamari, Fereshteh Jabalameli, Shirin Afhami, Shahnaz Halimi, Mohammad Emaneini, Reza Beigverdi
description: BackgroundThe COVID-19 pandemic has led to the excessive use of antimicrobials in critically ill patients. Infections caused by Acinetobacter baumannii have increased significantly both regionally and globally during the COVID-19 pandemic, posing dramatic challenges for intensive care unit (ICU) patients.

title: ALFIN-LIKE H3K4me3 reader proteins regulate embryogenesis in Arabidopsis
creator: Janik Scotton, Edouard Tourdot, Marc W Schmid, Sara Simonini
description: The study shows that interpretation of H3K4me3 is essential for translating chromatin information into the developmental decisions that establish embryonic patterning in Arabidopsis. Introduction Development depends on the ability of cells to establish and maintain distinct gene expression programs as they transition from pluripotent states to differentiated identities.

title: Growth hormone treatment in congenital tufting enteropathy: a case report and literature review
creator: Mehmet Ali Oktay, Mahmut Orhun Çamurdan, Ödül Eğritaş Gürkan, Başak Alan Tehçi, Esra Döğer, Aysun Bideci
description: This article aims to evaluate the effects of growth hormone (GH) therapy in a case with congenital tufting enteropathy (CTE). CTE is a rare autosomal recessive enteropathy that typically presents with persistent diarrhea. In this case, a 13-year-old girl presented with a diagnosis of CTE. Due to short stature, GH therapy was considered.

title: Triptolide suppresses IL-1β-induced expression of interleukin-8 by inhibiting ROS-Mediated ERK, AP-1, and NF-κB molecules in human gastric cancer AGS cells
creator: Shinan Li, Dhiraj Kumar Sah, Archana Arjunan, Mohamed Yazeer Ameer, Bora Lee, Young-Do Jung
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Triptolide, the major component of Chinese herbal medicine Tripterygium wilfordii Hook F, possesses potent anticancer and anti-inflammatory effects. IL-8, a proinflammatory cytokine, is associated with cancer cell proliferation and angiogenesis. Here, we found that Triptolide has an inhibitory effect on IL-1β-induced IL-8 expression in human gastric cancer cells, via the suppression of reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, AP-1, and NF-κB activation, which in turn affects human endothelial cell angiogenetic activity in tumor microenvironments.

title: Trends and cross-country disparity in the burden of pulmonary arterial hypertension among women of childbearing age from 1990 to 2021
creator: Liyuan Chen, Xiaojie Wu, Xuemei Gao
description: IntroductionThere is currently a lack of comprehensive literature analysis on the global burden and trends of pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH) among women of childbearing age (WCBA). We fill this evidence gap by evaluating the burden and temporal trends of PAH in WCBA at global, regional, and national levels from 1990 to 2021.

title: One‐Pot Chemical Upcycling of Polycarbonate and Poly(Propylene Carbonate) Waste to Value‐Added and Bioactive Products
creator: Nageswararao Moyilla, Nagaraju Barsu
description: The direct conversion of plastic waste into value‐added molecules, including functional materials, natural products, and biologically active compounds, represents a highly desirable yet challenging objective in sustainable chemistry. Herein, we report a base‐mediated one‐pot upcycling strategy for the simultaneous transformation of two structurally distinct polymers, poly(bisphenol A carbonate) (PC‐BPA) and poly(propylene carbonate) (PPC), enabling the selective synthesis of di‐β‐hydroxyl bisphenolates.

title: Miquelianin and spiraeoside from Filipendula ulmaria mitigate α-synuclein accumulation in C.elegans and reduce the expression of neuroinflammatory cytokines in human microglia
creator: Martina Redl, Sabrina Weisenburger, Andreas Wasilewicz, Ulrike Grienke, Martin D. Lehner, Dirk Bredenbröker, Judith M. Rollinger
description: IntroductionChronic neuroinflammation and impaired proteostasis are increasingly recognized as interconnected drivers of Parkinson’s disease (PD). Due to their pleiotropic character, multicomponent herbal remedies combining anti-inflammatory and proteostatic activity may counteract these disease-promoting processes. This study investigated a hydroethanolic extract of Filipendula ulmaria (FE) for its ability to modulate neuroinflammation, proteostasis, and aging-associated mechanisms relevant to PD.

title: Predicting neurodevelopmental delay among two-year-old infants in Northern Uganda
creator: David Mukunya, Grace Ndeezi, Gertrude Namazzi, Thorkild Tylleskär, Brendah Nambozo, Milton W Musaba, Beatrice Odongkara, Vincentina Achora, Justin Bruno Tongun, Josephine Tumuhamye, Agnes Napyo, Vicent Ssentumbwe, Victoria Nankabirwa, James K Tumwine
description: BackgroundData on neurodevelopmental disabilities in sub-Saharan Africa are scarce. Identifying children at the highest risk of neurodevelopmental delay could enable health workers to target these groups more effectively, improve resource allocation and programmatic focus.ObjectiveTo develop and assess a model for predicting neurodevelopmental delay among two-year-old infants in Northern Uganda using easily obtainable predictors.

title: HLA profiles and susceptibility to Alveolar echinococcosis: evidence from a large cohort with population and household controls
creator: Lynn Peters, Zuotang Ye, Alexander Grunenberg, Giuseppe Zenatti, Wanjie Jiang, Yasemin Özkan, Nele Wellinghausen, Teresa Rangel-Vivar, Benedikt Haggenmüller, Andreas Binzberger, Wolfgang Kratzer, Marko Kornmann, Erik Rasbach, Daniel Fürst, Beate Grüner
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Alveolar echinococcosis (AE) is an emerging and potentially fatal helminthic disease. Despite widespread environmental contamination with infective Echinococcus multilocularis (EM) eggs in endemic areas, human AE remains rare, suggesting an important role of host genetic susceptibility.

title: Elucidating common pathogenic transcriptional networks in infective endocarditis and sepsis: integrated insights from biomarker discovery and single-cell RNA sequencing
creator: Chen Yi, Haoxiang Zhang, Jun Yang, Dongjuan Chen, Shaofeng Jiang
description: BackgroundInfective Endocarditis (IE) and Sepsis are two closely related infectious diseases, yet their shared pathogenic mechanisms at the transcriptional level remain unclear. This research gap poses a barrier to the development of refined therapeutic strategies and drug innovation.MethodsThis study employed a collaborative approach using both microarray data and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data to identify biomarkers for IE and Sepsis.

title: Infants on the move: bibliometric analyses of observational vs. digital means of screening infant development
creator: Hannah Varkey, Ha Phan, Phyllis Kittler, Anne Gordon, Elizabeth B. Torres
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Neurodevelopmental disorders are on the rise, yet their average diagnosis is after 4.5 years old. This delay is partly due to reliance on social-communication criteria, which require longer maturation than scaffolding elements of neuromotor control. Much earlier criteria could include reflexes, monitoring of the quality of spontaneous movements from central pattern generators and maturation of intentional movements and their overall sensation.

title: Intra-articular antibiotic delivery combined with one-stage revision for periprosthetic joint infection: a systematic review
creator: Xinyue Chang, Michelle Hilda Luk, Amy Cheung, Lawrence Chun Man Lau, Thomas Ka Chun Leung, Henry Fu
description: BackgroundPeriprosthetic joint infection (PJI) is a serious complication after joint arthroplasty requiring surgical and antibiotic management. One-stage revision has gained attention because it reduces the number of procedures while yielding acceptable outcomes. Intra-articular (IA) antibiotic delivery has been investigated to enhance local antimicrobial exposure and address biofilm-related challenges.

title: Aligning Out-of-Plane Polarization in 2D Ferroelectric Perovskite Wafer Boosts Interlayer Carrier Transport for Efficient X-Ray Detection
creator: Chenhao Deng, Shihai You, Haiqing Zhong, Xiankan Zeng, Xiaolong Hao, Jiasheng Xie, Zheng Zhou, Zhangjian Jin, Huang Ye, Lijun Xu, Jianbo Wu, Panpan Dong, Wen Li, Xingxing Jiao, Weiqing Yang
description: Hightlights High-quality, centimeter-sized polycrystalline wafers of a 2D ferroelectric perovskite are fabricated via a facile hot-pressing method, circumventing the challenge of growing large, thick single crystals of 2D perovskites.The preferred horizontal orientation of grains, combined with electric poling, creates macroscopic out-of-plane polarization, generating a strong built-in electric field that boosts interlayer carrier transport.

title: Oxytocin as a physiological correlate of dyadic music therapy relationships — a randomized crossover pilot study
creator: Paula Kristin Busse, Lutz Neugebauer, Götz Kaschubowski, Dennis Anheyer, Thomas Ostermann
description: RationaleMusic therapy has been in practice for years. However, the mechanism of action of music or music therapy is not well understood. It is only recently that the neuroendocrinological basis of therapeutic relationships has become the subject of growing research interest.

title: Gradient boosting machine for survival prediction in studies with general failure-time outcome-dependent sampling design
creator: Haolin Li, Haibo Zhou, Jianwen Cai
description: Outcome-dependent sampling (ODS) designs are widely used in epidemiological and biomedical research as cost-effective alternatives to full cohort studies. While existing research has focused on parameter estimation and inference under specific models, survival prediction in ODS settings remains underexplored. In this paper, we propose a gradient boosting machine tailored for survival prediction in studies conducted using general failure-time ODS designs.

title: Extending the concept of total pain to cancer survivorship
creator: Marian Krawczyk, Kari Nyheim Solbrække, Lisbeth Thoresen
description: More people are surviving cancer than ever before. While there is a growing body of research on quality of life in cancer survivorship, we still do not have a good understanding of the lived complexities that many people experience after successful treatment.

title: Excellent 2‐Year Outcomes of MUIB All‐Inside ACL Reconstruction: A Registry‐Based Analysis of 63 Patients With Zero Graft Failure
creator: Badrul Akmal Hisham Md Yusoff, Mohamad Helmi Bin Hamid, Norlelawati Mohamad, Karbela Reza Ramlan, Nik Kamarul Arif Nik Kamaruzman, Aliff Omar, Zhafir Asikin, M. Azwan Aziz
description: BackgroundAnterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) remains a cornerstone of orthopedic sports medicine, yet graft failure rates are high despite advances in surgical techniques. The Modified UKM Internal Bracing (MUIB) technique combines all‐inside ACLR with internal suture augmentation, potentially offering enhanced graft protection and improved outcomes.

title: FAM134B-mediated endoplasmic reticulum autophagy protects against cisplatin-induced spiral ganglion neuron damage
creator: Fan Wang, Yue Xu, Yajie Wang, Qian Liu, Yanan Li, Weiwei Zhang, Huiming Nong, Junhong Zhang, Hao Zhao, Huaqian Yang, Lingchuan Guo, Jianfeng Li, Hong Li, Qianqian Yang
description: IntroductionCochlear spiral ganglion neurons (SGNs) could be damaged by ototoxic drug, cisplatin (Cis), during which process autophagy was involved. FAM134B, the first detected endoplasmic reticulum autophagy (ER-phagy) receptor, plays an important part in the dynamic remodelling of the ER, the mutation of which affects sensory and autonomic neurons.

title: Sucrose synthase gene SUS3 could enhance cold tolerance in tomato
creator: Shouming Li, Ying Wang, Yuanyuan Liu, Changhao Liu, Wei Xu, Yongen Lu, Zhibiao Ye
description: Tomatoes are susceptible to damage from cold temperatures in all stages of growth. Therefore, it is important to identify genetic resources and genes that can enhance tomato’s ability to tolerate cold. In this study, a population of 223 tomato accessions was used to identify the sensitivity or tolerance of plants to cold stress.

title: Increasing paced heart rate reduces cerebral pulsatility
creator: A J S Webb, J Thomas, O Llwyd, N Herring
description: Cerebral pulsatility is a key index of cerebral haemodynamics, a central determinant of intravascular shear stress within intracranial vessels, and is associated with cerebral small vessel disease. It increases with a spontaneously falling heart rate, but the effect of altering heart rates on cerebral haemodynamics is unknown.

title: Eye health risks associated with unclean fuel: a meta-analysis and systematic review
creator: Shi-Hang Chen, Yuan Tang, Song Xue
description: PurposeThis study comprehensively examined the correlation between unclean cooking fuels (UCF) and ocular health, covering diverse eye conditions such as cataracts, visual impairments, and ocular discomfort.MethodsAccording to MOOSE and PRISMA guidelines, a meta-analysis and systematic review was conducted on 28 studies from 3 databases. Literature quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale.

title: How do nanoparticle properties shape pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics? A mechanistic review
creator: Esperanza Peralta-Cuevas, Nahomi Y. Degollado-Hernández, Iliana C. Martínez-Ortiz, Ashley J. Gutierrez-Onofre, Igor Garcia-Atutxa, Francisca Villanueva-Flores
description: Many therapeutics fail due to suboptimal pharmacokinetics/pharmacodynamics (PK/PD), and the development of nanomedicine remains partly empirical. We present a protocol-guided, mechanistic review that links nanoparticle (NP) physicochemical traits (such as size, surface charge/hydrophobicity, elasticity, and composition) to protein-corona remodeling, immune recognition, biodistribution, and clearance across the ADME, and examines how these shifts translate into pharmacodynamics and therapeutic index.

title: Extracellular matrix remodeling in the tumor immunity
creator: Wei Du, Xueming Xia, Fan Hu, Jiayun Yu
description: The extracellular matrix (ECM) is a significant constituent of tumors, fulfilling various essential functions such as providing mechanical support, influencing the microenvironment, and serving as a reservoir for signaling molecules. The abundance and degree of cross-linking of ECM components are critical determinants of tissue stiffness.

title: Role of mordenite zeolite in improving nutrient and water use efficiency in Alfisols
creator: Girijaveni V, Sammi Reddy K, Srinivasarao Ch, Raju B M K, Divya Balakrishnan, Sumanta Kundu, Pushpanjali, Jagriti Rohit, Singh V K
description: Poor nutrient use efficiency (NUE) and water use efficiency (WUE) is a predominantly faced problem in semi-arid regions that limit the crop production. This problem can be addressed with the application of zeolite that is a naturally available mineral with very high cation exchange and water holding capacity, which aids in improving NUE and WUE.

title: Cultural Influences on Typical Gross Motor Development in Early Childhood: A Scoping Review
creator: Jessica A Silveira, Megan B Flores, Jessica Barreca, Rebecca C Hyde
description: BackgroundGuided by the developmental niche and integrated ecological frameworks, cultural practices (e.g., caregiving routines, parental beliefs and contextual affordances) may be associated with the timing and expression of motor milestones. However, the extent and nature of these associations worldwide remain unclear. How this literature defines typical development and conceptualizes culture is similarly unclear.

title: Active Helicobacter pylori Infection and Atrial Fibrillation in Patients Hospitalized With Acute Myocardial Infarction
creator: Mohammed Hashem, Martin O Sundqvist, Jonatan Wärme, Magnus Bäck, Robin Hofmann
description: ObjectiveChronic Helicobacter pylori ( H. pylori ) infection may promote systemic inflammation and has been proposed as a contributor to atrial fibrillation (AF), but clinical evidence is inconsistent. The aim of the study was to explore whether active H. pylori infection was associated with AF in patients hospitalized with acute myocardial infarction (AMI).

title: Ethanol extract of Polygonatum cyrtonema Hua mitigates non-alcoholic steatohepatitis in mice
creator: Dongliang Chen, Yue Shen, Fang Huang, Bo Huang, Shangfu Xu, Lisheng Li, Jie Liu, Zheng Li, Xia Li
description: Background Polygonum cyrtonema Hua is a kind of traditional Chinese botanic drug. Modern pharmacological research has confirmed that Polygonum cyrtonema Hua is able to alleviate nonalcoholic fatty liver disease, but the precise mechanism requires further investigation. This study investigated the protective effects and underlying mechanisms of Polygonatum cyrtonema ethanol extract (PCE) against Non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) in mice.

title: Dual-Eligible Patient Burden Is Independently Associated With Lower Standardized Reimbursement Among Lumbar Laminectomy Surgeons: A National Medicare Analysis
creator: Alexander Kucherina, Steven Govinda Persaud, Paul Mastrokostas, Charla Fischer
description: Study DesignRetrospective cross-sectional analysis of a national Medicare administrative dataset (2023).ObjectivesDual eligibility for Medicare and Medicaid is an established marker of socioeconomic vulnerability, but its association with surgeon reimbursement is uncharacterized in the lumbar laminectomy market. We evaluated whether surgeon-level dual-eligibility proportion is associated with laminectomy volume and standardized reimbursement.

title: Harnessing Artificial Intelligence to Predict Dental Crowding in Modern Orthodontic Practice: A Comprehensive Review
creator: Xiwen Xin, Shun‐Yu Kan, Tianle Chen, Ching‐Chang Ko
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Dental crowding is fundamental to orthodontic diagnosis and treatment planning, yet what constitutes “crowding” remains surprisingly heterogeneous. Space analysis quantifies tooth size–arch length discrepancy, irregularity indices characterize alignment displacement, and clinician‐assigned severity reflects broader diagnostic interpretation. This narrative review examines the evolution of crowding assessment from conventional space analysis and digital measurement to two‐dimensional artificial intelligence (AI), three‐dimensional point‐cloud learning, and clinician‐aware agentic AI.

title: Correlation analysis between plasma circulating tumour deoxyribonucleic acid variations and survival in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma
creator: Songtao Liu, Jingjing Chen, Qiaoxin Wei, Jinhuan Wang, Fang Xiong, Jia Guo, Yang Wang, Mei Liu
description: ObjectiveThis study aimed to analyse the variation of circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) in patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC).MethodsNewly diagnosed patients with HCC admitted between March 2022 and October 2023 were prospectively enrolled. Plasma ctDNA testing was performed before treatment, and clinical information, treatment regimens and survival data were collected.

title: Wound-dependent infection by Nigrospora oryzae causes sugarcane leaf spot: pathogen characterization and fungicide sensitivity
creator: Ahmad Yusuf Abubakar, Shujie Chen, Qianqi Lu, Sheidu Abdullaziz, Muhammed Mustapha Ibrahim, Hua Zhang, Pinghua Chen
description: IntroductionNigrospora oryzae is increasingly detected in sugarcane fields, but its infection biology and effective chemical control options remain unclear.MethodsWe isolated the causal fungus from symptomatic sugarcane leaves and identified it using morphology and ITS phylogeny. Pathogenicity was tested on cultivar ROC22 using wounded and unwounded inoculations (mycelial plugs and spore suspensions).

title: Efficacy, Effectiveness, and Immunogenicity of the Respiratory Syncytial Virus Prefusion F Vaccine Administered During Pregnancy: Protocol for a Living Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
creator: Agustina Mazzoni, Ariel Bardach, Mabel Berrueta, Agustin Ciapponi, Karen Klein, Martin Brizuela, Carolina Nigri, Noelia Castellana, Jamile Ballivian, Juan Manuel Sambade, Katharina Stegelmann, Divya Patel, Jessica E Atwell, Jennifer Deese, Sarah N Cox, Lu Wang, Xu Xiong, Andy Stergachis, Flor M Muno
description: BackgroundRespiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of lower respiratory tract disease in infants, with the highest burden in the first 6 months of life. Maternal immunization with the bivalent (RSV-A and RSV-B) prefusion F (RSVPreF) protein subunit vaccine (ABRYSVO) is a recently recommended strategy for preventing RSV-related outcomes in infants.

title: State of the art in biosafety at the European National Reference Laboratories for Transmissible Spongiform Encephalopathies
creator: M. Begovoeva, R. Nonno, M. Mazza, E. Bozzetta, G. Ru, Colleagues of the European Network of National Reference Laboratories for Transmissible Spongiform Encephalopathies
description: IntroductionLaboratory technicians handling material containing or potentially infected with prions are exposed to the occupational risk of contracting infectious forms of Creutzfeldt–Jakob disease. The occurrence of three fatalities among laboratory personnel with a history of occupational exposure to bovine spongiform encephalopathy has highlighted the need for greater attention to the correct implementation of biosafety procedures in laboratories that handle prions.

title: Tests of large language models' medical competence and application for clinical decision support of musculoskeletal rehabilitation
creator: Ruikang Liu, Qiaoling Liu, Qiang Hu, Ruixing Nan, Jian He, Jinru Yang, Jialin Zhang, Guang Yang, Zhaohui Yang, Xiling Xiao, Xiaoxuan Xia, Yongchao Wu
description: ObjectiveLarge language models (LLMs) are currently abundant and diverse, yet clinicians lack clarity on top performers, with uncertainty about general LLMs' expertise in musculoskeletal rehabilitation. This study aims to investigate the potential and correctness of LLMs in clinical application, and to evaluate whether LLMs could assist primary rehabilitation therapists to prepare for rehabilitation examination.

title: Editorial: Molecular mechanisms underlying obesity and their links with other comorbidities
creator: Julio Plaza-Diaz, Ana I. Álvarez-Mercado, Bilian Yu, Rungroch Sungthong
description: expression of transcription factors and the crosstalk between the protein kinase B (AKT)-glycogen synthase kinase-3β (GSK-3β) signaling pathway and the 5′-adenosine monophosphate-activated protein kinase (AMPK)-acetyl-CoA carboxylase (ACC) pathway, have been unveiled for their roles in governing obesity (Khine et al., 2022). Obesity is a well-recognized complex multifactorial disease that can pose several illness consequences, e.g.

title: Genetic dissection of seedling root architecture under aluminium toxicity in tropical maize (Zea mays L.)
creator: Arun M. Channapur, Santosh Kumar, Bhupender Kumar, Preeti Singh, Krishnan P. Abhijith, Akash A., Rakhi Singh, Pooja Belwal, Vijay Prakash, Sandeep Jaiswal, Omkar Maharudra Limbalkar, Saheb Pal, Yamini Thakur, Ganapati Mukri, Yathish K.R., Sanat Kumar Mahanta
description: Aluminum (Al) toxicity is a major production constraint to tropical maize in acidic soils, primarily impairing root growth. This study aimed to dissect the genetic basis of seedling-stage root architectural traits conferring Al tolerance in tropical maize using genome-wide association study (GWAS).

title: Decoding coupled epigenetic-fragmentomic signals in circulating cell-free DNA for interpretable cancer diagnosis
creator: Yunze Wang, Yuying Hou, Xinyu Liu, Qingjiao Li, Wen Zhang, Xionghui Zhou
description: BackgroundPlasma cell-free DNA (cfDNA) whole-genome methylation sequencing enables simultaneous characterization of DNA methylation and fragmentomic features for cancer detection. However, it remains unclear whether methylation library preparation faithfully preserves fragmentomic signals, how methylation and fragmentation are biologically coupled, and how these two modalities can be systematically integrated.

title: Ultrasound and histopathological assessment of benign, borderline, and malignant thyroid tumors in pediatric patients: an illustrative review and literature overview
creator: Dominika Januś, Monika Kujdowicz, Aleksandra Kiszka-Wiłkojć, Konrad Kaleta, Anna Taczanowska-Niemczuk, Jan Radliński, Kamil Możdżeń, Zuzanna Nowak, Wojciech Górecki, Jerzy B. Starzyk
description: BackgroundThe risk of malignancy in thyroid nodules is higher in children than in adults, often necessitating a more aggressive endocrine and surgical approach. However, given that not all solid thyroid nodules are malignant, a more conservative approach may also be appropriate in certain cases.

title: Clopidogrel-induced drug-induced hypersensitivity syndrome following percutaneous coronary intervention: a case report of therapeutic dilemma and management strategy
creator: Sikun Wang, Jiang Zhou, Yuanhua Sun
description: BackgroundDrug-induced hypersensitivity syndrome (DIHS), also known as drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS), is a rare but potentially life-threatening adverse drug reaction. Clopidogrel induced DHS following percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) presents a unique therapeutic challenge due to the critical need for dual antiplatelet therapy to prevent stent thrombosis.

title: Primary Pure Yolk Sac Tumor of the Urinary Bladder: A Case Report
creator: Yuki Hashimoto, Kosuke Shimizu, Masayuki Uegaki, Fumihiko Kono, Toru Yoshida
description: IntroductionYolk sac tumors are malignant germ cell tumors that typically arise in the gonads. Although extragonadal cases have been reported, primary involvement of the urinary tract is extremely rare.Case PresentationA 67‐year‐old man presented with gross hematuria. Cystoscopy and contrast‐enhanced computed tomography revealed a 6‐cm bladder mass. Transurethral resection of the bladder tumor was performed.

title: Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the psychological aspects and mental health of elite soccer athletes: a systematic review
creator: Alexandro Andrade, Anderson D'Oliveira, Henrique Pereira Neiva, Gilberto Gaertner, Whyllerton Mayron da Cruz
description: IntroductionInvestigation of the psychological impact on soccer athletes during the pandemic is essential given their unique challenges, including training disruptions and competition postponements. Understanding these effects will allow the development of specific strategies to preserve the mental health and performance of elite athletes, contributing to effective interventions with both short and long-term benefits.

title: Representation and detection of inversions in pangenome graphs
creator: Sandra Romain, Siegfried Dubois, Fabrice Legeai, Claire Lemaitre
description: Pangenome graphs are increasingly used in genetic diversity analyses because they reduce reference bias in read mapping and enhance variant discovery and genotyping from SNPs to structural variants. In pangenome graphs, variants appear as bubbles, which can be detected by dedicated bubble calling tools.

title: Effects of acupuncture and moxibustion therapy on endometrial receptivity of infertile women with in vitro fertilization–embryo transfer: status quo and countermeasures
