creator: Xiao-Zhu Guo, Zhen Qin, Deng-Hui Wu, Han Han, Yan-Hua Han, Xiao-Ke Wu, Yue-Hui Zhang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundIn vitro fertilization–embryo transfer (IVF-ET) is a core assisted reproductive technology (ART) for infertile couples, but poor endometrial receptivity (ER) severely impairs embryo implantation and reduces success rates, imposing significant psychological and economic burdens.

title: The association between extreme heat and sperm quality in a chronically heat-exposed population
creator: Samuel H. Gunther, Bing Yang Tan, Jason K. W. Lee, Shaili P. Sashidharan, Shiao-yng Chan, Qiong Wang, Zhongwei Huang
description: Background:Extreme heat has detrimental effects on male fertility. Previous studies conducted mainly in temperate countries have reported an association between higher ambient temperatures and decreased sperm quality. These findings might not be applicable to populations in tropical regions, who are chronically exposed to high ambient heat.

title: Highly‐Time‐Resolved Measurements of Tryptophan's Distribution and Homeostatic Regulation in Live, Intact Animals
creator: Yuyang Wu, Chelsea N Brown, Zeki Duman, Rose Mery Bakestani, Carl M Kirkpatrick, Joao Hespanha, Tod Kippin, Kevin W Plaxco
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Current theories regarding tryptophan's homeostatic regulation, which are derived from in vitro, post‐mortem, and cell‐culture studies, lack any direct evidence supporting their occurrence in living subjects. In response, here we have used 20 s resolution, multi‐hour plasma measurements to confirm, for the first time, that the cooperativity and tryptophan‐induced stabilization of tryptophan 2,3‐dioxygenase (TDO) seen in vitro and in cell culture hold in live, intact animals.

title: Long non-coding RNAs in response to Ebola virus vaccine-induced immunity
creator: Izabela Mamede, Thomaz Luschër-Dias, Isabelle Franco Moscardini, Patrícia Gonzales-Dias, Bárbara Marinho, Fernando Marcon, Thiago Dominguez Crespo Hirata, Michael Eichberg, Donata Medaglini, Ali M. Harandi, Claire-Anne Siegrist, Tom H. M. Ottenhoff, Francesco Santoro, Marylyn M. Addo, André Gonçalve
description: Long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs) have emerged as critical regulators of gene expression, yet their role in shaping human responses to vaccination remains largely uncharacterized. Here, we analyzed RNA-sequencing data from three independent human cohorts vaccinated with the rVSVΔG-ZEBOV-GP Ebola vaccine to profile lncRNA expression dynamics.

title: Risk factors for neurological complications in adult ECMO patients: a systematic review and meta-analysis
creator: Meijun Dong, Peipei Gu, Lingyun Cai, Yan Zhu, Li Sheng, Jiangshuyuan Liang, Shuhua Zhao, Fei Zeng
description: ObjectiveAiming to systematically review risk factors for neurological complications in adults receiving ECMO support.MethodsA comprehensive computerized search was conducted in Chinese and English databases for studies examining risk factors of neurological complications in adult ECMO patients, supplemented by manual and reference tracking, with the search period extending up to April 2025. Meta-analysis and sensitivity analyses were performed using Stata 18.

title: The interaction of post-activation potentiation and fatigue on skeletal muscle twitch torque and displacement
creator: Georg Langen, Frank Warschun, Olaf Ueberschär, Michael Behringer
description: IntroductionTensiomyography (TMG) assesses skeletal muscle contractile properties based on the electrically stimulated radial muscle displacement. As the relationship between twitch displacement and associated torque is poorly understood, it is unclear how it is affected by post-activation potentiation and muscle fatigue. This study investigated how the interaction of potentiation and fatigue affects the rectus femoris (RF) twitch displacement and associated torque.

title: Author Correction: Obesity-associated macrophages dictate adipose stem cell ferroptosis and visceral fat dysfunction by propagating mitochondrial fragmentation
creator: Yan Tao, Jinhao Zang, Tianci Wang, Peixuan Song, Zixin Zhou, Huijie Li, Yalin Wang, Yiyang Liu, Haipeng Jie, Mei Kuang, Hui Zhao, Fuwu Wang, Shen Dai, Chun Guo, Faliang Zhu, Haiting Mao, Fengming Liu, Lining Zhang, Qun Wang

title: Host-resistance in Allium genotypes against pantaphos producing Pantoea ananatis
creator: Brendon K. Myers, Navjot Kaur, Michelle P. MacLellan, Ronald Gitaitis, Angelo Antonio Manzatto, Adriano Ferrasa, Elkin Fernando Rodas-Mendoza, Jhon Jairo Giraldo-González, Roberto H. Herai, Bhabesh Dutta
description: IntroductionOnion (Allium cepa L.) is a globally important crop severely affected by Pantoea ananatis, the causal agent of onion center rot (OCR). The pathogen’s virulence is driven by the chromosomally located HiVir cluster, which produces the phytotoxin pantaphos. Despite its economic significance, resistant Allium genotypes against P. ananatis have not been identified.

title: Two pediatric type II achalasia cases complicated by candidal and eosinophilic esophagitis: Successful peroral endoscopic myotomy treatment
creator: Fabio Rotondo, Antonio Marseglia, Anna Locatelli, Dalila Tedeschi, Marco Gentile, Francesco Perri, Maria Rosa Pastore, Massimo Pettoello Mantovani
description: Achalasia is a rare esophageal motility disorder in children, often leading to delayed diagnosis. We report the first two pediatric cases treated with peroral endoscopic myotomy (POEM) at our center, both classified as type II achalasia and complicated by mucosal disease. A 15‐year‐old girl presented with progressive dysphagia and weight loss, diagnosed with type II achalasia and Candida esophagitis.

title: Hematopoietic cell transplantation using treosulfan-based conditioning for IL-10 receptor deficiency
creator: Madhavi Lakkaraja, Erica G. Schmitt, Amika K. Sood, Karin Chen, Arunkumar J. Modi, James W. Verbsky, Troy Torgerson, Ghassan Wahbeh, Aleksandra Petrovic, K. Scott Baker, Megan A. Cooper, Lauri M. Burroughs
description: Lakkaraja and Schmitt et al. observe that IL-10 receptor deficiency is a life-threatening inborn error of immunity associated with early-onset inflammatory bowel disease and found that employing hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) using treosulfan-based conditioning results in excellent survival with full donor engraftment. Importantly, anakinra effectively serves as a bridge to HCT.

title: Heterologous investigation of metabotropic and ionotropic odorant receptors in ab3A neurons of Drosophila melanogaster
creator: Johan Henning Pettersson, Alberto Maria Cattaneo
description: In insects, antennal ionotropic receptors (IRs) and odorant receptors (ORs) are among the main sensors of olfactory cues. To functionally characterize the subunits from these receptors, the use of ab3A neurons from transgenic Drosophila melanogaster represented one of the most powerful tools, allowing the identification of ligands (deorphanization) and decrypting their pharmacological properties.

title: Assessing PAH exposure during construction work of railroad switches using creosote-impregnated ties
creator: Jessika Hagberg, Håkan Westberg, Bo Strandberg, Christian Lindh, Ing-Liss Bryngelsson, Pål Graff
description: The toxicological effects of creosote are primarily attributed to exposure to polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) and related compounds. This study aimed to assess worker exposure by measuring PAHs in the breathing zone using full-shift air samples, urinary concentrations of 1-hydroxypyrene (1-HP), and dermal exposure through a tape stripping technique.

title: Correction to ‘Transcriptome-wide analysis of Arabidopsis DICER-LIKE1 RNA substrates’
creator: Unknown
description: e residues were inadvertently misassigned, leading to the erroneous reporting of the mutations as E1378Q and E1597Q instead of the correct E1508Q and E1697Q. This has been corrected in section Results and discussion, under heading Catalytically inactive DCL1 interacts with the microprocessor component HYL1 and stabilizes co-immunoprecipitated pri-miRNA.

title: CYP2D6 ‐Guided Opioid Therapy for Chronic Pain: A Multi‐Center Pragmatic Randomized Controlled Trial
creator: Todd C Skaar, Rachel A Myers, Roger B Fillingim, John T Callaghan, Kerri L Cavanaugh, Hrishikesh Chakraborty, Jordan F Baye, Emily J Cicali, Michael T Eadon, Erica N Elwood, Elizabeth C Harris, Lindsay J Hines, Khoa A Nguyen, Michelle A Ramos, Marc Rosenman, Azita Sadeghpour, Saskia Shuman, Rajbir S
description: The analgesic effectiveness of several opioids depends on CYP2D6‐mediated metabolism to more active opioid receptor agonists. CYP2D6 activity is impacted by genetic variability and medications that inhibit CYP2D6. We conducted a pragmatic, multi‐center, randomized, controlled trial to determine whether CYP2D6‐guided opioid prescribing improves chronic pain.

title: Sustainable Routes Toward Amino Acid‐Based Surfactants: Borrowing Hydrogen Catalysis and Beyond
creator: Maximilian Fellert, Ben L. Feringa
description: Amino acid‐based surfactants combine renewable head groups with tunable amphiphilic functional groups and are therefore attractive candidates for the development of more sustainable surfactants. However, bio‐based building blocks alone cannot guarantee sustainability. Moreover, it depends on the choice of synthetic route, waste generation, feedstock origin, catalyst, product performance, toxicity, and environmental fate.

title: Variations in the plasticity of functional traits indicate the differential impacts of abiotic and biotic factors on the structure and growth of trees in tropical dry forest fragments
creator: Ravi Kant Chaturvedi, Santosh Kumar Pandey, Anshuman Tripathi, Laxmi Goparaju, Akhilesh Singh Raghubanshi, J. S. Singh
description: Abiotic and biotic factors have considerable impact on the plasticity of plant functional traits, which influences forest structure and productivity; however, their inter-relationships have not been quantified for fragmented tropical dry forest (TDF) ecosystems. We asked the following questions: (1) what are the variations in the plasticity of functional traits due to soil moisture availability in TDF fragments?

title: Characterization of serum metabolome and respiratory microbiota in children with influenza A virus infection
creator: Xinyi Shi, Shenghao Hua, Zeyuan Chen, Weiyi Cao, Mengqing Xiao, Wenlong Pei, Zhe Cao, Zhan Zhang, Haibing Yang, Xuejun Shao, Yu Xia
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The risk of children being infected with Influenza A virus (IAV) is high, and if not treated promptly, it can lead to serious illness. Compared with control group, IAV infection decreased the contents of platelet, white blood cell, lymphocyte, eosinophil, basophil, CD3+ T cells, CD4+ T cells, CD8+ T cells, and B cells, while increasing the number of red blood cell.

title: Risk factors for malignancy in pediatric subacute/chronic focal craniocervical lymphadenopathy
creator: Yishai Haimi-Cohen, Eyal Elron, Lital Oz-Alcalay, Lama Hejly, Roy Hod, Liat Ashkenazi-Hoffnung
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). AimsTo describe the factors associated with malignancy in otherwise healthy children with focal persistent isolated craniocervical lymphadenopathy at low risk for malignancy, in order to aid in decisions of nodal surgical excision.Material and methodsDemographic and clinical data were retrospectively obtained for children with subacute and chronic craniocervical lymphadenopathy, treated from January 2008 to December 2020 at a general pediatric ambulatory clinic of a tertiary center.

title: A Compact and Fast Single‐Spike TTFS Encoder With Ultralow Operating Voltage for Efficient Neuromorphic Fourier Transform
creator: Yang Wu, Qi Wei, Junfeng Zhang, Lirou Su, Ning Mao, Beibei Huang, Jiaying Chen, Dian Huang, Shengzhong Feng, Yishu Zhang, Shuai Zhong
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Fourier transform (FT) is an indispensable mathematical foundation for frequency‐domain analysis in modern signal processing. However, conventional FT hardware relies on complex digital logic circuits, leading to high power consumption and poor adaptability. Spiking neural networks (SNNs) with time‐to‐first spike (TTFS) encoding offer advantages in energy efficiency, yet existing TTFS encoders suffer from high operating voltage, slow encoding speed, complex peripheral circuits, and redundant spike outputs. Here, we propose a compact, ultralow‐voltage, and ultra‐fast single‐spike TTFS encoder based on a Pt/TaOx/V device.

title: Weed Segmentation in Soybean Fields and Variable-Rate Herbicide Prescription Map Generation Based on UAV Imagery and Improved YOLOv11-seg Model
creator: Yaohua Yue, Anbang Zhao
description: IntroductionWeeds pose a major threat to soybean yield during the early seedling stage, where accurate identification of their spatial locations and contours is essential for precise field management. This study proposes an improved UAV-based YOLOv11-seg framework for high-precision weed segmentation in soybean fields.MethodsA real-field weed dataset was established under complex agricultural environments.

title: Fatigue in living kidney donors compared to a German general population sample: an exploratory study
creator: Dilek Akkus, Adrian Westenberger, Gunilla Einecke, Wilfried Gwinner, Uwe Tegtbur, Mariel Nöhre, Martina de Zwaan
description: BackgroundClinical studies have not conclusively clarified whether fatigue scores in living kidney donors after donation are fundamentally different from general population samples. Moreover, the association between sociodemographic and donor specific factors and fatigue in donors is not well understood.Patients and methodsFatigue scores of 358 living kidney donors on average 7.

title: Historical studies on the use of Rhubarb in Japan
creator: Misato Ota, Toshiaki Makino
description: BackgroundRhubarb product is the crude drug derived from the root or rhizome of Rheum or other related plants, and has been used since ancient times in Asian and European countries. However, the original plant species for Rhubarb product had been confused throughout its long history and across different areas.

title: The ‘analysis of gene expression and biomarkers for point-of-care decision support in Sepsis‘ study; temporal clinical parameter analysis and validation of early diagnostic biomarker signatures for severe inflammation andsepsis-SIRS discrimination
creator: Tamas Szakmany, Eleanor Fitzgerald, Harriet N. Garlant, Tony Whitehouse, Tamas Molnar, Sanjoy Shah, Dong Ling Tong, Judith E. Hall, Graham R. Ball, Karen E. Kempsell
description: IntroductionEarly diagnosis of sepsis and discrimination from SIRS is crucial for clinicians to provide appropriate care, management and treatment to critically ill patients. We describe identification of mRNA biomarkers from peripheral blood leukocytes, able to identify severe, systemic inflammation (irrespective of origin) and differentiate Sepsis from SIRS, in adult patients within a multi-center clinical study.

title: Sex testing in women's sport: historical harms, contemporary risks, and World Athletics' 2025 policy shift
creator: Silvia Camporesi, Marcus Mazzucco, Maria José Martínez Patiño, Jonathan Ospina-Betancurt, Sarah Teetzel
description: The history of systemic, mandatory sex testing of all women athletes in sport is now well documented, with hundreds of articles, entire books, and doctoral dissertations analyzing the scientific, legal, and ethical aspects of sports governing bodies' determination to verify that competitors in the women's event were women and that men did not sneak into women's sports.

title: Notes from the Field: Molecular Detections of Cladophialophora bantiana at a Clinical Reference Laboratory — United States, 2009–2026
creator: Maria T. Nelson, Thao T. Truong, Lori A. Bourassa, Dallas J. Smith, Joshua A. Lieberman
description: of infection is fully understood. What is added by this report? During January 2009–July 2026, 48 confirmed cases and one probable case of C. bantiana were detected in clinical samples (predominantly central nervous system tissue [88%]) originating in 22 jurisdictions and tested at a single clinical reference laboratory; detections of the fungus increased approximately fourfold from 2023 to 2025.

title: Acute kidney disease after acute kidney injury: incidence, risk factors, and association with de novo chronic kidney disease
creator: Sujia Hu, Xingyang Zhao, Yichun Cheng, Shuwang Ge
description: Acute Kidney Disease (AKD) is defined as acute kidney injury (AKI) persisting for 7 to 90 days and represents a window for interventions to improve renal outcomes. However, data on AKD remain underexplored. This retrospective cohort study at Tongji Hospital, China, included 23,868 adult patients who survived at least one AKI episode between January 2015 and April 2024.

title: OsteoStrong and dynamic exercise in older women: rethinking comparative effectiveness
creator: Furkat Ruzmetov, Rizaev Jasur, Laziz Jumayev, Aminjon Amonov, Xondamir Ahmadov, Baxodir Usmanov, Farrukh Narzullayev, Tarazi Naghashidi
description: Exercise is a cornerstone of osteoporosis management, yet the comparative effectiveness of isometric machine‑based training versus dynamic multicomponent exercise remains unclear. Lindberg and colleagues conducted a randomized trial comparing OsteoStrong (OS) to dynamic multicomponent exercise (DME) in 194 older women with osteopenia or osteoporosis, finding superior improvements in gait speed, back endurance, and balance with DME.

title: Profiling of small RNAs derived from tomato brown rugose fruit virus in infected Solanum lycopersicum plants by deep sequencing
creator: Mangle Chen, Donghai Wang, Jiali Yang, Yuhao Cao, Xuemei Song, Yuwen Lu, Hongying Zheng, Jiejun Peng, Guanwei Wu, Jian Wu, Junmin Li, Jianping Chen, Fei Yan, Shaofei Rao
description: Tomato brown rugose fruit virus (ToBRFV) is an emerging, rapidly spreading virus belonging to the genus Tobamovirus which seriously decreases tomato yields. RNA silencing is an evolutionarily conserved antiviral mechanism. In virus-infected plants, virus-derived small interfering RNAs (vsiRNAs) are one of the key components involved in the RNA silencing-based antiviral activity in plants.

title: Can grip strength capture what chair standing does? methodological considerations on functional measures and successful aging in three international cohorts
creator: Zebo Kudratova, Azamat Karabaev, Vazira Raxmanova, Arofat Sadikova, Shahlo Axmadjonova, Farzan Vira Bagheri
description: Population aging has accelerated globally, making successful aging a key public health priority. Zhuang and Gao address the prospective association between cumulative average grip strength and successful aging using three international cohorts. While their multi-cohort design offers valuable cross-population insights, several methodological choices warrant consideration. Grip strength may not fully capture functional determinants of successful aging.

title: IMiD/CELMoD-induced growth suppression of adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma cells via cereblon through downregulation of target proteins and their downstream effectors
creator: Yu Wang, Shunsuke Shimosaki, Emi Ikebe, Hidekatsu Iha, Jun-ichi Yamamoto, Nichole Fife, Tomonaga Ichikawa, Mitsuo Hori, Masao Ogata, Yoshiyuki Tsukamoto, Naoki Hijiya, Masatsugu Moriyama, Shotaro Hagiwara, Shuichi Kusano, Masumichi Saito, Kamruddin Ahmed, Akira Nishizono, Hiroshi Handa, Kazuhiro Mor
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Adult T-cell leukemia/lymphoma (ATL) is an aggressive T-cell neoplasia associated with human T-cell leukemia virus type 1 (HTLV-1) infection and has an extremely poor prognosis. Lenalidomide (LEN; a second-generation immunomodulatory drug [IMiD]) has been employed as an additional therapeutic option for ATL since 2017, but its mechanism of action has not been fully proven, and recent studies reported emerging concerns about the development of second primary malignancies in patients treated with long-term IMiD therapy.

title: Aberrant one-carbon metabolism and ancestral genetics underlie edematous severe acute malnutrition
creator: Natasha C. Lie, Yixing Han, Qing Li, Aarti Jajoo, Jared Redmond, Aparna Haldipur, Solome Zewdu, Emilyn Banfield, Shanker Swaminathan, Sharon Howell, Orgen Brown, Roa Sadat, Nancy J. Hall, Kwesi Marshall, Katharina V. Schulze, Thaddaeus May, Marvin E. Reid, Carolyn Taylor-Bryan, Mark J. Manary, Indi
description: Edematous severe childhood malnutrition is distinct from the non-edematous form of malnutrition and remains a major cause of under-five mortality. Its etiology remains unclear, although aberrant one-carbon metabolism has emerged as a potential contributor. Here, we assess genetic variants at loci known to influence one-carbon metabolism, and determine their association with edematous malnutrition in Jamaica and Malawi.

title: Symptom improvement with dosing above 9 g of low-sodium oxybate: effectiveness and safety in participants with narcolepsy in the DUET study
creator: Jerald H. Simmons, Logan D. Schneider, Chad M. Ruoff, David T. Plante, Deborah A. Nichols, Teresa L. Steininger, Marisa Whalen, M. Todd Kirby, Jing Dai, Alyssa Cairns, Richard K. Bogan
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). PurposeEvaluate effectiveness/safety of low-sodium oxybate (LXB; Xywav®) dosages > 9 g/night in participants with narcolepsy (type 1 [NT1] or 2 [NT2]).MethodsJazz DUET (prospective, multiple-cohort, open-label study [NCT05875974]) included screening, 9-day baseline (LXB 9 g/night [“LXB 9 g BL”]), 2–8-week titration, 2-week stable-dose, 9-day end-of-treatment (LXB > 9 g– ≤ 12 g [“optimized LXB > 9 g EOT”]; twice-nightly, first/second max doses = 7.5/4.5 g), and 2-week follow-up.

title: Atlas‐Guided CD55‐Enriched Neutrophil Extracellular Vesicles for Complement–Macrophage Modulation in Diabetic Wounds
creator: Tairong Cui, Jieying Li, Jibing He, Jia Wang, Yun Qian, Yilin Jin, Liuqing Yang, Zaijin Tao, Ziyun Li, Zhengsheng Chen, Wenjing Wang, Xin Ma, Jinglei Wu
description: Diabetic wounds are characterized by persistent inflammation and impaired immune resolution, yet the therapeutic translation of single‐cell atlases into rational immunomodulatory strategies remains limited. Here, integration of diabetic‐wound single‐cell transcriptomic datasets identifies a neutrophil subpopulation enriched in cluster of differentiation 55 (CD55) with complement‐regulatory and reparative features.

title: The effect of knowledge, attitude, and practice model-based health education on psychological well-being and self-efficacy of patients with concurrent cerebrovascular stenosis and coronary heart disease: a quasi-experimental study
creator: Qiyu Zhou, Yuli Qian, Dan Zhang, Huan Xu, Bei Yuan, Wenfeng Tian, Qiong Li
description: ObjectiveThis research aimed to evaluate the effect of knowledge, attitude, and practice model-based health education on patients with cerebrovascular stenosis and coronary heart disease who underwent simultaneous interventional therapy.MethodsSixty patients with cerebrovascular stenosis complicated with coronary heart disease and treated in The Third People’s Hospital of Hubei Province, from February 2019 to April 2021 participated in the study.

title: From data to action: leveraging Global Burden of Disease Studies for rheumatic and musculoskeletal diseases
creator: Shudan Chen, Yueyang Liu, Yu Xin, Yifan Qiu, Xuqiang Geng, Jiafeng Zhang
description: vely low, their chronicity, disability burden, and societal impact are profound (2). From the perspective of practicing rheumatologists, the burden of RMDs is not merely reflected in epidemiological curves, but in delayed diagnoses, irreversible joint or organ damage, prolonged pain, and loss of functional independence encountered daily in clinical practice.

title: Licochalcone B suppresses oxidative stress and apoptosis accompanied by upregulating Nrf2/HO-1 pathway to ameliorate diabetic nephropathy in mice
creator: Shan Luo, Yake Lan, Ruoqi Zhang, Zhongqiu Luan
description: IntroductionDiabetic nephropathy (DN), as a complication of diabetes, is one of the major causes of end-stage renal disease. Licochalcone B (LCB), a flavonoid active component derived from licorice, is well known for its anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties. However, the influence of LCB on DN remains unclear. This research investigated the effect of LCB on DN and elucidated the regulatory mechanism.

title: A randomized placebo−controlled clinical trial of oral green tea epigallocatechin 3−gallate on erythropoiesis and oxidative stress in transfusion−dependent β−thalassemia patients
creator: Kornvipa Settakorn, Sasinee Hantrakool, Touchwin Petiwathayakorn, Nuntouchaporn Hutachok, Adisak Tantiworawit, Pimlak Charoenkwan, Nopphadol Chalortham, Anchan Chompupoung, Narisara Paradee, Pimpisid Koonyosying, Somdet Srichairatanakool
description: β−Thalassemia patients suffer from ineffective erythropoiesis and increased red blood cell (RBC) hemolysis. Blood transfusion, erythropoietic enhancement, and antioxidant supplementation can ameliorate chronic anemia. Green tea extract (GTE) is comprised of catechin derivatives, of which epigallocatechin−3−gallate (EGCG) is the most abundant, presenting free−radical scavenging, iron−chelating, and erythropoiesis−protective effects.

title: The SEPALLATA-like gene HrSEP1 in Hippophae rhamnoides regulates flower development by interacting with other MADS-box subfamily genes
creator: Di Cong, Xue Zhao, Chang Ni, Mengru Li, Luwen Han, Jianlin Cheng, Hongzhang Liu, Huijing Liu, Dan Yao, Shuying Liu, Guoshuang Chen
description: MADS-box genes are classified into five categories: ABCDE, including SEP1, SEP2, SEP3, SEP4, and other homologous genes, which play important roles in floral organ development. In this study, the cDNA sequence of the HrSEP1 gene was cloned by RT-PCR and confirmed that this gene belongs to the MADS-box gene family.

title: The impact of linguistic vs. cultural imperialism on language learning
creator: Somayeh Razmjoo Moghadam, Ghasem Barani
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). The current study systematically reviewed selected literature on background, current conceptualization, and direction of the issues of linguistic and cultural imperialism in publications of applied linguistics and language teaching to determine themes in the field. To do this, based on the inclusion/exclusion criteria, provided in the PRISMA Chart, 30 most updated and recent articles (mainly since 2020) were selected from the 5 main publications in the field through the advanced search engines.

title: Application of deep brain stimulation for the treatment of childhood-onset dystonia in patients with MEPAN syndrome
creator: Jaya Nataraj, Jennifer A. MacLean, Jordan Davies, Joshua Kurtz, Amanda Salisbury, Mark A. Liker, Terence D. Sanger, Joffre Olaya
description: IntroductionMitochondrial Enoyl CoA Reductase Protein-Associated Neurodegeneration (MEPAN) syndrome is a rare inherited metabolic condition caused by MECR gene mutations. This gene encodes a protein essential for fatty acid synthesis, and defects cause progressively worsening childhood-onset dystonia, optic atrophy, and basal ganglia abnormalities. Deep brain stimulation (DBS) has shown mixed improvement in other childhood-onset dystonia conditions.

title: The added value of post-mortem MRI in forensic imaging: an observational study in the Netherlands
creator: Cédrique A. S. Gregoire, Maartje M. A. Eggen, Geneviève A. J. C. Crombag, Alida A. Postma, J. Martijn Nobel
description: ObjectivesIn the Netherlands, post-mortem radiology aids forensic investigation, using a full-body post-mortem computed tomography (PMCT) scan and a post-mortem magnetic resonance imaging (PMMRI) scan in specific cases. Application of PMMRI varies between countries and institutions in the absence of international guidelines. This study analyses current use and added value of PMMRI in a single forensic imaging institution in the Netherlands.

title: Socio-economic inequalities in minimum dietary diversity among Ethiopian children aged 6–23 months: a decomposition analysis
creator: Nigusu Worku, Amare Mesfin Workie, Lamrot Yohannes, Mihret Getnet, Wubshet Debebe Negash, Adina Yeshambel Belay, Lakew Asmare, Hiwot Tadesse Alemu, Demiss Mulatu Geberu, Melak Jejaw, Kaleb Assegid Demissie, Misganaw Guadie Tiruneh, Asebe Hagos
description: BackgroundGlobally, inappropriate feeding practices account for more than two-thirds of all cases of child mortality during the first 2 years of a child’s life. For a long time, Ethiopia has suffered from the double burden of malnutrition: overnutrition and undernutrition both pose significant challenges, particularly for children. Undernutrition is mainly caused by wealth and educational disparities across the country.

title: Establishing rabbit critical-size bone defects to evaluate the bone-regeneration potential of porous calcium phosphate ceramics
creator: Wei Lei, Yan Wu, Hao Yuan, Ping He, Jingqi Wu, Jingrong Chen, Yuxiao Liu, Hongmei Zhang, Joost D. de Bruijn, Xuerong Xiang, Ping Ji, Huipin Yuan, Mingzheng Li
description: Critical-size bone defects (CSDs), which are those that do not self-repair in a given period, are essential for evaluating bone-regeneration strategies. We established CSDs models in the rabbit cranium and ulna, and the bone-regeneration capacities of porous calcium phosphate (CaP) ceramics were assessed. A 12.

title: VIBE: an R-package for VIsualization of Bulk RNA Expression data for therapeutic targeting and disease stratification
creator: Indu Khatri, Saskia D. van Asten, Leandro F. Moreno, Brandon W. Higgs, Christiaan Klijn, Francis Blokzijl, Iris C. R. M. Kolder
description: BackgroundDevelopment of cancer treatments such as antibody-based therapy relies on several factors across the drug-target axis, including the specificity of target expression and characterization of downstream signaling pathways. While existing tools for analyzing and visualizing transcriptomic data offer evaluation of individual gene-level expression, they lack a comprehensive assessment of pathway-guided analysis, relevant for single- and dual-targeting therapeutics.

title: The effects of adolescents' sleep duration on life satisfaction: utilizing the autoregressive cross-lagged (ARCL) model
creator: Eun Jin Jung
description: IntroductionSleep duration in youth is a key factor that significantly influences mental health. However, there have been limited studies examining the direct impact of adolescents' sleep on life satisfaction. This study aims to analyze the effects of adolescents' sleep duration on their life satisfaction.

title: LLM‐Assisted Design of Ultralow‐κ Chalcogenides
creator: Yujie Liu, Congran Jia, Yuzhou Hao, Xuejie Li, Yang Wang, Artem Oganov, Jun Sun, Xiangdong Ding, Turab Lookman, Zhibin Gao
description: Accelerating the discovery of materials with extreme lattice thermal conductivity (κ) is limited by the high cost of first‐principles screening. Here, we develop an LLM‐assisted low‐κ discovery workflow, where Bayesian optimization (BO) proposes candidates, an LLM performs evidence‐conditioned re‐ranking, and physics‐based structure generation, stability validation, and κ calculations serve as the acceptance criteria.

title: Hepatic steatosis and postprandial hyperglucagonemia in early type 2 diabetes: Revisiting the liver–α‐cell axis
creator: Yu‐Ning Kuo, Jun‐Sing Wang
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). bolism and the emergence of glucagon‐based pharmacotherapies, increasing attention has focused on the interplay between glucagon regulation and hepatic lipid metabolism in type 2 diabetes. The study “Increased Early Postprandial Glucagon Concentrations in Humans with Newly Diagnosed Type 2 Diabetes and Steatotic Liver Disease” 1 examined the association between postprandial glucagon and hepatic lipid content (HLC) and whether amino acids or nonesterified fatty acids (NEFAs) contribute to this relationship.

title: Stretchable h‐BN/TPU Fibers for Passive‐Active Dual‐Mode Thermal Management and Wearable Haptic Interfaces
creator: Yiwei Zhou, Shanshan Long, Bo Chen, Maohua Li, Linhong Li, Yue Qin, Rongjie Yang, Hanxi Chen, Cheng‐Te Lin, Yixiang Xu, Kean How Cheah, Nan Jiang, Jinhong Yu
description: Wearable thermal interfaces require rapid, spatially confined thermal feedback together with mechanical compliance, yet existing passive thermal‐management textiles and active thermal‐haptic devices remain largely separate. Here, a stretchable h‐BN/TPU composite fiber is developed by coupling microfluidic spinning with non‐solvent‐induced phase separation.

title: cPRIME enables endogenous mapping of genetic variant effects at RNA level
creator: Ghanem El Kassem, Constanze Westphal, Marvin Doebel, Jasmine Hillmer, Tanja Seifert, Michael Boettcher
description: Understanding the functional consequences of genetic variants, particularly those classified as variants of uncertain significance (VUS), is a major challenge in genomics. While variant effects at protein level are well recognized, roles in post-transcriptional regulation are increasingly appreciated. Here, we introduce cPRIME (prime editing with cDNA readout), a scalable method for assessing variant effects at RNA level.

title: Sternoclavicular Joint Reconstruction for Chronic Anterior Instability: An Updated Sternal Docking Technique With a Modified Girth Hitch
creator: Nate J Dickinson, Ryan J Froom, Mikalyn T DeFoor, Tomas Aguirre, Christopher R Bine, Matthew T Provencher
description: Chronic anterior sternoclavicular joint instability can be functionally limiting in active patient populations, requiring reconstruction in patients who fail to achieve acceptable outcomes with nonoperative treatment. A variety of reconstruction techniques have been described including allograft or autograft figure‐of‐8 reconstruction, intramedullary graft reconstruction, synthetic suture‐based reconstruction, and tenodesis of the sternocleidomastoid or subclavius.

title: Combined Management of Meniscus Root Tear and High Tibial Osteotomy: A Surgical Strategy Using 3‐Dimensional Printing
creator: Arash Sherafatvaziri, Morad Karimpour, Ghazaleh Moradkhani, Yasaman Ghahremani, Fardis Vosoughi, Alireza Mirzamohamadi, Ramin Shayan‐moghadam
description: Combining high tibial osteotomy with meniscal posterior root repair is technically challenging because of the limited metaphyseal bone stock, the proximity of the transtibial tunnel to the osteotomy site, and the risk of implant conflict or tibial fracture. To address these challenges, we describe a surgical technique that integrates computed tomography‐based 3‐dimensional (3D) preoperative planning with patient‐specific 3D‐printed surgical guides.

title: Transcriptomic signatures of severe acute mountain sickness during rapid ascent to 4,300 m
creator: Ruoting Yang, Aarti Gautam, Rasha Hammamieh, Robert C. Roach, Beth A. Beidleman
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). IntroductionAcute mountain sickness (AMS) is a common altitude illness that occurs when individuals rapidly ascend to altitudes ≥2,500 m without proper acclimatization. Genetic and genomic factors can contribute to the development of AMS or predispose individuals to susceptibility.

title: Psychometric Validation of the Kannada Translated Version of the Adult Adolescent Sensory Profile
creator: Shalini Quadros, Ravindra N. Munoli, Podila Satya Venkata Narasimha Sharma
description: Background:Sensory modulation assessment is an integral part of occupational therapy practice; however, validated assessment tools in Indian regional languages are absent. One of the most widely recommended tools for measuring sensory modulation is the Adult Adolescent Sensory Profile (AASP). It is available only in English and a few other languages.

title: Listening to your partner: serotonin increases male responsiveness to female vocal signals in mice
creator: Kayleigh E. Hood, Laura M. Hurley
description: The context surrounding vocal communication can have a strong influence on how vocal signals are perceived. The serotonergic system is well-positioned for modulating the perception of communication signals according to context, because serotonergic neurons are responsive to social context, influence social behavior, and innervate auditory regions.

title: Renal Abscess Secondary to Urinary Tract Obstruction Caused by Pelvic Organ Prolapse: A Report of Two Cases
creator: Hiroki Sai, Kumiko Kato, Atsushi Kiyota, Yukiko Tsunoda, Masashi Kato
description: IntroductionPelvic organ prolapse can cause urinary tract obstruction, leading to hydronephrosis, pyelonephritis, and in rare cases, renal abscess.Case PresentationWe report two elderly women with advanced pelvic organ prolapse who developed renal abscesses. Both presented with pyelonephritis and acute renal impairment accompanied by bilateral hydronephrosis. Imaging demonstrated poorly enhanced renal lesions consistent with renal abscess.

title: Recalibrating the kidney failure risk equation for a Mediterranean European population: reducing age and sex inequality
creator: Daniel Bundó-Luque, Oriol Cunillera-Puértolas, Sílvia Cobo-Guerrero, José Romano, Ariadna Arbiol-Roca, José Alberto Domínguez-Alonso, Josep Maria Cruzado, Betlem Salvador-González
description: IntroductionChronic kidney disease (CKD) patients may develop kidney failure (KF), receiving renal replacement therapy (RRT) in some cases. The Kidney Failure Risk Equation (KFRE-4), predicting RRT risk, is widely validated but not in a primary care Mediterranean European population. We aim to recalibrate KFRE-4 accordingly, considering death as a competing risk, to improve performance.

title: A rare instance of Ogilvie syndrome in a pediatric patient with a complex medical history: A case report
creator: Kirby Lampe, Victoria Sarata, Aileen Har, Fernando Zapata
description: Acute colonic pseudo‐obstruction or Ogilvie's syndrome is an acute dilatation of the large bowel without an obstructive lesion. Symptoms include abdominal distension, nausea and vomiting, constipation, and occasional dyspnea. The disorder most commonly involves the cecum and right colon and is most frequently seen in male patients above the age of 60.

title: Suspected fibrosing cholestatic hepatitis in an immunocompetent child with hepatitis C: Case report
creator: Sara Bohon, Regino Gonzalez‐Peralta, Robert J. Fontana, Richard Cordle, Robin LeGallo, Frank DiPaola
description: A 12‐year‐old boy presented to our center with elevated aminotransferases, jaundice, right upper quadrant tenderness, and hepatomegaly. Evaluation revealed a highly elevated blood hepatitis C virus (HCV) ribonucleic acid (RNA) level, and liver biopsy showed canalicular and intrahepatic cholestasis, feathery degeneration of hepatocytes, and periportal/perisinusoidal fibrosis.

title: Dysregulated Cholesterol Metabolism, Chronic Inflammation, and Disability in Severe Progressive Multiple Sclerosis
creator: Taylor R Wicks, Mujeeb Shittu, Anna Wolska, Diala Ghazal, Bianca Weinstock‐Guttman, Alexander Burnham, Alan T Remaley, Robert Zivadinov, Murali Ramanathan
description: BackgroundDysregulated lipid metabolism, which can affect remyelination and neural repair, has not been extensively investigated in progressive multiple sclerosis (PMS). The goal was to examine whether dysregulated cholesterol metabolism was associated with disability in PMS.MethodsThe study sample comprised 53 Severe PMS patients (Expanded Disability Status Scale, EDSS score: 7.0–9.

title: Genetics of psycho-emotional well-being: genome-wide association study and polygenic risk score analysis
creator: Anna Yurievna Yakovchik, Darya V. Tolynyova, Daria A. Kashtanova, Ekaterina R. Sutulova, Mikhail V. Ivanov, Alexandra A. Mamchur, Veronika V. Erema, Lorena R. Matkava, Mikhail V. Terekhov, Antonina M. Rumyantseva, Olga I. Blinova, Aleksandra I. Akinshina, Sergey I. Mitrofanov, Vladimir S. Yudin, Val
description: BackgroundPsycho-emotional well-being is essential for living a life of satisfaction and fulfillment. However, depression and anxiety have become the leading mental health issues worldwide, according to the World Health Organization. Both disorders have been linked to stress and other psychological factors. Their genetic basis remains understudied.

title: Changes in Midrange and End Range Adjacent Segment Motion 3 Years After One‐ Or Two‐Level Cervical Arthrodesis
creator: Clarissa M. LeVasseur, Samuel W. Pitcairn, Xinyi Dan, Yan Ma, David O. Okonkwo, Jeremy D. Shaw, William F. Donaldson, Joon Y. Lee, William J. Anderst
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundBiomechanical cadaver studies consistently find that cervical arthrodesis leads to increased motion adjacent to the arthrodesis. However, in vivo evidence indicates adjacent segment end range motion does not reliably increase at 1 year after one‐level or two‐level cervical arthrodesis.

title: Targeting Nupr1‐Mediated p53 Mitochondrial Sequestration Alleviates Aortic Dissection by Restoring the Gadd45b‐Dependent Survival Program
creator: Xi Yang, Ke‐Yuan Chen, Yue Tian, Zong‐Sheng Jiang, Jian Lei, Xing‐Hui Zhuang, Jiang‐Bin Wu, Le‐Le Tang, Hao‐Yu Li, Xiao‐Hui Chen, Yue Wang, Yu‐Mei Li, Zhi‐Huang Qiu, Zi‐Wen Cai, Liang‐Wan Chen
description: Aortic dissection (AD) is a catastrophic cardiovascular emergency triggered by severe pathological stress. While continuous stress drives vascular smooth muscle cell (VSMC) apoptosis via mitochondrial dysfunction, the precise upstream orchestrators linking these stress signals to the mitochondrial apoptotic cascade remain elusive.

title: Human-enhanced tsunami hazard in large lakes
creator: Muhammad Naveed Zafar, Pierre Sabatier, Denys Dutykh, William Rapuc, Raphaël Paris, Andrea Piccin, Pascal Vuillemin, Flavio S. Anselmetti
description: Worldwide, human-induced erosion enhances sediment delivery to lake deltas, increasing their susceptibility to collapse. In Lake Iseo, northern Italy, two millennia of intensified land use tripled sediment flux, oversteepening the delta and preconditioning it for failure. Here we show from geological records and numerical simulations that earthquakes in 1117 CE (Mw 6.5) and 1222 CE (Mw 6.

title: Same Name, Moving Target: Model Version Drift in Syntheses of Large Language Models for Mental Health
creator: Bing Zhang Sr
description: us. I wish to raise an unaddressed threat to the pooled estimates: model version drift. Over the review’s search window (November 2022 to March 2026), “GPT-4” (OpenAI) did not denote a single intervention: released in March 2023, it was followed by API snapshots (gpt-4-0314, gpt-4-0613, gpt-4-1106-preview, and later GPT-4o releases) whose behavior differed materially.

title: Twenty questions from the surgeon to the radiologist to better plan an open partial horizontal laryngectomy
creator: Erika Crosetti, Giovanni Succo, Silvia Sapino, Ilaria Bertotto, Stefano Cirillo, Massimo Petracchini, Gabriele Fondello, Giulia Arrigoni, Martina Tascone, Cesare Piazza, Davide Farina, Marco Ravanelli
description: Open partial horizontal laryngectomies (OPHLs) represent a valuable therapeutic option for tumors of the intermediate T-category and, in selected cases, for locally advanced tumors with low-volume extra-laryngeal extension. The eligibility of patients treated with this type of surgery has increased with the introduction of the modular approach to OPHL planning.

title: S-propargyl-cysteine promotes the stability of atherosclerotic plaque via maintaining vascular muscle contractile phenotype
creator: Li Ping, Li Zhi-Ming, Zhang Bi-Shan, Zhu Lei, Yu Bo, Zhu Yi-Chun, Wang Ming-Jie
description: Introduction: Plaque rupture in atherosclerosis contributes to various acute cardiovascular events. As a new sulfide-containing donor, S-propargyl-cysteine (SPRC) has been reported to play a beneficial role in cardioprotection, potentially through its anti-inflammatory, anti-oxidative and anti-atherogenic activities. Our previous study observed an increase in eNOS phosphorylation in endothelial cells.

title: Irreparable Posterosuperior Rotator Cuff Tears Treated With InSpace Balloon With or Without Arthroscopic Subscapularis Repair: Short‐Term Clinical Outcomes in a Multicenter Retrospective Study
creator: Yash Sewpaul, Adam Mansour, Alexandra Makenzie, Albert D. Mousad, Casey M. Beleckas, Komal Singh, Samer S. Hasan, Jonathan C. Levy, Michael H. Amini, Robert U. Hartzler
description: PurposeTo evaluate the short‐term clinical outcomes of subacromial balloon implantation and concomitant procedures including subscapularis repair for irreparable posterosuperior rotator cuff tears.MethodsThis retrospective multicenter study included patients aged ≥40 years who underwent InSpace Balloon implantation between September 2021 and October 2024, with a minimum 12‐month follow‐up. Patients undergoing posterosuperior cuff repair were excluded.

title: In ovo myo-inositol administration: impacts on growth performance and metabolic profiles in broiler chickens
creator: Nataliia Shomina, Vera Sommerfeld, Markus Rodehutscord, Korinna Huber
description: Myo-inositol (MI) plays key roles in cellular signaling, membrane structure, and metabolic regulation, with its effects in poultry primarily explored through direct dietary MI supplementation. In this study, we aimed to assess the effects of in ovo MI administration on post-hatch performance and metabolism of broiler chickens.

title: Based on bioinformatics, SESN2 negatively regulates ferroptosis induced by ischemia reperfusion via the System Xc−/GPX4 pathway
creator: Jiejie Hu, Lijun Qin, Guoqiang Zhu, Jingjing Ren, Hongxia Wang, Jing Jin, Haixue Zheng, Dan Li, Zhaoming Ge
description: IntroductionCerebral ischemia–reperfusion (IR) causes severe secondary brain injury. Previous studies have demonstrated that ferroptosis is involved in IR-induced brain injury. However, whether IR induces ferroptosis in brain microvascular endothelial cells (BMVECs) is not fully understood.Materials and methodsOxygen–glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGDR) was performed in bEND.

title: Testosterone and Anterior Cruciate Ligament Injury and Reconstruction Outcomes: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis
creator: Dave Osinachukwu Duru, David Kwan Ryung Lee, Prushoth Vivekanantha, Marc Daniel Bouchard, Osama Alzobi, Loiy Alkhatib, Bashir A Zikria, Ashraf Hantouly, Moin Khan
description: Context:Testosterone influences connective tissue biology, neuromuscular performance, and postoperative recovery. However, its clinical impact on anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury risk and outcomes after ACL reconstruction (ACLR) remains unclear.Objective:To evaluate the association between testosterone replacement therapy (TRT) or endogenous testosterone levels and ACL tear incidence, ACLR revision, patient-reported outcome measures (PROMs), strength, and complications.

title: High levels of domestic transmission and drug resistance –analysis of national surveillance data for shigellosis, the Netherlands, 2018 to 2024
creator: Boas van der Putten, Hendrik Sauskojus, Anouk Meijs, Daan Notermans, Maren Lanzl, Eelco Franz, Maaike van den Beld, Roan Pijnacker, on behalf of the ISIS-AR study group
description: BACKGROUNDAntimicrobial resistance (AMR) among Shigella species is increasing, which is concerning. Strengthening surveillance is key to obtaining accurate, timely and actionable data on shigellosis.AIMWe aimed to describe Dutch national shigellosis surveillance data from 2018 to 2024, spanning the implementation of national genomic surveillance in 2022.

title: Distinct Clinical Features of Multiple Myeloma With t(11;14): A Post Hoc Analysis of JSH‐MM‐15 Study
creator: Taku Tsukamoto, Yuji Shimura, Shinsuke Mizutani, Takahiro Fujino, Haruya Okamoto, Mitsuhiro Itagaki, Hiroshi Handa, Takayuki Shimizu, Morio Sawamura, Tadao Ishida, Satoru Kosugi, Shuichi Ota, Makoto Yoshimitsu, Yutaka Shimazu, Isamu Sugiura, Hirohiko Shibayama, Shin‐ichi Fuchida, Hiroyuki Takamatsu,
description: t(11;14) (q13;q32) occurs in approximately 15%–25% of multiple myeloma (MM) cases and has traditionally been regarded as a standard cytogenetic risk factor. However, recent evidence suggests that MM with t(11;14) exhibits heterogeneous biological characteristics and clinical outcomes distinct from those associated with other cytogenetic risk categories.

title: Unsteady MHD transport of a tangent-hyperbolic ternary hybrid nanofluid over a permeable stretching surface with variable thermal conductivity and nonlinear radiation
creator: Abanti Datta, Amitava Dutta, Arka Banerjee, Sayantan Mukherjee
description: This work is a numerical exploration of the unsteady MHD transport of a ternary hybrid nanofluid of tangent-hyperbolic flow over a permeable stretching surface. The working fluid consists of Cu, and nanoparticles dispersed in ethylene glycol. The model includes nonlinear radiation, variable thermal conductivity, Joule heating, and Darcy-Forchheimer porous effects.

title: Cyanobacteria in sustainable agriculture: from bioactive metabolites toward mechanistically validated biostimulants
creator: Mauricio Junior Machado, Bruno Bachiega Navarro, Fernanda Rios Jacinavicius, Marli Fátima Fiore
description: Cyanobacteria are emerging as multifunctional components of sustainable agroecosystems, with the potential to influence nutrient cycling, soil structure, plant-associated microbiomes, and crop responses to environmental stress. This review integrates current knowledge of the molecular and physiological mechanisms underlying these effects, emphasizing nitrogen fixation, nutrient mobilization, phytohormone biosynthesis, extracellular polymeric substances, biocontrol-related metabolites, and stress mitigation.

title: Genome evolution of Mediterranean olives following DNA repeats diversification
creator: Flavia Mascagni, Samuel Simoni, Gabriele Usai, Alexis Ryo, Marco Castellacci, Ugo Rogo, Marilena Ceccarelli, Luciana Baldoni, Tommaso Giordani, Lucia Natali, Andrea Cavallini, Guillaume Besnard
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The olive tree (Olea europaea L. europaea) is one of the most representative perennial crops of the Mediterranean Basin, yet the genomic processes underlying its domestication and diversification remain poorly understood. Here, we investigated repeatome variation across 20 accessions, including 11 wild oleasters and nine cultivated varieties, using comparative clustering of high‐throughput sequencing data, complemented by structural analyses of transposable elements (TEs) and tandem repeats (TRs).

title: Decoupling Stable Cyclic Deformation From Defect Accumulation in Metals
creator: Chenjun Ye, Shaofan Ge, Tian Yang, Leyi Tang, Kang Wang, Y Morris Wang, Jun Ding, Zan Li, Di Zhang, En (Evan) Ma
description: Fatigue resistance in metals is fundamentally constrained by a long‐standing dilemma: the strain hardening required to suppress deformation localization is typically achieved through the accumulation of dislocations and other defects that ultimately promote fatigue damage. Whether cyclic plasticity can be sustained without progressive defect storage remains an unresolved question.

title: Microbiota evaluation in acute appendicitis: a preliminary study of appendix and childhood oral microbiota
creator: Renata Thomaz Katzenelson, Pedro Izzo, Beatriz Rissi Corrallo, Camila Lopes Crescente, Alana Cintra Alcantara, Fabíola Galbiatti de Carvalho, Leonardo Souza Marques, Emerson Tavares de Sousa, Thaís Manzano Parisotto
description: Despite the uncertainty of the sequence of events leading to appendicitis, the microbiome is presumed to play a central role in the pathogenesis. This preliminary cross-sectional study aimed to evaluate the intestinal microbes in distinct phases of acute appendicitis compared to the oral microbiota, considering the status of dental caries.

title: Changes in hormone receptor when breast cancer metastasizes to the colon: case report and literature review
creator: Huimeng Li, Liying Yang, Xiqiang Sun, Zhuquan Wang, Shuangwei Qin, Chengcheng Li, Gongwu Liu, Fengming Xie, Weiwei Gao
description: The metastasis of breast cancer to the colon is a rare occurrence, especially in the presence of changes in estrogen and progesterone receptors. To date, literature has only reported two cases of invasive ductal carcinoma and two cases of invasive lobular carcinoma metastasizing to the colon with concurrent changes in hormone receptors.

title: Scoping review of precision child and youth mental health research: dwelling in possibility
creator: Joonsoo Sean Lyeo, Angelica Blais, Paula Cloutier, Addo Boafo, Aroldo Dargél, Amanda Helleman, Tanya Tanya, Esperance Kashala-Abotnes, Christina Honeywell, Kathleen Pajer
description: IntroductionPrecision child and youth mental health (PCYMH) offers a promising array of tools and methodologies to address the intensifying burden of mental health challenges in child and youth populations. However, the current state of PCYMH research requires better characterization. To this end, we conducted a scoping review aiming to provide a ‘lay of the literature’ for this emerging field.

title: ‘We don’t know nearly enough’: an online survey exploring perspectives of specialists who support children with brain-based visual impairments
creator: Josephine Sabrina Jakubowski, Eloise May, Rebecca Findlay, Nicola McDowell, Samantha K. Simkin, Lisa M. Hamm
description: IntroductionChildren with brain-based visual impairments (some of whom have a diagnosis of Cerebral Visual Impairment, or ‘CVI’) represent a growing and underserved population within vision services. These children often have more complex needs than those with ocular visual impairments and benefit from specialist support from multiple disciplines.

title: Application of deep learning for real-time detection, localization, and counting of the malignant invasive weed Solanum rostratum Dunal
creator: Shifeng Du, Yashuai Yang, Hongbo Yuan, Man Cheng
description: Solanum rostratum Dunal (SrD) is a globally harmful invasive weed that has spread widely across many countries, posing a serious threat to agriculture and ecosystem security. A deep learning network model, TrackSolanum, was designed for real-time detection, location, and counting of SrD in the field. The TrackSolanmu network model comprises four modules: detection, tracking, localization, and counting.

title: Hot spots and frontiers in bone-tendon interface research: a bibliometric analysis and visualization from 2000 to 2023
creator: Hao Xiao, Boyuan Wen, Dong Yan, Quansi Li, Yujie Yang, Xianye Yin, Deyu Chen, Jiachen Liu
description: ObjectiveIn this research, we investigated the current status, hotspots, frontiers, and trends of research in the field of bone-tendon interface (BTI) from 2000 to 2023, based on bibliometrics and visualization and analysis in CiteSpace, VOSviewer, and a bibliometric package in R software.

title: Esophageal resonance Raman spectroscopy tracks mixed venous oxygenation in experimental shock and hypoxemia
creator: Tysen DeWaard, Bonne L Keijer, Franklin Ducatez, Cassidy Ferron, Jason Zhang, Yifeng Peng, Padraic Romfh, John N Kheir
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionMixed venous oxygen saturation (SvO2) reflects the balance between systemic oxygen delivery and consumption and is widely used as an indicator of tissue oxygenation in critically ill patients. However, its measurement requires invasive venous access.

title: Polygenic scores for longevity in relation to brain MRI measures in a cohort of 70-year-olds
creator: Nazib M Seidu, Olof Lindberg, Silke Kern, Lina Rydén, Lars-Olof Wahlund, Margda Waern, Rosaleena Mohanty, Nira Cedres, Henrik Zetterberg, Kaj Blennow, Hanna Falk Erhag, Anna Zettergren, Eric Westman, Henne Holstege, Ingmar Skoog
description: Population-based studies on the relation between polygenic longevity scores (PGLSs) and specific brain regions on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) are few. We aimed to investigate this relationship in a population of 70-year-olds from Gothenburg, Sweden (N = 675). We constructed two PGLSs (one with and one without the APOE locus) using longevity GWAS summary statistics.

title: Unlocking binding properties of single-domain antibodies targeting the polymeric immunoglobulin receptor to enhance mucosal enrichment of IgG against respiratory syncytial virus
creator: Jia Liu, Jiwon Jung, Siqun Zhou, Shi-Juan Chen, Jiping Huang, Yinyan Tang, Karin Vroom, Soha Motlagh, Daoyang Chen, Huong Trinh, Peter Worthington, Daphne Y. Ma, Zhiyun Wen, Bin Luo, Daniela Bumbaca Yadav, Jia Yao Phuah, Zhifeng Chen, Kalpit A. Vora, Masahisa Handa
description: A major driver of mucosal immunity is immunoglobulin A (IgA) that can translocate across mucosal epithelial barriers to protect against various pathogens in luminal spaces of the human body. The transcytosis of IgA is primarily mediated by the polymeric Ig receptor (pIgR), which is highly expressed in mucosal tissues and selectively transports polymeric IgA, but not IgG.

title: Visualized analysis of core themes and emerging frontiers in global chikungunya virus studies
creator: Jing Tian, Yonggang Li, Yuanlong Zhao, Xiaoli Tao
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundChikungunya virus (CHIKV) is a mosquito-borne alphavirus that has caused multiple outbreaks worldwide in recent years, resulting in millions of infections and severe complications such as chronic arthritis, posing an ongoing threat to global public health.ObjectiveThis study employs bibliometric methods to systematically analyze the core themes, development trends, and research frontiers in CHIKV research, aiming to provide a scientific basis for research planning and prevention strategies.MethodsBased on the Web of Science Core Collection database, a total of 3,709 relevant publications from 2015

title: Characterization and anti-inflammatory studies of supramolecular assemblies of chlorogenic acids with metal ions
creator: Zhen-Min Zhang, Ru-Yue Zhang, Lian Zhu, Zi-Xuan Liu, Han-Xiu Deng, Jie-Fu Tang, Jia-Yu Zhang, Wei Cai
description: IntroductionSelf-assembled natural small molecules are believed to have numerous potential applications, particularly in the material and pharmaceutical industries, as self-assembly increases the anti-inflammatory, antitumor, antiviral, and other biological activities. In this study, we synthesized more potent potential anti-inflammatory agents by combining chlorogenic acids with metals (iron and copper).MethodsSupramolecular assemblies were synthesized by combining chlorogenic acids with iron and copper.

title: NuXLApp: Interactive data analysis and visualization for protein‐nucleic acid crosslinking mass spectrometry
creator: Arslan Siraj, Sergei Moshkovskii, Tom David Müller, Henning Urlaub, Oliver Kohlbacher, Timo Sachsenberg
description: Protein‐nucleic acid (protein‐Nu) interactions are crucial for many cellular processes and biological functions. Crosslinking mass spectrometry (XL‐MS) has emerged as a powerful method for identifying these interactions. However, the analysis of protein‐Nu XL‐MS data requires an integrated workflow from raw data processing to results inspection and validation.

title: Flow Cytometric Lymphocyte Subset Enumeration for Lymphopenia Grading and C‐Reactive Protein‐Defined Inflammation Discrimination
creator: Shicheng Li, Tingting Fu, Yang Yang, Yuwei Pu, Wenying Yan, Junjun Zhang

title: Effect of probiotic lozenges on improvement in tympanometric classification within 12 weeks in children aged 3–6 years with adenoid hypertrophy and otitis media with effusion undergoing non-surgical management: a randomized controlled trial
creator: Jun Shi, Yu Liu, Xiaoning Chen, Xiaofei Hou, He Chen, Luomeng Chen, Le Li

Restoring middle-ear ventilation and clearing effusion are key goals during non-surgical management, and tympanogram classification serves as the main clinical indicator.

title: Quadratic descriptors and reduction methods in a two-layered model for compound inference
creator: Jianshen Zhu, Naveed Ahmed Azam, Shengjuan Cao, Ryota Ido, Kazuya Haraguchi, Liang Zhao, Hiroshi Nagamochi, Tatsuya Akutsu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Compound inference models are crucial for discovering novel drugs in bioinformatics and chemo-informatics. These models rely heavily on useful descriptors of chemical compounds that effectively capture important information about the underlying compounds for constructing accurate prediction functions. In this article, we introduce quadratic descriptors, the products of two graph-theoretic descriptors, to enhance the learning performance of a novel two-layered compound inference model. A mixed-integer linear programming formulation is designed to approximate these quadratic descriptors for inferring desired compounds with the two-layered model.

title: Refining risk prediction in geriatric heart failure: the emergency heart failure mortality risk grade‑BI model under scrutiny
creator: Kianoush A. h. Saberi L., Durdona Alimova, Sherzod Niyazov, Kholmurod Qayumov, Parvina Gaffarova, Xamida Juraqobilova, Zaynura Kadirova

title: Electrophysiological hallmarks for event relations and event roles in working memory
creator: Xinchi Yu, Jialu Li, Hao Zhu, Xing Tian, Ellen Lau

The current ERP study was designed to answer two questions: How is maintaining events (e.g., the tiger hit the lion) neurally different from maintaining item coordinations (e.g., the tiger and the lion)?

title: Deep learning analysis of MRI to assess rectal cancer treatment
creator: Heather M. Selby, Ashley Y. Son, Vipul R. Sheth, Todd H. Wagner, Erqi L. Pollom, Arden M. Morris

The subjectivity and variability in MRI-based cCR assessments highlight the need for objective, quantitative tools.

This study aimed to examine the mental health of children with vision impairment and associated factors in North-western China during the COVID-19 pandemic.

title: Trace amine-associated receptors (TAARs)2-9 knockout mice exhibit reduced wakefulness and disrupted REM sleep

title: The trend of phylogenetic and epitope variations of SARS-CoV-2 Omicron sub-lineages in Iran
creator: Mehdi Shabani, Ahmad Nejati, Jila Yavarian, Kaveh Sadeghi, Sevrin Zadheidar, Akram Sadat Ahmadi, Monire Ghadirali, Arghavan Zebardast, Adel Abedi, Mohammad Hossein Najmi, Nazanin-Zahra Shafiei-Jandaghi, Talat Mokhtari-Azad

title: Toward Sustainable Separation and Recovery of Critical Metals From Discarded Industrial Perovskite Solar Modules

Ultrasonic water leaching removes >99.8% of Pb from the perovskite layer without detectable dissolution of other target metals.

creator: Ilker Sengul, Demet Sengul
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The recent report by Gao and colleagues highlights an infrequent yet clinically significant manifestation of papillary thyroid carcinoma, PTC: isolated cutaneous metastasis appearing 8 years post‐resection. While the rarity of the case is undeniable, this critique explores the nuances of the diagnostic discordance observed—specifically the thyroglobulin, Tg, negativity in the metastatic lesion despite PAX‐8 and TTF‐1 positivity—and challenges the authors' hypothesis regarding the role of thyrotropin suppression. Furthermore, we examine the therapeutic decision to pursue conservative local excision over comprehensive systemic intervention.

title: Risk factors and clinical outcomes of cytomegalovirus infection following haploidentical hematopoietic stem cell transplantation in patients with aplastic anemia: a single-center retrospective study
creator: Jia Feng, Xinhe Zhang, Zhengwei Tan, Yuechao Zhao, Huijin Hu, Junfa Chen, Liqiang Wu, Qinghong Yu, Dijiong Wu, Baodong Ye, Wenbin Liu
description: BackgroundCytomegalovirus (CMV) infection remains a critical cause of mortality after allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, despite significant advancements in CMV prevention and treatment with the introduction and widespread use of letermovir. However, in China, due to limitations in the availability and cost of medications, some patients still face challenges in accessing letermovir.

title: Molecular Genetic Analysis and Prenatal Diagnosis of a Family With MECP2 Duplication Syndrome
creator: FengQiu Lin, DingGuo Chen, ZhengLin Lu, Yu Huang, ChunFang Wang, JuHua Liang, XueJuan Nong, ZhengYi Chang, FuBo Wei, GuiDan Xu
description: ObjectiveThis study aimed to conduct a molecular genetic analysis and prenatal diagnosis for a family with MECP2 duplication syndrome (MDS), with the goal of improving diagnostic accuracy and enabling informed reproductive decisions to reduce the incidence of this condition.MethodsThe study involved a proband (a 15‐week‐old fetus), his symptomatic older brother, and their parents.

title: Interfacial Reconstruction Enables Enhanced Thermoelectric Performance in Bismuth Telluride‐Based Alloys
creator: Wenyi Chen, Xiao‐Lei Shi, Meng Li, Chao Zhang, Konstantin Faershteyn, Siqi Liu, Yongqi Chen, Chengjiong He, Wanyu Lyu, Jun Pei, Nanhai Li, Zhi‐Gang Chen
description: Bismuth telluride‐based alloys are the benchmark thermoelectric materials for near‐room‐temperature power generation and solid‐state cooling, yet further performance improvements through conventional optimization strategies remain challenging. Here, we introduce an interfacial reconstruction strategy by incorporating SnSe into Bi0.4Sb1.6Te3. Interdiffusion and chemical reconstruction at the Bi0.4Sb1.6Te3/SnSe heterointerfaces synergistically regulate charge‐carrier transport and phonon scattering.

title: Spatial transcriptomics unveils the in situ cellular and molecular hallmarks of the lung in fatal COVID-19
creator: Carlos A. Garcia-Prieto, Eva Musulen, Daniela Grases, Veronica Davalos, Gerardo Ferrer, Belén Pérez-Miés, Tamara Caniego-Casas, José Palacios, Xavier Saenz-Sardà, Elisabet Englund, Eduard Porta, Manel Esteller
description: Severe Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) can induce progressive diffuse alveolar damage (DAD) leading to fatal outcomes. Here, we leveraged data from Visium spatial transcriptomics for COVID-19 and control lung samples to unravel insights into cellular and molecular events driving lethal COVID-19.

title: Aim high, hit ×10: psychological strategies driving the success of South Korean archers
creator: Joonyoung Lee, Suyoung Hwang
description: IntroductionSouth Korean archers have excelled in global competitions. However, limited research exists on the factors contributing to their long-term success, particularly in the context of achieving ×10 scores. This qualitative study investigated the exceptional success of South Korean archers, focusing on their achievement of ×10 scores.

title: FKS1/2-variant independent mechanisms underlying the emergence of resistance in echinocandin-refractory Candida auris infections
creator: Hugh Gifford, Arnab Pradhan, Ben Caswall, Sarah E. Murphy, Ian Leaves, Matt B. Edmondson, Tanmoy Chakraborty, Duncan Wilson, Surabhi K. Taori, Neil A. R. Gow, Rhys A. Farrer, Alistair J. P. Brown, Tihana Bicanic
description: The emerging fungus Candida auris is a drug resistant global public health threat and WHO critical priority pathogen. Recommended first-line invasive candidiasis treatment is echinocandin monotherapy, but C. auris can develop on-treatment resistance via FKS1/2 gene mutations and additional, previously unexplained mechanisms. To better understand echinocandin failure in C. auris, we sequenced the genomes of echinocandin refractory FKS1/2 wild-type C.

title: Improving Musculoskeletal Care Quality With a Web-Based Clinical Decision Support System in UK Primary Care: Mixed Methods Cluster-Randomized Controlled Trial
creator: Jonathan Hill, Hollie Birkinshaw, Muhammed Usman, Tammy Millward, James Bailey, Simon Wathall, Rebecca Naylor, Robert Malcolm, Melissa Pegg, Hayden Holmes, Kate Lee, Tanya Wright, Adrian Chudyk, Alex Braybrooke, Roanna Burgess, Martyn Lewis
description: BackgroundMusculoskeletal (MSK) conditions account for one in seven general practice consultations in the United Kingdom. Despite national guidelines, suboptimal care remains common. Digital clinical decision support systems (CDSSs) offer a promising route to improve care quality but have not been robustly evaluated in MSK primary care.

title: Enhancing Mental Wellness in Kenyan Adolescents and Young People: Protocol for a Platform Development and Usability Study
creator: Paul Macharia, Irene Misoi, Njeri Ngaruiya, Anne Mbwayo, Md Shafiqur Rahman Jabin, Javad Sarvestan
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundMental health disorders are a leading cause of disability among adolescents and young people in Kenya, yet access to appropriate and timely support remains severely limited due to shortages of trained professionals, stigma, financial barriers, and geographical inequities. Digital mental health interventions, particularly those leveraging AI, present a promising opportunity to expand access to culturally relevant, low-stigma mental wellness support in low- and middle-income country (LMIC) settings.

title: Prevalence and associated factors of severity levels of anemia among women of reproductive age in sub-Saharan Africa: a multilevel ordinal logistic regression analysis
creator: Lire Lemma Tirore, Abriham Shiferaw Areba, Aklilu Habte, Mitiku Desalegn, Abraham Sahilemichael Kebede
description: BackgroundSub-Saharan Africa is the most anemia-prone region, with several of the sub-region’s countries having a substantial prevalence of the anemia among women of reproductive age. Nonetheless, no adequate study has been conducted to illustrate severity levels and associated factors of anemia among women of reproductive age.

title: Frailty mediated the association between tooth loss and mortality in the oldest old individuals: a cohort study
creator: MingXia Wang, Xiaomeng Deng, Hanjie Chen, Yuhan Diao, Chang Liu, Jun Gao, Xin Tang, Xiaoyan Li, Yan Liu, Jun Duan
description: IntroductionTooth loss is associated with increased mortality risk; however, the mechanism underlying this is still not clear. The objective of this study was to explore whether frailty mediates the association between tooth loss and mortality risk among the oldest old individuals.MethodsThe participants were followed up from 1998 to 2018 in the Chinese Longitudinal Healthy Longevity Survey (CLHLS).

title: Correction
creator: Yang X., Wang Q., Xiao B., Wang Q., Deng W., Osherov N., Li, R., Liu W.
description: online version. The correct figures are: Growth rate and hyphal microscopic characteristics. (A) Colony size observation. (B) Growth rate detected by XTT assay. (C) Microscopic characteristics of hyphal morphology under white light and fluorescence microscopy following calcofluor white staining (×200 magnification). Susceptibility to calcineurin inhibitors, triazoles, and the combination of FK506 and CAS.

title: Approach to large thrombus burden in ST-elevation myocardial infarction
creator: Rohit Mody, Debabrata Dash, Bhavya Mody, Umanshi Dash, Rajeev Gupta
description: In ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI), Primary Percutaneous Coronary Intervention (PPCI) is the preferred treatment. However, High Thrombus Burden (HTB), defined by extensive thrombus in the Infarct-Related Artery (IRA), particularly with “cut-off” occlusion patterns and large vessel diameter (>3.5 mm), presents a major challenge.

title: Front-of-pack labeling and perceived nutritional quality in adults with and without chronic disease: results from a quasi-experimental study
creator: Patricio Pérez-Armijo, Samuel Durán-Agüero, Enrique Echevarría-Orella, Luis Carlos Abecia-Inchaurregui, Unai A. Pérez de Arrilucea Le Floc’h, Rafael Almendra-Pegueros
description: IntroductionNoncommunicable diseases (NCDs) are a leading global health concern, linked to poor dietary choices and misperceptions about food healthfulness. Front-of-pack labeling (FOPL) systems, such as Nutri-Score (NS) and Warning Labels (WL), aim to guide healthier food choices, yet their effectiveness in populations with chronic conditions remains underexplored.

title: Sometimes it’s good to be lucky: blood flow, glutathione, oxidative stress, and mitochondria
creator: Walter Gay Bottje
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). I knew the Ray Padovan who had coached me in age-group swimming one summer. I lucked out because EIU had a strong biology program that helped me in graduate school and beyond. After my first semester, Padovan told me I would receive a tuition scholarship through the Athletic Department based on my GPA (not for my phenomenal swimming ability). I came out of Eastern with a BS in Zoology that included 5 physiology courses and a minor in Chemistry.

title: Exploring the tumor micro-environment in primary and metastatic tumors of different ovarian cancer histotypes
creator: Bingqing Xie, Susan Olalekan, Rebecca Back, Naa Asheley Ashitey, Heather Eckart, Anindita Basu
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Ovarian cancer is a highly heterogeneous disease consisting of at least five different histological subtypes with varying clinical features, cells of origin, molecular composition, risk factors, and treatments. While most single-cell studies have focused on High grade serous ovarian cancer, a comprehensive landscape of the constituent cell types and their interactions within the tumor microenvironment are yet to be established in the different ovarian cancer histotypes.

title: Insulin-mediated ciliary remodeling in the choroid plexus epithelium
creator: Marleen Trapp, L Aurica Ritter, Greta Döking, James Cleland, Anthony D Hill, Annarita Patrizi
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The choroid plexus (ChP) epithelium plays a crucial role in cerebrospinal fluid production and brain homeostasis. ChP is mainly composed of multiciliated epithelial cells that exhibit a noncanonical ciliary organization whose function is still debated. Insulin signaling is known to be important for central nervous system function, but its role in ChP function and ciliary organization has not been elucidated yet.

title: Sex-informed estrogen receptor modulation in schizophrenia: a male-focused ERβ/GPER1 framework for cognitive and negative symptoms
creator: John Carlson
description: Treatment-resistant schizophrenia (TRS) remains a major unmet clinical need, particularly in males who exhibit more severe negative and cognitive symptoms and limited responsiveness to dopamine-based therapies. Estrogenic signaling—especially through estrogen receptor beta (ERβ) and the G-protein–coupled estrogen receptor 1 (GPER1)—has emerged as a promising neuromodulatory target for these domains.

title: Reading Between the ABCs: Intrinsic Disorder and Evolutionary Dynamics of Non-Canonical Regions in ABC Transporters
creator: Ichda Arini Dinana, Yukihiko Kubota, Masahiro Ito
description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ATP-binding cassette (ABC) transporters are one of the largest superfamilies of membrane proteins, but little is known about the structural and evolutionary features of their non-domain regions. To clarify the diversity of these non-canonical regions across evolutionary lineages, we performed an analysis of intrinsically disordered regions, site-specific selection and predicted post-translational modification (PTM) sites among five architectural classes involving 1581 prokaryotic and eukaryotic sequences. Linker and flanking regions were more disordered than transmembrane and nucleotide-binding domains in all architectures.

title: Survey of Bacterial Chondronecrosis with Osteomyelitis Lesion Incidence in Broiler Farms in Kazakhstan Regions
creator: Anh Dang Trieu Do, Gulim Assetova, Andi Asnayanti, Aizhan Akhmetzhanova, Assel Zhexenayeva, Dauletbek Muratbayev, Dilora Senkebayeva, Bakytzhan Bolkenov, Adnan Alrubaye
description: Simple SummaryLameness from bacterial bone infection is an important issue affecting global poultry production, negatively impacting animal welfare and productivity. Despite this, there is a significant knowledge gap and documentation of this disease in many regions of the world, such as the Republic of Kazakhstan.

title: Feeding ecology and behavioral adaptations shape injury patterns in central European ants
creator: Melvin Kenneth Opolka, Alina Koeters, Erik Thomas Frank, Palestina Guevara-Fiore
description: Injuries are common in animals and represent a major threat to individual survival. They can result from inter- or intraspecific conflict, predation, or pugnacious prey. Despite their potential ecological and evolutionary importance, injury patterns remain poorly documented in animal populations.

title: Evaluation of radiographic heart size measurement repeatability and reproducibility among veterinary students with varying training levels
creator: Radu Andrei Baisan, Vasile Vulpe
description: Vertebral heart scale (VHS) and vertebral left atrial size (VLAS) are commonly used to assess the heart size. It remains unknown if observers with different levels of training within the same protocol would improve the repeatability and reproducibility. This study aims to describe the measurement errors and to assess if different levels of experience can influence the outcome.

title: Electrophysiological Substrate and Ablation Outcomes in Atrial Fibrillation With Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: A Propensity‐Matched Multicenter Study
creator: Umair Abrar, Fazal Ghaffar, Muhammad Zuhaid, Huzaifa Bin Afzaal, Palwasha Abbasi, Muhammad Hasnain Iqbal, Moʻminov Jahongir Zokirjon oʻgʻli, Sifat Ullah Safi
description: BackgroundAtrial fibrillation (AF) is the most common sustained arrhythmia in hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), yet the intracardiac electrophysiological substrate underlying recurrence following catheter ablation remains poorly characterized. We compared the atrial substrate and ablation outcomes between HCM‐AF patients and propensity‐score‐matched lone AF controls.MethodsThis multicenter retrospective study was conducted across three tertiary centers in Pakistan (2015–2023).

title: An active and multifunctional curcumin-zein composite film for shelf-life extension in sustainable food packaging
creator: Zhihua Liu, Lingying Chen, Xiaozhi Zheng, Junlin Li, Jiankun Ding, Chen Cai, Xiaofang Chen, Haiming Yu, Qunlong Pan
description: Conventional plastic packaging faces significant challenges due to its non-biodegradable nature and lack of active preservation functionality, leading to environmental pollution and food waste. To address these issues, this study developed a curcumin-zein composite film as a multifunctional active packaging material based on natural polymers. Systematic characterization confirmed that curcumin was incorporated into the zein matrix through intermolecular interactions.

title: Phytochemical Characterization and Neuropharmacological Assessment of Combretum indicum Methanolic Extract With Integrated Molecular Docking and Dynamics Simulation for Anxiety and Depression Therapy
creator: Zobayed Islam, Md. Ashraful Alam, Sakib Ahamed Bhuiyan, Sabikun Naher, Nilufar Sultana, S. M. Naim Uddin
